title: Identity layer: org is re-pointable on update (tenant boundary)
description:
Confirmed against a live PB 0.39.8 (throwaway container).

animals / markings / weights updateRule is `AUTH && org = @request.auth.org` with no isset guard — 1700000043 deliberately exempted the three identity-layer collections. But an UPDATE rule's plain field ref resolves against the STORED record (the repo's own finding, 1700000043 + federfall-ti77), so:

  PATCH /api/collections/animals/records/<id>  {"org": "<other org>"}

passes: the stored org is still mine. Verified as a plain carer:
  - animals.org  -> 200 (record leaves the org)
  - markings.org -> 200
  - weights.org  -> 200
  - egg_records.org -> refused (1700000056 has the isset guard)
  - create straight into another org -> refused (create resolves against the new record)

Impact: the moved animal becomes invisible to its own org and visible/writable to the target org, while its org-1 children keep pointing at it. A supervisor of the TARGET org can then delete it, and `cascadeDelete` on animal takes org 1's cases, weights, markings and egg records with it. Probe confirmed: after the foreign delete, org-1 weights left=0, cases left=0. This is federfall-ti77's scenario through the other door — ti77 blocked re-pointing the child's animal, not re-pointing the animal's org.

Reachability: the launch org id is the hardcoded constant `org00000default` (1700000001), so a member of any secondary org needs no secret to push records into it.

Fix: append `&& @request.body.org:isset = false` to the animals / markings / weights update rules (new migration, guest-safe AUTH form). The app never sends `org` on update for these three — verified in edit_animal_sheet.dart, weight_entry_sheet.dart, marking_sheet.dart (org is create-only) — so this is `fix:`, not breaking. Pin it in test_rules.py next to the [animal org scope] block.

title: Editing an aviary 404s: the form resends the frozen `org` field
description:
Editing an aviary — e.g. changing its capacity — fails with PocketBase's 404
"The requested resource wasn't found." for EVERY role that is allowed to do it
(coordinator and supervisor alike). The record exists and the user may write it;
the 404 is the update RULE not matching.

## Cause

`1700000083_freeze_org_and_plan.js` appended `&& @request.body.org:isset = false`
to `aviaries.updateRule`, on the stated assumption that "the app only ever sends
these fields on CREATE". For aviaries that is not true:
`aviary_form_sheet.dart:66-78` builds ONE body used by both branches and it
carries `'org': org`, so every save from the edit form trips the guard. A rule
mismatch on update is a 404 in PocketBase, not a 403 — hence a "not found" for a
record the user is looking at.

Live rule as migrated:

    (@request.auth.id != "" && @request.auth.is_active = true
     && @request.auth.role != "guest" && org = @request.auth.org
     && (@request.auth.role = "coordinator" || @request.auth.role = "supervisor"))
    && @request.body.org:isset = false

## Second instance, same defect

`disposition_sheet.dart:147-176` sends `case` AND `org` in the body it reuses for
update, and `dispositions` has carried `@request.body.case:isset = false &&
@request.body.org:isset = false` since `1700000043_freeze_access_relations.js`.
Editing an existing disposition 404s the same way. Reproduced below.

The other sheets that send `'org'` are clean — they are all create-only branches
(weights, markings, journal, placements, animals, sponsorships, the code-list
admin, medication products). `codelist_admin.dart:329-333` shows the intended
shape: `org` spread into the create call only.

## Reproduction (live PocketBase, throwaway instance)

Against a fresh instance provisioned exactly like `tests/run.sh` does:

    [1] aviary capacity edit
      supervisor, app body (with org): 404 The requested resource wasn't found.
      coordinator, app body (with org): 404
      supervisor, without org:          200
      superuser (rules bypassed):       200

    [2] disposition edit
      supervisor, app body (case+org):  404 The requested resource wasn't found.
      supervisor, without case+org:     200

## Why the suite missed it

Every aviary PATCH in `test_rules.py` uses the SUPERUSER token (`T`), and
superusers bypass access rules entirely — so the frozen-field guards are only
ever exercised by the handful of tests that deliberately PATCH `org` as a real
user and assert the refusal. Nothing asserts that the body the APP sends still
gets through.

## Fix

1. `aviary_form_sheet.dart` — move `'org': org` into the `repo.create` call, as
   `codelist_admin.dart` and `sponsorship_sheet.dart` already do.
2. `disposition_sheet.dart` — same for `'case'` and `'org'`.
3. Add a guard so the next frozen field does not land here again: a test that
   PATCHes each affected collection as a NON-superuser with the body the app
   actually sends. The durable version is a sweep — for every collection whose
   `updateRule` contains `@request.body.<f>:isset = false`, assert no Dart update
   branch sends `<f>` — but a per-collection live PATCH in `test_rules.py`
   catches the same thing without a Dart parser.

Note the app-side fix alone restores the behaviour; the guards are correct as
they stand and must not be relaxed (they are the tenant boundary
1700000083/1700000043 exist to close).
close_reason: Fixed in ea6bf74: both sheets now send the frozen fields on create only; guarded by two widget tests plus a [frozen fields vs. the client] block in test_rules.py.

title: Animal-scoped rows can be re-pointed onto another carer's bird
description:
Confirmed against a live PB (throwaway container, real carer tokens, 2026-08-10 —
i.e. AFTER federfall-piu5 and the whole q7ks custody epic):

  PATCH weights/<own>   {animal: <another carer's bird>}   -> 200
  PATCH markings/<own>  {animal: <another carer's bird>}   -> 200
  PATCH exams/<own>     {animal: <another carer's bird>}   -> 200
  and the victim then READS the injected weight on their bird (1 row)

This is federfall-piu5's shape in the other direction. piu5 constrained the
`case` a row is filed into (1700000081); the `animal` a row hangs off is still
free. Custody does not see it: 1700000079's predicate resolves `animal.` against
the STORED record on update (1700000043's finding), so it checks custody of the
bird the row is moving AWAY from. The actor needs no relationship whatsoever to
the target.

Impact differs by collection:

  * `weights` / `markings` are ORG-WIDE READABLE, so an injected row is visible
    to everyone including the victim — it lands on the animal detail, in the
    weight trend chart, and in `case_report_rows`' markings column and therefore
    the annual report.
  * `exams` are case-scoped readable, so a re-pointed exam pollutes the target
    bird's lifetime record only for people who could already read the exam.
    Wrong data, narrower blast radius.

## Why this is not a one-line isset guard

`animal` is DELIBERATELY exempt from 1700000043's isset guards, because egg
re-attribution is a real feature: `egg_reassign_sheet.dart` moves a record to the
bird that actually laid it, and `test_rules.py` asserts `egg.animal IS mutable
(reassignment)`. So:

  * `weights.animal` / `markings.animal` / `exams.animal` have no re-point UI at
    all and could simply be frozen (`@request.body.animal:isset = false`), the
    way 1700000081 froze `case` / `applied_in_case`. Cheap, and it matches the
    app: no client sends `animal` on an update to any of the three (verify before
    relying on it).
  * `egg_records.animal` must stay mutable, so it needs custody of the INCOMING
    animal — which a rule cannot express on update for the same stored-record
    reason. That is a hook, shaped like `animal_org_scope.pb.js` but asking
    lib_custody.js's holds() instead of comparing orgs. Note animal_org_scope
    already walks exactly this set of collections, so it is the natural home.

## Testing

`test_rules.py`'s `[case-scoped writes]` block is the neighbour: same fixtures
(one bird per carer, both holding their own), asserting the re-point is refused
for the frozen three and refused-unless-custody for eggs. Keep the existing
`egg.animal IS mutable` assertion passing — with a custody-holding actor, which
it currently has by accident rather than by design.

## Wider point

Both this and piu5 are the same failure mode: a relation field that no rule
constrains, on a collection whose rules were written to be about something else.
Both were found by ad-hoc probing, not by a sweep. Worth doing the sweep —
enumerate every relation field on every client-writable collection and state, per
field, whether it may change after create and what authorises the new target.
close_reason: Closed

title: test_rules.py: [custody] block
description:
Pin the whole matrix from the epic against a live PocketBase, plus the parts the probe did not reach.

From the verified probe (all 11 rows): active carer / edit-share on the OPEN case ALLOWED; carer of a DISPOSED case, edit-share on a DISPOSED case, read-share on the open case, unrelated carer refused; ready_for_release still custody; the aviary keeper ALLOWED on their resident and refused on a bird in no aviary; coordinator + supervisor override.

Must also cover, none of which the probe touched:
- the CREATE-side hops (`animals.createRule`, `cases.createRule`) — create resolves field refs against the SUBMITTED record, which is a different evaluation path from update.
- the weights/markings/egg_records chains (one hop deeper through `animal.`).
- the ROUTES: intake re-identification, exam, merge — the collection sweep cannot see them.
- the isset guards: `org`, `current_aviary`, `lifetime_status` rejected on update.

Explicitly assert the correlation, with a comment saying why: an edit-share on a DISPOSED case of an animal that ALSO has someone else's open case must be refused. That is the single fact the no-denormalized-column decision rests on, and `cases_repository.dart:301` documents a differently-shaped back-relation that does NOT correlate — so this must fail loudly if a PocketBase upgrade changes it.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Jan-Henrik Bruhn
comments.text: The app-side mirror now exists and is pinned: apps/federfall/test/core/auth/roles_test.dart restates the epic's 11-row matrix against animalWritableBy/animalAdmissibleBy, including the correlation trap (my closed case + another carer's open one must not add up to custody). [custody] in test_rules.py is what proves the SERVER still answers the same way — so the two suites are the pair, and a PocketBase upgrade that breaks the back-relation correlation should fail there, not here.

title: App: gate every affordance on the same custody predicate
description:
Decision 6: no control that the server will refuse. `roles.dart` already states it owns this mirroring ('These gate what the UI *offers* so users aren't shown actions they can't perform').

New predicate alongside `caseEditableBy`:

    bool animalWritableBy(Animal animal, AppUser? me, {required Aviary? aviary, required List<Case> cases, required List<CaseShare> shares})

Call sites to gate:
- animal_detail_screen.dart:101 (edit button) and :186 / case_detail_screen.dart:701 (AnimalAvatar editable:) — photo edit is an animal write.
- edit_animal_sheet.dart, add_animal_sheet.dart (the aviary FAB is already behind canManageAviaries; it becomes 'is this aviary's keeper').
- weight_entry_sheet, marking_sheet, egg_entry_sheet + their delete paths.
- 'open a new case' entry points on an animal.

DATA PROBLEM worth planning before coding: the predicate needs the bird's open case and its aviary's keeper, and not every screen has them. animal_detail has the lifetime record (cases); the animals REGISTRY list does not, and neither does the aviary flock list. Either a provider that resolves custody per animal id, or a projection on the animal read — decide once rather than per screen, or this leaks N+1 requests into the two paged feeds (federfall-trep: no screen reads a collection to narrow it on the device).

Also: a read-only badge, like cases already have. A carer looking at a bird they do not hold should be told why the controls are absent, not left wondering.
close_reason: Closed

title: Custody predicate in the hook routes (lib_custody.js)
description:
A custom route bypasses the collection rules it writes through, which is exactly why lib_auth.js exists ('a missing clause is a hole rather than a blemish'). Custody is its next member.

New `pb_hooks/lib_custody.js`: given an app handle, an auth record and an animal id, return whether the caller holds that bird — coordinator/supervisor, the keeper of `current_aviary`, the active carer of a non-disposed case, or an edit-share holder on one. Stateless, like lib_auth/lib_audit (each pooled JSVM holds its own instance).

Call sites:
- intake.pb.js — re-identification branch only; a brand-new animal has no custodian to check.
- exam.pb.js — writes exams + findings against an animal.
- merge_animals.pb.js — already supervisor-only, so this is a no-op today; add the call anyway so the gate does not depend on the route staying supervisor-only.

test_rules.py's guest sweep walks COLLECTIONS, so a route that forgets this sails straight through it — the [custody] test block has to drive the ROUTES too, not only the collections.
notes: Landed narrower than filed, deliberately: only intake.pb.js got the check. exam.pb.js already gates on assertCanEditCase and an exam is a CASE record — requiring animal custody there would refuse a carer's late exam on their own closed case. merge_animals.pb.js is supervisor-only, where the call is a literal no-op; its header now records that custody must be added if that gate is ever widened. Both reasons are in the source, not just here.
close_reason: Closed

title: Opening a case follows custody
description:
`cases.createRule` is `AUTH && org && active_carer = @request.auth.id` — anyone may open a case on any bird, including another keeper's resident.

    cases.createRule = <existing>
      && ( COORD_SUP
           || animal.current_aviary = ""
           || animal.current_aviary.keeper = @request.auth.id )
      && animal.lifetime_status != "deceased"

Reading of the model: a bird AT LARGE is anyone's to admit (that is the whole point of re-identification at intake), a bird in an aviary is its keeper's, and a deceased bird cannot be admitted at all without a supervisor — a new case on one means the death record was wrong.

Note `animal.lifetime_status` is reliable HERE in a way it is not elsewhere: the lag documented in the epic is about it staying stale on re-admission, i.e. too conservative for 'deceased', never falsely deceased.

CRITICAL: intake does not go through this rule. `POST /api/federfall/intake` (intake.pb.js) writes the case inside its own transaction and bypasses collection rules entirely, so the same check must be re-stated there or the rule is decorative. Same for exam.pb.js and merge_animals.pb.js. Put the predicate in a `lib_custody.js` module next to lib_auth.js and require() it INSIDE each handler (JSVM isolation — file-level bindings are not in scope).
close_reason: Closed

title: Custody rules on weights / markings / egg_records
description:
Decision 4: recording a weight or a ring on a bird you do not hold — an aviary resident above all — requires custody. Reverses 5yg.4's org-wide-writable stance for these three collections.

- READ stays org-wide (`org = @request.auth.org`): re-identification depends on seeing every bird's markings and weight series, and 1700000010's header is explicit that privacy is enforced at the CASE level.
- create/update/delete become the custody predicate, resolved through `animal.` — i.e. one forward hop then the epic's clauses (`animal.current_aviary.keeper`, `animal.cases_via_animal.…`). That is one hop deeper than what was probed; verify before writing the migration, and fall back to a denormalized column only if a chain fails to correlate.
- keep the existing narrower deletes where they are already narrower (weights + egg_records are author-or-supervisor, 1700000047 / 1700000056) — custody is a floor, not a widening.
- `roles.dart`'s `weightDeletableBy` / `eggDeletableBy` doc comments claim 'Recording and editing stay open to the whole org like the rest of the identity layer' — that sentence becomes false and must be rewritten, not left to mislead.
- this also closes federfall-piu5 (weights/markings written into a case the author cannot read): the custodian of the animal IS that case's carer. Keep piu5's `@request.body.case:isset = false` / `applied_in_case:isset = false` guards anyway — they stop a row being moved between two cases of the same bird.
close_reason: Closed

title: Custody rules on animals (update + create)
description:
Apply the verified rule from the epic to `animals.updateRule`, and the mirror to `animals.createRule`.

Create side: the only client create path is add_animal_sheet.dart (a resident, straight into an aviary). Gate it on being that aviary's keeper, or coordinator/supervisor:

    animals.createRule =
      AUTH && org = @request.auth.org
      && (@request.body.current_aviary:isset = false
          || COORD_SUP
          || current_aviary.keeper = @request.auth.id)

On CREATE, field refs resolve against the SUBMITTED record, so `current_aviary.keeper` reads the incoming aviary — verify that hop specifically, the update-side probe does not cover it.

This supersedes federfall-ftm2 (aviary population was gated to coordinator+ in the UI but org-wide on the server); close it as absorbed once this lands.

Depends on the isset guards (federfall-1hgp, federfall-7no9) — without them `current_aviary` is client-writable and the keeper branch grants itself.
close_reason: Closed

title: aviaries.keeper becomes required
description:
Custody's aviary branch resolves through `current_aviary.keeper`, so a keeperless aviary is a bird nobody can write about except a coordinator/supervisor. Decision: an aviary always has a keeper.

- migration: `aviaries.keeper` required = true, plus a backfill for existing rows (they are almost certainly null — the field has been a display-only label since 1700000008). Pick the org's supervisor as the fallback and say so in the migration header; a migration cannot ask.
- `Aviary.keeper` becomes non-nullable in federfall_models (+ mapper, + clinical_mappers_test).
- aviary_form_sheet.dart: the keeper dropdown gets `Validators.required`; drop the 'No keeper' option and the `aviaryKeeperNone` ARB string in both locales.
- aviaries_screen / aviary_detail: the `keeper == null` branches go away.

Blocks the animals rules — the keeper branch is unsound until this holds.
close_reason: Closed

title: Custody model: authority over a bird follows who holds it
description:
Replace the org-wide-writable "identity layer" (5yg.4) with a custody model: the
right to write about a bird belongs to whoever currently holds it, and it hands
off along the events that already move the bird.

## The model

| state                              | custodian            | may edit the bird + its animal-scoped rows | may open a new case |
|------------------------------------|----------------------|--------------------------------------------|---------------------|
| in care (open case)                | case.active_carer, plus edit-share holders on that case | custodian            | custodian           |
| in aviary                          | aviary.keeper        | keeper                                     | keeper              |
| released / transferred / returned  | nobody               | coordinator/supervisor                     | ANYONE (a bird at large is anyone's to find) |
| deceased                           | nobody               | coordinator/supervisor                     | coordinator/supervisor |

Coordinator/supervisor is a blanket override throughout.

## Decisions taken (2026-08-10)

1. The active set is `in_care || ready_for_release` (+ `""` for parity with the
   case browser's facet) — a carer keeps custody through ready-for-release.
2. Edit-share holders on the open case DO get animal edit. Read-shares do not.
3. Coordinators keep the override alongside supervisors.
4. Weights / markings / egg_records are NOT left org-wide writable. Recording a
   weight or a ring on someone else's bird — an aviary resident above all —
   requires custody. This reverses 5yg.4's stance and `roles.dart`'s
   "Recording and editing stay open to the whole org like the rest of the
   identity layer". READ stays org-wide: re-identification depends on it.
5. `aviaries.keeper` becomes REQUIRED. An aviary always has a keeper.
6. The app must not offer what the server will refuse — every affordance gated
   by the same predicate (no edit button that 403s).

## Why lifetime_status is NOT the key

`lifetime_status` is derived from the last DISPOSITION and deliberately lags:
`intake.pb.js:118` sets `in_care` only when intake creates a BRAND-NEW animal;
the re-identification branch skips it on purpose (federfall-sinp — the
derivation hooks order dispositions by `created`, not `disposed_at`, so writing
a lifetime state there would clobber an aviary residency when archived cases are
backfilled). So a re-admitted released bird stays `at_large_released`, and a
resident under treatment stays `in_aviary` with `current_aviary` still set.

Rules therefore key on the CAUSE, not the label: the open case and the aviary
relation, both of which are live. No denormalized `custodian` column — the
traversal self-heals (a handoff changes `active_carer` and custody follows in
the same write; a keeper change re-points every resident at once), and this repo
has already paid for a derived field with five writers (`current_aviary`,
1700000052).

## The rule, verified

Probed against a live PocketBase 0.39.8 (throwaway container, real carer tokens,
rules patched in and driven through the REST API). AUTH is the guest-safe form.

    animals.updateRule =
      AUTH && org = @request.auth.org
      && ( COORD_SUP
           || current_aviary.keeper = @request.auth.id
           || (cases_via_animal.active_carer ?= @request.auth.id && ACTIVE)
           || (cases_via_animal.case_shares_via_case.shared_with ?= @request.auth.id
               && cases_via_animal.case_shares_via_case.access ?= "edit"
               && ACTIVE) )
      && @request.body.org:isset = false
      && @request.body.current_aviary:isset = false
      && @request.body.lifetime_status:isset = false

    ACTIVE = (cases_via_animal.status ?= "in_care"
              || cases_via_animal.status ?= "ready_for_release")

Result matrix — all 11 rows correct:

    active carer of the open case            ALLOWED
    EDIT share on the OPEN case              ALLOWED
    carer of the DISPOSED case               refused
    EDIT share on the DISPOSED case          refused
    READ share on the open case              refused
    unrelated carer                          refused
    carer of a ready_for_release case        ALLOWED
    keeper of the resident's aviary          ALLOWED
    unrelated carer, resident bird           refused
    coordinator / supervisor                 ALLOWED

Two findings that de-risk the whole epic:

* **The back-relation clauses DO correlate on 0.39.8**, including the two-hop
  `cases_via_animal.case_shares_via_case.*` chain: an edit-share on a DISPOSED
  case is refused while the same animal has someone else's OPEN case. This is
  the shape `cases_repository.dart:301` warns about, so it must be PINNED by a
  test, not assumed — but it works, and it is what makes the denormalized
  column unnecessary.
* `status ?!= "disposed"` also passes the matrix, but the explicit set is what
  ships: the case browser deliberately names its statuses rather than negating
  (federfall-jt5u), and the two must agree.

The last three isset guards are load-bearing, not hygiene: without them anyone
can PATCH `current_aviary` and hand themselves the keeper branch.

## Scope note

`POST /api/federfall/intake`, `/exam` and `/merge-animals` bypass collection
rules entirely, so custody has to be re-stated inside those handlers — that is
what `lib_auth.js` exists for and this is its next member.

## Release

Tightening rules rejects calls older clients still make, so this is `feat!:` —
it cuts 1.0.0. App and server ship together; an older APK would show controls
that now 403. Accepted (2026-08-10).
notes:
q7ks.1 landed as b6cb1b8 (feat!). Note the major bump arrives HERE, not at q7ks.2 as the epic body predicted: requiring aviaries.keeper already rejects a call an older client makes (an aviary save with no keeper). So 1.0.0 is cut by this commit, and the release-sequencing warning in the epic now applies from q7ks.2 onward within the 1.x line rather than as the major boundary itself.

Verified during q7ks.1 and useful for the rest: PocketBase auto-applies pending migrations on `serve`, so a `migrate down` is undone the moment a server starts — testing a backfill needs a fixture migration injected into a tempdir copy of pb_migrations (the run_cron.sh pattern), not a revert. `migrate down` is also interactive and needs `y` on stdin.

q7ks.6 landed as c58bbea (plain `feat`, not `feat!` — it only narrows what the
app offers to what the server already enforces; the wire contract is untouched).
The design decision .6 asked for, settled once:

* Custody is resolved PER ANIMAL, in `features/animals/custody_providers.dart`,
  not per row. The N+1 worry was misplaced: neither paged feed needs custody —
  the animals registry and the aviary flock list are pure navigation, with no
  write control on a row. So the gate lives only on screens showing one bird,
  where the animal and its case summaries are already loaded.
* The case branch reads `case_summaries` (org-wide), NOT `cases`
  (access-scoped). Asking the collection would hide another carer's open case
  from the predicate while the server still counts it — and, worse, would make
  "nobody holds this bird" answer yes for a bird in someone's kitchen, which is
  the admissibility branch.
* The share branch is one user-wide `case_shares` query
  (`PbCaseSharesRepository.editSharedWith`), `edit` only.
* Coordinator/supervisor short-circuits before any fetch. An unreadable
  enclosure grants nothing rather than propagating, and cannot make a resident
  read as at-large because "housed" is taken off the animal.

Three UI/server mismatches were found and fixed in the same commit:
`markings.delete` was offered to every editor though it is supervisor-only since
1700000010; the aviary "add resident" FAB was coordinator-only while
`animals.createRule` names the keeper too (the other half of ftm2); and intake
re-identification linked a bird with no admissibility check, so
`requireAdmissible()` refused it only after the whole wizard was filled in.

q7ks.7 landed as ee7f03b. All seven children done; the model is in force
end to end.

.2–.5 each shipped the checks for their own migration, so .7 was the four things
none of them could reach: the `cases.createRule` deceased clause (the ROUTE half
was covered, the rule's backstop was not), UPDATE on the animal-scoped records
(a different evaluation path from CREATE — an update rule resolves `animal.`
against the STORED record), `markings.delete` staying supervisor-only, and the
two routes that deliberately do NOT check custody. That last one is the half a
coverage list cannot see is missing: `merge-animals` is supervisor-only and the
role gate stands in for custody, and `exam` must keep letting a carer write up a
late exam on their own CLOSED case. Both now fail loudly if someone "tightens"
them.

The new assertions were mutation-checked rather than assumed: widening
`markings.delete` to the author and dropping the deceased clause from
`cases.create` fail exactly those checks and nothing else.

Backend suite 873 passed / 0 failed (850 before the epic). App suite 1003
passed, coverage 82%.

Still open and related, neither in this epic's scope: federfall-piu5's remaining
create-side half (a carer holding a bird through their own open case can still
attach a weight to a DIFFERENT, older case of that bird — one they cannot read),
and federfall-sinp (lifetime_status derived by `created` rather than
`disposed_at`), which is why the whole model keys on the open case and the
aviary relation instead of that field.

title: Weights/markings can be written into a case the author cannot read
description:
Confirmed against a live PB (throwaway container). Carer B cannot GET carer A's private case (404), yet:

  POST weights   {animal: A's bird, case: A's case, weight_g: 42}      -> 200
  POST markings  {animal: A's bird, applied_in_case: A's case}          -> 200
  PATCH weights/<B's own>  {case: A's case, animal: A's bird}           -> 200

and A then sees the injected rows in their own case timeline (probe read them back with A's token).

Root cause: weights/markings rules are pure org scope (1700000020 for weights, 1700000010 for markings) with no constraint on `case` / `applied_in_case`, and 1700000043 exempted them from the isset guards. So private-by-default holds for READS but not for WRITES — the exact 'child record re-pointed into a foreign case's timeline' escalation 1700000043's header describes, left open for the two collections it classified as identity layer.

The rows also reach the annual report and case_report_rows, so this is not only cosmetic.

Suggested fix (needs a design call — see federfall-1hgp/7no9 which are unambiguous):
  - CREATE: require the named case to be one the writer may edit, i.e. append
      && (@request.body.case:isset = false || case.active_carer = @request.auth.id
          || SUP || (case.case_shares_via_case.shared_with ?= @request.auth.id
                     && case.case_shares_via_case.access ?= "edit"))
    (create rules resolve field refs against the SUBMITTED record, so this checks the incoming case);
  - UPDATE: `&& @request.body.case:isset = false` (weights) /
    `&& @request.body.applied_in_case:isset = false` (markings). The app sends neither on update — weight_entry_sheet.dart and marking_sheet.dart put them in the create branch only.
Case-less weights/markings (the aviary path) stay open, which is what keeps the identity-layer stance intact.

Related: cases.animal is NOT isset-guarded either, so a carer can re-point their own case onto any other bird in the org (probe: 200). Only the cross-org case is blocked, by animal_org_scope.pb.js. That gives an indirect route to rewrite a foreign bird's lifetime_status via a disposition on one's own case.
notes: Half-narrowed by federfall-q7ks.3 (b50e8f4): custody now stops a STRANGER writing weights/markings on a bird they never held, which was the headline. What remains is narrower but still real — a carer who holds a bird through their OWN open case can attach a weight to a DIFFERENT, older case of that same bird, one belonging to another carer they cannot read. Fix is the create-side constraint on the incoming case / applied_in_case (the suggested rule in this issue still applies) plus the update-side isset guards. Deliberately left out of q7ks.3 so it gets its own test matrix.
close_reason: Closed

title: animals.current_aviary / lifetime_status are client-writable
description:
Confirmed against a live PB (throwaway container), as a plain carer with no relation to the bird:

  PATCH animals/<id> {"current_aviary": "<other aviary>"} -> 200
  PATCH animals/<id> {"lifetime_status": "deceased"}      -> 200

Both fields are documented as hook-derived: 1700000002's header says lifetime_status 'is maintained by hooks from the latest case disposition', and 1700000052/aviary_stays.pb.js treat current_aviary as the single funnel every residency writer goes through. Nothing enforces that — animals.updateRule is bare org scope.

Consequences:
  - a member can relocate a bird between enclosures with no disposition; the aviary_stays ledger dutifully closes the old stay and opens a new one (probe showed exactly that), so the ledger records a move that no case history explains;
  - a member can declare any bird deceased, or resurrect one, decoupling lifetime_status from the disposition chain main.pb.js reconciles;
  - the same PATCH can empty an aviary.

The audit log DOES catch all of it (animal.updated with from_label/to_label on current_aviary, and the lifetime_status transition) — detection exists, prevention does not, and it is supervisor-only to read.

Fix: append to animals.updateRule
  && @request.body.current_aviary:isset = false
  && @request.body.lifetime_status:isset = false
Hook writers use app.save(), which bypasses API rules, so main.pb.js / merge_animals.pb.js / aviary_stays.pb.js are unaffected. The app only ever sends these two on CREATE (add_animal_sheet.dart) — never on update — so not wire-breaking.

Note the side effect: there is then no client path to move a resident between aviaries. There is none today either (the only route is a placed_in_aviary disposition), but if one is ever wanted it must be a hook route like intake/exam, not a raw PATCH.

title: Conditions donut: arc geometry uses a different denominator than its labels
description:
The statistics 'Conditions' donut draws each slice as a share of the conditions actually recorded, while every percentage printed on and beside the slices is a share of total intakes. With 2 PMV / 1 Gefiederschaden / 1 suems out of 14 intakes, the blue arc occupies HALF the ring and is labelled 14%. The chart's picture and its own numbers disagree.

Only this chart is affected: statistics_screen.dart:321 is the sole caller that passes an explicit `total` (`total: s.intakes`), which it does deliberately because a case can carry several conditions and the shares would otherwise sum past 100%. That fixed the arithmetic and left the geometry lying. Outcomes and By-species pass no total, so their arcs and labels agree.

Found in a Dieter Rams design review (principle 6, honest) of the running app.
design:
In BreakdownPie.build (lib/ui/widgets/breakdown_pie.dart:80), the sections are built only from `slices` (entries + folded tail), so fl_chart normalises the arcs over the counted sum while the titles and legend divide by `sum = total ?? counted`.

Fix: when `total` is given and exceeds the counted sum, append a remainder slice of `sum - counted` in the existing neutral `otherColor`, so the ring divides the same whole the labels do. It needs a label distinct from otherLabel ('Other' means 'tail categories' here, not 'no condition recorded') — something like 'No condition recorded'.

Alternative if a remainder slice reads badly for a non-exhaustive set: drop the donut for Conditions and keep only the rows beneath it, which already carry every category and its exact count.
close_reason: Fixed in 652c098, but not the way the DESIGN section proposed. A remainder slice cannot work: lib_stats.js conditionCounts() counts DISTINCT CASES per label, so a case with several diagnoses is counted several times and the sum can exceed intakes — intakes − Σ counts goes negative, and where positive it is not 'cases with no condition recorded'. Diagnoses partition no whole, so no ring is honest for them. Replaced the donut with a new BreakdownBars widget: one bar per leading diagnosis, length = count/intakes, plus a caption naming the denominator ('Anteil an den Aufnahmen'). Rows below unchanged. BreakdownPie's 'total' parameter is gone entirely, so no chart can be handed a denominator its arcs don't use; PieEntry -> ChartEntry, shared. Tests: test/ui/breakdown_bars_test.dart pins geometry against label (incl. overlapping counts summing past the total); breakdown_pie_test pins ring == sum of parts.

title: Derive animal lifetime_status order-aware (disposed_at, not created)
description:
`animals.lifetime_status` / `current_aviary` are derived by hooks that assume
dispositions are entered chronologically. That holds for live use and breaks for
archive/backfill work (entering historical cases for birds that already have a
current state).

Two defects:

1. **The disposition create hook does not check whether the new disposition is
   the latest.** `pb_hooks/main.pb.js:156-157` applies the new row's type
   unconditionally and clears `current_aviary` for any non-aviary type. Entering
   an archived `released` disposition for a bird that is currently an aviary
   resident flips `lifetime_status` to `at_large_released`, clears
   `current_aviary`, and — via `aviary_stays.pb.js:64` reacting to that field
   change — closes the open residency with `ended_at = now`, i.e. a false
   present-dated end on a stay that is still running. Only the
   after-update/after-delete paths (`main.pb.js:199`, `:268`) run the "latest
   across all of the animal's cases" reconcile; create skips it.

2. **"Latest" is measured by the wrong column.** `dispositions` has a real event
   date, `disposed_at` (`pb_migrations/1700000008_aviaries_and_dispositions.js:75`),
   but every reconcile sorts by `created` (the autodate). So the invariant is
   "the most recently inserted disposition wins", not "the latest event wins",
   and backfilling a history in any non-chronological order yields the wrong
   final state. `merge_animals.pb.js:199` has the same ordering.

## Fix

Single-source the derivation: a `pb_hooks/lib_derive.js` (alongside `lib_org.js`)
exporting one reconcile that orders by `COALESCE(disposed_at, created)`, called
from the disposition create path too instead of the blind apply, with the
`current_aviary` / `aviary_stays` write conditional on the disposition actually
being the latest. `merge_animals.pb.js` should call the same function.

Keep the existing no-disposition fallbacks: `in_care` by default, and
`merge_animals.pb.js:223`'s case-less aviary residency (federfall-0ua6) must
survive.

## Once this lands

`intake.pb.js` can set `lifetime_status` on the re-identification branch too (it
currently sets it only when creating a new animal, precisely because of defect
2), so a returning bird stops reading "Released" through its whole second stay.
A case-create hook setting `in_care` also becomes considerable — it was rejected
for now as the same class of bug.

## Testing

Needs a live PocketBase (`backend/pocketbase/tests/run.sh`). Add a
`test_rules.py` block that inserts dispositions OUT of chronological order and
asserts the animal's final state follows `disposed_at`; include the archived-
disposition-vs-current-resident case, asserting the open `aviary_stays` row is
left alone.

Also needs a data migration to backfill `lifetime_status = "in_care"` for
animals with no disposition and an empty status (pre-existing rows from before
the intake fix).
