title: vet_appointments is missing 1700000043's immutable-boundary guard — cross-org timeline injection
description:
1700000064 created vet_appointments with case-child rules copied from the other children, but WITHOUT the '&& @request.body.case:isset = false && @request.body.org:isset = false' suffix that 1700000043 appended to all twelve other case children.

PocketBase resolves plain field references in an UPDATE rule against the STORED record (1700000043's own finding). vet_appointments.updateRule is:
  AUTH && case.org = @request.auth.org && (case.active_carer = @request.auth.id || SUP || edit-share)

So the active carer of case X (or an edit-share holder) can:
  PATCH /api/collections/vet_appointments/records/<id> {"case": "<any other case id>"}
and the rule passes against case X while the row lands on the target case. The target may be another carer's private case OR A CASE IN ANOTHER ORG, since the org check also reads the stored parent. 'org' is unguarded the same way and can be set to a foreign org.

Impact: write-side. The attacker cannot read the target case afterwards (list/view follow the new parent), so this is clinical-record tampering / injection, not a read leak: a fabricated vet appointment (vet, reason, outcome free text) appears in a case timeline its owner did not write, potentially in another organisation.

Nothing else covers it: animal_org_scope.pb.js only guards 'animal' relations, and 1700000064 explicitly states appointments need no hook. test_rules.py's [immutable boundary relations] block only exercises case_shares, cases and journal_entries, so the sweep never touched this collection.

Fix: new migration appending the isset guard to vet_appointments.updateRule (same shape as 1700000043 / the re-derivation in 1700000053). Then extend the test block to cover EVERY guarded collection rather than the three it samples — that generalisation is what stops the next collection repeating this.
close_reason: Closed

title: Audit update-diff path is unguarded: relation ids and free text land in the log
description:
`CONTENT_FIELDS` is an allowlist that covers only create/delete. `diff()` is a denylist (IGNORED_FIELDS + SENSITIVE), so on an UPDATE:

1. `cases.admission_reasons` (multi-relation, maxSelect 99) logs raw JSON id arrays: it is absent from RELATION_TARGETS, and labelOf() takes a single id while normalize() collapses the value to '["id","id"]'. The field name is untranslated too (auditFieldLabel falls through to the raw column). Same for find_location/city/region/found_at/intake_notes/intake_weight_g/is_releasable and admitted_by/transported_by (labelled value, raw field name).

2. `journal_entries.text` (max 10000) is diffed, so a journal EDIT writes 500 chars of both old and new prose into the append-only table — contradicting the invariant stated twice in lib_audit.js (LABEL_FIELDS / CONTENT_FIELDS: 'the row records that a note was written, never the note'). A carer editing a name out of a note leaves the original logged for the retention window. cases.intake_notes and the other free-text notes fields are the same class.

3. Neither guard can see this: audit_labels_test.dart parses CONTENT_FIELDS only, and test_rules.py's informative() counts a non-empty `changes` as informative — it measures structure, not readability.

Fix: admission_reasons in RELATION_TARGETS + multi-id label resolution (snapshotted, joined); a FREE_TEXT redaction map for the diff path; the missing field names in auditFieldLabel; and a schema-driven guard in test_rules.py (live PB) that every diffable field of an audited collection has a translation in audit_labels.dart.
close_reason: Closed

title: Audit: every relation-valued change renders as a raw record id
description:
auditValueLabel (audit_labels.dart:239) has no notion of a relation field, so any relation that changes in an update diff prints its target's id:

  animals.current_aviary  -> 'Voliere: 8k2m4p7q1w3e5r9'   (moving a bird between aviaries — one of the events this log exists for)
  cases.active_carer      -> 'Zustaendig: <id>'
  markings.type, medications.route, case_conditions.condition, exams.examiner,
  quarantine_records.set_by, medication_administrations.administered_by,
  cases.admitted_by, follow_ups.created_by

This can only be fixed SERVER-SIDE: AuditEvent is deliberately non-expandable ('what you see is what was true when it happened'), and the app could not resolve a since-deleted aviary anyway. diff() needs the same snapshot-the-label treatment subjectLabel() already does — a per-collection relation map, one indexed read per changed relation field, on write paths that already do several.

Shape: extend a change entry with from_label / to_label. Same treatment for contentOf() so creates/deletes stay consistent if a relation is ever allowlisted.
acceptance_criteria: a relation change stores the target's label beside the id; the renderer prefers the label; the label is snapshotted so a later rename or delete does not change what the row says; diff()'s signature stays backward-compatible for its other callers.
close_reason: RELATION_TARGETS (by field name, since this schema names a relation the same thing everywhere) + RELATION_FIELDS (per-collection, for 'type', which is a marking_types relation on markings and a text outcome on dispositions) + labelOf(); diff() and contentOf() take an optional app and record from_label/to_label. AuditFieldChange gained fromLabel/toLabel + fromDisplay/toDisplay, and auditChangeSide() keeps a snapshotted label out of the enum/date resolution — it is already human text. Pinned backend-side on the current_aviary move.

title: Audit: a handoff and a share name a user by id, not by name
description:
lib_audit.js refine() puts USER IDS in detail:
  - placements/created -> case.handoff: detail.from / detail.to are from_user / to_user ids (lib_audit.js:819-833)
  - case_shares -> case.shared / case.share_revoked: detail.with is the shared_with id (lib_audit.js:782-791)
audit_labels.dart:387-393 prints them verbatim, so a supervisor reads

  Fall uebergeben
  Anna Mueller · 04.08.2026 14:30 · Bernd Weber
  Uebernommen von: k9x2m4p7q1w3e5r
  Abgegeben von: a1s2d3f4g5h6j7k

Bernd's NAME is already in the subtitle — LABEL_RELATIONS.placements.to_user resolves it at emit time. So the id is both illegible and a duplicate of the line above it.

Fix, additive and wire-safe: snapshot the label next to the id (to_label / from_label / with_label) the same way subject_label and case_label are already snapshotted, and prefer it in the renderer with the id as fallback. Keep the ids — they are what refs/correlation is for.
acceptance_criteria: detail carries to_label/from_label/with_label; the renderer shows the name and falls back to the id; the handoff fact no longer repeats the subtitle; app + backend assertions for both actions (neither is covered today).
close_reason: detail carries to_label/from_label (handoff) and with_label (share), resolved via labelOf() at emit time; the renderer prefers the label and falls back to the id for pre-existing rows. Two duplications removed with it: the subject-label subtitle is dropped when a labelled fact already names the same thing, and 'abgegeben von' is dropped when from_user was the actor (which it is on every handoff made through the app). Backend assertion caught that users are labelled by NAME before email — A is 'Alice', not a@f.local.

title: [epic] Audit log renders ids where names belong, and English where German belongs
description:
Follow-up to federfall-by7w / federfall-9k2g. The audit log's DESIGN survives review — snapshot labels instead of relations, wire values instead of server-side translation, redaction, envelope-always-renders, severity as the one filter that needs no vocabulary. What falls short is the last mile: what a supervisor actually reads on screen.

Four classes of defect, found by reading every emitter against the renderer:

1. Raw 15-char PocketBase ids reach the user in three places — handoff detail, share detail, and every relation-valued entry in an update diff. In the first two the name was already resolved at emit time and sits in the subtitle, so the id is unreadable AND redundant.
2. auditFieldLabel/auditValueLabel both accept a collection and never use it, so 'type' and 'status' collide across collections and produce a wrong label on one side and an untranslated English value on the other.
3. 20 of the fields the CONTENT_FIELDS allowlist deliberately chose have no translated label, so a German-first UI prints the English column name.
4. Recorded-but-unreachable information: a diff shows 3 of N changes with no way to see the rest, and refs / request_id / user_agent / actor_role / several detail keys are stored, indexed, parsed — and rendered nowhere.
close_reason: All six children done across three commits (f04db4e, ef2c06b, 2d00531). The design needed no rethinking; the last mile did. Every id a reader could see is now paired with a snapshotted label (handoff, share, every relation-valued change), both label functions honour their collection, all 57 recorded fields are named in both languages, the whole row is reachable through a detail sheet (all changes, truncation stated, actor role, user agent, request-correlated siblings), and the screen can ask the four questions the query layer always could. Three new guards: the CONTENT_FIELDS label sweep, the topic partition, and backend assertions on handoff/share/aviary labels. 577 backend, 801 app, coverage 79.4%.

title: Audit: a test that fails on an uninformative event
description:
The control that stops this class of bug coming back, and the reason it was not caught: qt96.7's coverage test asserts every collection is AUDITED, never that its events SAY anything. All four empty rows passed a green suite.

In test_rules.py, after the emitter section has exercised every audited collection, assert that each distinct action present in audit_events carries at least one of: a non-empty subject_label, a non-empty changes array, or a non-empty detail. Allow a short, justified exemption list (auth.login needs nothing beyond its actor).

Guard it the way the coverage test is guarded — assert the sweep saw a plausible number of distinct actions, so a filter typo cannot make it pass vacuously.
close_reason:
In test_rules.py's [audit coverage] section: every row must name its subject, name its case, record what changed, or carry a typed payload — any one is enough. Guarded like the coverage check (>=50 rows, >=20 distinct actions) so a filter typo cannot pass it vacuously. 573 passed, 0 failed.

It caught a real gap on its first run: an AVIARY-scoped journal entry. journal_entries is dual-parent (case XOR aviary), the text is deliberately never recorded, and an aviary entry has no case — so those rows said literally nothing. Fixed by resolving the aviary name as the subject label, which is not the text.

One exemption, with its reason in the test: finder.created / finder.deleted / finder.orphan_deleted. Everything about a finder is withheld on purpose — finder_retention.pb.js scrubs their PII on a schedule and a copy here would outlive the scrub — so such a row can only ever say THAT a finder record was touched, by id.

title: Audit: carry the case number on every case-scoped row
description:
The row has case_id — an opaque 15-char PocketBase id — and nothing a person can read. Every case-scoped line in the audit screen and the whole per-case activity section therefore identify their case by nothing at all.

Add a case_label TEXT column (new migration, additive) alongside case_id and snapshot the case number into it, the same way actor_label and subject_label snapshot their subjects. A relation or a client-side lookup would both break the moment the case is deleted, which is exactly when the audit row matters most.

Touches: migration, lib_audit.js (resolve once per emit — the case record is usually already in hand), AuditEvent, and the renderer/tile so a line reads '2026-014' instead of nothing.

Wire-contract note: additive, so feat: not feat!:.
close_reason:
Migration 1700000069 adds audit_events.case_label; emit() resolves it (free when the subject is the case, otherwise one indexed read, and only for rows that belong to a case); intake and case_report pass it in from the record they already hold. Model field + rendered as an auditFactCase fact, suppressed in the per-case section where every row shares the case. 4 backend + 3 Dart assertions; 571 backend, 770 app, 107 models, analyze + format clean, migration up/down/up clean.

A snapshot rather than a read-time lookup for the same reason actor_label and subject_label are snapshots: a supervisor deleting a case cascades through its whole timeline, so resolving the id later would fail exactly when the row matters most.

This is what makes journal.created readable — it has no subject label by design, so before this it named nothing at all; now it reads 'Journaleintrag geschrieben · Sabine · 2026-001'.

title: Audit: give every audited collection a meaningful subject label
description:
lib_audit.js's LABEL_FIELDS covers 12 collections; every case-timeline child is missing, so subject_label is '' for weights, journal_entries, case_conditions, dispositions, placements, medication_administrations, egg_records, follow_ups, quarantine_records, exams and exam_findings. The screen therefore shows a title and no subject.

Two kinds of label are needed and only the first is a field read:
- Direct: weights -> '301 g', egg_records -> the count, follow_ups/vet_appointments -> the date, aviaries/animals -> the name (already works).
- RESOLVED AT EMIT TIME: case_conditions.condition, markings.type, medication_administrations.medication and medications.route are RELATIONS into user-managed code lists. The id is useless in a log and the code-list row can be renamed or deleted later, so the emitter must read the referenced record once and snapshot its label ('Katzenbiss'). That is a lookup per emit — acceptable, it is one indexed read on a write path that already did several.

Keep it neutral: a label is a name, a number, a code or a user-authored code-list string. Never a German phrase — enum-ish content (a disposition type) belongs in detail as a wire value so the app translates it. See the epic's design rule.

finders stays deliberately empty (emit() forces it).
close_reason:
LABEL_FIELDS extended (medication_administrations), plus LABEL_RELATIONS (case_conditions.condition, case_shares.shared_with, placements.to_user/aviary, markings.type fallback) and LABEL_QUANTITIES (weights -> '301 g'). subjectLabel() takes an optional app to resolve relations. 8 new assertions; 557 passed, 0 failed.

Verified on a live stack: a diagnosis now reads 'Katzenbiss' rather than a code-list id, a share and a handoff name the person, and each row snapshots the value AS IT WAS (the weight create says 300 g, its later update 310 g).

Two collections stay label-less ON PURPOSE and the tests pin both: finders (forced empty in emit) and journal_entries — free clinical text its author can still edit or delete, and the field most likely to mention a person in passing; copying it into an append-only table would quietly make it permanent.

Design rule applied throughout: a label is neutral (name, number, code, user-authored code-list string), never a translated phrase, because it is stored verbatim and the log is read in two languages. Enum-shaped content gets no label and travels as a wire value instead.

title: Audit: record what a create and a delete actually contained
description:
emitRecordChange() builds `changes` only for 'updated'. Give 'created' and 'deleted' the same treatment from a per-collection field allowlist, so a row says what was written and — more importantly — what was destroyed.

Shape: reuse `changes` with from=null for a create (renders as 'gesetzt auf X' with the existing auditChangeSet string, no new rendering needed) and to=null for a delete. Redaction and the 500-char clamp already apply.

An ALLOWLIST, not the whole record: dumping every column would put org/author/case relation ids and long free text into a table that has no delete path. Per collection, the two or three fields that identify what happened — weights: weight_g, measured_at; dispositions: type, disposed_at, aviary; case_conditions: condition, diagnosed_at; medications: drug, dose_rate, dose_unit; medication_administrations: drug, administered_at; journal_entries: NOT the text (clinical free text; record its presence, not its content); egg_records: count; follow_ups: due_at; vet_appointments: starts_at, vet; markings: code, type; placements: to_user, aviary; quarantine_records: quarantine_until.

Depends on the label work only for relation-valued fields (a condition id is useless on its own) — see the sibling issue.
close_reason:
CONTENT_FIELDS allowlist + contentOf() in lib_audit.js: creates emit their content as {field,to}, deletes as {field,from} — the same shape an update produces, so no new rendering was needed for the mechanism. Renderer additions: recorded timestamps are formatted (field-name suffix _at/_date, matching the schema convention) and enum values translated (disposition type, certainty, frequency, egg fate, hydration, mentation, body system) + 17 new field labels in de/en. 12 backend + 5 Dart assertions; 567 backend, 767 app, analyze clean, format clean.

Two bugs caught by reading real rows off a live stack instead of trusting the code — both the federfall-jumi family (a Go type crossing into JS):
- record.get() on a date field returns types.DateTime, an OBJECT. JSON.stringify kept the quotes, so every date was stored as '"2026-06-21 09:00:00.000Z"' and would have parsed as no date at all on the way out.
- An unset date therefore stored '""' and slipped past the emptiness check, so every create carried junk entries for fields nobody had filled in.
normalize() now unwraps any Go value that marshals to a JSON scalar. fieldsData() does NOT have this problem (it yields plain JS), which is why only the new create/delete path hit it and the update diff never did.

Deliberately empty: journal_entries (free clinical text), finders, organisations. case_shares too — refine() already puts who and what access into detail, and printing it twice is noise.

title: [epic] Audit log entries carry too little to be useful
description:
Shipped in federfall-qt96, the log records THAT something happened and almost never WHAT. Verified against a live stack (2026-08-04): a disposition, a journal entry, a diagnosis and a weight all produce a row with subject_label='', changes=null, detail=null. The outcome type — died vs released, the most consequential fact in the app — is stored nowhere. A supervisor reading the log cannot tell a euthanasia from a release, cannot see which bird weighed what, and sees only an opaque case id where the case number belongs.

Root causes, all in pb_hooks/lib_audit.js:
1. emitRecordChange() only builds `changes` for the 'updated' verb. A create and a delete record no field content at all — and a delete is the one event whose subject is gone afterwards.
2. LABEL_FIELDS covers 12 collections and none of the case-timeline children, so subject_label is empty for weights, journal_entries, case_conditions, dispositions, placements, administrations, egg_records, follow_ups, quarantine_records, exams.
3. The row carries case_id (an opaque 15-char id) but no case number, so nothing in a case-scoped line is human-readable.

DESIGN RULE for every fix here, from the original epic: the log stores neutral SNAPSHOTS and WIRE values, never a rendered sentence. A disposition type is stored as 'died' and translated by the app; a code-list diagnosis is stored as its label ('Katzenbiss') because that string IS the data and the code-list row may later be renamed or deleted; a case number, bird name or ring code is stored verbatim. Nothing goes in in German.
close_reason:
All 7 children complete. The log now says what happened, not just that something did.

Before: a disposition, a journal entry, a diagnosis and a weight each produced a row with subject_label='', changes=null, detail=null — verified on a live stack, and green in a 550-assertion suite.
After (same live check): 'Ausgang erfasst · Ausgang: Verstorben · Fall jetzt: Abgeschlossen · Vogel jetzt: Verstorben · Fall: 2026-001'.

Delivered: labels for every audited collection including ones resolved from another record; create/delete content from a per-collection allowlist; the case number on every case-scoped row (migration 1700000069); the disposition's derived flip; creates no longer rendered as diffs; a date-range filter; and the control that would have caught the whole thing.

Three bugs found by reading real rows off a live stack rather than trusting the code, all the same family (a Go type crossing into JS, cf. federfall-jumi): dates stored WITH their quotes and therefore unparseable; unset dates stored as '""' and slipping past the emptiness check; and — caught by the new control on its first run — aviary-scoped journal entries, which have no case and no text by design and so recorded literally nothing.

Standing lesson, now enforced by test: federfall-qt96.7 asserted every collection was AUDITED and never that its events SAID anything, which is exactly how four actions shipped empty and green.

title: Audit: models — AuditEvent envelope + sealed AuditDetail + enums
description:
federfall_models: AuditAction / AuditActorKind / AuditSeverity enums carrying wire values (fromWire via pbEnum). AuditEvent (freezed) + fromRecord, keeping BOTH AuditAction? action AND String rawAction — an unknown wire value is a normal state, not an error.
sealed class AuditDetail with AuditDetail.parse(action, json); FieldChangesDetail{List<FieldChange>}, per-action details (CaseHandoffDetail{from,to}, IntakeDetail, RoleChangedDetail, LoginFailedDetail{attempts}, ExportDetail{format,year}...), and UnknownDetail{raw} as the fallback.
FieldChange.from/to hold WIRE values — that is what lets the renderer do CaseStatus.fromWire(v) -> caseStatusLabel(l10n, ...).
INVARIANT to hold the line on: the envelope alone must render a usable line; detail only enriches. That keeps a new server-side action ADDITIVE under the major-version wire contract (feat:, not feat!:).
acceptance_criteria: Parse round-trip test per action; an unknown action string yields action==null + rawAction set + UnknownDetail and does not throw; dart test + build_runner clean.
close_reason:
packages/federfall_models: AuditAction (82 wire values, generated from the JS registry rather than typed by hand), AuditActorKind, AuditSeverity, AuditFieldChange, sealed AuditDetail (12 typed variants + none + unknown) and the AuditEvent envelope. 23 tests; whole package green (107).

The load-bearing test is audit_event_test.dart's registry check: it PARSES pb_hooks/lib_audit.js and asserts the two sets are equal in both directions, with a guard assertion so a broken regex cannot pass vacuously. An action the server can emit that the app cannot name now fails a Dart test.

Notes: freezed reads any factory named fromJson as an opt-in to json_serializable codegen, so the hand-written change mapper is AuditFieldChange.fromPb (matching GeoPoint.fromPb). AuditEvent keeps BOTH action and rawAction — an unknown action is a normal state, pinned by a test. Unknown actor_kind/severity degrade to system/info rather than throwing.

title: Audit: lib_audit.js emitter + action registry
description:
pb_hooks/lib_audit.js exporting emit(e, action, {subject, caseId, refs, changes, detail, severity}) plus a diff() helper and the per-collection sensitive-field redaction list.
FIRST: verify require() works in the PB 0.39.8 JSVM — it must be called INSIDE each handler (const audit = require(`${__hooks}/lib_audit.js`)) because file-level scope does not cross into handlers. Fallback if it does not work: a ~25-line inlined emit() per handler.
emit() resolves the actor from the RequestEvent (e.auth / e.requestInfo() / e.realIP() — RecordEvent from model hooks has NO auth), snapshots actor_label/role, and swallows its own errors into $app.logger(): an audit failure must never turn a successful domain write into a 500.
Content rules enforced here: never write finder PII into labels/payloads (finder subject_label = "") or the finder_retention scrub is defeated by its own audit trail; redact VALUES not the fact of change for users.password/tokenKey and finders identity/contact fields.
Also export the ACTIONS registry constant (single source of truth for valid action strings).
acceptance_criteria: A unit-ish backend check asserts: an emitted row has actor snapshots for a normal request and actor_kind=system with no actor for a cron path; a users.password change logs {field:'password',redacted:true} with no from/to; a finder subject carries no name; emit() failure logs and does not propagate.
notes:
VERIFIED on PB 0.39.8 (throwaway container, probe hooks — 2026-08-04):

- require() IS available inside handlers: typeof require === 'function'.
- require(`${__hooks}/lib_audit.js`) works inside a routerAdd handler, inside a
  cronAdd handler, AND inside an onRecordAfterCreateSuccess model hook. All three
  contexts confirmed. -> No inlined-per-handler fallback needed.
- The required module KEEPS ITS OWN file-level scope: a module-level const + a
  helper function referenced from an exported function both resolve correctly.
  So the emitter's SENSITIVE-field list and diff() can live at lib_audit.js file
  level even though hook files cannot do that.
- Relative require('./lib_audit.js') FAILS with 'GoError: Invalid module'. Always
  use the ${__hooks} absolute form.
- The .js extension is optional (require(`${__hooks}/lib_audit`) resolves) but
  keep it explicit.
- lib_audit.js does not end in .pb.js, so PB does not load it as a hook file —
  correct by construction.
- Re-confirmed the premise: file-level bindings in a .pb.js are NOT visible
  inside its own handlers (uncaught ReferenceError at request time).
- MODULE STATE IS PER-VM, NOT GLOBAL. A mutable module-level counter survives
  across sequential requests, but under 24 concurrent requests the counters
  DIVERGE (some calls restart at 1 while others are in the 40s) — PB pools JSVMs
  and each pooled VM holds its own module instance. => lib_audit.js MUST be
  stateless. Never use module state for correctness (dedup, counters, caches).
close_reason:
pb_hooks/lib_audit.js: emit(), diff(), ACTIONS (81 actions), SEVERITY/ACTOR consts, SENSITIVE redaction map. Behaviour verified on a live 0.39.8 instance via a throwaway probe hook (removed); real assertions land with the first call sites in qt96.3.

Findings worth carrying forward:
- e.set/e.get on the router event IS the per-request store — several emits in one request share a request_id, a cron emit gets its own. Module state could not do this (per-JSVM).
- emit() needs opts.record (or an explicit org) to resolve the org. A SUPERUSER has no org of their own, so an emitter that only passes {subject:{...}} silently drops superuser actions. Tier A emitters must pass record: e.record.
- Credentials are NOT in IGNORED_FIELDS: 'the password changed' is the signal; SENSITIVE strips only the values.
- Values over 500 chars are truncated with truncated:true — audit_events.changes has a maxSize and the rows can never be deleted.
- opts.app must be the transaction app when emitting from inside a route's runInTransaction (Tier B).

title: Audit: schema + append-only rules migration (1700000068) + tamper guard
description:
New collection audit_events: org(rel,req,idx), action(TEXT not select — an unlisted select value would throw inside a domain transaction and 400 a legitimate write), actor(rel users, cascadeDelete:false) + actor_label/actor_role/actor_kind snapshots, subject_collection/subject_id/subject_label as PLAIN TEXT (supervisor deletes cascade hard; the log must survive its subject), case_id(TEXT idx), refs(json), changes(json), detail(json), severity(info|notice|security), ip/user_agent (only when org.settings.auditLogClientInfo === true), request_id, created. Indexes (org,created)/(org,case_id,created)/(org,actor,created)/(org,action,created).
Rules: list/view = AUTH && role=supervisor && org=@request.auth.org && role != "guest" (redundant guest clause is required by test_rules.py's guest sweep); create/update/delete = null so the API can neither write nor erase.
Tamper guard in pb_hooks/audit.pb.js: onRecordUpdate("audit_events") always throws; onRecordDelete("audit_events") allows only rows older than the retention floor — checking the row's OWN age is what lets the retention cron work without a bypass flag (JSVM isolation rules out a shared store).
Document the deliberate non-goal in the migration header: no hash chain (only detects tampering by someone who already has the SQLite file, and needs the case_number write-lock trick on every event).
acceptance_criteria: Migration applies + reverts cleanly. test_rules.py: supervisor lists; carer AND coordinator get 403; create/update/delete rejected for every role; guest sweep passes; no cross-org leak. Manual Admin UI edit/delete of a fresh row is refused.
close_reason:
Migration 1700000068 + pb_hooks/audit.pb.js + 29 new assertions in test_rules.py (464 passed, 0 failed). Migration verified up/down/up clean.

DEVIATIONS from the epic design, both deliberate:
1. actor is actor_id TEXT, not a relation to users. PocketBase nullifies a non-cascade relation by SAVING the referring record, which fires onRecordUpdate — so the absolute append-only guard would have made deleting any audited user fail with 400. Pinned by the 'an audited user can still be deleted' assertion. org stays a relation (scoping boundary; required non-cascade relations have blocked org deletion since 1700000002 regardless).
2. Settings keys are snake_case: audit_retention_days (not auditRetentionDays), and lib_audit.js should use audit_log_client_info (not auditLogClientInfo), matching finder_retention_years already in that JSON.

Delete guard branches all pinned: fresh row refused, retention 0 = keep forever, row past the window deletable (the cron's path).

Note for every downstream task: read org settings with JSON.parse(rec.getString('settings')) — get() returns bytes. See federfall-jumi.

title: Intake draft (finder PII) survived sign-out and server switch
description:
The in-progress CaseIntakeDraft holds the FINDER's contact details (first/last name, phone, email, city) plus intake notes, find location and exact find coordinates — third-party PII of a member of the public, the same data the backend's finder_retention cron exists to minimise server-side.

It was only ever cleared by new_case_screen.dart (on a committed intake, or an explicit discard). signOut() purged the protected-file cache — with a doc comment explaining that leaving device-local data behind lets the next user of a shared device see the previous user's — but did not clear the draft. Same gap in LoginScreen._switchServer().

Impact: carer A fills in a finder's name and phone, backs out of the wizard, signs out; carer B signs in on the same device, opens the intake wizard, and is offered A's draft with that person's phone number. On web, same per browser profile. On server switch it was also a correctness bug: a draft restored against a different server carries an idempotencyKey that server has never seen.

Fix: signOut() and _switchServer() both purge the draft via a new purgeIntakeDraft() sibling of purgeProtectedFileCache() (same best-effort, fire-and-forget contract — a locked keystore must not block signing out). Accepted trade-off: signing out mid-intake now discards the draft.

Found in the 2026-08-04 whole-codebase security review.
close_reason: Fixed in e3f9d4d: purgeIntakeDraft() called from signOut() and LoginScreen._switchServer(); regression tests in profile_screen_test.dart (purges on confirm, keeps on cancel) and login_screen_test.dart (switch-server purge).

title: Self-host the engine's Noto text-fallback fonts (no fonts.gstatic.com)
description: Web builds fetch per-glyph Noto fallback fonts from fonts.gstatic.com whenever text contains a codepoint the bundled Roboto subset (923 cps) lacks; the CSP (font-src 'self') blocks it, producing an endless stream of console errors and tofu glyphs. Fix: mirror the engine's own fallback slices into web/noto/ at build time and point FlutterConfiguration.fontFallbackBaseUrl at our own origin, so the engine keeps its per-glyph selection but never reaches an external host.
close_reason: Bundled Noto Sans Symbols / Symbols 2 / Color Emoji (COLRv1) as pubspec asset fonts + AppTheme.fontFamilyFallback in ed22ce5, and fixed the ARB string (→ U+2192) that triggered it. Deliberately NOT the fontFallbackBaseUrl mirror approach (build-time downloads from gstatic were rejected); fonts are committed artifacts from the official Noto releases. CJK/Arabic/Indic still unbundled (~12MB) and still hit the CSP.

title: Web map tiles 403: Referrer-Policy stripped the only identification OSM gets
description:
Deployed web app got 403 from tile.openstreetmap.org on every raster tile (case detail map, statistics map, location picker); Android was fine.

Cause: web_headers.pb.js sent 'Referrer-Policy: same-origin', so cross-origin tile requests carried no Referer. On web flutter_map's userAgentPackageName is a no-op (browsers forbid scripts setting User-Agent, see flutter_map's network/tile_provider.dart). So tile requests had zero identification, which the OSM Tile Usage Policy says may be blocked -- and was.

Fix: Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin (the browser default). Cross-origin sends the bare origin only (no case URLs leak), same-origin keeps the full URL, downgrades send nothing. test_rules.py updated; DEPLOYMENT.md documents that a stricter proxy override reintroduces the 403.
close_reason: Fixed: Referrer-Policy is now strict-origin-when-cross-origin

title: Dashboard: carer workload card + carer case filter
description: Coordinator/supervisor-only dashboard card listing org members with their open-case counts; tapping a row opens the cases browser filtered to that carer (new CaseQuery.carer facet).
close_reason: Shipped in a05ff0a: coordinator/supervisor carer-workload card on the dashboard, CaseQuery.carer facet + filter-sheet picker, shared BreakdownCard, requestFocusOnTap:false on the filter dropdowns.

title: Make OAuth2 scopes configurable so OIDC group→role mapping can work
description:
`FEDERFALL_OIDC_*_GROUP` role mapping (`pb_hooks/oauth2_provisioning.pb.js:82-95`)
cannot fire against a real OIDC IdP, because the groups claim never reaches the
server.

PocketBase's generic OIDC provider hardcodes its scopes
(`tools/auth/oidc.go`: `openid`, `email`, `profile`) and `OAuth2ProviderConfig`
(`core/collection_model_auth_options.go`) exposes no scopes field —
`InitProvider()` calls SetClientId/Secret/AuthURL/TokenURL/UserInfoURL/
DisplayName/PKCE/Extra but never `SetScopes`. There is also no JSVM hook over
the auth-methods response (types.d.ts has onRecordAuth*/…WithOAuth2Request only,
and the latter fires *after* the token exchange), so no server-side hook can
widen the request. Putting `?scope=` into `FEDERFALL_OAUTH2_<NAME>_AUTH_URL`
does not work either: Go's `AuthCodeURL` appends its own `scope`, and the
duplicate loses.

Verified live against a Nextcloud IdP — the userinfo payload came back as:

    {"email":"…","email_verified":false,"family_name":"admin","name":"admin",
     "picture":"…","preferred_username":"admin","scope":"openid email profile",
     "sub":"admin","updated_at":1785693244}

no `groups` key. The user landed as `guest`; the earlier account only became
supervisor via the unrelated `firstUser` bootstrap path.

Upstream's position is that this is by design and belongs to the CLIENT:
pocketbase#3727 and pocketbase/discussions#7114 — "PocketBase doesn't restrict
you what scopes to use, it just comes with some minimal defaults. OAuth2 scopes
are usually specified as part of the authorization sign-in/sign-up url."
The Dart SDK's all-in-one call takes a `scopes:` option for exactly this.

Filed as a bug, not a feature: the group-mapping env vars are documented in
docs/DEPLOYMENT.md as working configuration, and they cannot work as shipped.
design:
Scopes are client-side, so the server can only *prescribe* them; the app
applies them. Additive and off by default — unset env ⇒ today's behaviour.

1. `pb_hooks/info.pb.js` — new optional `auth.oauth2Scopes` map, keyed by
   provider name, read from `FEDERFALL_OAUTH2_<NAME>_SCOPES` (space or comma
   separated). Keep `auth.oauth2` an array of name strings so older clients
   keep parsing it. Omit the key when nothing is configured.

2. `ServerInfo` / `ServerAuthOptions` (`lib/core/server/server_info.dart`) —
   parse it into `Map<String, List<String>>`, defaulting to `{}`.

3. `AuthRepository` (`packages/federfall_data/.../auth_repository.dart`) — both
   sign-in paths take `List<String> scopes = const []`:
   - `signInWithOAuth2` (web all-in-one, ~:243) passes `scopes:` straight to
     the SDK.
   - `signInWithOAuth2Code` (mobile, ~:279) has no SDK helper — rewrite the
     `scope` query param on the parsed authorization Uri.
   Both must REPLACE the param, matching the SDK
   (`queryParameters["scope"] = scopes.join(" ")`), so the configured value has
   to be the FULL list including `openid`. Empty list ⇒ leave PB's URL alone.

4. Login screen passes `serverInfo.auth.oauth2Scopes[provider]`.

5. `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` — document the PB limitation (this is what cost a
   debugging session), the new env var, and the Nextcloud specifics: the
   built-in `groups` claim needs the `groups` scope; `occ config:app:set oidc
   group_claim_type --value "displayname"` switches GIDs to display names; and
   the no-app-update alternative `occ oidc:create-claim groups profile
   <CLIENT_ID> getUserGroupsDisplayName`.

Wire contract: new optional response field + client fallback ⇒ NOT breaking,
no major bump.

Out of scope (file separately if wanted): hardening the claim parser for
`{id,name}` object shapes, and `FEDERFALL_OIDC_SYNC_ROLE` to re-apply the
mapping on every login instead of only at provisioning.
acceptance_criteria:
- Setting FEDERFALL_OAUTH2_OIDC_SCOPES="openid email profile groups" makes the app request that scope set, and the groups claim reaches oauth2_provisioning.pb.js
- A user in the FEDERFALL_OIDC_CARER_GROUP group is provisioned as carer, not guest
- Both sign-in paths honour it: web all-in-one and the mobile code-exchange flow
- Unset env / older server with no oauth2Scopes key ⇒ unchanged behaviour (PB's own scope param untouched)
- docs/DEPLOYMENT.md explains the PB scopes limitation and the Nextcloud recipe
- Non-breaking commit (no major bump); dart format clean, flutter analyze clean, flutter test + federfall_data dart test green
notes: Design revised during implementation: NO new operator env. Requesting the groups scope is implied by configuring a group mapping, so info.pb.js derives it — if any of FEDERFALL_OIDC_{SUPERVISOR,COORDINATOR,CARER}_GROUP / _ALLOWED_GROUPS is set, generic OIDC providers (name starts with 'oidc') get [openid, email, profile, <FEDERFALL_OIDC_GROUPS_CLAIM|groups>]. Social providers are excluded: an unknown scope fails their whole authorization request. Rejected FEDERFALL_OAUTH2_<NAME>_SCOPES — a second knob that can drift from the mapping, and one an operator can break by omitting openid. The wire field auth.oauth2Scopes and both app-side paths are unchanged.
close_reason: Shipped in 7056a73 (released as 0.11.1). NOT via the FEDERFALL_OAUTH2_<NAME>_SCOPES env in the original design — the scope list is derived from the group mapping being configured; see the notes. Test-only lint follow-up in 3a6c63f.

title: Code-list deletes state no consequence and don't offer the reversible alternative
description:
Deleting a code-list entry is the highest blast-radius single tap in the app and
has the weakest confirmation.

`CodelistAdminScreen._delete` (`features/admin/codelist_admin.dart:144`) shows a
title plus a one-line body naming only the entry:

- `conditionCodelistDeleteConfirm` -> `Delete "{label}" from the code-list?`
- `admissionReasonCodelistDeleteConfirm` -> `Delete "{label}" from the admission reasons?`
- `markingTypeCodelistDeleteConfirm` -> `Delete "{label}" from the marking types?`
- `medicationRouteCodelistDeleteConfirm` -> `Delete "{label}" from the routes?`

No count of the live records that reference the entry, and no statement of what
happens to them. An admission reason may be referenced by every case in the org;
a medication route by live prescriptions.

Three things make this worse:

1. **No server-side guard.** Nothing in `backend/pocketbase/pb_hooks/` checks
   references before a code-list delete, so the references are simply orphaned.
2. **Every other delete in the app states its consequence.** Same codebase:
   `medProductDeleteConfirm` -> "Existing prescriptions are unaffected";
   `prescriptionDeleteConfirm` -> "Logged doses are kept";
   `dispositionDeleteConfirm` -> "The case will re-open and the animal's status
   reverts"; and `confirmDeleteAnimal` /`confirmDeleteCase`
   (`features/animals/delete_record_dialogs.dart`) enumerate *awaited* real
   counts. These four are the only "are you sure?" dialogs left.
3. **The safe alternative already exists and is not offered.** Every code-list
   entry carries an `active` flag, and consumers deliberately keep a deactivated
   entry visible on records that already reference it — see
   `MedicationRouteDropdown` (`features/cases/medications/prescription_sheet.dart:593`):
   "Active routes, plus the current selection even if it has been deactivated, so
   an existing record's route stays visible." Deactivating preserves history;
   deleting destroys it. The delete dialog never mentions deactivation.

Fix, in order of value:

1. Count referencing records before showing the dialog and name the number, the
   way `confirmDeleteAnimal` does (awaited, not off a `.value` snapshot).
2. When the count is greater than zero, make "Deactivate instead" the primary
   action and demote delete.
3. Consider a server-side guard rejecting the delete while references exist, so
   the rule holds for any client.

Source: general design review (error prevention / control / recovery). Note this
is a *confirmation and copy* gap, not a rules gap — the delete itself is
correctly supervisor-gated.
close_reason: Confirmation now counts referencing records server-side, names the number, states the verified consequence (blanked field, or delete refused for marking types) and makes 'Deactivate instead' the primary action. Server-side guard (fix 3) deliberately skipped — it would contradict the demoted 'Delete anyway'. Commit e330249.

title: Show the offline state — onlineStatusProvider is computed but never displayed
description:
`core/connectivity/connectivity.dart:61` builds a careful online/offline signal:
the `connectivity_plus` interface reading *plus* a real `/api/health` probe
against the configured server, two-strike de-flapping (`confirmStatus`), a
re-probe on lifecycle resume, and a 30 s heartbeat. Its own doc comment refers
to "a spurious banner (federfall-vcm)".

No banner exists. Every consumer of `onlineStatusProvider` in `lib/` is realtime
plumbing:

- `core/realtime/collection_events.dart:28` — skip subscribing while offline
- `core/realtime/live_refresh.dart:20` — refetch on the offline->online edge
- `features/cases/case_realtime.dart:74` — same edge for the case bundle

Nothing renders it. Because the app is online-only with no cache
(`federfall-online-only-no-cache`), a carer whose self-hosted server is
unreachable finds out only by filling in a form and pressing Save — the
per-request `errorOffline` message is the first and only signal.

Fix: in `NavShell.build` (`features/home/nav_shell.dart:130` compact branch and
the rail branch above it) watch `onlineStatusProvider` and render one persistent
line above `navigationShell` while offline. The signal already exists and is
already de-flapped, so this is a display, not a feature.

Source: Dieter Rams design review (principles 4 understandable / 8 thorough).
close_reason: Closed

title: Stop premature re-login: bump users auth token duration + silent refresh on startup/resume
description: Users get logged out after the PocketBase users.authToken.duration elapses (default ~5d in this instance) because the client never refreshes the JWT. Two-part fix: (1) migration setting users.authToken.duration to 30d; (2) SessionRefresher that calls AuthRepository.refresh() on startup, on app resume, and on a slow heartbeat to roll the token window for active users. Affects OIDC and password logins equally.

Implemented per the task description: _PrintReportButton in case_detail_screen.dart, app-bar action guarded !kIsWeb, alongside _ShareReportButton, not canEdit-gated. comments.author: Jan-Henrik Bruhn
comments.text:
POST-CLOSE FIXES (found via live on-device testing, not caught by flutter test/analyze):

1. CRITICAL web-build regression: unified_esc_pos_printer unconditionally imports dart:io/dart:ffi with no working web fallback (its own dart.library.html guard doesn't detect the newer --wasm target either), so importing it from ANY file reachable by the web build broke 'flutter build web --wasm' outright -- !kIsWeb runtime guards don't help since the compiler resolves the whole import graph regardless of what's reachable at runtime. Fix: restructured lib/features/printing/ behind a dart.library.io conditional import (printer_service.dart declares platform-agnostic types like PrinterDeviceRef/ReceiptPaperSize/PrinterService; printer_service_native.dart is now the ONLY file importing unified_esc_pos_printer + package:image, selected via 'if (dart.library.io)'; printer_service_stub.dart is the web fallback). printer_settings.dart, printer_labels.dart, printer_config_sheet.dart, profile_screen.dart and case_detail_screen.dart were all updated to the new plain types. Verified both 'flutter build web --wasm --release' and 'flutter build apk' succeed.

2. 'Kein Drucker eingerichtet' on a cold first tap despite a printer being configured in a previous session: _PrintReportButton read printerSettingsProvider synchronously via ref.read(...).value, which is null while the keepAlive AsyncNotifier's shared_preferences load is still in flight (races it instead of awaiting it) -- visiting the profile screen first happened to warm the cache, masking the bug. Fixed to 'await ref.read(printerSettingsProvider.future)'.

3. User feedback on physical output: added feed()/feed(3) margins + cut to both printReceipt and printTestTicket (top margin trimmed to the library's own default single line per user follow-up -- tear-off edge already gives enough clearance there; bottom kept at 3 lines for real clearance before the auto-cutter blade). Reworked receipt.typ: the ESC/POS library hard-thresholds every pixel to black/white at a fixed midpoint (no dithering) -- gray fills sat right at that threshold and printed as a patchy mess, and Libertinus Serif's thin anti-aliased strokes got chewed up by the same cutoff. Switched to DejaVu Sans Mono (verified via 'typst fonts --ignore-system-fonts' as the only non-serif face bundled in the production alpine image without system fonts) at larger sizes, bold by default, all gray fills removed -- hierarchy now comes from size/weight, not color.

4. CRITICAL regression found via live server logs: EVERY plain PDF share request (no ?widthDots=) started failing hard with 'WidthDots must be an integer between 200 and 1024.' Root cause: case_report.pb.js checked 'widthDotsParam !== null' to detect presence, but PocketBase's query().get() returns '' (falsy empty string) for an absent param, not null -- confirmed against the existing convention in geocode.pb.js ('if (!q)'). '' !== null is true, so parseInt('') -> NaN failed the range check and threw for every non-receipt request. Fixed to a truthiness check ('if (widthDotsParam)'). Verified the corrected branching logic (absent/valid/invalid) against a standalone reproduction of the exact JS.

All fixes verified: flutter analyze clean, flutter test 425/425, dart format clean, flutter build apk + flutter build web --wasm both succeed, typst compile of both report.typ and receipt.typ still clean. Bug #4 (PDF share breakage) was NOT caught by any automated gate -- it only reproduced against the live PocketBase JSVM query API, which nothing in this repo's test suite exercises. Phase 5 should make sure the eventual live-hardware/live-server test pass (backend/pocketbase/tests via run.sh, or a manual curl) explicitly re-checks a plain PDF request now that this class of bug has bitten once.

title: Phase 3 — Printer connectivity in settings
description:
Configure and persist a printer in the profile/settings screen; support ALL transports (network/TCP verified first).

Tasks:
1. Add unified_esc_pos_printer to apps/federfall/pubspec.yaml. Android manifest: BLUETOOTH_CONNECT, BLUETOOTH_SCAN (+ neverForLocation if applicable), BLE + USB-host features. Guard all usage with !kIsWeb (no web support).
2. features/printing/printer_service.dart — thin interface (scan / connect / printBytes|printTicket / disconnect / stateStream) wrapping PrinterManager, so widget tests mock it and the plugin (which can't run in flutter test) stays out of the unit path. Keeps coverage gate >=75%.
3. features/printing/printer_settings.dart — persist chosen device (transport type + address + paper format receipt80/receipt58) in shared_preferences via a keepAlive riverpod notifier, mirroring reminder_settings.dart.
4. Add a Printer section to profile_screen.dart (guarded !kIsWeb): scan -> pick device -> save -> Test print. Consider renaming the screen title Profile -> Settings (l10n app_en.arb + app_de.arb, German primary). Add manual-entry for a network printer IP:port since TCP printers may not surface in scans.
acceptance_criteria: User can scan/select (or hand-enter a TCP host:port for) a printer, save it, and Test print produces output on the network printer. Config survives app restart. Nothing references the plugin on web.
notes:
Verified-first device: Epson TM-T88IV over Ethernet, raw TCP port 9100. Default the manual network-printer entry to port 9100. Confirm unified_esc_pos_printer's TCP transport targets 9100 and that Ticket.image() -> GS v 0 raster prints correctly on the TM-T88IV; add a cut() after the image.
REVISED: settings stores a PaperSize choice mapped to dot width (58->384, 72->512, 80->576), defaulting to 72mm/512 for the TM-T88IV. That ONE value feeds both the ?widthDots= sent to the server AND Ticket.create(PaperSize.x) at print time (must match so the pre-rasterized PNG prints 1:1 with no scaling). The library can't auto-detect width, so this is a required manual user choice — surface it clearly in the printer section. TM-T88IV network default host:9100.
UI PATTERNS from the package example app (adapt, don't copy wholesale — the demo is an interactive playground; ours must PERSIST a selection + support manual TCP entry):
- Scan: PrinterManager.scanAll(timeout: Duration(seconds:5), types: <List<PrinterConnectionType>?>) returns Stream<List<PrinterDevice>>; subscribe and accumulate. Filter chips over PrinterConnectionType.values, plus an 'All' (types=null) option.
- PrinterDevice is a sealed type — pattern-match for display/persistence: NetworkPrinterDevice(host, port), BlePrinterDevice(deviceId), BluetoothPrinterDevice(address), UsbPrinterDevice(identifier).
- Connect/state: manager.connect(device) (throws PrinterException), manager.disconnect(), manager.connectedDevice, manager.stateStream (connected/connecting/error) for a status indicator.
- Test print: Ticket.create(PaperSize.mmXX) + manager.printTicket(ticket).
DELTAS we must add beyond the demo: (1) persist the chosen device to shared_preferences by reconstructing the sealed PrinterDevice from stored fields (type + host/port|address|deviceId|identifier) on load; (2) a manual 'Add network printer' form (host + port default 9100) since scanAll may not surface a TCP printer reliably — build a NetworkPrinterDevice directly; (3) the saved PaperSize choice (dot width) lives alongside the device.
close_reason: Verified end-to-end on real hardware: profile screen's Printer section scans/connects/saves a device (network TCP verified against the Epson TM-T88IV) and Test print produces physical output. usb_serial's Gradle-9 incompatibility was resolved via a dependency_overrides pin to a maintained fork (AppsDevTeam/usbserial@v0.8.0) rather than downgrading the whole project's Gradle version or a from-scratch stub package -- see pubspec.yaml comment for the verification trail (API surface diffed against the hosted 0.5.2).

title: Phase 1 — Server: Typst receipt PNG rendering
description:
Add a receipt (narrow, thermal) rendering path to the existing case-report hook, keeping Typst as the single source of truth. No app dependency — testable standalone via curl against a running stack.

Tasks:
1. Extract shared Typst (STRINGS dict, small helpers, renderEvent) out of typst/report.typ into typst/report_common.typ; slim report.typ to import it. Adding a language / changing an event's text must stay a one-file edit for both PDF and receipt outputs.
2. Add typst/receipt.typ: single-column layout, page(width: <mm>, height: auto) driven by a 'format' input; condensed timeline as stacked blocks (not the 3-col table); keep a small dithered QR of deepLinkUrl; drop the animal photo by default (thermal raster looks rough).
3. Extend pb_hooks/case_report.pb.js: read ?format= (pdf|receipt80|receipt58). receipt80 -> 72mm/576px, receipt58 -> 48mm/384px. Compile with 'typst compile --format png --ppi 203' and return Content-Type image/png (no Content-Disposition). Branch ONLY at the tail — reuse ALL existing payload assembly (JSVM handlers can't share file-level helpers, so a single param-driven handler avoids duplicating ~300 lines). The .pdf path segment stays cosmetic for the receipt case; Content-Type is authoritative.

## Context
goja/JSVM has no Intl; tzOffsetMinutes handling already exists. Confirm the Dockerfile typstfetch stage + bundled fonts support PNG export. Rule/hook changes need a live PB (backend/pocketbase/tests via run.sh).
acceptance_criteria: curl '.../cases/{id}/report.pdf?format=receipt80' returns a 576px-wide PNG that renders the case chronology; ?format=pdf (or omitted) still returns the A4 PDF unchanged; report_common.typ is imported by both templates.
notes:
PRIMARY TARGET IS Epson TM-T88IV = 180 dpi / 512 dots at 72mm. So receipt80 MUST render at --ppi 180 -> 512px wide (page width 72mm). Do NOT use 203dpi/576 for this printer; keep 203/576 only as a note for generic 80mm hardware if a second profile is ever added. receipt58 stays 48mm/384px @203 for typical 58mm units. Consider a paper-cut trailer in the ticket (TM-T88IV has an auto-cutter) — but note the cut is added client-side by the printer library, not in Typst/PNG.
REVISED: no receipt80/receipt58 named formats. Handler takes ?widthDots=N (int, sane bounds e.g. 200..1024) and renders a PNG exactly N px wide: page(width: N/ppi * 1in, height: auto), typst compile --format png --ppi <ppi> (pick a fixed ppi ~203 so pt-sized fonts print at a legible physical size on typical 180-203dpi heads; dpi need not match the printer since raster is 1px=1dot). Keep ?format=pdf for the unchanged A4 path; presence of widthDots (or format=receipt) selects the PNG branch. receipt.typ takes widthDots as an input and lays out a single column to that width. TM-T88IV => widthDots=512.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Jan-Henrik Bruhn
comments.text:
Implemented per the REVISED (widthDots) design in the epic notes, not the older receipt80/receipt58 acceptance criteria on this task (superseded).

- typst/report_common.typ: extracted STRINGS/i18n + lbl/joinDash/joinDot/fmtDate/fmtDateTime/fmtAt/freqLabel/doseStr/renderEvent, parameterized on S (helpers now take S explicitly since Typst modules can't share a closed-over module-level var across imports). report.typ slimmed to import it; call sites updated (fmtDate(S,...), fmtAt(S,...), renderEvent(S,...)).
- typst/receipt.typ: single-column, page(width: widthDots/203 * 1in, height: auto), stacked timeline blocks, small QR, no photo. Takes sys.inputs.widthDots (string int) + the same data payload as report.typ.
- pb_hooks/case_report.pb.js: '?widthDots=' (200..1024, else 400 BadRequestError) branches ONLY at the compile/response tail — all auth/payload assembly (incl. photo fetch) is shared. Receipt path: typst compile --format png --ppi 203, template=receipt.typ, response Content-Type image/png, no Content-Disposition. format=pdf/omitted path is byte-identical to before.
- No named receipt80/receipt58 formats — client always sends the exact dot width (per epic's DESIGN REVISION note), so the endpoint is generic for any printer head width.

Verified by fetching the pinned typst 0.15.0 binary and running the exact compile invocations the hook constructs, against a realistic sample payload (all timeline kinds) plus edge cases (empty timeline, all-null optional fields): PDF renders byte-for-byte the same as before the refactor (visually confirmed), receipt PNG comes out at exactly 512px and 384px wide as requested. Did not curl the live auth-gated endpoint end-to-end — the local dev DB's seeded supervisor password didn't match and creating a new superuser to work around that was (correctly) blocked as a credential-escalation pattern; the hook JS was syntax-checked with node --check.

title: Receipt-printer report printing (ESC/POS, Typst single-source)
description:
Print the per-case report on ESC/POS thermal receipt printers, reusing the existing server-side Typst pipeline (pb_hooks/case_report.pb.js + typst/report.typ) as the single source of truth.

Approach: Typst renders a narrow, fixed-width (height:auto) page to a PNG raster at 203dpi (72mm/576px for 80mm; 48mm/384px for 58mm). The client feeds the PNG to unified_esc_pos_printer's Ticket.image()/printBytes(), so the server does zero ESC/POS protocol work and Typst stays the one source of truth for content/layout/i18n. The A4 PDF report is unchanged.

Client library: unified_esc_pos_printer (TCP / BT-Classic / BLE / USB; Android + desktop; no web). Target ALL transports for compatibility; NETWORK/TCP is the path verified first (only hardware currently on hand). Printer connectivity is configured in the profile/settings screen (per-device, shared_preferences), then a Print action on the case detail screen prints the selected format.

Web is unsupported by design (guard everything with !kIsWeb).

## Context
Related code: backend/pocketbase/pb_hooks/case_report.pb.js, backend/pocketbase/typst/report.typ, packages/federfall_data/lib/src/repositories/case_report_repository.dart, apps/federfall/lib/features/cases/case_detail_screen.dart (_ShareReportButton), apps/federfall/lib/features/profile/profile_screen.dart, apps/federfall/lib/features/reminders/reminder_settings.dart (shared_preferences pattern to mirror).
notes:
TARGET HARDWARE (first/primary): Epson TM-T88IV, networked.
- Resolution: 180 dpi (NOT 203). Print width 72mm = 512 dots. So the 80mm receipt format renders Typst at page(width: 72mm) + --ppi 180 => 512px wide. The generic 203dpi/576px figure elsewhere in this epic applies to cheap 80mm printers, NOT this Epson — make 'receipt80' target 180dpi/512px.
- Transport: raw TCP on port 9100 (JetDirect/ESC-POS), so the network path is host:9100 by default.
- Auto-cutter present: end the ticket with a partial/full cut.
- Older ESC/POS but supports the GS v 0 raster bit-image command, which is what unified_esc_pos_printer's Ticket.image() emits — raster PNG path works.
DESIGN REVISION — dynamic width, no named presets. The library (unified_esc_pos_printer) does NOT report printer dpi/width; the device object is connection-only. It exposes PaperSize enum: 58mm=384px, 72mm=512px, 80mm=576px, chosen by the developer/user (no auto-detect). NOTE: the Epson TM-T88IV is the library's mm72 (512 dots), NOT mm80/576 — 80mm paper but a 512-dot/180dpi head.

Contract: client sends the exact dot width, ?widthDots=N (from the user's paper-size choice in settings), and Typst renders a PNG EXACTLY N pixels wide (fixed server ppi; page width = N/ppi inches, height auto). For raster printing 1 image px = 1 printer dot, so dot width is the ONLY param that matters for paper fit; dpi/mm are irrelevant to fit. This makes the server generic for ANY head width, not just 384/512/576. The one stored paper-size setting drives BOTH the widthDots query param AND Ticket.create(PaperSize.x) at print time so they never drift.
close_reason: All 5 phases delivered and verified end-to-end on real hardware (Epson TM-T88IV, network/TCP): server-side Typst receipt rendering with dynamic widthDots, receipt PNG data-layer fetch, printer connectivity/settings UI, case-detail print action, and a full test/quality-gate pass. User confirmed live: test print, case receipt print, and plain PDF share all work on the physical printer. Two real regressions were caught and fixed via live testing beyond what flutter test could catch on its own: (1) unified_esc_pos_printer's unconditional dart:io/dart:ffi imports broke the web/wasm build outright despite !kIsWeb guards — resolved via a dart.library.io conditional-import seam so only one file touches the plugin; (2) case_report.pb.js's widthDots presence check used '!== null' where PocketBase's query API returns '' for an absent param, silently breaking every plain PDF request in production until caught from live server logs.

title: Extract shared create/edit sheet scaffold + save/error mixin (case-timeline forms)
description:
The ~12 create/edit bottom sheets each hand-roll the same scaffolding. Affected: weight_entry, marking, condition_entry, journal_entry, quarantine, placement, disposition, exam, follow_up, administration, prescription sheets + aviaries/aviary_form_sheet. Repeated pieces:
- Identical _save() error tail: 'on RepositoryException -> inline _error = errorMessage(l10n,e)' / 'on Object -> reportCaughtError + _error = errorGenericTitle', each with setState(_busy=false). Byte-identical across sheets (~29 copies of the catch block).
- Identical user/org guard: read currentUserProvider, throw RepositoryException('no org for current user') when null (12 files).
- Identical build() shell: guardUnsavedChanges -> Padding(fromLTRB(lg,0,lg,lg+viewInsets)) -> SingleChildScrollView -> Form(onChanged: markDirty) -> Column(min,stretch) with a titleLarge header, the _error block, and a trailing PrimaryButton(actionSave).
- Repeated state fields _formKey/_busy/_error/_isEditing (26 files with the _busy pair).
- Repeated inline _error display block (23 copies) and _pickDate showDatePicker(firstDate: DateTime(2000)...) (11 copies) and _trim helper (6 copies).
design:
Two-part extraction:
1) A SheetScaffold widget owning the padding+scroll+Form+title+error-slot+save-button layout (slots: title, children, isBusy, error, onSave). Composes with existing DiscardGuard/guardUnsavedChanges + showAppSheet + PrimaryButton.
2) A FormSheetState mixin (or small controller) owning _busy/_error and a runSave(Future<void> Function()) that wraps the try/catch tail once, plus a requireUserOrg() helper for the org guard.
Reuse existing DateField/pickDateTime for _pickDate and drop per-file _trim (a shared trimToNull). Migrate sheets incrementally. Note: PocketBase JSVM gotcha does not apply here (Dart side). Higher value but more invasive than federfall-d1et/985j/ko9m; consider doing it after those land. May be worth splitting per-sheet if the diff gets large.
acceptance_criteria: Shared SheetScaffold + save/error mixin exist and are adopted by all ~12 sheets; per-sheet _save catch block, org guard, build shell, _error block and _pickDate no longer duplicated; each migrated sheet's widget tests still green; flutter analyze clean.

title: Case detail: collapse ~17 requests into one expanded case fetch (caseBundle)
description:
Opening a case detail fires ~16-18 requests: caseById, animalById, finderById, the canEditCase share lookup, prior-case history, plus 12 separate list requests for the timeline (journal, weights, case_conditions, medications, administrations, markings, placements, dispositions, follow_ups, exams, exam_findings, quarantine). invalidateCaseTimeline (case_timeline.dart) re-fires all 12 on EVERY realtime event.

VERIFIED (2026-07-03, throwaway PB via tests/run.sh harness, as a plain carer with rules enforced): PocketBase back-relation expand fetches all 12 sources + animal + finder in ONE request:

GET /api/collections/cases/records/:id?expand=animal,animal.markings_via_animal,finder,journal_entries_via_case,weights_via_case,case_conditions_via_case,medications_via_case,medication_administrations_via_case,placements_via_case,dispositions_via_case,follow_ups_via_case,exams_via_case,exams_via_case.exam_findings_via_exam,quarantine_records_via_case

- all 12 back-relations resolve; exam findings nest under exams_via_case (flatten client-side)
- view rules enforced: a foreign carer still gets 404; expanded rows honor each collection's viewRule
- rule boundary stays PB rules (no new hook endpoint needed)

Design:
1. caseBundleProvider(caseId): one expanded getOne -> CaseBundle (case + animal + finder + the 12 lists). Needs a repo method that exposes the raw RecordModel expand (PbRepository.getOne maps to T and drops expand) — e.g. CaseBundle.fromRecord in federfall_models.
2. Turn the 12 leaf providers into derivations of the bundle so all tiles/sheets keep working unchanged; move the per-collection sorts client-side (weights measured_at asc, meds -started_at, doses -administered_at, journal -entry_at, follow_ups due_at asc, exams -examined_at, findings created asc, placements -moved_in_at, markings/quarantine as today).
3. invalidateCaseTimeline -> invalidate the bundle: 1 request per realtime event instead of 12.
4. animalById/finderById on the case detail read from the bundle.

Caveats:
- PB caps each expanded back-relation at 1000 records; long cases (years of daily doses) could hit it. Mitigation: if any expanded list has exactly 1000 entries, fall back to that collection's paged forCase fetch.
- weightsForAnimal/examsForAnimal (lifetime views) and casesForAnimal/caseSummaries stay separate — animal-scoped, different screens.
- case_shares_via_case could fold the canEditCase lookup in later (share viewRule may differ — verify first).

Net effect: case open ~17 -> ~4 requests; realtime refresh 12 -> 1.

title: animal_avatar: ref used after unguarded async gaps in the photo flow
description:
File: apps/federfall/lib/features/animals/animal_avatar.dart:104-141

_editPhoto calls ref.read (104-105) and ref.invalidate (137-141) after awaiting a bottom sheet, the image picker, and a network upload, with no mounted check anywhere; on a ConsumerWidget, using ref after the element unmounts throws. The camera flow on Android routinely backgrounds/destroys the activity; on return the code throws "Cannot use ref after the widget was disposed", the upload result is silently dropped, and the avatar providers are never invalidated (stale photo shown).

Fix: capture what is needed before the awaits and add mounted guards, matching the discipline used everywhere else in the codebase.

title: Switching servers reuses the previous server's persisted auth token
description:
Files: apps/federfall/lib/core/pocketbase/pocketbase_provider.dart:34-43, apps/federfall/lib/core/server/server_config_controller.dart:40-49

AuthTokenStorage uses one fixed key (federfall.auth) not scoped to the server URL, and neither setServerUrl nor clearServerUrl deletes it (only explicit signOut does). Failure: expired session -> /login -> "change server" -> configure server B: the rebuilt client seeds AsyncAuthStore with server A's payload, and the PocketBase client attaches any non-empty token as the Authorization header — server A's bearer token (identity claims) is transmitted to a different, potentially untrusted host. The provider docstring at line 25 explicitly promises "a clean auth store".

Fix: purge auth storage on server change, or key the storage by origin.

On web (path URLs enabled specifically for shareability) opening a shared link like /cases/abc123 with a restorable session always ends on /cases — the target case never opens. /cases/browse?... query strings are dropped too.

description:

If the user closes the external browser without finishing, the future never completes and there is no timeout or cancel path. title: Remove member can never succeed — users deleteRule allows self-delete only
description:
Files: apps/federfall/lib/features/admin/member_management_sheet.dart:146 (and :254), backend/pocketbase/pb_migrations/1700000010_access_rules.js:158

The sheet deletes another user via repo.delete(widget.member.id), but users.deleteRule is "id = @request.auth.id" (self-delete only, never widened by any later migration or hook route) — and the remove button is only rendered when !_isSelf, i.e. exclusively in the forbidden case. Every removal attempt by a supervisor fails with the localized "unauthorized" error; the feature is dead in production. test_rules.py only exercises deletes with the superuser token, so it does not catch this.

Fix: add a supervisor-scoped delete path (rule change or hook route, with last-supervisor + open-caseload guards server-side — see related TOCTOU issue) and extend test_rules.py to cover non-superuser deletes.

title: pbDate throws on malformed dates; mapper exceptions escape PbRepository._guard untranslated
description:
Files: packages/federfall_models/lib/src/converters.dart:16, packages/federfall_data/lib/src/pb_repository.dart:151-162

pbDate uses DateTime.parse (not tryParse), and _guard only catches TimeoutException and ClientException — fromRecord runs inside op() and its FormatException/TypeErrors are not caught. One record with a garbage date field makes an entire list() call throw a raw FormatException that bypasses the RepositoryException classification the UI error states depend on. All other converters are defensive (tryParse, tolerant coercions); pbDate is the outlier.

Fix: tryParse in pbDate + a last-resort mapping for mapper failures in _guard.

title: Location picker pairs a new pin with the previous pin's address on geocode failure
description:
File: apps/federfall/lib/features/cases/location/location_picker_screen.dart:116-137

title: Exam edit deletes all findings before re-creating them, non-atomically
description:
File: apps/federfall/lib/features/cases/exams/exam_sheet.dart:181-199

The edit path deletes every existing ExamFinding (186-188), then re-creates the new set in a sequential loop (191-199) — separate HTTP calls in an online-only app. A network drop between delete and create permanently loses the exam's clinical findings (the sheet shows an error, but the old rows are already gone). On the create path, a finding-create failure after the exam create (158-164) means retrying the sheet creates a duplicate exam. Contradicts the project's atomicity discipline (intake/handoff go through single-transaction hooks).

Fix: move exam+findings persistence behind a transactional hook route (like /api/federfall/intake), or at minimum create-before-delete with server-side replace.

title: Disposition edit leaves stale fields from the previous type on the record
description:
File: apps/federfall/lib/features/cases/disposition/disposition_sheet.dart:166-193

The update body only includes release_* when _isRelease, transfer_* when _isTransfer, vet when _isEuthanized, aviary when _isAviary. PocketBase keeps omitted fields on update, so changing released -> transferred keeps the stale release_location/release_type/release_geo. DispositionTile (disposition_tile.dart:45-50) renders release AND transfer fields unconditionally, so a corrected outcome displays leftover data from the wrong outcome type — a wrong clinical/legal record.

Fix: always send the full field set, blanking sections that do not apply ('' / {lon:0,lat:0} clear values, as edit_case_intake_sheet.dart:136-148 already does).

title: Unknown disposition wire value silently maps to DispositionType.died
description:
File: packages/federfall_models/lib/src/models/disposition.dart:41

`type: DispositionType.fromWire(d['type']) ?? DispositionType.died` maps any unrecognized or absent wire value to the most severe outcome. title: Security: case_shares can be re-pointed to any case after creation (privilege escalation)
description:
The case_shares update rule (backend/pocketbase/pb_migrations/1700000010_access_rules.js:131) is 'case.active_carer = auth || shared_by = auth || SUP' and nothing makes case/shared_with/org/access immutable. PocketBase evaluates plain field refs in update rules against the STORED record, so a carer can create a share on their own case, then PATCH the share's 'case' field to any other case in the org — granting themselves or an accomplice read/edit on a private case.

Fix: add '@request.body.case:isset = false && @request.body.shared_with:isset = false && @request.body.org:isset = false' to the update rule (new migration), or a hook field-guard like the users one in main.pb.js:295.

Same root cause in weaker form on all case child collections: an edit-share holder can re-point a journal_entries/weights row's case (or org) to a foreign case, injecting records into timelines they cannot read.

Add tests: backend/pocketbase/tests/test_rules.py covers share create/revoke (~line 318) but never PATCHes a share or re-points a child record.
close_reason: Fixed by migration 1700000043_immutable_boundary_relations.js: update rules on case_shares (case/shared_with/org), cases (org), all case child collections (case/org) and exam_findings (exam/org) now reject requests that include the boundary fields (@request.body.X:isset = false). case_shares.access stays mutable. Rule tests cover share re-point, child + grandchild re-point, and legit updates; suite green (113 passed).

title: Rewrite repository layer to use $PocketBase RequestPolicy.cacheAndNetwork
description:
All ~20 repository classes in packages/federfall_data/lib/src/repositories/ need to be reimplemented on top of $PocketBase instead of PbRepository.

Pattern for each repository:
- Keep Repository<T> interface unchanged
- Implement methods using $PocketBase.collection(name).{getOne,getList,create,update,delete}()
- Use requestPolicy: RequestPolicy.cacheAndNetwork (the offline-first default)
- Convert RecordModel → domain model via existing Case.fromRecord / Animal.fromRecord etc.
- Drop PrefsRecordCache usage entirely

Priority order: cases, animals, case_conditions, treatments, weights (the core daily-use data) first; then worklist_entries, findings, exams, and remaining collections.

title: Shared case not visible to recipient until full page reload
description:
Sharing a case with another user does not update the recipient's app live; they must hard-reload the whole web page before the shared case becomes accessible. No realtime push arrives, and closing/reopening the case view doesn't help.

ROOT CAUSE
The live-sync (core/realtime/live_refresh.dart + collection_events.dart) only re-fetches when a PB realtime event fires on a *subscribed* collection, and PB only emits an event for the collection whose record actually changed. Sharing creates a case_shares row — the 'cases' record itself is untouched — so the recipient's subscriptions never fire:
  - cases_screen.dart watches ['cases','animals'] only (not 'case_shares').
  - case_detail_screen.dart calls no liveRefresh at all.
A full reload works because the repo fetches server-first when online and the cases list rule now matches via case_shares_via_case.shared_with.

FIX
Subscribe the case-listing surfaces to 'case_shares' too, so a share/unshare to the current user invalidates and refetches:
  - cases_screen: liveRefresh(['cases','animals','case_shares'], invalidate casesBrowserDataProvider)
  - case_detail_screen: add liveRefresh(['cases','case_shares'], invalidate caseByIdProvider(caseId)) — also covers live revoke/unshare.
  - dashboard_screen: add 'case_shares' to its ['cases','dispositions'] watch for consistency.
PB delivers case_shares events to the recipient because the case_shares view rule allows shared_with = self.
close_reason: Fixed: watch 'case_shares' on cases browser, case-detail live-sync, and dashboard KPIs so a share/revoke refetches live. flutter analyze clean. Pending live two-user verification.
