title: A weight recorded without a case cannot be edited
description:
A weight is animal-scoped: `case` is optional on it, and the animal screen's
weight card offers a "record weight" action that takes none. Such a row was then
unreachable — not just uneditable:

* the case chronology reads `weightsForCase` → `repo.forCase(caseId)`, so a
  weight with no case appears in NO case timeline, and `WeightEntryTile` (the
  only edit/delete affordance in the app) lived only there;
* the animal screen's card showed the LATEST reading as a plain non-tappable
  `ListTile` plus the trend chart, so older readings existed only as dots on a
  chart.

Fix: the card lists the whole history, newest first, using the same
`WeightEntryTile` as the case timeline — same menu, same custody gate. Its
`caseId` became nullable (null = the animal's own history) and its delete now
invalidates `weightsForAnimalProvider` as well as the case bundle, matching what
the entry sheet's save already did.

Not touched, and worth a separate decision: a case's chronology still shows only
weights whose `case` names it. A weight taken during a case but recorded from
the animal screen is not in that case's timeline.
close_reason: Fixed in 65bcb60: the animal weight card lists the full history with the shared WeightEntryTile.

title: A keeper may edit their own aviary
description:
`aviaries.update` has been coordinator/supervisor since 1700000010, from a time
when `keeper` was a display-only label ("Owner / responsible person"). It is not
one any more: required since 1700000076, and write AUTHORITY since 1700000077 —
`current_aviary.keeper` is what lets someone write about the birds living there,
place a bird into the enclosure, and read its patronages (1700000085). The
person who answers for an enclosure could not correct its capacity, location or
notes; that had to be relayed to a coordinator. Same UI/server gap federfall-ftm2
closed for the "add resident" FAB, in the other direction.

## What the keeper may not change: who the keeper is

Reassignment stays a coordinator action. It is the one field on the row that
hands something over rather than describing the enclosure: naming somebody else
grants them custody of every resident AND the sponsor PII of every patronage
hanging off them (inline name, address, mobile — federfall-5s5j).

Expressed as `isset = false || = @request.auth.id` rather than a bare freeze
(the shape 1700000051 uses for `users.org`): the edit form sends the whole
record including `keeper`, which is required, so a hard freeze would 404 every
keeper's edit — exactly the defect federfall-t7ad was filed for. "You may send
it as long as it still names you" lets an unchanged value through while refusing
a handover.

Untouched: `org` stays frozen, create stays coordinator/supervisor (making an
enclosure is not the same as running one), delete stays supervisor.

Not a wire break — the rule accepts strictly more requests than before.
close_reason: Implemented in 693b6a9: 1700000086 names the keeper in aviaries.update; reassignment stays coordinator-only via isset||self.

title: Patronage overview: one coordinator/supervisor screen for all patronages
description:
A single screen listing every Patenschaft in the org, active and past, for
coordinators and supervisors only.

## Why

Today a patronage is only reachable through the bird it belongs to
(`_SponsorshipSection` on the animal detail), and access resolves through
`animal.current_aviary.keeper` — so a keeper sees their own residents' patronages
and nobody has a view of the whole. That is right for a keeper and wrong for the
role that has to answer the questions a rehab actually gets asked: who is
currently sponsoring, what does that come to per month, whose patronage has
lapsed, and which sponsors need a Zuwendungsbestätigung this year.

It is also the only place the rows that no keeper can reach are visible at all: a
patronage on a bird that has left aviary care, or an orphan whose bird was
deleted (federfall-5s5j.4 decided those are KEPT), belong to coord/sup alone by
the read rule. Without this screen they are unreachable outside the Admin UI.

## Shape

- Coordinator/supervisor only. `sponsorships`' list rule already grants exactly
  that (1700000085's `COORD_SUP` branch), so no rule change is needed — but the
  ROUTE has to be gated too (`canViewReports`-style, the statistics screen's
  stance), or a carer reaches a screen that renders an empty list and a heading
  about data they may not see.
- Server-side filtered and cursor-paged, per federfall-trep: a pure query object
  → `filterFor()` → `PbReadOnlyRepository.page()` → a feed notifier with
  `loadMore`/`retryPage` → the shared `PagedListTail`. This list grows with the
  org and must not be read whole to narrow it on the device.
- Facets: active / ended / all (an `ended_at`-based split, stated as an explicit
  set the way the case browser's "active" is), interval, and a debounced
  (~300 ms) search over `sponsor_name` + `city`. The empty state must tell
  "nothing yet" from "no matches" by whether the query narrows anything.
- Each row names the SPONSOR first (this screen is about people, unlike the
  animal detail's card) with the bird and the amount beneath it, and taps through
  to the animal.
- A total: sum of active patronages normalised to a monthly figure, in integer
  CENTS throughout (`amount_cents`; never a double — see `parseAmountToCents` /
  `formatAmountCents`). `one_time` is not a monthly figure and must be counted
  separately rather than divided into one.
- Rows whose bird is gone (orphans) render with the bird slot empty rather than
  being hidden — they are the rows most likely to need attention, and they are
  the reason this screen exists for coord/sup at all.

## Where it hangs — DECIDED

Its own screen, NOT a section of the admin hub: `/admin` is gated on
`canManageTeam`, i.e. supervisor only (`router.dart:458`), while sponsorships are
readable by coordinators too — a section there would be unreachable for half its
audience. The screen itself is gated on `canViewReports`, which is exactly
`coordinator || supervisor`, the same set as 1700000085's read rule.

The way in is a small TEASER CARD on the dashboard, which opens the screen.
`_CarerWorkloadCard` (dashboard_screen.dart) is the shape to copy, down to its
two habits: it renders `SizedBox.shrink()` for any other role rather than an
empty card, and its loading state is `shrink()` too — the card slots into the
dashboard's own scroll view, so a spinner would shove the caseload around on
every refresh. It simply appears once loaded.

A statistics entry is not ruled out and may follow, but the teaser is the decided
first cut: a rehab wants the figure on the way past, not after choosing a period.

## The teaser needs an aggregate, and it cannot be summed on the device

The card wants two numbers: how many patronages are running, and what they come
to per month. The count is one cheap `count()` (its `totalItems`); the SUM is
not — and federfall-trep forbids reading the collection to add it up on the
device, while federfall-nmwi says the app aggregates nothing client-side any more.

Recommended: extend `GET /api/federfall/stats` (`lib_stats.js` + `stats.pb.js`)
with a `sponsorships` block — `{active, monthlyCents, oneTimeCents}`. That route
already loads the org's rows once, is already `canViewReports`-gated, and a
statistics card later would read the same numbers. Additive, so `feat:`.

Two things to get right there:

* **The block is NOT period-scoped**, and everything else in that payload is.
  "What is running right now" has nothing to do with `?year=` / `?month=`, so it
  has to be documented as period-independent — otherwise it reads as a figure for
  the selected period and is wrong every time somebody changes the period.
* **`one_time` is not a monthly figure.** Count it separately; dividing a single
  donation into a month invents a number.

The alternative is a dashboard count view on 1700000070's pattern (COUNT + SUM
grouped by org). It would need its own guest-safe access rules for a figure the
stats route can already serve, so it is the second choice — though a SQL `SUM`
beats a JS reduce if the row count ever justifies it.

## PII, and what this screen must not become

Every row is a private person's name, address and mobile. So: no export button in
the first cut (a CSV of donor contact details leaving the app is its own decision,
and `report.exported` would have to cover it), and nothing here may be logged —
reading is not an audited action anywhere in this app, and adding it here would
put sponsor names into a table nothing can delete from, which is exactly what
`SENSITIVE.sponsorships` exists to prevent.
close_reason: Shipped in 1dc834c: /sponsorships screen (canViewReports-gated, keyset-paged by sponsor_name, active/ended/interval facets + debounced sponsor/city search), a dashboard teaser card, and a period-INDEPENDENT sponsorships block on GET /api/federfall/stats ({total,active,monthlyCents,oneTimeCents,noIntervalCents}). Deviation worth knowing: a row taps through to the sponsorship DETAIL SHEET rather than straight to the animal — the sheet is where the address a Zuwendungsbestätigung needs lives, it is the only surface an orphan has at all, and it now carries a 'Zum Vogel' link for the rows that still name one. No export, no audit row, as decided.

title: Sponsorships: model, repository, UI and the aviary-transfer warning
description:
Model, repository and UI for Patenschaften, including the transfer warning.

## Model + data

1. `packages/federfall_models/lib/src/models/sponsorship.dart` — freezed +
   `fromRecord` from a PB `RecordModel`. `interval` is an enum carrying a `wire`
   value (so a Dart rename stays wire-safe). `amount_cents` is an `int`.
2. `packages/federfall_data/lib/src/repositories/sponsorships_repository.dart`
   on `PbRepository<Sponsorship>`.
3. Bind it in `apps/federfall/lib/data/repository_providers.dart`.

Run `dart run build_runner build` in `federfall_models` — codegen is required,
not optional.

## UI

4. `features/aviaries/sponsorship_providers.dart` (`@riverpod`, by animal id) +
   `sponsorship_sheet.dart` (create/edit, the `showXSheet()` pattern the case
   timeline uses).
5. `_SponsorshipSection` card in `animal_detail_screen.dart`, alongside
   `_WeightSection` / `_MarkingsSection`. Render the card ONLY when the viewer is
   the current aviary's keeper or a coord/sup. An always-present empty
   "Patenschaften" card tells the whole org that this bird has the feature
   applied to it, which is a leak even with no values in it.
6. **`features/cases/disposition/disposition_sheet.dart` — the transfer warning.**
   When `type == placed_in_aviary` AND the chosen aviary differs from the
   animal's `current_aviary` AND the sponsorship count is > 0, show a warning
   banner before submit. It must say:
   - how many patronages will move (a COUNT, never a sponsor name)
   - who gains access — the target aviary's keeper, by name
   - that the current keeper loses access
   Same banner, different sentence, for a disposition that clears
   `current_aviary` (released / died / transferred): the patronage becomes
   coordinator/supervisor-only and no keeper can reach it.
7. `app_de.arb` + `app_en.arb` (German is the primary UI language), then
   `flutter gen-l10n`. Interval labels as an enum→label helper in the
   `features/cases/cases_labels.dart` style, resolving `l10n` like `Validators`.
8. Dates through `formatLocalDate` (`ui/widgets/date_field.dart`) — the only
   thing in `lib/` allowed to turn a `DateTime` into a date string.
   `date_field_test.dart` sweeps for violations and will fail otherwise.

## Money in the form

Parse and render `amount_cents` at the edge; never hold a double. Locale-aware
input (German decimal comma) — check whether an existing numeric field
(`medications` dose) already solves this before writing a new parser.

## Tests

9. Widget tests with `mocktail` repo overrides via `ProviderContainer(overrides:)`.
   At least: the section is hidden for a non-keeper; the banner appears on an
   aviary CHANGE; the banner stays absent on a same-aviary re-save.
10. Keep `flutter test --coverage` above 75% (CI's `min_coverage` gate).

## Gates, all from the REPO ROOT

`dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed .`, `flutter analyze` (the root
run covers the packages — a run inside `apps/federfall` does not, which is how 9
issues once shipped in `federfall_data`), `flutter test` from `apps/federfall`,
`dart test` in each touched package.
close_reason: Closed

description:
Rule + cron tests for `sponsorships`, against a live PocketBase
(`backend/pocketbase/tests/run.sh`). Not runnable from the Flutter suite.

## `test_rules.py` — new `[sponsorships]` block

- the aviary's keeper reads its residents' sponsorships
- a DIFFERENT aviary's keeper gets nothing
- the bird's own carer gets nothing (this is the point of the feature: custody of
  the bird is not access to the patronage)
- coordinator and supervisor read (decided)
- create on a bird with no `current_aviary` is refused
- create on a resident of somebody else's aviary is refused
- `animal` re-point is refused (the freeze)
- guest is refused everywhere

**The move test is the feature.** Keeper A creates a sponsorship on their
resident; a `placed_in_aviary` disposition moves the bird to keeper B's aviary;
A now gets nothing and B reads it. Assert BOTH directions — a rule that returned
nothing to everyone would pass a one-sided test just as well.

Also assert the terminal case: after a `released` disposition clears
`current_aviary`, no keeper reads the row and coord/sup still do.

## `RELATION_GUARDS`

Add `"sponsorships": {"animal": "frozen", "org": "frozen"}`. That registry fails
BOTH ways, so the entry has to match what the guards actually do.

No edits needed to the guest sweep or `[relation org scope]`: the sweep finds the
rules itself, and `org_scope.pb.js` asks the SCHEMA which relations are
org-scoped — `animals` carries an `org`, so the guard fires on the new collection
without being told about it.

## `test_cron.py` + `tests/run_cron.sh`

One `sed` line rewriting `sponsorshipRetention`'s schedule to `* * * * *`, on the
existing `auditRetention` / `finderPiiRetention` template.

- a window measured in days cannot be reached by backdating (`created` is a
  server-owned autodate), so make the window vanishingly small
  (`0.000001` days = 86 ms) instead of trying to age a row.
- assert PER-ORG windows, not just one. The window is read from a JSON field,
  i.e. through the `getString()` + `JSON.parse` trap, and a single-org test
  cannot tell a working settings read from a broken one.
- assert a fresh orphan inside `ORPHAN_GRACE_MS` survives.

Kept out of `run.sh` / CI because it waits for a wall-clock minute boundary.

## Verify with real exit codes

Run each suite so its OWN exit code survives — piping through `grep` reports the
filter's status and has hidden real failures in this repo before.
close_reason: Closed

title: Sponsorships: collection, access rules, write guards, orphan purge
description:
Backend for `sponsorships` — collection, rules, write guards, orphan purge.
Verify against a RUNNING stack; rule/cron tests are Python and cannot run in the
Flutter suite.

## 1. `1700000085_sponsorships.js`

Collection + fields per the epic (no `aviary` field — access is live through
`animal.current_aviary`). Rules, every one suffixed
`&& @request.auth.role != "guest"` or `test_rules.py`'s guest sweep fails:

- `list` / `view` / `update` / `delete`:
  `AUTH && org = @request.auth.org && (COORD_SUP || animal.current_aviary.keeper = @request.auth.id)`
- `create`: `AUTH && org = @request.auth.org` — the real gate is the hook below.
  Do NOT try `@request.body.animal.current_aviary.keeper`: "this bird is
  currently in an aviary you keep" is a cross-record invariant, and a two-hop
  body resolution is not something this repo has proven.

The one-hop-through-`animal` read form IS proven ground: 1700000079 probed
exactly that predicate against a live 0.39.8, including the trap case where a
second clause on the same back-relation is satisfied independently. Pin it in
tests rather than trusting the note.

## 2. `pb_hooks/sponsorships.pb.js`

`*Request` variants only, so server-side writers and the Admin UI stay exempt.

- create: `animals.current_aviary` must be non-empty AND `lib_custody.js`'s
  `keeps()` must pass for it (coord/sup override). This is the "only birds
  assigned to an aviary" rule.
- freeze `animal` and `org` with the `&& @request.body.<f>:isset = false`
  suffix — 1700000082's shape, for 1700000082's reason (on UPDATE a plain field
  reference resolves against the STORED record, so a rule cannot guard the
  destination).

`require()` inside the handler with the `${__hooks}` absolute form — file-level
helpers are not in scope in an isolated handler context.

## 3. `lib_audit.js`

- actions: `sponsorship.created` / `.updated` / `.deleted`
- `SENSITIVE.sponsorships = [sponsor_name, sponsor_pronouns, address,
  postal_code, city, region, mobile]`
- `notes` into the free-prose denylist (diff() is a denylist, so an edit would
  otherwise copy both old and new prose)
- `subject_label` empty, exactly like a finder subject

`audit_events` is supervisor-only AND append-only with a tamper guard nothing can
delete from (1700000068). A sponsor's name logged there outlives every scrub —
the same hole `finder_retention.pb.js` exists to close.

## 4. `merge_animals.pb.js`

Add `"sponsorships"` to the re-point list. Left out, the merge does not leave the
rows behind — it DESTROYS them inside its transaction and answers 200
(federfall-0ua6, where `egg_records` and `aviary_stays` were both added after
that list was written). Update the merge screen's moves summary to match.

## 5. `pb_hooks/sponsorship_retention.pb.js`

Daily cron. Deletes sponsorships whose `animal` no longer exists, once older than
the org's window. `animal` is `cascadeDelete: false`, so deleting a bird leaves
the donation record as an orphan — kept (readable by coord/sup, invisible to
keepers since the predicate yields nothing) and then deleted after the window.

- read the window through `lib_org.js`'s `settingsOf` / `positiveNumber`
  (`sponsorshipRetentionMonths`). NEVER a fresh `getString()` + `JSON.parse`:
  `record.get()` on a JSON field hands JS a byte array, `settings.someKey` is
  `undefined`, and the code falls through to its default in silence
  (federfall-jumi — it had already disabled two windows).
- carry an `ORPHAN_GRACE_MS` like `finder_retention.pb.js`, so a row written
  moments before its animal is never mistaken for an orphan.

## Done when

Migration applies and reverts cleanly, hooks load, and Phase 2's tests are green
against a live stack.
close_reason: Closed

title: Patenschaften: sponsorship records for aviary residents
description:
Aviary residents can carry a **Patenschaft** (sponsorship): who sponsors the bird
(name, pronouns, postal address, mobile), how much they give and from when.

The data is PII and is treated as such: it is readable by the keeper of the
aviary the bird currently lives in, plus coordinators and supervisors — nobody
else in the org, not even the bird's carer.

## Shape (decided)

ONE collection `sponsorships`, sponsor details stored INLINE on the row — not a
shared `sponsors` person table on the `finders` pattern. A shared table would let
keeper A read a sponsor's PII the moment keeper B's bird acquired the same
sponsor. Inline means each keeper only ever holds their own copy. Accepted cost:
a person sponsoring two birds is entered twice.

Fields: `animal` + `org` (both frozen), `sponsor_name` (required, 200),
`sponsor_pronouns` (free text 50 — a select would be presumptuous),
`address`/`postal_code`/`city`/`region` (mirroring `finders`), `mobile` (50),
`amount_cents` (number, min 0 — integer cents, never a float for money),
`interval` (select: monthly/quarterly/yearly/one_time), `started_at`,
`ended_at` (empty = active), `notes` (2000).

## Access follows the bird, live

There is deliberately NO frozen `aviary` snapshot on the row. Access resolves
through `animal.current_aviary.keeper`, so **moving a bird to another aviary
moves its sponsorship with it** — nothing to re-point, nothing that can drift.
That is the requested behaviour, not a side effect.

Because the transfer is silent server-side, the UI warns at the one place that
can trigger it: a `placed_in_aviary` disposition. `current_aviary` is
isset-guarded against client writes (1700000075) and only `lib_derive.js` sets
it, so the disposition sheet is the whole surface.

The warning is always computable by whoever triggers it, and that is not luck:
`disposition_custody.pb.js` already requires custody to move a bird, so the
mover is the current keeper or a coord/sup — all three can read the sponsorships
they are about to hand over. There is no "warn about data you cannot see" case.

`animal` stays FROZEN even so: a re-point would be a second, unwarned route for
pushing PII into another keeper's view.

## Accepted consequence

When the bird leaves aviary care entirely (released / died / transferred),
`lib_derive.js` clears `current_aviary` and NO keeper can read the sponsorship
any more — only coordinator/supervisor. That is correct (there is no owner to be
the owner) but it means winding a patronage down needs a coord/sup, and the
keeper who entered it loses their own rows. The disposition warning says so.

## Wire contract

New collection, new fields, no changed route or response shape — additive.
Ships as `feat:`, NOT `feat!:`; a major bump would force every user to update
for nothing.
close_reason: All five children closed. Shipped in e9424f0 (feature) + 2f2743d (the retention decision). The one thing the epic's own shape got wrong is recorded in the sponsorships-required-relation-trap memory: required + non-cascading does not leave an orphan, it refuses the animal delete. Follow-up federfall-ys7z carries the coordinator/supervisor patronage overview.

title: A stale carer can evict another keeper's resident by correcting their own old placement
description:
The residual of federfall-mpm4, left open on purpose and named in
`lib_custody.js`'s `requireOutcomeWrite` header.

`disposition_custody.pb.js` refuses a disposition write that would move a bird
into the writer's own hands. It deliberately does NOT refuse one that moves the
bird into NOBODY's hands: correcting a placement to a `released` (or deleting
it) ends with the bird at large, which is not an escalation — and being able to
correct the outcome you recorded is the workflow that gate exists to protect.

## The act

1. B was the carer of a case on bird X, closed in 2024 by
   `placed_in_aviary` naming C's enclosure. X has lived there since.
2. B PATCHes that disposition to `type: released` (or deletes it).
3. `lib_derive.js` re-derives `current_aviary = ""`, `aviary_stays.pb.js`
   closes the residency with a present-dated `ended_at`, and C's flock is one
   bird smaller.

Nothing here is refused: the gate fires (the aviary changes), B does not hold
X, but nobody else would hold X without B's row (that row IS why C holds it),
and the destination is no enclosure at all — so branch (b) does not trip.

## Why it was not fixed with mpm4

The two acts are indistinguishable from state alone. A placement row is the
reason the bird is where it is, so setting that row aside always answers
"nobody holds it" — for the honest correction (a carer fixing the enclosure
they just named) and for this. mpm4's fix separates them by DESTINATION, which
catches the custody grab and by construction cannot catch an eviction. The only
remaining discriminator is time ("has anything happened since"), and a resident
in an enclosure has no further events, so even that does not separate them.

## Scope, accurately

* **Not a custody escalation.** B gains nothing directly. The two-step version
  (evict, then admit the now-at-large bird through `/api/federfall/intake`,
  which `requireAdmissible` allows for a bird nobody holds) does get B custody
  — but as two visible acts, not one silent one.
* **Not silent.** The registry shows the bird at large, the enclosure's
  `aviary_stays` row closes, and `lib_audit.js` records the disposition edit
  with actor, type and the aviary it moved off.
* **In-org only** and repairable: a supervisor (or the keeper, via a fresh
  placement on a case they carry) can put the bird back.
* **Pre-existing**, and wider before mpm4: the same edit could re-point the
  resident at the writer's own enclosure until `disposition_custody.pb.js`
  landed.

## Shape a fix could take

Needs a decision, not a patch — the candidates all cost something:

* Require plain custody for ANY write that changes `current_aviary`. Closes it
  completely, and makes a wrong-enclosure placement supervisor-only to repair
  (`childEdit` binds a disposition to its case's carer, so the keeper who now
  holds the bird cannot edit the row).
* Give the keeper standing on the dispositions that house their residents —
  widen `childEdit` for `dispositions` where `aviary.keeper = auth.id` — and
  then require custody. Repairs the friction the first option creates, at the
  price of a rule that reaches sideways out of the case.
* Notify rather than refuse: leave the write, surface it to the keeper. Cheapest
  and matches "not silent", but there is no notification channel in the app yet.
close_reason: Fixed in 1c43001 (user's call, 2026-08-10): the moving leg of requireOutcomeWrite is now plain custody with no correction exemption. The 'nobody else holds it once this row is set aside' branch was dropped because a placement row IS the reason the bird is where it is, so it answered yes for an honest repair and for an eviction alike, and no reading of the state separates them. Cost accepted: handing a bird over is not reversible by whoever handed it over — repairs are the keeper's (admit it on a case of their own, 1700000078's keeper branch) or a supervisor's, both pinned in test_rules.py. The re-opening leg keeps the weaker form, so deleting a wrong outcome (death record included) still works for its carer.

title: A stale carer can take custody back by re-opening their own closed case
description:
The sibling route to federfall-mpm4, same root cause, different act — and it
needs no disposition at all. Found while probing whether federfall-8f1m had
widened anything, and VERIFIED against a live 0.39.8 (throwaway probe appended
to test_rules.py, then reverted):

    probe setup: the bird is recorded dead, its case closed    PASS
    probe: B, its former carer, holds nothing                  PASS
    probe: B can re-open their own closed case                 PASS  (200)
    probe: ...and holds the bird again                         PASS
    probe: ...which now reads in_care                          FAIL  (deceased)
    probe: a stranger's intake on it is refused                PASS  (403)

## The mechanism

`cases.status` carries no guard of any kind. 1700000075 isset-guards the derived
fields on `animals`, and 1700000081/1700000082 freeze the relations, but `status`
is an ordinary select field and `cases.update` is `caseEdit`
(`active_carer = auth.id || SUP || edit-share`) with no status clause. So the
carer of a case closed years ago can

    PATCH /api/collections/cases/records/<their old case>  {"status": "in_care"}

and 1700000077's custody predicate — `cases_via_animal.active_carer ?= auth.id
&& cases_via_animal.status ?= "in_care"` — matches again. They hold the bird.

## Scope, accurately

* **Pre-existing.** 1700000077 keyed custody on case status from the start;
  federfall-8f1m changed nothing here. It is filed now because this line is
  where it was looked for.
* **Not a lifetime-status flip.** The probe's one FAIL is the good news: the
  re-opened case is an OLDER admission than the death that closed it, so
  `deriveState()` still answers `deceased`. The registry keeps saying so, and
  `requireAdmissible`'s deceased refusal still stands for everyone else.
* **In-org only** (`org_scope.pb.js`, federfall-jo1l) and audit-logged
  (`case.updated` carries the status change with an actor label).
* **Repairable**: a supervisor can re-close or delete the case.

## Why mpm4's fix would not close it

mpm4 is about who may WRITE A DISPOSITION; this route writes none. Both come
from the same sentence — "active_carer of a disposed case never expires" — so
whatever answers that sentence has to cover both acts, which is the reason
these are linked rather than merged.

## Shape a fix could take

Either the same shape as mpm4 (an act that would RE-TAKE a bird needs current
custody or coordinator/supervisor), or narrower and cheaper: gate the
disposed -> open transition specifically. Re-opening a case is a real
correction workflow — a disposition entered by mistake — but it is today
performed by DELETING the disposition, which is already supervisor-only and
already re-opens the case through `reconcileCase()`. That suggests the direct
status write has no workflow behind it at all, and a
`@request.body.status:isset = false`-style guard for the `disposed` case (or a
hook refusing the transition below supervisor) may cost nothing. Check
case_detail/status UI before assuming that: `ready_for_release <-> in_care` must
stay freely writable, it is only the transition out of `disposed` that is at
issue.
close_reason: Fixed in 505dad1: case_status.pb.js refuses a status that contradicts the case's outcome, so re-opening a disposed case means deleting the outcome (the correction path that already re-opens it). The delete route into the same place is gated by disposition_custody.pb.js's custody predicate. Both probes from this issue are pinned in test_rules.py's [custody: taking a bird back] block.

title: A stale carer can take custody of a bird by dating a placement just-past
description:
The residual half of federfall-j163, left explicitly rather than drifted into.

`dispositions` create/update is gated by 1700000010's `childEdit`
(`case.active_carer = auth.id || supervisor || edit-share`), and `active_carer`
of a DISPOSED case never expires — so the carer of a case closed years ago can
still write dispositions on it forever.

Since 1700000077 that is write authority, not just a label: a disposition of
type `placed_in_aviary` sets `animals.current_aviary`, and
`current_aviary.keeper = @request.auth.id` is a custody branch on `animals`
(and, through 1700000079, on the animal-level record collections). So:

1. B was the carer of a case on bird X, closed in 2024.
2. B keeps an aviary of their own (or is its keeper by any route).
3. B adds `placed_in_aviary` on that old case naming their own enclosure,
   dated YESTERDAY — the latest event in X's history.
4. `lib_derive.js` re-derives `current_aviary = B's aviary`, and B is now a
   custodian of a bird in someone else's care.

## What this is NOT

* Not the future-date hole. federfall-j163 fixed that
  (`disposition_dates.pb.js`); this needs no future date at all, only a date
  later than the bird's last real disposition.
* Not cross-org: `org_scope.pb.js` (federfall-jo1l) now refuses an aviary from
  another organisation, so this is an insider path within one org.
* Not silent: `lib_audit.js` logs the disposition with actor, type and aviary,
  and a supervisor can delete the row (which re-derives).
* Not a way to hide the bird: since federfall-8f1m an OPEN case still forces
  `lifetime_status = in_care`, so the registry keeps saying the bird is in
  care — only `current_aviary` (and the write access hanging off it) moves.

## Why it was not fixed with j163

The obvious clauses both break shipped workflows, which is why this is filed
rather than patched:

* A **case-status** clause (`case.status != "disposed"`) would forbid EVERY
  disposition edit: any case carrying a disposition IS disposed, so the whole
  correction path (UX Phase B, `disposition_sheet.dart` in edit mode, and the
  `[hooks: disposition edit/delete reconciliation]` block) would 403. It is
  self-defeating — the only way to fix a wrong outcome is to edit the row that
  made the case closed.
* A **custody** clause ("you must still hold the bird") would forbid correcting
  a historic case for a bird now in someone else's care, which is exactly what
  archive/backfill work is (federfall-sinp's whole motivation).

## Shape a fix could take

Narrow the widening rather than the workflow: allow editing/correcting a
disposition on a closed case, but require CURRENT custody (or
coordinator/supervisor) specifically for a disposition that MOVES the bird —
i.e. `type = placed_in_aviary` naming an aviary, or any row that would become
the animal's latest event. The disposition sheet's create path is the one that
needs the gate; its edit path on an old case does not.

Needs a decision on whether "would become the latest event" is expressible in a
hook cheaply (it is: `lib_derive.js` already computes it), and on whether
coordinators — who cannot repair `current_aviary` directly, since it is
isset-guarded against every client (1700000075) — should be the override.
close_reason: Fixed in 505dad1: disposition_custody.pb.js refuses a disposition write that would change the animal's derived current_aviary (or, on delete, re-open its case) unless the writer holds the bird — or nobody else does once that row is set aside AND the write does not end with the bird in the writer's own care. Correcting/withdrawing/deleting your own fresh outcome all still work; residuals filed as federfall-q11w (eviction) and federfall-ehzz (destination keeper's consent).

title: dispositions.disposed_at is unvalidated and now steers the custody derivation
description:
Raised during the /security-review of the custody line, then DOWNGRADED out of the
report — it is an integrity/robustness gap, not a newly-reachable privilege
escalation. Recorded because the tension is real and undocumented.

`pb_hooks/lib_derive.js` orders dispositions by
`COALESCE(NULLIF(disposed_at,''), created)`. `disposed_at` is a bare `date` field
(1700000008) with no bound and no validating hook, and `dispositions`
create/update/delete is still governed only by 1700000010's `childEdit`
(`case.active_carer = auth.id || supervisor || edit-share`) — no custody clause
and no case-STATUS clause, so a carer stays `active_carer` of a case forever,
including after it is disposed.

So a carer who once held a bird can add a disposition to their own closed case
with `disposed_at` far in the future and pin that bird's derived state — which
since 1700000077 includes `current_aviary`, i.e. write authority.

## Why this is NOT reported as a vulnerability

* Pre-1700000080 the create hook applied the newest-WRITTEN row blindly, so the
  same eviction needed no future date at all. This line made the damage harder to
  cause, not easier.
* The keeper-branch variant additionally requires an aviary already assigned to
  the attacker, and only a coordinator/supervisor can assign one (1700000010).
* The "at large, then admit it" variant is a bypass of hardening that only
  arrived in this same line (`requireAdmissible`); before it, any member could
  open a case on any animal.
* Repair exists: a supervisor can delete the row, and any carer of another case
  on the bird can out-date it (the disposition sheet lets `disposed_at` be
  chosen). Not unrepairable — though note a COORDINATOR cannot, since `SUP` in
  these rules means supervisor only and `current_aviary` is isset-guarded against
  every client (1700000075).
* It is audit-logged (`type` / `disposed_at` / `aviary` with an actor label).

## Worth fixing anyway

`lib_derive.js`'s own header says "nothing security-relevant may key off this
ordering" — written in the same line that made 1700000077 key off its output.
Either that sentence is wrong or the ordering needs a guard. Cheapest honest fix:
reject a `disposed_at` more than a small skew in the future, in an
`onRecordCreate`/`onRecordUpdate` hook on `dispositions`. A future disposition is
not a thing that can have happened, so this costs no real workflow.

Consider also a case-status or custody clause on the `dispositions` rules: the
right to correct a closed case's outcome forever, for a bird now in someone
else's care, is broader than the custody model intends anywhere else.
close_reason: Closed

title: Derive lifetime_status from open cases too, so a returning bird stops reading 'Released'
description:
`animals.lifetime_status` is derived from DISPOSITIONS only (`pb_hooks/lib_derive.js`),
and "this bird has an open case" is not a disposition. So a re-admitted bird keeps
reading whatever its LAST disposition said — `at_large_released` for a returning
bird, `in_aviary` for a resident under treatment — through the whole of its new
stay, and the registry chip says so.

`intake.pb.js` cannot simply set `in_care` on its re-identification branch to fix
this, which is what the comment there now explains: it would be a value the
derivation cannot reproduce, so the next disposition edit on that animal would
flip it back while the case is still open. (The brand-new-animal branch is fine
precisely because `in_care` IS what `deriveState()` computes for a bird with no
disposition.)

## Fix

Teach `deriveState()` about open cases: a bird with a non-disposed case is
`in_care` regardless of what its latest disposition said — the disposition
describes a PAST episode, the open case describes now. Concretely, in
`lib_derive.js`, before consulting `latestDisposition()`, check for a case in the
active set (`in_care` / `ready_for_release` / `""`, the set federfall-jt5u names).

Two things to settle rather than assume:

* **`current_aviary` must NOT follow.** A resident under treatment is still that
  enclosure's bird, and since 1700000077 `current_aviary` is a custody pointer —
  emptying it on admission would take the keeper's write access with it, which is
  the same failure federfall-sinp just fixed. So the open case decides
  `lifetime_status` and leaves `current_aviary` exactly as it was.
* That makes `lifetime_status = in_care` with `current_aviary` set a legitimate,
  reachable state. Check what reads the pair: `housed()` filters on
  `current_aviary` (fine), the dashboard's aviary tile and
  `aviaryOccupancyCounts` likewise. The registry/animal-header chip would say
  "In care" for a bird physically in an enclosure — probably right, but it is a
  UI decision, not a derivation one.

Once this lands, the case-create hook setting `in_care` (rejected during sinp as
the same class of bug) is unnecessary: the derivation answers it.

## Testing

`test_rules.py`'s `[disposition ordering]` block is the neighbour to extend —
admit a released bird again and assert it reads `in_care` while the new case is
open, then that it falls back to the latest disposition once the case is disposed.
Add a resident-under-treatment case asserting `current_aviary` and the keeper's
custody both survive.
notes: Split out of federfall-sinp, whose ordering fix landed first.
close_reason: Closed

title: Aviary population: server allows what the UI reserves for coordinators
description:
aviary_detail_screen.dart gates the 'Bewohner hinzufügen' FAB behind canManageAviaries (coordinator/supervisor) and its own doc comment says 'Coordinators/supervisors can edit the aviary, add residents and write journal entries'. The server disagrees: aviaries create/update IS coordinator+ (1700000010), but the animal that becomes a resident is created through animals.create, which is bare org scope. Probe (plain carer): renaming an aviary -> refused; adding a resident to it -> 200.

So the enclosure's name is better protected than its occupancy.

Fix: make create-into-an-aviary match the UI gate —
  animals.createRule = AUTH && org = @request.auth.org
                       && (@request.body.current_aviary:isset = false
                           || COORD_SUP)
Intake creates its animal server-side in intake.pb.js (rules bypassed) and never sets current_aviary, so nothing else is affected.

Pairs with federfall-7no9: once current_aviary is unwritable on update, create is the only remaining client route into an aviary, and this closes it to the same role the UI already assumes.
notes: Likely absorbed by federfall-q7ks.2: custody gates create-into-an-aviary on being that aviary's keeper, which is strictly narrower than the coordinator+ gate proposed here. Close as superseded when q7ks.2 lands rather than doing both.
close_reason: Superseded by federfall-q7ks.2 (3434db0). Custody gates create-into-an-aviary on being that aviary's keeper — strictly narrower than the coordinator+ gate proposed here, and pinned in test_rules.py's [custody: animals] block ('a carer cannot add one to someone else's aviary').

title: Verify present_at_find against a live PocketBase
description:
The migration and the audit change cannot be exercised by the Flutter suite —
`backend/pocketbase/tests/test_rules.py` needs a running stack (`tests/run.sh`).

## Assertions to add

- **Audit** (`[audit]` block, near the existing `marking.created` /

title: Marking sheet: 'Bei Fund' checkbox that disables the date picker
description:
`apps/federfall/lib/features/cases/markings/marking_sheet.dart`.

## Behaviour

- New `bool _presentAtFind` in `_MarkingSheetState`, initialised from
  `widget.marking?.presentAtFind ?? false`.
- A `CheckboxListTile` (or the sheet's existing switch/checkbox idiom — match
  what other sheets use rather than inventing one) directly above the existing
  `DateField`, labelled "Bei Fund" / "Present when found", with a subtitle
  explaining it: the bird already carried this when it was found.
- Ticking it sets `DateField(enabled: false)` and replaces the shown value with
  the resolved find date, so the user sees WHICH date is being stored rather
  than a blank. Unticking restores the previously picked date (keep the
  `_appliedAt` field; only the enablement and the value source change).
- The checkbox is hidden entirely when `widget.caseId == null` — no case, no
  find moment (see the epic's decision note).
- `markDirty()` on toggle, like `_pickDate` does.

## Resolving the anchor date

`case.foundAt ?? case.admittedAt ?? case.created`, read from the case the sheet
already has in scope via `caseBundleProvider(caseId)` / `casesProvider` —
whichever the sheet can reach without a second fetch. If the bundle is not yet
loaded, keep the checkbox disabled rather than guessing a date.

## Payload

`_save`'s `body` gains `'present_at_find': _presentAtFind`, and `'applied_at'`
becomes the resolved find date (UTC ISO) when the flag is on, the picked date
otherwise. Both create and update paths — the flag must be clearable on an edit.

## l10n

New keys in `app_en.arb` + `app_de.arb` (German is primary):
`markingFieldPresentAtFind`, `markingFieldPresentAtFindHelp`. Then
`flutter gen-l10n`.

## Tests

Extend `apps/federfall/test/features/cases/markings/markings_test.dart`:
- ticking the box disables the DateField and the create payload carries
  `present_at_find: true` with `applied_at` equal to the case's `found_at`;
- `found_at` null falls back to `admitted_at`;
- no `caseId` => no checkbox rendered;
- an edit that unticks it writes `present_at_find: false`.

title: Markings: record a marking as already present when the bird was found
description:
A ring/marker a bird already carried when it was found is not something we
applied — today the sheet forces a date onto it, and the entering carer either
guesses or picks "today", which puts a ring the bird arrived wearing into the
middle of its treatment chronology.

Add a "Bei Fund" checkbox to the marking sheet. Ticking it disables the date
picker, records the marking as pre-existing, and anchors it to the case's find
moment so it lands at the start of the case timeline instead of at the moment
of data entry.

## Design decisions

- **New optional bool `markings.present_at_find`** rather than reusing a
  marking type. `marking_types` is a supervisor-managed code list saying WHAT
  the marking is (Finderring / Vereinsring / Mikrochip); provenance is an
  orthogonal fact — a Vereinsring is normally found-with, an Auswilderungsring
  never is, and neither is derivable from the other. Additive optional field =
  wire-safe, so this ships as `feat:`, not `feat!:` (CLAUDE.md wire contract).
- **`applied_at` is still written, snapshotted from the case.** The flag is the
  semantic; the date stays materialised because three readers sort and window on
  it and none of them can see a flag: `PbMarkingsRepository.forAnimal`
  (`sort: -applied_at`), `_MarkingEvent.at` in the case timeline, and
  `case_report_rows`'s markings column (`COALESCE(NULLIF(mk.applied_at,''),
  mk.created) <= AS_OF`, 1700000067). Leaving `applied_at` null would fall the
  view back to `created`, i.e. the data-entry date, which for a backfilled case
  can be AFTER the disposition — the ring the bird arrived wearing would then
  drop out of the annual report's markings column entirely.
- **Anchor date = `case.found_at ?? case.admitted_at ?? case.created`.** Snapshot,
  not derived: editing the case's find date later does not retro-move existing
  markings. Deriving would mean the SQL view and the repository sort could not
  see the date at all.
- **The checkbox only exists with a case context.** `showMarkingSheet` takes an
  optional `caseId` (null from the animal detail screen's `_MarkingsSection`,
  e.g. an aviary resident with no open case) — with no case there is no find
  moment to anchor to, so the checkbox is hidden there.
- **`applied_by` keeps its authorship stamp** (`lib_authorship.js` ACTOR_FIELDS)
  even when present_at_find: it means "who recorded this", not "who ringed the
  bird", and no UI surface prints it as the latter.

## Out of scope

- Changing `case_report_rows` — a found-with ring already satisfies the window
  (`applied_at` = find moment <= AS_OF) and is already printed. Flagging the
  provenance IN the report is a separate call.
- Backfilling existing markings. There is no signal that distinguishes them.

## Open question for the review

The seeded type "Finderring" (1700000040) may already be read by some users as
"the ring it was found with". If so the checkbox and that type will look
redundant on screen — worth a sentence in the type's admin help, or a rename.
close_reason: Closed

title: Code lists are not seeded for orgs created after their migration
description:
Found while designing Mikroskopie (docs/MICROSCOPY_DESIGN.md section 2.1).

Every supervisor-managed code list is seeded by a MIGRATION iterating the
organisations that exist at migration time (1700000012 conditions, 1700000039
admission_reasons, 1700000040 marking_types, 1700000041 medication_routes,
1700000060 medication_products). No hook seeds an org created afterwards --
bootstrap_supervisor.pb.js, settings.pb.js and main.pb.js all do nothing here.

Consequence: a second organisation starts with EVERY code list empty. Diagnoses,
admission reasons, marking types and routes all have to be typed from scratch, and
nothing tells the supervisor that a starting set was supposed to exist.

Not currently biting (single-org deployments), but it is a trap for the first
multi-org install, and Mikroskopie will inherit it the moment it ships.

Fix shape: an onRecordAfterCreateSuccess("organisations") hook that seeds the
default vocabulary, with the seed sets moved somewhere both it and the migrations
can read (lib_seed.js), so the two cannot drift.

title: Intake wizard step 1 asks for nothing on the common path
description:
Step 1 'Animal' of the new-case wizard holds a re-id search (for the rare returning bird), a species dropdown already pre-filled to Stadttaube, and an optional name. For the overwhelmingly common admission the carer taps Next on an untouched screen. Step 3 is entirely optional too; only step 2 carries a required field (at least one admission reason).

Deleting step 1 removes a tap from every single admission, and makes the intake read as the two real decisions — what happened to this bird, and what do I want to attach — instead of three, one of which is ceremony.

This was the single highest-leverage edit identified in a Dieter Rams design review (principle 10, as little design as possible).
design:
lib/features/cases/new_case_screen.dart:762 (_buildAnimalStep).

Move the _SpeciesField to the top of the intake step (_buildIntakeStep, :810) and put the re-id search behind one 'Returning bird?' link beside it. The optional name field can go to step 2 (now step 1) or to the finish step.

Knock-on work:
- _currentStep is 0/1/2 with species validated on step 0 and reasons on step 1 (_next, :647) — both required checks collapse onto one step.
- _WizardHeader/_WizardNav total goes 3 -> 2; caseSectionAnimal may stop being a step title.
- The draft store persists _currentStep (:677) — a restored draft written by an older build can name step 2, so clamp on restore.
- Widget tests that page through three steps.
notes: Overlaps federfall-gd46 (drop the quarantine-days field from the intake wizard) — both restructure the intake steps. Do them in one pass, or land gd46 first since it only removes a field.
close_reason: Won't do — the three-step wizard shape stays deliberately. The step-0 problem it named (opening on the rare returning-bird path) is fixed in federfall-tekz by reordering species and name above the re-id search. See the decision comment on this issue for why the two-step collapse was rejected.

comments.author: Jan-Henrik Bruhn
comments.text:
Decision: the three-step shape stays. Reviewed collapsing to two steps (and a rebalanced by-story split — bird/problem vs. find-circumstances/documentation) and judged the three headings honest enough not to pay the restructuring cost: the merged step ran to ~9 fields including a 12-chip reason group, so the two-step version mostly moved the imbalance rather than removing it.

What the issue was actually pointing at — step 0 opening on the rare returning-bird path — is fixed in federfall-tekz by reordering: species (prefilled) and name lead, the re-id search sits below them. Keeping this open only if the three-step wizard is revisited wholesale; otherwise close as won't-do.

federfall-gd46 (drop the quarantine field) stands on its own and still shortens step 1.

title: Report routes spawn an unbounded typst subprocess per request (authenticated CPU exhaustion)
description:
Both report routes synchronously shell out per request with no concurrency cap and no rate limit (the limiter added by geocode.pb.js covers only the geocode paths):
  - annual_report.pb.js:342 — $os.cmd('typst','compile',...).run(), gated by requireReporting (coordinator/supervisor)
  - case_report.pb.js:596/608 — same, gated by requireMember, i.e. ANY active non-guest member, for any case they can view

One authenticated member looping GET /api/federfall/cases/<id>/report.pdf spawns one typst process per request and can exhaust CPU and temp space on a small self-hosted box. Insider/compromised-account DoS rather than anonymous, but the app has no other subprocess surface.

Related scalability issue in the same handler: annual_report passes the entire payload as a single argv element ('--input','data='+JSON.stringify(payload)) and lib_stats.loadCaseRows reads with limit 0 (unbounded). For an org with a few thousand cases the serialized payload can approach or exceed ARG_MAX (~2 MB per argument on Linux), at which point the compile fails with an opaque error rather than a report. Passing the JSON via a temp file (--input reading a path, or sys.inputs from a file the template loads) removes both the argv ceiling and the process-listing exposure of the payload.

Fix ideas: a rate-limit rule for the two report path prefixes (the mechanism already exists in geocode.pb.js), and/or a simple in-flight counter rejecting concurrent renders with 429/503.
close_reason: Closed

title: Animal merge silently deletes the duplicate's egg records and aviary-stay history
description: merge_animals.pb.js re-points only cases/markings/weights/exams (line 122) before tx.delete(duplicate). But two more collections carry a direct animal relation with cascadeDelete:true — egg_records (1700000056) and aviary_stays (1700000052), both added after the merge route's list was written. Merging a duplicate that has egg records or stay history cascade-deletes those rows inside the merge transaction: no error, no warning, and the merge screen's summary (merge_animal_screen.dart) doesn't count them either. Fix: add egg_records and aviary_stays to the re-point loop (and consider the survivor stay-reconciliation the aviary_stays hook does on animal save).
close_reason: Fixed in dd25cb0: egg_records + aviary_stays added to the merge re-point loop (with the open-stay reconciliation), case-less residency preserved, survivor saved once so the ledger hook sees one transition. Pinned by test_rules.py's [animal merge] block and the merge screen widget test.

title: Three surfaces still pull whole collections to the device
description:
federfall-80tc (CSV export), federfall-nmwi (statistics) and federfall-s0wk (dashboard) each removed a full-collection read. Two more are gone now; three remain.

DONE
  worklist_providers.dart — casesRepo.list() -> forCarer(me). It read every case
      the caller may see (org-wide for a coordinator) and kept the handful they
      carry. The disposed check stays client-side on purpose: it is the one
      predicate needing a server `!=`, and federfall-jt5u records one of those
      disagreeing with the arithmetic on three runs out of four.
  intake_map_providers.dart — cases now come from the new
      CasesRepository.admittedBetween when a period is selected, which is the
      NORMAL path (the screen opens on 'this year', not 'all time'); animals come
      from byIds over the ids those cases name, projected to id,species,name.
      Note admittedBetween is INCLUSIVE at both ends, unlike countAdmittedBetween's
      half-open calendar range — the map filters again on the device with inclusive
      bounds, so the two conventions have to match or a case exactly on the
      boundary lands in one answer and not the other.

REMAINING — and none is a straight swap:
  cases_browser.dart:237,238   casesRepo.list() + animalsRepo.list()
      DELIBERATE. Its doc says filtering happens client-side because 'the dataset
      for a single association stays small enough that this is simpler and more
      responsive than round-tripping each filter change'. That trade-off is
      defensible; the question is only where it stops being true. If it changes,
      the whole filter/search UX moves server-side with it — a much bigger job
      than swapping one call, and one that needs the facets below to move too.
  case_facets.dart:119,120     dispositionsRepo.list() + caseConditionsRepo.list()
      Only loaded when a facet actually reads them (CaseQuery.needsFacets), and
      they exist to build caseId->outcome / caseId->conditions maps for
      client-side filtering. Tied to the browser decision above.
  animals_providers.dart:28    animalsRepo.list()
      The animals registry list screen, same client-side-filtering shape.

Measure first: row counts on a real instance, so the call is made on numbers
rather than on the word 'all'. Note federfall-bpw6 is fixed, so these no longer
re-run every time a browser window regains focus.
notes:
All three surfaces converted; filtering is server-side and the lists page by cursor.

cases_browser.dart  — casesRepo.list()+animalsRepo.list() -> CasesRepository.browse()
    (CaseBrowseQuery -> filterFor -> keyset page) + animalsRepo.byIds for the
    page's animals, projected to id,species,name,photo.
case_facets.dart    — DELETED. The diagnosis facet is now a filter clause
    (case_conditions_via_case.condition.label ?= / .free_text ?=), so no per-case
    rows are read at all. terminalDispositionByCase survives in cases_browser.dart:
    dispositions_via_case.type ?= x is a SUPERSET of 'terminal outcome is x', so
    the feed narrows the page it gets back — only while the facet is set.

    search as name ~ q || markings_via_animal.code ~ q.
Bonus, same code path: markingsRepo.allActive() (every active marking in the org)

a back-relation cannot be constrained twice (two clauses match independently), so a
marking-code search now also matches REMOVED markings; and the outcome superset above.
The active split is an explicit status set, never status != 'disposed' (federfall-jt5u).

Verified: flutter analyze clean from the root, dart format clean, 875 app tests +
182 data-package tests green, coverage 81.5% (gate 75), and run.sh 672/672 against a
live PocketBase including a new [case browser filters] block that pins every new
filter form — plus that a carer's widened scope still returns nothing of another
carer's.

title: Refocusing the window refetches the worklist and the case list
description:
Observed on web: unfocusing and refocusing the browser window reloads the dashboard's Today card. It is NOT realtime — realtime is working; this is the session heartbeat cascading through an identity dependency.

The chain:
  1. Flutter web maps window focus to AppLifecycleState.resumed.
  2. session_refresh.dart:57 — AppLifecycleListener(onResume: () => refresh()) rolls the PocketBase token.
  3. refresh() saves the new token, so pb.authStore.onChange emits. PbAuthRepository.changes is documented as firing on 'login/logout/refresh' (auth_repository.dart:16,207).
  4. current_user.dart:17 — currentUserProvider listens to repo.changes and calls ref.invalidateSelf().
  5. Anything that WATCHES currentUserProvider.future recomputes in full.

Consumers that therefore refetch on every refocus:
  - worklist_providers.dart:103 (worklistSource) — all cases + 6 more queries. Feeds the Today card AND the Today tab.
  - cases_browser.dart:226 (casesBrowserData) — all cases + all animals.
  - cases_providers.dart:57 (canEditCase), org_settings_providers.dart:47, reminders.dart:70.
(form_sheet.dart:34 and codelist_admin.dart:273 use ref.read, so they do not subscribe — fine.)

None of these care about the token. They want the user's ID (or role), which a refresh does not change. The dependency is simply too coarse.

Fix: depend on the field, not the object — riverpod 3.3.2 has selectAsync:

  final me = await ref.watch(currentUserProvider.selectAsync((u) => u?.id));

A token refresh then produces the same selected value and no dependent recomputes. Check each consumer for what it actually needs (canEditCase needs id + role, so select a record of both).

Worth a test per converted consumer: emit an auth change with an unchanged id and assert the repo was queried once, not twice.

Compounds federfall-trep: the refetch this triggers is the expensive one.
close_reason: Closed

title: Dashboard Today card blinks out on every reload
description:
The dashboard's Today preview renders `ref.watch(worklistProvider).maybeWhen(data: ..., orElse: () => SizedBox.shrink())`. `maybeWhen` has no skipLoadingOnReload, so ANY non-data state collapses the card to nothing:

  - the worklist ticker invalidates `worklistProvider` every minute (a pure recompute, but the provider is async so it still passes through AsyncLoading)
  - it invalidates `worklistSourceProvider` every 15 minutes, which refetches over the network — the card is gone for the whole round trip
  - every realtime event on worklistLiveCollections does the same
  - an ERROR hides the card until the next tick, with nothing said

The Today screen never had this because it goes through AsyncValueView, which sets skipLoadingOnReload/skipLoadingOnRefresh and keeps data through a network error. worklist_providers.dart's ticker doc already claims that behaviour for BOTH surfaces ('AsyncValueView keeps the current list visible during the reload ... so nothing flashes or shifts'), so the card was the odd one out rather than a deliberate difference.

Fixed by giving the card the same policy plus a 2px progress bar in a permanently reserved slot, so a refresh says so instead of vanishing and nothing shifts.
close_reason: Closed

title: pb_hooks: five hand-rolled copies of the route auth gate
description:
Every hook ROUTE re-implements the same gate inline: exam.pb.js:32, intake.pb.js:45, merge_animals.pb.js:41, case_report.pb.js:34, and (as requireReportingAuth) lib_stats.js — active auth, not a guest, has an org, plus a role clause that differs per route.

This is the rule boundary in code form, and a missed clause is a hole, not a cosmetic slip. The guest wall is exactly the thing that has needed re-applying before (1700000045_guest_wall_refresh.js), and test_rules.py's guest sweep only walks COLLECTIONS — a route that forgot the guest clause would pass that sweep. The copies have already drifted in shape: some throw 'No organisation.' on a separate line, merge_animals gates on supervisor by inequality, lib_stats on coordinator|supervisor by two comparisons.

Now that lib_audit.js and lib_stats.js have established that a required module is the one thing isolated JSVM handlers CAN share, put the gate in a lib_auth.js: requireMember(e) -> org, requireSupervisor(e), requireReporting(e) (coordinator|supervisor, the org-wide-figures gate). Move lib_stats.js's requireReportingAuth there and have it re-export or call through, so lib_stats stays about statistics.

Then extend test_rules.py's guest sweep to the ROUTES, so the wall is asserted where it is now only reviewed.
close_reason: lib_auth.js holds requireMember/requireSupervisor/requireReporting; exam, intake, merge_animals, case_report, annual_report and stats all call it, and requireReportingAuth moved out of lib_stats.js. test_rules.py's guest sweep now parses routerAdd out of pb_hooks/*.pb.js and asserts every declared route gives a guest 403 and an anonymous caller 401 — /api/federfall/info the one named exemption. All 8 routes pass.

title: Cover the remaining cron jobs with run_cron.sh
description:
federfall-qt96.12 gave auditRetention a real test (tests/run_cron.sh + test_cron.py: patch the schedule to '* * * * *' in a copied pb_hooks, run a throwaway container, assert). Three cronAdd jobs are still never executed by any test:

- finder_retention.pb.js — the GDPR PII scrub and the deletion of finders no case references. This is the one that matters: if it silently stops running, the app's data-protection promise is broken and nothing says so. It also reads its window from org settings, i.e. through the getString()+JSON.parse trap that federfall-jumi already broke once.
- geocodeCachePurge
- idempotencyKeyPurge

Each is one sed line in run_cron.sh plus assertions in test_cron.py. Note a window measured in days cannot be reached by backdating (created/found_at autodates are server-owned) — either use a vanishingly small window as test_cron.py does, or seed a record whose driving date IS client-settable (finders' case dates are).

title: Audit: a diff shows 3 of N changes and nothing can reach the rest
description:
audit_labels.dart:454-465 renders '5 Felder geaendert' and then .take(3), and AuditEventTile (audit_screen.dart:264) is a ListTile with no onTap. The other two changes are UNREACHABLE, not merely unshown — on an append-only log that is the one item here I would call a correctness bug rather than polish.

The same missing surface is where everything else the log records but never shows belongs:
  - AuditFieldChange.truncated — parsed, never surfaced, so a value clamped at 500 chars renders as if it were complete
  - actor_role — snapshotted; 'Anna (Betreuerin)' beats 'Anna' on the security rows
  - user_agent — recorded on opt-in and parsed, while only ip is displayed
  - request_id — stored and indexed so the rows of one action can be read together; that has no UI at all
  - detail keys the renderer drops: DispositionDetail.currentAviary, CaseIntakeDetail.intakePhotos, ExamSavedDetail.created (create vs update), ReportExportedDetail.lang, animal.merged's field_choices

Fix: tap a row for a detail sheet — full change list, every fact, actor + role, ip/user agent when recorded, and the sibling rows of the same request_id.
acceptance_criteria: every recorded change is reachable; truncation is visible as truncation; the sheet shows actor role and (when recorded) user agent; request_id correlates to the other rows of the same action; AuditQuery gains a requestId filter.
close_reason: audit_detail_sheet.dart, opened by tapping a feed row. Shows every change (the line still summarises + take(3)), states truncation instead of implying completeness, names the actor's snapshotted role, shows user_agent beside ip, and reads back the request_id siblings — the correlation id finally has a surface. AuditQuery.requestId + PbAuditEventsRepository.forRequest() (list + 'created,id' sort: a handful of rows read as a sequence wants neither keyset paging nor newest-first). DispositionDetail.currentAviaryLabel now renders too. 5 sheet tests + 2 data-layer tests.

title: Audit: 20 recorded fields print their English column name in a German-first UI
description:
Cross-checking every field in lib_audit.js's CONTENT_FIELDS against auditFieldLabel's switch: 20 have no arm and fall through to the raw column name.

  markings: applied_at, removed_at · case_conditions: onset_date, resolved_date
  medications: started_at, ended_at · placements: moved_in_at, where_holding
  dispositions: release_type, transfer_type · exams: body_condition
  exam_findings: system · egg_records: laid_at, fate
  vet_appointments: attended_at, cancelled_at · quarantine_records: set_at
  active (aviaries + all five code lists)

So a release reads: 'Ausgang: Freigelassen · disposed_at: 04.08.2026 · release_type: soft'.

Falling back to the column name is the right SAFETY NET for a field nobody has translated yet — that stays. But these are the fields the allowlist deliberately picked as 'what this event was about', so every one of them should have a label. Reuse the existing arb keys where the app already names the field elsewhere rather than minting 20 new ones.
acceptance_criteria: no field in CONTENT_FIELDS renders as its column name; a test enumerates the allowlist and fails on any field without a translated label, so a future CONTENT_FIELDS entry cannot ship unlabelled.
close_reason: All 20 unlabelled fields named, reusing the existing arb key wherever the app already names the field (markingFieldApplied, conditionFieldOnset, medStarted, placementFieldMovedAt, dispositionFieldReleaseType, examBodyConditionLabel, eggFieldDate/Fate, aviaryFieldActive) plus 6 new keys de/en. The guard parses CONTENT_FIELDS out of lib_audit.js — 57 field entries across 22 collections — and fails on any that renders as its column name in either language, so a future allowlist entry cannot ship unlabelled.

title: Audit: field and value labels ignore their collection, so 'type' and 'status' collide
description:
auditFieldLabel (audit_labels.dart:191) and auditValueLabel (:239) both TAKE a collection parameter and never read it. Two collisions follow, and both produce text that is not merely unhelpful but wrong:

  - 'type' => auditFieldType = 'Ausgang', value resolved via DispositionType. For markings.type (a relation into marking_types) that renders 'Ausgang: 7x9k2m3...' — wrong label and an id.
  - 'status' resolves via CaseStatus only. exam_findings.status is FindingStatus (normal/abnormal), never matches, and falls back to the raw English wire value — even though findingStatusLabel already exists at cases_labels.dart:116.

Fix: match on (collection, field) before falling back to field alone. The parameter is already threaded through every call site.
acceptance_criteria: markings.type and dispositions.type get different labels; exam_findings.status renders through findingStatusLabel; a test pins each collision so the next shared column name cannot silently reintroduce it.
close_reason: Both label functions now match (collection, field) before falling back to field alone. markings.type -> markingFieldType 'Art' vs dispositions.type -> 'Ausgang'; exam_findings.status -> findingStatusLabel instead of CaseStatus (which never matched, leaving the English wire value on screen).

title: Audit log view: filter by date range
description:
AuditQuery already carries from/to and PbAuditEventsRepository.filterFor already binds them as a half-open UTC range (federfall-qt96.9, tested) — only the UI is missing.

Add a date-range control to AuditScreen next to the severity chips: presets (today / 7 days / 30 days) plus a custom range via showDateRangePicker, and a way back to unfiltered. The feed provider is keyed on AuditQuery, so changing the range already rebuilds the feed from the top with a fresh cursor — nothing in the paging needs to change.

Boundaries in the caller's local zone, converted to UTC by filterFor (a day boundary read in UTC would put a 23:30 event on the wrong day). ARB strings de + en.
close_reason:
Date-range filter in AuditScreen: Today / 7 days / 30 days presets plus a custom range via showDateRangePicker, alongside the severity chips. 3 widget tests; 773 app tests, analyze + format clean.

Only the UI was missing — AuditQuery.from/to and filterFor's half-open UTC binding already existed and were tested from qt96.9, and the feed provider is keyed on the query so changing the range rebuilds from the top with a fresh cursor by itself.

Two details: the picker returns whole DAYS, so the upper bound is the start of the day AFTER the chosen end or a 23:30 event falls outside its own range; and the picker's lastDate is today, since a log cannot contain the future and offering it would only mislead. The 'All' chip clears both filters at once.

Note for future tests here: the chip row scrolls horizontally and the later chips are off-screen at the default 800px test surface — ensureVisible before tapping.

title: Audit: record the disposition's derived flip, and stop rendering creates as diffs
description:
NARROWED (2026-08-04, after federfall-9k2g landed). As originally filed this asked for typed AuditDetail variants across the timeline kinds; 9k2g made most of that redundant by carrying the content in changes, which already renders. What is genuinely left:

(a) The derived flip is still recorded nowhere. main.pb.js's dispositions hook sets cases.status='disposed' and flips animals.lifetime_status / current_aviary, and the original design says a derived side effect belongs in the triggering action's detail — case.handoff does this via detail.carer_moved, disposition.created does not. Read the reconciled case+animal after e.next() (the model hook has run by then) and record the resulting statuses. The DELETE case is the interesting one: removing the last disposition reverts the case to in_care, and that reversal is invisible today. Needs one typed AuditDetail variant + rendering + ARB.

(b) A create currently renders as a diff: 'Ausgang erfasst — 2 Felder geändert: Ausgang: gesetzt auf Verstorben · Ausgang am: gesetzt auf 21.06.2026 09:00'. Accurate and clunky. A create is not a diff and should not read like one: when no change entry has BOTH a from and a to (i.e. it is create or delete content rather than an update), render each as a plain 'field: value' fact instead of a summary line.

DROPPED: typed variants for weight/condition/medication/administration/quarantine/placement — their content already renders from changes once (b) lands.
close_reason:
Narrowed as agreed and delivered: (a) refine() now reads the reconciled case+animal after e.next() and records case_status / lifetime_status / current_aviary in the disposition's detail, with a DispositionDetail variant + rendering + ARB; (b) auditLine renders create/delete content as plain 'field: value' facts instead of running it through the diff wording. 2 backend + 3 Dart assertions; 575 backend, 776 app, analyze + format clean.

refine() gained an app parameter and may now return {action: null} to enrich the detail without renaming the action — the disposition keeps its own action and only gains context.

The delete path is the one that mattered most and was invisible: removing the last disposition reopens the case, and nothing said so.

DROPPED as agreed: typed variants for weight/condition/medication/administration/quarantine/placement. Their content renders from  now that a create no longer reads as a diff.

comments.author: Jan-Henrik Bruhn
comments.text: Correction to the close note (shell ate a backticked word): the last line should read 'their content renders from the changes column now that a create no longer reads as a diff'.

title: Org settings are silently ignored: get() on a json field returns bytes, not an object
description:
PocketBase JSVM: record.get(<json field>) hands JS a types.JSONRaw, i.e. a BYTE ARRAY (constructor Array, indices as keys), not a decoded object. Property access therefore reads undefined and the code falls through to its default — silently, with no error anywhere. record.getString() returns the raw JSON text and JSON.parse()s fine. Verified on PB 0.39.8 with a probe hook against a live instance (2026-08-04, while implementing federfall-qt96.1, whose delete guard hit exactly this).

Two shipped, documented features are broken by it:

- pb_hooks/finder_retention.pb.js:70 — settings.finder_retention_years is always undefined, so the org-configurable GDPR retention window NEVER applies. Every org gets the hardcoded 2 years no matter what is configured.
- pb_hooks/main.pb.js:99 — settings.quarantineDefaultDays is always undefined, so the org-configurable quarantine default NEVER applies. Every org gets 14 days.

Fix is JSON.parse(org.getString('settings') || '{}') in both (see pb_hooks/audit.pb.js for the pattern + comment).

NOT affected, do not 'fix' these: intake.pb.js:90 and geocode.pb.js:110/254 pass get()'s value straight back to Go (e.json), and JSONRaw marshals correctly there — proven green by test_rules.py's 'replaying the key returns the ORIGINAL result'.

Both broken paths are cron/hook code that test_rules.py cannot reach directly, which is why this survived. Verify a fix the documented way: copy pb_hooks to a tempdir, rewrite the cron schedule to '* * * * *', run a throwaway container.
close_reason: Fixed in a48e1be + 1f588a4; verified live 2026-08-07 (run_cron.sh 13/13, run.sh 662/662). See comment.

comments.author: Jan-Henrik Bruhn
comments.text:
Worth fixing as a DEDUP, not two edits: the org-settings read exists five times — correct (JSON.parse(org.getString('settings') || '{}')) in audit.pb.js:68, audit.pb.js:165 and lib_audit.js:1148, broken (org.get('settings')) in finder_retention.pb.js:70 and main.pb.js:99. Both broken sites are the only two that were written without copying from a correct one.

Put it in a shared module instead — orgSettings(app, orgId) returning a decoded object (and {} for a missing org), alongside the lib_auth.js proposed in federfall-75sy — so the JSONRaw trap has exactly one place it can be got wrong. Then the fix is verified once, the documented way (tests/run_cron.sh against a rewritten schedule).

comments.author: Jan-Henrik Bruhn
comments.text:
Verified fixed against a live stack, 2026-08-07 — both halves, both suites green.

The dedup the previous comment asked for shipped in a48e1be (lib_org.js:
settingsOf/positiveNumber/flag) and 1f588a4. Both broken sites now read through
it: finder_retention.pb.js:77-88 and main.pb.js:98-103. audit.pb.js (x2) and
lib_audit.js:1144 were converted from their own correct copies, so the trap has
exactly one place left to be got wrong. intake.pb.js and geocode.pb.js are
deliberately still on get() — they marshal straight back to Go.

tests/run_cron.sh: 13 passed, 0 failed. It proves the decode per-org, not just
once: 'Scrub Now' (finderRetentionMonths 0.000001) was anonymised, 'Keep Long'
(1200) kept its PII, and 'Legacy Key' (finder_retention_years) still honours the
