tests/run.sh: 662 passed, 0 failed, covering the quarantine half — an org at 14
and an org at 15 days get different defaults (test_rules.py:3003/3009), which a
broken read could not produce.

title: Audit: supervisor-only audit screen + per-case activity section
description:
features/admin/audit/: audit_providers.dart (cursor-paging AsyncNotifier over AuditEventsRepository.page), entry from ManagementScreen (already supervisor-gated), filter chips by severity/action group/actor/date range.
Per-case: an Aktivitaet section on case detail filtered by case_id. Follow the unified-timeline styling rather than a new list idiom.
acceptance_criteria: flutter analyze clean, widget tests with mocktail-overridden repo providers, coverage stays above the 75% gate; a carer sees no entry point and the request 403s.
close_reason:
features/admin/audit/: audit_providers.dart (AuditFeed cursor-paging AsyncNotifier keyed on AuditQuery + caseActivityLog), audit_screen.dart (AuditScreen, AuditEventTile, CaseActivitySection), hub entry + /admin/audit route + repository provider, and the section wired into the case detail Overview. 8 widget tests; 762 app tests green, flutter analyze clean, coverage 78.9% (gate 75).

Decisions: severity is the only surfaced filter (it separates access/security from clinical work without knowing action names). CaseActivitySection renders SizedBox.shrink() — not an empty state — for non-supervisors AND on error, and the test pins both, including that a carer never even issues the request. loadMore() is a no-op while in flight or exhausted so the scroll listener can fire freely, and a failed append keeps the rows on screen rather than replacing them with an error.

EPIC COMPLETE (12/12).

title: Audit: rendering layer — audit_labels.dart + ARB (de/en)
description:
The renderer returns STRUCTURE, not a sentence: class AuditLine{title, subtitle?, facts, icon} built by auditLine(l10n, event) switching over the sealed detail.
Three lookup layers, each with a raw fallback so an unknown key degrades honestly instead of blank: auditActionTitle(l10n, action) (null -> l10n.auditActionUnknown(rawAction)); auditFieldLabel(l10n, collection, field); auditValueLabel(l10n, collection, field, wireValue) delegating to cases_labels.dart.
Actor has three render states: snapshot label / l10n.auditActorSystem when actor==null / l10n.auditActorDeleted(label) when the snapshot exists but the relation nullified.
German is primary. Run flutter gen-l10n after editing the arb files.
acceptance_criteria: A test over AuditAction.values asserts every action renders a non-empty AuditLine in de AND en; unknown action + unknown field + unknown enum value each render something readable.
close_reason:
lib/features/admin/audit/audit_labels.dart + 126 ARB strings per language (82 action titles, actor/severity/fact/change strings). 21 tests; flutter analyze clean.

The load-bearing test iterates AuditAction.values in BOTH languages and asserts every action renders a non-empty title from an event with no detail and no changes — the envelope-alone contract. A second test asserts de and en titles differ for most actions, which catches a copy-paste that left English German.

Three fallback layers, each degrading to the stored string rather than to blank: unknown action -> auditActionUnknown(raw), unknown field -> the column name, unknown enum value -> the wire string. A redacted change renders as 'geändert (Wert nicht protokolliert)' with no value and no arrow.

Note: auditLine needs both add() (label+value, skipped when empty) and flag() (the label IS the statement) — the first version silently dropped every label-only fact, including the failed-login window.

title: Audit: keyset paging on PbReadOnlyRepository + AuditEventsRepository + AuditQuery
description:
PbReadOnlyRepository.list() auto-paginates the WHOLE result set — wrong for a 10^5-row table. Add Future<PbPage<T>> page({filter, sort, perPage}) doing KEYSET paging (created < {:cursor}), not offsets: an append-only feed shifts under offset paging.
AuditEventsRepository extends PbReadOnlyRepository<AuditEvent> so a write is a compile error. AuditQuery (freezed: actor, actions, severity, caseId, subjectId, from, to) -> PbFilter via filterExpr with bound params (never string interpolation).
acceptance_criteria: page() returns a stable sequence while new rows are being inserted; AuditQuery covers every filter the UI offers; dart test green for federfall_data.
close_reason:
PbCursor/PbPage + PbReadOnlyRepository.page() (keyset), PbAuditEventsRepository (read-only by type — the collection has no write rules at all) and AuditQuery with filterFor(). 14 tests; data package green (143).

Keyset, not offsets, and the reason is correctness not speed: an append-only feed grows at the end being read from, so ?page=2 shows some rows twice and skips others. The cursor is (created, id) — created alone loses rows written in the same millisecond.

Two details worth remembering: page() fixes sort to '-created,-id' and does NOT accept a sort parameter (it must match the cursor or paging silently returns nonsense), and a fields projection always gets id+created added back or every cursor would be unbuildable.

title: Audit: collection-coverage test (the control replacing the catch-all)
description: Because emitters are hand-written, a newly added collection is silently unaudited. A test enumerates every non-view collection and asserts each is either covered by a registered emitter or listed in an explicit NOT_AUDITED allowlist (geocode_cache, idempotency_keys, audit_events itself, code lists...). Adding a collection then FAILS a test instead of going unlogged.
acceptance_criteria: Test passes on the current schema; adding a dummy collection makes it fail with a message naming the collection.
close_reason:
6 assertions in test_rules.py's [audit coverage] section (550 passed, 0 failed). Acceptance criterion verified for real: created a dummy_widgets collection on a live instance and the check reported 'unclassified: dummy_widgets'.

Key decision: the audited set is PARSED OUT OF pb_hooks/lib_audit.js, not mirrored in Python. A mirror would keep passing after someone removed a collection from the real map. Both parses have explicit guard assertions (>=15 collections, >=40 actions, >=25 schema collections, >=15 distinct emitted actions) so a broken regex fails loudly instead of passing vacuously.

Second half of the control:  is TEXT (no select validation), so the test also asserts every action the whole suite actually emitted exists in the registry — a typo'd action string would otherwise be stored and render as an unknown line forever.

NOT_AUDITED (with reasons, in the test): audit_events, geocode_cache, idempotency_keys, aviary_stays.

comments.author: Jan-Henrik Bruhn
comments.text: Typo in the close note above (shell ate a backticked word): it should read 'the action COLUMN is TEXT (no select validation)'.

title: Audit: export events + system/cron events
description:
Exports move data off-system, so they are logged even though reads are not: report.exported (annual — include year + format), case_report.printed, gdpr.export.
System tier (actor_kind=system, no actor): finder.pii_purged, finder.orphan_deleted, audit.purged, oauth2.user_provisioned, supervisor.bootstrapped.
acceptance_criteria: Both annual-report formats and the label print emit a row naming the format; the finder retention cron emits system-attributed rows.
close_reason:
Exports: report.exported (annual PDF + CSV, with year/lang/rows) and case_report.printed (pdf + receipt), emitted after the bytes exist so a failed render is not reported as an export. System: finder.pii_purged and finder.orphan_deleted from the retention cron, oauth2.user_provisioned, supervisor.bootstrapped. 6 new assertions in test_rules.py (544 passed, 0 failed).

The four paths test_rules.py cannot reach were verified live instead (copied pb_hooks to a tempdir with the cron rewritten to '* * * * *', DEFAULT_RETENTION_YEARS/ORPHAN_GRACE_MS zeroed, container started with FEDERFALL_SUPERVISOR_EMAIL): all four rows appeared with actor_kind system/cron, no actor, correct severity, and the finder rows carried an empty label. The orphan delete emits BEFORE tx removal — afterwards there is no org to file it under.

gdpr.export was REMOVED from the registry: the Datenauskunft does not exist yet (federfall-qocb). oauth2.user_provisioned is implemented but unverified end-to-end (no OAuth2 flow completes in the test stack).

Still unemitted and intentionally kept: audit.purged, which belongs to the retention cron in qt96.12.

title: Audit: auth + access/security events
description:
auth.login, auth.oauth2_login, auth.login_failed, auth.password_reset, auth.mfa_*; user.invited/role_changed/deactivated/deleted (hook into the existing guards in main.pb.js); case.shared / case.share_revoked. severity=security.

Two catches:
(a) A failed login for an UNKNOWN email has no org — log to the PB logger only, never an unauthenticated write into an org's table.
(b) A failed login for a KNOWN email is a log-flood vector and must be collapsed. CORRECTED APPROACH (the original 'increment detail.attempts' plan contradicted the append-only tamper guard in .1, which throws on EVERY update — and it cannot be a module-level counter either, since module state was measured to be per-JSVM and diverges under concurrency):
  - Emit AT MOST ONE auth.login_failed row per (actor, 5-minute bucket). Suppress the rest by first querying audit_events for an existing row with that action+actor since the bucket start (a read, always allowed; served by the (org, action, created) index).
  - The row's semantics are therefore 'at least one failed login in this window', carried explicitly as detail.window_minutes: 5 — NOT an exact count.
  - Add a separate auth.login_blocked (severity=security) when PB's own rate limiter trips, which is the signal a supervisor actually needs.
  - The tamper guard keeps NO carve-out for updates. That absoluteness is the point of it.
acceptance_criteria: Successful and failed logins land with severity=security; 20 rapid failures for one user produce one row with attempts=20; a failure for an unknown email produces no row.
close_reason:
pb_hooks/audit_auth.pb.js (login, oauth2 login, password reset) + users/case_shares via the generic Tier A hooks with refine() doing role_changed / deactivated / reactivated / mfa_enabled|disabled / password_changed / case.shared|share_revoked. DEFAULT_SEVERITY map added so an action's severity cannot differ by call site. 21 assertions; 538 passed, 0 failed.

Findings:
- MFA IS per-user here (users.mfa_enabled, migration 1700000032), so auth.mfa_* are reachable as a refined users.updated.
- auth.login_blocked REMOVED from the registry: PB's rate limiter answers 429 from middleware before any hook runs.
- Password changes are invisible in fieldsData() (no hash; only the rotated tokenKey, which an email change also rotates). Detected from the request body keys, passed to emitRecordChange as hints.bodyKeys.
- A wrong password is distinguished from an MFA challenge by calling e.record.validatePassword() BEFORE e.next() — both otherwise surface as a 401 from e.next().
- auth.oauth2_login is implemented but UNVERIFIED: no OAuth2 flow can complete in the test stack (same gap as federfall-8qz).
- Unrelated: case_shares.create requires shared_by = @request.auth.id; the old tests only ever created shares as superuser, so this was never exercised.

title: Audit: emitters for the custom routes (intake, merge_animals, exam)
description:
Custom routes use e.app.save() so request hooks never fire — each route emits ONE semantic event from INSIDE its existing transaction (atomic with the write, and a better description than five record.created rows: intake is one human action).
case.intake (animal+finder+case+weight+quarantine under one request_id), animal.merged, exam.recorded/updated. Note the idempotency replay path must NOT emit a second event.
acceptance_criteria: A real intake produces exactly one case.intake row with the right request_id and refs; a replayed idempotency key produces none; a rolled-back intake leaves no audit row.
close_reason:
Emitters added inside the existing transactions of intake.pb.js (case.intake), exam.pb.js (exam.saved) and merge_animals.pb.js (animal.merged), each with opts.app = tx so the event commits with the writes. 19 assertions; 517 passed, 0 failed.

Notes: the merge emit runs BEFORE tx.delete(duplicate) — the duplicate's id and label survive nowhere else. merge_animals had no test coverage at all before this, so the route itself is now exercised too. field_choices is rebuilt from the three known keys rather than passing raw client input, which could otherwise blow the json size limit and lose the event silently.

title: Audit: domain emitters for collection-API writes (tagged request hooks)
description:
Hand-written semantic events per audited collection — no untagged sweep. Pattern (RecordRequestEvent is the only place auth/IP exist):
  onRecordUpdateRequest((e) => { const before = e.record.original().fieldsData(); e.next(); audit.emit(e,'weight.updated',{changes:diff(before,e.record.fieldsData())}) }, 'weights');
e.next() FIRST so a failed save logs nothing; the audit row therefore lands after the domain commit and cannot roll it back (accepted — see emit()'s error swallowing).
Cover: cases (created/updated/status/deleted), weights, journal_entries, case_conditions, medications + medication_administrations, placements, dispositions, markings, quarantine_records, egg_records, exams, vet_appointments, aviaries, aviary_stays, animals, follow-ups.
Derived side effects (share-on-handoff, animals.lifetime_status flips) are NOT separate events — fold them into the triggering action's detail.
acceptance_criteria: Each listed collection emits a named action on create/update/delete with a correct case_id where applicable; every emitted action is in the registry; a failed save emits nothing.
close_reason:
pb_hooks/audit_domain.pb.js (3 generic handlers over lib_audit.js's COLLECTION_ACTIONS, 22 collections) + 34 assertions in test_rules.py (498 passed, 0 failed).

Deviations from the task list, both discovered by running it:
- aviary_stays is NOT audited: superuser-only rules, written exclusively by aviary_stays.pb.js from animals.current_aviary, so a request hook can never fire. Moving a bird is the animal.updated. AVIARY_STAY_* actions were removed from the registry — an unused action means an unused Dart enum value and ARB string.
- organisations WAS added (not on the list): supervisors change org settings (retention, quarantine defaults, audit_log_client_info) and that deserves a trace. Needed an emit() fix — an org has no 'org' field, so a superuser dashboard edit resolved no org and was silently dropped.
- exam_findings added with its own actions (the exam route writes them in-transaction, but the collection API is open).

Registry additions: case.created (a case created outside the intake route), placement.updated, finder.deleted, exam_finding.{created,updated,deleted}.

Also note: a hook-created row (quarantine_records on case create) never fires a request hook, so quarantine.set only appears if a client creates one directly.

title: [epic] Audit log — supervisor-only, structured event trail
description: Org-scoped, append-only audit log: every meaningful action, by whom, with metadata. Visible to supervisors ONLY. Events are stored as structured objects (stable action code + typed json payload + snapshot labels), never as pre-rendered strings — the app translates them via l10n. Decisions taken: (1) no bulk read logging, but exports ARE logged; (2) supervisors only for now; (3) hand-written semantic events only — no untagged catch-all sweep, with a collection-coverage test as the compensating control.
design:
# Audit log — design

Supervisor-only, org-scoped, append-only log of who did what, with metadata.

## 1. An event is an envelope + a typed detail — never a rendered string

```
AuditEvent
├── envelope   — always present, always renderable on its own
│   action, at, actor{id,label,role,kind}, subject{collection,id,label},
│   caseId, refs, severity, requestId, ip?, userAgent?
└── detail     — action-specific typed payload (json column)
    e.g. CaseHandoffDetail{from,to}  /  FieldChangesDetail{[{field,from,to}]}
```

HARD RULE (forward compatibility): the envelope alone must render a usable line;
`detail` only enriches. That is what makes "add a new action" ADDITIVE under the
repo's major-version wire contract — an older client seeing an unknown action
renders a generic envelope line instead of crashing, so new actions ship as
`feat:`, not `feat!:`.

## 2. Schema — collection `audit_events` (migration 1700000068_audit_log.js)

- `org`                relation → organisations, required, indexed (scoping boundary)
- `action`             TEXT, required. `domain.verb`, e.g. `case.handoff`.
                       Deliberately NOT a `select`: a hook emitting an unlisted
                       value would throw inside a domain transaction and turn a
                       legitimate write into a 400. Validity is enforced by a
                       registry constant + test instead.
- `actor`              relation → users, nullable, cascadeDelete:false
- `actor_label`,
  `actor_role`,
  `actor_kind`         TEXT snapshots. kind ∈ user|system|cron|superuser.
                       The relation nullifies when a user is deleted; the log
                       must still say who.
- `subject_collection`,
  `subject_id`,
  `subject_label`      TEXT — plain text, NOT relations. Supervisor deletes
                       cascade hard (cases.animal since 1700000057) and audit
                       rows must survive the thing they describe.
- `case_id`            TEXT, nullable, indexed — the one hot query
                       ("everything on this case") gets a real column
- `refs`               json — other ids {animal,user,aviary,disposition,…}
- `changes`            json — [{field,from,to}] kept out of `detail` so one
                       generic renderer handles all `*.updated` actions
- `detail`             json — the typed payload
- `severity`           TEXT info|notice|security — lets the UI filter
                       role/share/auth events out of the noise
- `ip`, `user_agent`   TEXT nullable — personal data, written ONLY when
                       `org.settings.auditLogClientInfo === true` (default off)
- `request_id`         TEXT — correlates the rows of one request (intake writes
                       several records under one id)
- `created`            autodate — the timestamp; sort key is (created, id)

Indexes: (org, created), (org, case_id, created), (org, actor, created),
(org, action, created).

### Two content rules, both non-negotiable

1. NO PII in labels or payloads. Finders are referenced by id only
   (`subject_label` for a finder is ""). Otherwise `finder_retention.pb.js`'s
   GDPR scrub is defeated by its own audit trail. Bird names are fine.
2. A per-collection sensitive-field list redacts VALUES, not the fact of change:
   `users.password`/`tokenKey`, `finders.*` identity/contact →
   `{field:"phone", redacted:true}` with no from/to. Emitters see raw request
   bodies, so this is where credentials would otherwise land.

## 3. Access rules ARE the append-only boundary

```js
const AUTH = '@request.auth.id != "" && @request.auth.is_active = true';
list/view: `${AUTH} && @request.auth.role = "supervisor"
            && org = @request.auth.org && @request.auth.role != "guest"`
create/update/delete: null   // superuser + hooks only
```

Hooks write via `e.app.save()`, which bypasses rules — so nulling all three
write rules costs nothing and makes the collection unwritable and unerasable
through the API. The redundant guest clause is there because `test_rules.py`'s
guest sweep looks for it. Supervisors only, decided; widening to coordinators
later tightens nothing, so it stays non-breaking either way.

Tamper guard in `pb_hooks/audit.pb.js` (defence in depth vs the Admin UI):

```js
onRecordUpdate((e) => { throw new BadRequestError("append-only") }, "audit_events");
onRecordDelete((e) => { /* allow only rows older than the retention floor */ }, "audit_events");
```

The delete guard checking the row's OWN age is what lets the retention cron work
without a bypass flag — JSVM isolation rules out a shared "I am the purger" store.

NON-GOAL (document in the migration header): no hash chain. It only detects
tampering by someone who already has the SQLite file, and doing it right needs
the `case_number` serialising write-lock trick on EVERY event.

## 4. Emission — hand-written semantic events only (decided)

No untagged catch-all. Every event is an explicit, named domain event emitted at
a known site. Better prose and no `record.updated` noise; the cost is that a new
collection is silently unaudited until someone writes the emitter — see the
coverage test in §7, which is the compensating control.

Emitter: `pb_hooks/lib_audit.js`, `require()`d INSIDE each handler
(`const audit = require(`${__hooks}/lib_audit.js`)`) — file-level scope does not
cross into handlers.

VERIFIED on PB 0.39.8 (throwaway container, 2026-08-04) — no fallback needed:
- `require` is available inside route handlers, cron handlers AND record model
  hooks; all three confirmed.
- The required module keeps its OWN file-level scope, so the SENSITIVE list and
  `diff()` can live at lib_audit.js file level even though a .pb.js cannot do that.
- Relative `require("./lib_audit.js")` fails (`GoError: Invalid module`) — the
  `${__hooks}` absolute form is mandatory.
- `lib_audit.js` is not `*.pb.js`, so PB does not load it as a hook file.
- MODULE STATE IS PER-JSVM, NOT GLOBAL: a module-level counter diverges under
  concurrent requests (PB pools VMs, each with its own module instance).
  => lib_audit.js MUST be stateless; never keep counters/dedup/caches in it.

`emit()` swallows its own errors into `$app.logger()`: an audit failure must
never turn a successful domain write into a 500.

### Tier A — collection-API writes: TAGGED request hooks, one per audited event

`RecordRequestEvent` is the only place `e.auth` / `e.requestInfo()` / `e.realIP()`
exist (model hooks get `RecordEvent`, which has no auth at all).

```js
onRecordUpdateRequest((e) => {
  const before = e.record.original().fieldsData();
  e.next();                                   // throws ⇒ nothing is logged
  audit.emit(e, "weight.updated", { changes: diff(before, e.record.fieldsData()) });
}, "weights");
```

`e.next()` first ⇒ no phantom events for failed saves. Trade-off: the audit row
lands after the domain commit, so it cannot roll it back (see `emit()` above).

### Tier B — custom routes

`intake`, `merge_animals`, `exam` never fire request hooks (they use
`e.app.save()`), so each emits ONE semantic event from inside its existing
transaction — atomic with the write, and a better description than five
`record.created` rows. Intake is one human action.

### Tier C — system paths

`finder.pii_purged`, `finder.orphan_deleted`, `audit.purged`,
`oauth2.user_provisioned`, `supervisor.bootstrapped` — actor_kind `system`,
no actor.

### Tier D — auth + access

`auth.login`, `auth.oauth2_login`, `auth.login_failed`, `auth.password_reset`,
`auth.mfa_*`, plus `user.role_changed` / `user.deactivated` from the existing
guards in `main.pb.js`, and `case.shared` / `case.share_revoked`.

Two catches:
- A failed login for an UNKNOWN email has no org ⇒ PB logger only, never an
  unauthenticated write into an org's table.
- A failed login for a KNOWN email is a flood vector ⇒ collapse it: AT MOST ONE
  row per (actor, 5-minute bucket), the surplus SUPPRESSED (query for an existing
  row since the bucket start — a read, always allowed).
  The row means "at least one failure in this window" (`detail.window_minutes`),
  NOT an exact count. Incrementing a counter on the row would need an UPDATE,
  which the append-only guard forbids — and module state cannot hold the count
  either (per-JSVM, diverges under concurrency). Exact counts are not what a
  supervisor needs; add `auth.login_blocked` (severity=security) for when PB's
  own rate limiter trips, which is the real signal.
  The tamper guard keeps NO update carve-out. That absoluteness is its point.

### Reads (decided)

No bulk read logging. DO log exports — they move data off-system:
`report.exported` (annual, incl. `format`), `case_report.printed`,
`gdpr.export`. Logging "supervisor opened the audit log" is a common compliance
ask and can be added later without a schema change.

### Derived side effects

NOT separate events. Share-on-handoff and `animals.lifetime_status` flips are
consequences of a human action and belong in that action's `detail`.

## 5. Dart model layer (`federfall_models`)

```dart
enum AuditAction {
  caseIntake('case.intake'), caseHandoff('case.handoff'),
  userRoleChanged('user.role_changed'), …;
  final String wire;
  static AuditAction? fromWire(Object? v) => pbEnum(values, (e) => e.wire, v);
}
enum AuditActorKind { user('user'), system('system'), cron('cron'), superuser('superuser') }
enum AuditSeverity  { info('info'), notice('notice'), security('security') }
```

`AuditEvent` (freezed) keeps BOTH `AuditAction? action` and `String rawAction`:
an unknown wire value is a normal state, not an error.

```dart
sealed class AuditDetail {
  static AuditDetail parse(AuditAction? a, Map<String, dynamic> json) => switch (a) { … };
}
final class FieldChangesDetail extends AuditDetail { final List<FieldChange> changes; }
final class CaseHandoffDetail  extends AuditDetail { final UserRef from, to; }
final class UnknownDetail      extends AuditDetail { final Map<String, dynamic> raw; }
```

`FieldChange.from/to` hold WIRE values — which is exactly why the enum `wire`
convention pays off: `CaseStatus.fromWire(change.to)` → `caseStatusLabel(l10n,…)`.

## 6. Data layer (`federfall_data`)

`AuditEventsRepository extends PbReadOnlyRepository<AuditEvent>` — a write is a
compile error (the read-only/mutable split already exists).

Two additions needed:
- `PbReadOnlyRepository.list()` auto-paginates the WHOLE result set — wrong for
  10^5 rows. Add `Future<PbPage<T>> page({filter, sort, perPage})` doing KEYSET
  paging (`created < {:cursor}`), not offsets: an append-only feed shifts under
  offset paging.
- `AuditQuery` (freezed: actor, actions, severity, caseId, subjectId, from, to)
  → `PbFilter` via `filterExpr` with bound params.

## 7. Coverage test (the control that replaces the catch-all)

A backend test enumerates every non-view collection and asserts each is either
covered by a registered emitter or listed in an explicit NOT_AUDITED allowlist
(`geocode_cache`, `idempotency_keys`, `audit_events` itself, code lists…).
Adding a collection then FAILS a test instead of silently going unlogged.

## 8. Rendering: objects → strings

The renderer returns structure, not a sentence, so the UI can lay it out:

```dart
class AuditLine { final String title; final String? subtitle;
                  final List<AuditFact> facts; final IconData icon; }
AuditLine auditLine(AppLocalizations l10n, AuditEvent e);  // switch over sealed detail
```

Three lookup layers, each with a raw-value fallback so an unknown key degrades
honestly instead of blank:

1. `auditActionTitle(l10n, action)` — exhaustive switch; null →
   `l10n.auditActionUnknown(rawAction)`
2. `auditFieldLabel(l10n, collection, field)` — "status" → „Status"
3. `auditValueLabel(l10n, collection, field, wireValue)` — delegates to
   `cases_labels.dart`

ARB, German primary:
`"auditCaseHandoff": "{actor} hat den Fall an {to} übergeben"`.

Actor rendering has three states: snapshot label; `l10n.auditActorSystem` when
`actor == null`; `l10n.auditActorDeleted(label)` when the snapshot exists but the
relation nullified.

## 9. App layer

`features/admin/audit/` — `audit_providers.dart` (cursor-paging `AsyncNotifier`),
entry from `ManagementScreen` (already supervisor-gated), plus an "Aktivität"
section on case detail filtered by `case_id`.

## 10. Retention & GDPR

`cronAdd("auditRetention", "30 3 * * *")` — `org.settings.audit_retention_days`,
default 730, `0` = keep forever.

- Audit rows are personal data about STAFF ⇒ they belong in the Datenauskunft
  export (federfall-qocb).
- Cron jobs are invisible to `test_rules.py`, so verify this one the documented
  way: copy `pb_hooks` to a tempdir, rewrite the schedule to `* * * * *`, run a
  throwaway container.

## 11. Testing

- `test_rules.py`: supervisor lists; carer + coordinator 403; create/update/delete
  rejected for every role; guest sweep; cross-org leak.
- Backend behaviour: a real intake produces exactly one `case.intake` row with
  the right `request_id`; a `users.password` change logs a redacted change with
  no values.
- Dart: `detail` parse round-trip per action; unknown-action fallback; a test
  over `AuditAction.values` asserting every one renders a non-empty `AuditLine`
  in `de` and `en`.

## 12. Wire-contract note

Additive throughout: a new collection, new hooks, a new read-only endpoint-free
surface. Ships as `feat:` — NOT breaking.
close_reason:
All 12 children complete. Delivered: migration 1700000068 (append-only, supervisor-only audit_events) + tamper guard + retention cron; lib_audit.js emitter with an 82-action registry; emitters across Tier A (22 collections, one generic handler per verb), Tier B (intake/exam/merge), Tier C (cron/system) and Tier D (auth, users, shares); the coverage test that fails when a new collection goes unaudited; the Dart model/data/rendering layers; and the supervisor screen plus per-case activity section.

Verification: backend 550 assertions (test_rules.py), models 107, data 143, app 762, coverage 78.9%, analyze clean, migration up/down/up clean. The four paths test_rules.py cannot reach (2 cron emitters, bootstrap, retention purge) were verified against throwaway containers with rewritten schedules.
