title: Case report PDF omits vet appointments and egg records
description:
`pb_hooks/case_report.pb.js` claims to mirror the app's case timeline ("Gather
everything the case timeline shows (mirrors CaseBundle.fromRecord /
case_timeline.dart's event list)") but two kinds the timeline renders never make
it into the PDF:

- **`vet_appointments`** (federfall-fnpo) — not gathered at all. A vet visit,
  its reason and, worse, its **outcome** (what the vet actually said) is exactly
  the kind of thing a report handed to the next carer or an authority is for.
  Case-scoped, so it is a plain `byCase("vet_appointments")`.
- **`egg_records`** (federfall-4agw) — not gathered at all. Animal-scoped (no
  `case` field on purpose), so it needs the `byAnimal` shape `markings` already
  uses: `findRecordsByFilter("egg_records", "animal = {:a}", …)` inside the
  existing `if (animalId)` block.

Both also need a `renderEvent` branch plus `kindTitle` entries in
`typst/report_common.typ` — in **both** the `de` and `en` string tables, or the
kind falls through to `S.kindTitle.at(e.kind, default: e.kind)` and prints the
raw collection-ish key with an empty detail.

## Shape

Mirror what the tiles show, no more:

- vet appointment: sort on `starts_at || created`; detail = vet · reason, the
  outcome set apart (it is a different fact from the reason — see
  `VetAppointmentTile`'s `_OutcomeBox`), and the resolution — attended,
  cancelled, or neither. An unresolved past appointment must not silently read
  as attended.
- egg record: sort on `laid_at || created`; detail = count, fertility, fate,
  attribution, notes. Enum values are `wire` strings, so they need `lbl()`
  tables like `S.hydration` etc., not raw passthrough. `attribution` other than
  `confirmed` matters — a "suspected" egg presented as fact is a data-quality
  claim the report should not make.
- Photos on egg records are out of scope; the report embeds one photo only.

## Acceptance

- A case with an appointment (with and without an outcome, attended /
  cancelled / open) and an egg record renders both in the chronology, in both
  locales, with no raw enum wire strings and no untranslated kind key.
- Verified against a running stack (the report route is a hook + typst render —
  the Flutter suite cannot cover it).
close_reason: Both kinds now gathered by case_report.pb.js and rendered by report_common.typ in de+en (PDF + receipt); egg records narrowed to the case window like eggsInCaseWindow; receipt grid fixed so a long kind title no longer overprints the date. Verified against a running stack, plus new assertions in tests/test_rules.py.

title: Promote first intake photo to animals.photo and drop the avatar fallback
description:
The animal header avatar is not one field, and the two it can resolve to have
different access scopes — so whether a bird has a visible portrait depends on
who is looking.

`pickAvatarSource` (`apps/federfall/lib/features/animals/animals_providers.dart:85-104`)
returns `animals.photo` when set, else the first `intake_photos` entry of the
newest case that has one. The candidate list comes from `casesForAnimal` →
the rule-filtered `cases` list endpoint, and `cases.intake_photos` is
case-scoped (active_carer / coordinator / supervisor / share —
`1700000010_access_rules.js:93-105`), while `animals.photo` is org-wide
readable identity-layer data (`:63-72`, protected-file gate resolves against
the *animals* viewRule — proven by `test_rules.py:717-719`, where the
outsider carer `d` who is denied the case at `:407-409` still gets the photo).

Result: a carer with no case on the bird sees a placeholder where a carer on
the case sees a photo. Confusing in the org-wide animal list, and it makes
re-identification (the reason the identity layer is org-wide at all) worse
exactly for the person who has no case yet.

## Fix

Promote the first intake photo to `animals.photo` at intake when the animal
has none, then delete the fallback path.

- `pb_hooks/intake.pb.js` already holds the uploaded files
  (`findUploadedFiles("intake_photos")`, ~line 59-61) and creates or loads the
  animal in the same transaction (~104-119), setting `intake_photos` at ~151.
  Set `photo` on the animal in that same tx when it is empty — covers both the
  new-animal and existing-animal (re-identification) branches.
- Only fill when empty: never overwrite a portrait a user chose, and never
  re-promote on a later case (the wizard has an explicit set/replace/remove
  flow in `animal_avatar.dart`).
- Then drop `pickAvatarSource` / `AvatarSource` / `AvatarCollection` and
  collapse `_avatarUrl` to read `animals.photo` only. Tests to update:
  `test/features/animals/animals_providers_test.dart:42-73`.

## Open questions / risks

- **File copy in the JSVM.** The uploaded `File` objects are being saved onto
  the `cases` record; reusing the same objects for a second `tx.save` on the
  animal needs verifying against the running stack (PB should store a second
  copy under its own generated name, but confirm — a shared filename across
  two collections would be a deletion hazard). Fallback: re-read the stored
  case file and build a new upload via `$filesystem`.
- **Backfill.** Existing animals with no `photo` but with case intake photos
  will keep showing a placeholder once the fallback is gone — that is a
  *regression* for the carer who could see it before. Needs a migration that
  copies the newest case's first intake photo into `animals.photo` for every
  animal where it is empty.
- **Privacy check.** This deliberately widens one clinical photo per bird from
  case-scoped to org-wide. That is the point (it becomes identity data), but it
  should be a conscious decision, and the intake wizard copy may want to say
  so. Alternative if not acceptable: keep the fallback and instead prompt for a
  separate portrait at intake.
- Wire contract: not breaking. No request/response shape changes, no removed
  field, no rule tightening — `animals.photo` is already an optional field the
  app writes.

## Verification

- `backend/pocketbase/tests/test_rules.py` via `run.sh` against a live stack:
  outsider carer `d` sees a portrait for a bird whose only photo came in via
  intake.
- `flutter analyze` clean, `flutter test` green, coverage ≥ 75%.
notes: Privacy scope clarified: the exposure is the FINDER, not the bird. 1700000027's comment names 'patient and finder-linked photos' — an intake photo is often shot at handover and can carry the finder's hands/home/car/house number, while finders' PII is otherwise case-gated (1700000010:118-124). Promoting one such photo to the org-wide identity layer widens that by one image per bird. Judged acceptable, with two cheap mitigations: intake should nudge for a bird-only portrait, and the existing set/replace/remove flow in animal_avatar.dart lets anyone swap out a photo with a person in it.
close_reason: Closed

title: Vet appointments per case (Today card + configurable-lead reminders)
description:
Carers currently have no place to record that a bird has a **vet appointment** on
a specific date and time. The closest thing is `follow_ups`, but that is a
date-only, self-owned recheck ("look at the wound Thursday") — it has no vet or
clinic, no time-of-day semantics, and no separation between what was planned and
what came out of the visit. Conflating the two would make the worklist unable to
tell "I should check the bird" from "be at Dr. X at 14:30".

So: a new per-case timeline record for vet appointments, surfaced on the Today
card, with an on-device reminder fired a user-configurable interval *before* the
appointment.

## Scope

**Backend — new `vet_appointments` collection** (new numbered migration, next
free number after `1700000063`; never hand-edit an existing one):

- `case` (relation -> `cases`, required, `cascadeDelete: true`)
- `starts_at` (date, required) — an instant, not a day; the UI shows date + time
- `vet` (text) — practice / vet name, free text (no clinics collection yet)
- `reason` (text, max 2000) — why the appointment was made
- `outcome` (text, max 2000) — filled in *after* the visit; this is the
  "add notes afterwards" requirement
- `attended_at` (date, optional) — the done-stamp, mirroring
  `follow_ups.done_at`; set when the carer marks the appointment as kept
- `cancelled_at` (date, optional) — appointments do get cancelled, and that is
  not the same as "not yet attended"; the worklist must stop nagging
- `created_by` (relation -> `users`), `org` (relation -> `organisations`),
  `created`/`updated` autodates

Access rules: copy the case-scoped `childView` / `childEdit` predicates from
`1700000023_follow_ups.js` verbatim (carer / coordinators+supervisors / shared
for read; carer / supervisor / edit-shared for write). They already include the
guest-safe `is_active` form. Self-contained migration — resolve every collection
with `findCollectionByNameOrId` inside `migrate()`.

This is case-scoped with no `animals` relation, so `animal_org_scope.pb.js`
needs no change.

**Models / data:**

- `packages/federfall_models`: `VetAppointment` freezed model + `fromRecord`
  mapper. No enums needed unless the outcome gets categorised (it should not
  for v1).
- `packages/federfall_data`: `VetAppointmentRepository extends PbRepository<…>`
  in the usual shape, plus a provider in
  `apps/federfall/lib/data/repository_providers.dart`.

**Case timeline (follow the established pattern):** new folder
`apps/federfall/lib/features/cases/vet_appointments/` with
`vet_appointments_providers.dart`, `showVetAppointmentSheet()` in
`vet_appointment_sheet.dart` (create + edit), and `vet_appointment_tile.dart`
built on the shared `TimelineItem`; a sealed `_Event` subclass in
`case_timeline.dart`; an entry in `add_entry_sheet.dart`. Mirror
`features/cases/follow_ups/` — it is the closest analogue.

The sheet needs two modes, because the record is written twice: *before* the
visit (starts_at / vet / reason) and *after* (outcome + mark attended, or
cancel). The tile should offer "Termin wahrgenommen" / "Notiz ergänzen" /
"Abgesagt" actions inline rather than making the carer reopen a full editor.

**Worklist / Today card:**

- New `WorklistKind.vetAppointment` in
  `apps/federfall/lib/features/worklist/worklist.dart`, produced in
  `buildWorklist()` from the case's upcoming appointments, with a label in
  `worklist_labels.dart` and an icon in `worklist_tile.dart`.
- Severity: `overdue` once `starts_at` has passed with no `attended_at` /
  `cancelled_at`, `upcoming` before that. Skip anything attended or cancelled.
- Because appointments are timed, the Today window has to include *today's
  later* appointments, not just things already due — check how the existing
  kinds bound their window in `buildWorklist()` and keep it consistent rather
  than inventing a second notion of "today".
- Feeding this needs the appointments in whatever the worklist provider already
  fetches (`worklist_providers.dart`); a server-side view like
  `medication_due` is *not* required — `starts_at` is a plain stored instant, no
  computation.
- Live-sync: subscribe/invalidate the leaf provider that actually fetches the
  appointments, not the worklist parent (see the
  `live-sync-invalidate-leaf-not-parent` memory).

**Reminders (`features/reminders/`)** — the medication reminder machinery is
already there and is exactly the right seam:

- Extend `reminder_plan.dart` with `planVetAppointmentReminders()` alongside
  `planMedicationReminders()`. Same rules: only schedule instants in the
  *future*, one stable id per appointment via `reminderNotificationId(id)`
  (FNV-1a over the record id — do not use `String.hashCode`), payload =
  `AppRoutes.caseDetail(caseId)`.
- The scheduler is `replaceAll`-style (reconcile the whole desired set), so the
  vet reminders must be planned into the **same** `replaceAll` call as the
  medication ones — planning them separately would have each wipe the other's
  notifications. That is the main trap in this issue.
- **Configurable lead time:** new setting next to `MedicationRemindersEnabled`
  in `reminder_settings.dart` (`SharedPreferences`, per device — reminders are
  scheduled on-device, so the preference is too). A `Duration` chosen from a
  small set of offsets (e.g. 1 h / 3 h / 12 h / 1 day / 2 days), default 1 day.
  Fire time = `starts_at - lead`; if that instant is already past, skip
  (consistent with the existing "don't nag about the past" rule).
- Expose the toggle + lead-time picker in `features/profile/profile_screen.dart`
  where the medication reminder toggle already lives. Enabling is the moment to
  request the OS permission.
- Web gets `NoopReminderScheduler` for free.

**l10n:** every string in `app_en.arb` + `app_de.arb` (German is primary), then
`flutter gen-l10n`. Label helper for the new worklist kind in
`worklist_labels.dart`.

## Wire contract

Additive only — a new collection, no changed request/response shapes. **Not** a
breaking change, so a plain `feat:` commit. Nothing an older client reads is
removed or made required.

## Acceptance

- A carer can add a vet appointment to a case (date + time, vet, reason), see it
  in the case chronology, and add an outcome note after the visit.
- Upcoming and missed appointments appear on the Today card and the Today
  screen; attended/cancelled ones do not.
- With reminders enabled, an OS notification fires the configured interval
  before the appointment and opens the case on tap; medication reminders still
  work (i.e. `replaceAll` was not split).
- Rule tests in `backend/pocketbase/tests/test_rules.py` cover the new
  collection, including the guest sweep; verified against a live stack (restart
  the dev stack after adding the migration — see
  `pb-migration-restart-dev-stack`).
- `dart format` clean, `flutter analyze` clean, `flutter test` green, coverage
  still above the CI gate; `dart test`/`dart analyze` green in both touched
  packages.

## Explicitly out of scope

System-calendar export (ICS / "add to calendar") — filed separately as a
follow-up.
close_reason: Shipped in c1b09af (collection + model + repo + timeline sheet/tile + Today card + reminders with configurable lead), b5ceeab (calendar export, federfall-v3a8) and 2889c55 (case report). Re-closing: the original close (dolt bq1pofaj, 2026-08-03 13:36) was clobbered at 13:42 when a 'git pull --rebase' checked out origin/main, rewrote .beads/issues.jsonl to the pre-close version and auto-import folded that stale row back into the DB.

title: Serve map tile configuration from /api/federfall/info at runtime
description:
Map source is currently **build-time only**: `MAP_MODE` / `MAP_TILE_URL` /
`MAP_STYLE_URL` / `MAP_ATTRIBUTION` are `String.fromEnvironment` constants in
`apps/federfall/lib/config/app_environment.dart:47-83`, baked into the web
bundle by `Dockerfile:75-78` (`--dart-define-from-file=dart_defines/production.json`)
and into the APK at `flutter build apk` time.

A self-hoster running the published `ghcr.io` image therefore cannot switch to
a raster / self-hosted tile server at all — they must fork and rebuild the
image. The only runtime knob today is `FEDERFALL_MAP_TILE_ORIGINS`, which is
purely the CSP allowlist in `pb_hooks/web_headers.pb.js:100` and does not
change which tiles the app requests.

Intent was always for the server to prescribe this at runtime via the info
endpoint.
design:
Additive, fail-open — mirrors how version/auth discovery already works.

**Server (`pb_hooks/info.pb.js`)** — add an optional `map` block, omitted
entirely when no `FEDERFALL_MAP_*` env is set:

    map: { mode, tileUrl, styleUrl, attribution, attributionUrl }

from `FEDERFALL_MAP_MODE` / `_TILE_URL` / `_STYLE_URL` / `_ATTRIBUTION` /
`_ATTRIBUTION_URL`. Endpoint is unauthenticated, but tile URLs are not secret.
Keep the existing defensive style: a bad/missing value must never 500 `/info`.
Remember the JSVM isolation gotcha — define helpers inside the handler.

**App** — extend `ServerInfo` (`lib/core/server/server_info.dart`) with an
optional `ServerMapConfig` in `tryParse`, then resolve at the map widgets as
`serverInfo?.map?.x ?? AppEnvironment.x`. `serverInfoProvider` is already
`keepAlive` and awaited by the router gate before login, so the value is in
hand before any map builds. Dart defines stay as the fallback: an older server
that omits `map` behaves exactly as today.

**Wire contract:** additive optional field + client-side fallback ⇒ NOT
breaking. Do not use `feat!`/`BREAKING CHANGE` (see CLAUDE.md — a major bump
forces every user to update for nothing).

Two things to get right:

1. **CSP coupling (the real catch).** On web a server-prescribed tile URL is
   still blocked unless its origin is in the policy `web_headers.pb.js` sends.
   Requiring the operator to set both `FEDERFALL_MAP_TILE_URL` and
   `FEDERFALL_MAP_TILE_ORIGINS` consistently just relocates the footgun —
   derive the CSP origins from the configured map URLs, and keep
   `FEDERFALL_MAP_TILE_ORIGINS` as an additive escape hatch (sprite/glyph
   hosts on another origin). Native apps have no CSP and just take the value.
2. **Attribution must travel with the URL**, not stay a define — a server
   pointed at a commercial provider that still renders OSM attribution is a
   licensing problem.

**Open question to check before coding:** the raster-vs-vector switch is read
at widget-build time via `AppEnvironment.mapMode`. Verify whether the map
widget can flip modes reactively (vector goes through `vector_map_tiles`,
raster through plain flutter_map tile layers) or whether a mode change needs a
full rebuild/restart of the map subtree.
acceptance_criteria:
- FEDERFALL_MAP_MODE=raster + FEDERFALL_MAP_TILE_URL on the stock ghcr.io image switches the web SPA to raster tiles with no rebuild
- The same works on the Android app against that server
- Tiles actually render on web: CSP from web_headers.pb.js permits the configured origin without setting FEDERFALL_MAP_TILE_ORIGINS separately
- Attribution shown matches the server-configured provider
- A server with no FEDERFALL_MAP_* env, and an older server with no `map` key in /info, both fall back to the dart-define defaults (vector/OpenFreeMap)
- Commit is non-breaking (no major bump); backend/pocketbase/tests/test_rules.py CSP assertions updated
- flutter analyze clean, flutter test green, dart format clean
close_reason: Implemented in 908e20c. /api/federfall/info serves an optional all-or-nothing map block (mode + URL + attribution, plus optional attributionUrl/apiKey); the app resolves it through MapConfig/mapConfigProvider with the dart-defines as fallback. CSP origins are derived from the same FEDERFALL_MAP_* URLs in web_headers.pb.js, so TILE_ORIGINS is no longer something the operator has to keep in sync. Verified: 372/372 backend rule tests (new /info map + CSP derivation assertions), 658 app tests, analyze clean, coverage 79.68%. Non-breaking (feat:). Open question in the ticket answered: the vector path DID need a keyed rebuild — StyleReader reads the style in initState, so MapTileLayer is keyed on the resolved config and swaps when /info lands (the router only awaits serverInfo on the unauthenticated path, so a warm start can beat it). Key-secrecy follow-up: federfall-msb6.

title: condition_labels view: server-side diagnosis vocabulary + breakdown counts
description:
The case browser's diagnosis filter is populated from the `conditions` code
list, so a diagnosis recorded as free text (`case_conditions.free_text`) is
not offerable — and the statistics condition breakdown still aggregates the
whole `case_conditions` collection on the device (the second half of
federfall-80tc).

Add a `condition_labels` view collection, following the `animal_species`
precedent (1700000042), which solves the same free-text-vocabulary problem
for species:

    SELECT MIN(cc.id) AS id, cc.org AS org,
           COALESCE(c.label, cc.free_text) AS label,
           MAX(cc.condition) AS condition,
           COUNT(DISTINCT cc.`case`) AS case_count
    FROM case_conditions cc
    LEFT JOIN conditions c ON c.id = cc.condition
    GROUP BY cc.org, label

Access rule is the crux and does NOT inherit animal_species' reasoning.
That view is justified by "animals are already org-wide readable"; here
`case_conditions` is not — its list rule is the childView predicate. The
code-list half of the labels leaks nothing (`conditions` is already
org-readable), but free text is user-typed prose on a specific case. So
gate the free-text rows by role:

    AUTH && org = @request.auth.org && (condition != "" || COORD_SUP)

Carers therefore get the recorded code-list vocabulary (no dead options);
coordinators/supervisors additionally get the free-text tail.

Then repoint statistics' byCondition at case_count instead of aggregating
case_conditions client-side. Counts are org-wide, which is correct because
the statistics screen is coordinator/supervisor-only (canViewReports) —
but that coupling must be documented at the provider.

Caveats: free text does not dedup ("Katzenbiss" vs "katzenbiss" vs
"Katzenbiss li. Flügel" are three rows) — sort by frequency, don't pretend
to merge. Needs test_rules.py coverage including the guest sweep, verified
against a live stack (run.sh); the Flutter suite cannot cover it.
close_reason: condition_labels view added (1700000062) with free-text rows role-gated via (condition != '' || COORD_SUP). Filter dropdown reads it; statistics byCondition reads case_count instead of aggregating case_conditions client-side. 8 new assertions in test_rules.py, all 345 pass against a live PB.

title: Placement's location fields: one duplicates the carer, one borrows "Voliere" for something that can never be one
description:
The placement sheet (`features/cases/placements/placement_sheet.dart`) offers
three free-text location fields above the comments:

- `placementFieldWhere` "Untergebracht bei" (`where_holding`)
- `placementFieldEnclosure` "Voliere / Gehege" (`enclosure`)
- `placementFieldArea` "Bereich" (`area`)

**1. "Untergebracht bei" duplicates the carer relation on the same form.**
Since federfall-0se6 the carer dropdown is always visible, one field above it.
A typed relation and a free-text restatement of the same fact, adjacent.

**2. "Voliere / Gehege" names something a placement can never refer to.**
An animal in an org aviary is not in an open case: `placed_in_aviary` is a
*disposition*, and `pb_hooks/main.pb.js:129-161` closes the case, sets
`lifetime_status = in_aviary` and sets `animals.current_aviary` from
`disposition.aviary` — "a resident that later falls ill gets a NEW case rather
than reopening this one". `aviary_stays` (and every flock list / occupancy
count) derives from `current_aviary` through
`pb_hooks/aviary_stays.pb.js`.

So the two states are deliberately separate: in care = with a carer, tracked by
placements; in an aviary = a resident, case closed. The placement form's label
invites the user to type the one thing this record must never mean, in prose
that nothing can read, while the app's real `aviaries` registry sits one tab
away. It reads as a broken integration, but the integration is not supposed to
exist — the label is simply wrong.

The field's honest purpose is where the bird sits *at the carer's place*: a box,
a cage, a room.

Proposed fix (UI + l10n only, no migration):

- Drop `where_holding` from the form. The carer relation answers it. Keep the
  column so existing rows still render in `placement_tile.dart`.
- Relabel `enclosure` to say what it is — a container at a carer's place
  ("Käfig / Box"), with the word "Voliere" gone.
- Decide whether `area` ("Bereich") earns a second free-text level of location
  granularity at a carer's home, or whether one "Wo genau" field replaces both
  (keeping `area` rendered by the tile for legacy rows).

Found while merging the placement/handoff kinds (federfall-0se6). An earlier
version of this issue claimed case birds could never reach an aviary; that was
wrong — the disposition path does it.
close_reason: Closed

title: Destructive confirm buttons are distinguished from Cancel by colour alone
description:
Both confirmation dialogs put the destructive action and Cancel side by side as
identical `TextButton`s:

- `_DestructiveDialog` (`features/animals/delete_record_dialogs.dart:195-207`) —
  Cancel and the confirm differ only in `foregroundColor: theme.colorScheme.error`.
- `confirmAndDelete` (`core/error/quick_action.dart:40-56`) — the generic
  confirm-then-delete used by every timeline tile, the code lists and the animal
  merge. Here the confirm gets **no** colour treatment at all, so the only thing
  separating "Cancel" from "Delete permanently" is the label text.

Consequences:

- **Colour-only meaning** (WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.1) on the most dangerous controls in
  the app. Red/green colour vision deficiency affects roughly 8% of men, and
  `_DestructiveDialog` guards a cascade that destroys an animal, all of its
  cases, and their entire timelines.
- **No weight difference** means the squint test gives the two buttons equal
  prominence, on a dialog whose whole purpose is to make the user stop.

Fix: give the destructive action a filled treatment
(`FilledButton` with `colorScheme.error` / `onError`) against a plain
`TextButton` Cancel, so shape and weight carry the distinction and colour is
redundant rather than load-bearing. Apply to both dialogs so the pattern is
consistent, and consider adding a leading `Icons.delete_forever` to the confirm
in `_DestructiveDialog` for the cascade case.

Source: general design review (accessibility / error prevention).
close_reason: DestructiveActionButton carries the treatment in one place: filled error/onError so shape+weight distinguish it from Cancel, plus delete_forever on the cascade deletes. New 'demoted' outlined mode keeps the code-list 'Deactivate instead' as the primary. Applied to both named call sites plus six more hand-rolled dialogs with the same defect. Commit 237e986.

title: iOS Info.plist still lists 'es' in CFBundleLocalizations
description: apps/federfall/ios/Runner/Info.plist declares CFBundleLocalizations as [en, es] — leftover from the Very Good CLI scaffold. The app ships en + de (lib/l10n/arb/app_en.arb, app_de.arb) and its UI is locale-locked to German (lib/app/view/app.dart:33). iOS uses this list for locale negotiation, so German may not be offered//reported correctly on iOS. Replace 'es' with 'de'. Found during the 2026-07-26 documentation audit; the (now deleted) apps/federfall/README.md was the only doc describing this step.
close_reason: Fixed: CFBundleLocalizations is now [de, en] (the scaffold's 'es' is gone). Also set the Xcode project's developmentRegion/knownRegions to de — NSLocale.preferredLanguages filters against the bundle's localizations and falls back to the development language, so with region=en an iOS device set to a language we do not ship would have reported 'en' and the app would have come up English, contradicting kFallbackLocale=de established in federfall-qdsa. Info.plist validated as parseable; the iOS build itself is unverified (no macOS/Xcode available here). Note the issue text's 'UI is locale-locked to German' is stale as of federfall-qdsa.

title: CSV export: no progress feedback, and it loads three full collections on-device
description:
Two problems in `_exportCsv` (`features/statistics/statistics_screen.dart:132`).

**No progress affordance.** The export button only greys out while `_exporting`
is true. Its two siblings for the same class of action — fetch something from
the server and hand it to the share sheet — swap their icon for an inline
spinner: `_ShareReportButton` and `_PrintReportButton`
(`features/cases/case_detail_screen.dart:152` and `:241`). So the app has an
established busy affordance for exactly this and the CSV button does not use it.
On a slow link the user sees a dead icon and no indication anything is happening.

**It pulls the whole org to the phone.** The method calls `animalsRepo.list()`,
`casesRepo.list()` and `dispositionsRepo.list()` unpaginated, then builds the
CSV client-side. For a long-running org that is three full-collection fetches
and the whole join held in memory on a handset. The infrastructure to avoid this
already exists — `pb_hooks/case_report.pb.js` renders PDFs server-side.

Fix: (a) give the icon the same inline spinner as its two siblings; (b) move the
CSV assembly behind a hook endpoint alongside the existing report renderer,
keeping `buildCaseReportRows`/`encodeCaseReportCsv` as the tested pure core, or
at minimum paginate the three reads.

Source: Dieter Rams design review (principle 8 thorough / 9 efficient).
close_reason: CSV export now reads the pre-joined case_report_rows view (one small row set) and the button shows the inline spinner its sibling share/print actions use.

title: Statistics intake-map preview drops tile attribution
description:
`_MapPreview` (`features/statistics/statistics_screen.dart:346`) renders a
`MapTileLayer` with no `MapAttribution`. The doc comment makes it a deliberate
design call: attribution "belongs on the interactive intake map screen this card
links to, not on a thumbnail too small to make it legible".

Two problems with that reasoning:

1. **Inconsistent.** The case detail's `_FindMap`
   (`features/cases/case_detail_screen.dart:787`) is also a small, static,
   non-interactive preview and it *does* include `const MapAttribution()`. Two
   thumbnails, same role, one attributed.
2. **Probably not ours to decide.** Tile attribution is generally a condition of
   the tile licence (OpenFreeMap / OSM data), not a styling preference. "Too
   small to be legible" is an argument for a smaller preview or a link, not for
   dropping the notice.

Fix: either add `MapAttribution` to `_MapPreview` (matching `_FindMap`), or
confirm against the configured tile provider's terms that a linked-through
thumbnail is covered and record that finding in the comment so it does not read
as an aesthetic choice.

Source: Dieter Rams design review (principle 6 honest / 8 thorough).
close_reason: MapAttribution added to _MapPreview; the 'too small for attribution' comment replaced with the licence rationale. Test that asserted its absence was vacuous (empty stats never build the preview) — replaced with one that pumps a location.

title: Unify the two KPI tile designs (dashboard vs statistics)
description:
The same object — a metric tile — is drawn two different ways:

`features/dashboard/dashboard_screen.dart:264` `_KpiCard`
- `displaySmall` + `FontWeight.w600` + `FontFeature.tabularFigures()` + `height: 1`
- an `_IconChip` tonal square, a `labelLarge` onSurfaceVariant label, a chevron
- tappable (seeds a `CaseQuery` or switches tab)
- width from a `LayoutBuilder` — half the available space

`features/statistics/statistics_screen.dart:202` `_Kpi`
- `headlineMedium`, no weight override, no tabular figures
- no icon, `bodyMedium` label at full contrast, no chevron
- not tappable
- `SizedBox(width: 160)` — a hardcoded magic number, not an `AppSpacing` token

The dashboard version is the better one and is clearly the considered design.
The statistics version also has a concrete layout bug in the fixed 160 px width:
German stat labels are long ("Durchschnittliche Verweildauer") and the box does
not respond to text scale, so the text wraps or overflows where the dashboard's
responsive tile would not.

Fix: extract the dashboard's `_KpiCard` into `ui/widgets/` as a shared
`KpiCard` (tap optional), and use it in both places. That fixes the fixed-width
bug as a side effect.

Source: Dieter Rams design review (principle 3 aesthetic / 7 long-lasting —
one system, not two).
close_reason: Fixed: extracted the dashboard's considered design into shared lib/ui/widgets/kpi_card.dart (KpiCard + KpiGrid) and lib/ui/widgets/icon_chip.dart, now used by both the dashboard and the statistics screen. The chevron follows onTap, so the non-tappable statistics tiles no longer promise a destination. The fixed SizedBox(width: 160) is gone — KpiGrid derives width from constraints, so long German labels at large text scales get room to wrap.

title: Intake wizard loses everything if the app is killed mid-form
description:
`NewCaseScreen` (`features/cases/new_case_screen.dart`) is the biggest form in
the app: three steps, roughly twenty fields, staged photos, optional finder PII.
`DiscardGuard` correctly prompts on a back gesture while dirty, and
`_idempotencyKey` (line 114) makes a *resubmit* safe.

Neither protects the compose phase. The app is online-only with no local cache,
and all wizard state is plain `State` fields on the widget. An incoming phone
call, an OS low-memory eviction, or a crash between step 0 and Save loses the
whole intake — which is exactly the field scenario: a phone in one hand and a
bird in the other, in a rehab centre.

Fix: persist the wizard's in-progress values (and the staged photo paths) to
local storage on change, keyed to the `_idempotencyKey` that already identifies
this attempt, and offer to restore on re-entry. Clear it on successful submit or
on an explicit discard. Note the photos are `XFile`s from the picker — the paths
survive, the bytes should not need copying.

Source: Dieter Rams design review (principle 2 useful / 8 thorough).
close_reason: Implemented: CaseIntakeDraft + platform-selected store, debounced autosave with a lifecycle flush, explicit restore prompt (24h staleness), cleared on commit/discard. Draft adopts the idempotency key so a crash mid-submit replays instead of duplicating. Native = keychain/keystore (holds finder PII); web = localStorage with the finder PII and blob: photo paths dropped and the draft flagged partial so the prompt says so. Staged photo paths are reopened on restore (StagedPhotoLoader, injectable) and vanished ones reported. 35 tests in new_case_screen_test.dart + case_intake_draft_test.dart (100% line cov) + case_intake_draft_store_test.dart.

comments.author: Jan-Henrik Bruhn
comments.text: Reversed the finder-PII decision at the owner's request: the draft now carries the finder's contact details on ALL platforms, web included. `forPlaintextStore()` became `withoutPhotoPaths()` — the web store's only reduction is the staged photo paths, which are blob: URLs scoped to the document and therefore dead by restore time. The 'partial' flag and its restore-prompt note now cover photos only.

title: Merge the placement and handoff entry kinds into one
description:
The add-entry sheet lists **placement** and **handoff** as two separate kinds in
the same group (`features/cases/add_entry_sheet.dart:167-178`). Both call
`showPlacementSheet` and both write one `placements` record. The only difference
is `PlacementMode`, which decides whether the carer dropdown renders at all
(`_showCarerPicker`, `features/cases/placements/placement_sheet.dart`).

So the picker offers the user a choice between two rows that open the same form,
one of them with a field hidden — and the hidden field *is* the distinction they
were asked to make up front.

The backend already models this the right way: per CLAUDE.md, "a handoff is just
a placement with `to_user` — the hook derives the `active_carer` change in the
same transaction." The UI should match: one "Placement" entry whose carer picker
is always visible. Choosing a carer other than the current one is the handoff,
and the record and hook behave exactly as they do now.

Watch out for: `_isHandoff` currently also requires `mode == handoff`, and
`_CaseActions` plus `placement_tile.dart` pass the mode explicitly — all three
call sites need updating together.

Source: Dieter Rams design review (principle 10 / principle 4 — the mode is a
hidden third state of one form).
close_reason: Closed

title: Trim the case Overview actions card from six buttons to two
description:
`_CaseActions` (`features/cases/case_detail_screen.dart:519-586`) stacks up to
six full-width buttons at the bottom of the Overview tab: status toggle, record
outcome, handoff, edit intake, share, delete.

Three of those verbs are already reachable from the History tab's add-entry
sheet (`features/cases/add_entry_sheet.dart`) — outcome, handoff, and arguably
the status change. The result is that the case's two tabs each own a different
partial menu of the same actions, and nothing tells the user which is
authoritative. The code even records the reason outcome was duplicated ("its
most important lifecycle step, so it sits next to its sibling actions instead of
only inside the History add-entry sheet", federfall-m1z) — a fair argument that
nonetheless produced the split.

Proposed shape — keep two buttons in the card:

- the status toggle (the only lifecycle control with no timeline record of its own)
- record outcome

and relocate the rest to where their subject already is:

- edit intake -> a pencil in the header, beside the name and intake data it edits
- share -> the app bar, next to the PDF/print read-actions it belongs with
- delete -> the app-bar overflow (still supervisor-gated, still error-coloured)

Source: Dieter Rams design review (principle 10, as little design as possible —
the app's weakest principle and this is its densest instance).
close_reason: Closed

title: Deleting a case orphans its finder's PII
description:
Found while scoping supervisor deletion of animals and cases.

`cases.finder` does not cascade, and nothing else points at a `finders` row. So
deleting a case (or an animal, once `cases.animal` cascades) leaves the finder's
contact record — name, phone, email, address — with no case referencing it.

That matters because `pb_hooks/finder_retention.pb.js` purges finder PII on a
schedule derived from *case closure*. With no case left, an orphaned finder has
no closure date to measure from, so the retention sweep may never reach it: the
PII outlives the record that justified collecting it. REQUIREMENTS.md §Open
questions 4 sets that retention at a configurable default of 2 years after the
episode closes (DSGVO), and §Security lists data-subject deletion as in scope —
so an unreachable finder row works against both.

Deliberately NOT bundled into the deletion feature: the right behaviour needs a
decision. Candidates:
- purge a finder when its last referencing case is deleted (a hook on
  `cases` delete, checking for remaining references — a finder can be linked
  from several cases);
- have the retention sweep also claim finders with zero referencing cases,
  measuring from the finder's own `created`;
- keep the row on purpose (some orgs want a repeat-finder history) and instead
  make it reachable — an "unlinked finders" admin view.

Verify against a live stack either way: retention behaviour is a hook, so
`test_rules.py` is where it gets proven.
acceptance_criteria: Deleting the last case that references a finder either purges the finder or leaves it reachable to the retention sweep; asserted in test_rules.py.
close_reason: Orphan pass added to the finderPiiRetention cron: finders that no case references are DELETED (not scrubbed), at the next sweep, without waiting out the retention window. CORRECTION to the issue as filed — the sweep did not miss orphans; it already measured an unlinked finder from its own `created`, so PII was anonymised, in fact sooner than if the case had merely closed. The real gap was that the row waited out the full window despite nothing referencing it, and the anonymised husk then stayed forever. Deleting beats anonymising because an unreferenced finder is unreachable: finders are only read through a case bundle, so the location the scrub keeps feeds no statistic and the case→finder link that justified keeping the row is gone. The pass runs over ALL finders (not just pii_purged = false) so earlier husks are collected, and holds orphans for a 24h grace period so a finder written moments before its case is never mistaken for one. NOT covered by test_rules.py — no cronAdd job is reachable from it. Verified manually against a live stack with the schedule rewritten to '* * * * *' and grace 0: still-referenced finder keeps its PII, one whose case was deleted goes, one never linked goes. CLAUDE.md now records that crons are untestable there plus the tempdir/fast-schedule recipe.

title: Supervisor deletion of animals and cases (UI + cases.animal cascade)
description:
The server already permits both deletions and the UI exposes neither.

`animals.delete` and `cases.delete` are both `AUTH && SUP && org =
@request.auth.org` (1700000010), and `PbRepository.delete` exists on both
repositories. Nothing in `apps/federfall/lib` calls either.

## The one real bug: `cases.animal` does not cascade

Every other animal relation cascades (`markings`, `weights`, `exams`,
`egg_records`, `aviary_stays`), but `cases.animal` is `cascadeDelete: false`
(1700000004). Deleting an animal therefore orphans its cases — and every
case-scoped child hangs off `case`, not `animal`, so journal entries,
medications, administrations, conditions, placements, dispositions, follow-ups,
shares, quarantine records, exams and exam findings all survive pointing at a
dead animal id. That is the dangling-row class `animal_org_scope.pb.js` already
has to code around (federfall-ti77).

Fix: a migration flipping `cases.animal` to `cascadeDelete: true`. Case-scoped
children then cascade the rest of the way down on their own — verified: every
`case` relation is already `cascadeDelete: true`.

`weights` / `markings` / `egg_records` deliberately do NOT cascade from a case
(they are animal-level, 1700000020 / federfall-4agw), so deleting a case leaves
them on the bird and only deleting the animal removes them. Correct as is.

## UI

Supervisor-only, gated by a new `canDeleteAnimal` / `canDeleteCase` in
`core/auth/roles.dart` mirroring the server rule (like `weightDeletableBy`).

- Animal detail: the app bar currently carries edit + merge as direct icons,
  with a comment that a one-item overflow is just chrome. With a second
  supervisor action that reasoning flips — merge + delete move into one overflow
  menu, the edit icon stays.
- Case detail: the same delete action for supervisors.

Confirmation must enumerate the blast radius before destroying it (decision
taken with the user: an open case does NOT block the delete, it is named in the
warning instead). For an animal, counts come from the existing per-animal
providers (`casesForAnimal` incl. how many are not disposed, `weightsForAnimal`,
`eggsForAnimal`, `markingsForAnimal`, `examsForAnimal`) — the same set the merge
flow's `_MovesSummary` shows, so no new queries. Per-case children (journal,
medications, …) are covered as prose rather than exact counts, which would cost
one query per case. For a case, every count is already in the case bundle, so it
is free.

## Tests

`test_rules.py`: deleting an animal removes its cases and their children (assert
a journal entry / disposition / quarantine row is gone), a plain carer cannot
delete either, another org's supervisor cannot; deleting a case leaves the
animal-level weights / markings / egg_records intact. Widget tests: the action
is absent for carers and coordinators, the dialog names the open-case count, and
confirming calls `delete`.
acceptance_criteria: A supervisor can delete an animal or a case from the app; the confirmation enumerates what will be destroyed and names any still-open case; deleting an animal removes its cases and every case-scoped child (cases.animal now cascades); weights/markings/egg_records survive a case delete but not an animal delete; carers and coordinators see no delete action; rule tests + widget tests green.
close_reason: Migration 1700000057 flips cases.animal to cascadeDelete (the only actual bug — every other animal relation already cascaded, and every case relation does, so one flag completes the subtree). canDeleteRecords in roles.dart; confirmDeleteAnimal/confirmDeleteCase in features/animals/delete_record_dialogs.dart with a shared _DestructiveDialog that enumerates the blast radius; animal detail moves merge+delete into one supervisor overflow (the old 'one-item overflow is just chrome' comment no longer applies with two actions); case delete sits last in the Overview actions card behind a divider, in the error colour. Open cases warn rather than block, per the user's decision. Counts are AWAITED, not read off provider snapshots — a loading .value would have rendered 'No cases' on the one dialog that must not understate what it destroys. Found and fixed a second pre-existing bug: main.pb.js's disposition reconcile looked up the parent case by id and threw when the case was itself being deleted; because it runs onRecordAfterDeleteSuccess nothing rolled back, so a successful delete returned 400. Gates: 310 rule assertions (16 new for deletion/cascade), 494 app tests (+10), analyze/format clean, coverage 78.26%. Also updated the obsolete ti77 dangling-row assertion, which 1700000057 made unreproducible via the API. Orphaned finder PII filed as federfall-yw74.

title: weights / markings can be re-pointed at another org's animal
description:
Found while building federfall-4agw.1 (egg_records), whose rule tests caught the
same hole in the new collection.

The animal identity-layer collections are org-wide writable (5yg.4) and are
deliberately exempt from 1700000043's `@request.body.<field>:isset = false`
guards — a re-point "grants the writer nothing they don't already have
org-wide". That reasoning holds WITHIN an org, but nothing checks that the
`animal` a row points at is in the SAME org:

    PATCH /api/collections/weights/records/<id>  {"animal": "<other org's animal>"}

`org = @request.auth.org` still passes (the row's own org is untouched, and
`org` carries the isset guard), so the write succeeds. Result: a row scoped to
org A hangs off org B's animal. Org B cannot read it (list/view are org-scoped),
but B's animal now owns it — and `cascadeDelete: true` on `animal` means
deleting that animal destroys another org's clinical history.

A rule cannot fix this: plain field references in an UPDATE rule are evaluated
against the STORED record (1700000043's own finding), so `animal.org =
@request.auth.org` would check the OLD animal and ignore the incoming one.

Confirmed absent for `weights` and `markings`: no hook targets either
collection (pb_hooks only hooks animals, cases, dispositions, egg_records,
journal_entries, placements, users), and 1700000020 sets their create/update
rules to the bare org-scoped predicate. `exams.animal` is denormalized the same
way — the atomic route guards it (test: "exam save CANNOT denormalize a
foreign-org animal"), but the direct collection API may not.

Fix: the pattern established in pb_hooks/egg_records.pb.js — an
onRecordCreate/onRecordUpdate guard asserting `animal.org == record.org`, the
same way intake.pb.js / exam.pb.js / main.pb.js validate their referenced
records. Add rule-test assertions alongside the egg_records ones.

Not fixed in 4agw because it is a pre-existing hole in collections that epic
does not touch.
acceptance_criteria: A weight, marking and exam row cannot be created with, or PATCHed to, an animal belonging to another org; test_rules.py asserts it for each collection the way it does for egg_records.
close_reason: animal_org_scope.pb.js rejects an `animal` relation naming another org's bird on cases / weights / markings / exams / egg_records, replacing the egg-only hook from 4agw.1 (variadic onRecordCreate/onRecordUpdate tags, so one body covers all five). Exams carry an optional org, so the guard falls back to the parent case's org — it can't be dodged by omitting the field. The UPDATE guard only fires when `animal` actually changes: cases.animal does not cascade, so rows pointing at a hard-deleted bird already exist, and re-validating every save would make them permanently unsaveable and break unrelated writes like the dispositions hook bumping case.status. 18 new assertions in test_rules.py (create + re-point + same-org-move per collection, the no-org exam case, and the dangling row staying editable while still refusing a cross-org re-point); 294 green against a live stack. CLAUDE.md's backend section now records the hook.

title: eggs.4 — reassignment sheet, animal-detail egg section, l10n
description:
The reassignment flow (the reason this feature is shaped the way it is) plus the
animal's lifetime egg surface and full l10n.

## `egg_reassign_sheet.dart`

Opened from the egg tile's overflow menu on both the case timeline and the
animal-detail section. Three stacked parts:

1. **Scope** — "nur dieses Ei" vs "ganzes Gelege (N Eier)", from
   `groupIntoClutches`. This is the ergonomic point: you normally learn the
   layer's identity for a whole clutch at once, not per egg.
2. **Candidates first, search second** — the co-residents of the egg's animal AT
   `laid_at`, from `aviary_stays`
   (`started_at <= laid_at && (ended_at = '' || ended_at >= laid_at)`); that
   ledger is exactly why no aviary is denormalised onto the egg. In a pair this
   is a one-tap list. Below it the existing `reidSearchProvider` field for
   anything else — same widget shape as `_CandidateSearch` in
   `merge_animal_screen.dart`.
3. **Summary of what moves**, mirroring `_MovesSummary`, because this writes to
   ANOTHER animal's record.

The write:

    repo.update(egg.id, {'animal': target, 'attribution': 'confirmed'});

Sequentially over the selected rows. No transaction, no custom route: nothing
derived depends on it, so a partial failure is harmless and retryable — report
"3 von 4 umgebucht" and let the user re-run on the rest. Photos travel with the
row; a JSON PATCH that omits a file field leaves it alone.

Add a one-line hint that a row moves whole: if only 1 of a 2-egg row belongs to
the other hen, edit `count` down and add a row on the other animal.

Afterwards invalidate `eggsForAnimalProvider` for BOTH animals plus
`caseBundleProvider` for any open case detail.

Also wire the tile's "Bestätigen" action here (presumed -> confirmed, one PATCH).

## `_EggSection` in `animal_detail_screen.dart`

Card between `_WeightSection` and `_ExamsSection`, same structure as those:
`Card` + `titleMedium` header + `IconButton(Icons.add)` +
`AsyncValueView` WITH retry — a load failure must never render as "keine Eier"
(federfall-5cle).

- Last laying date, "N Eier in 12 Monaten · M insgesamt", and "K unbestätigt" in
  the header when any are presumed.
- Recent clutches as list tiles (newest first) with the "vermutlich" chip, a
  single leading thumb when the row has photos (a full strip would fight the card
  layout), and the same overflow menu.
- A 12-month BAR chart of eggs per month (`fl_chart`, like `WeightTrendChart`) —
  laying is seasonal, so a cumulative line would say little. Renders nothing when
  there are no eggs in the window. Presumed eggs are included in a lighter shade
  rather than hidden.
- `'egg_records'` added to `ref.liveRefresh([...])` and
  `..invalidate(eggsForAnimalProvider(animalId))` to the invalidation cascade.

## l10n (both app_en.arb and app_de.arb, then `flutter gen-l10n`)

German leads the wording: `eggNewTitle` (Ei-Ablage erfassen), `eggEditTitle`,
`eggFieldDate` (Gelegt am), `eggFieldCount` (Anzahl Eier), `eggFieldFertility`
(Befruchtung), `eggFieldFate` (Verbleib), `eggFieldUncertain` (Legerin unsicher),
`eggFieldNotes`, `eggPhotosLabel` (Fotos), `eggAddPhoto`, `eggTakePhoto`,
`eggCountLabel` ({count, plural, =1{1 Ei} other{{count} Eier}}),
`eggPresumedChip` (vermutlich), `eggConfirmAction` (Bestätigen),
`eggReassignAction` (Umbuchen), `eggReassignTitle` (Ei umbuchen),
`eggReassignScopeSingle`, `eggReassignScopeClutch`,
`eggReassignCandidatesTitle` (Mitbewohner am {date}),
`eggReassignPartial` ({done} von {total} umgebucht), `eggEditAction`,
`eggDeleteAction`, `eggDeleteTitle`, `eggDeleteConfirm`,
`animalSectionEggs` (Eier), `animalNoEggs`, `animalEggsSummary`,
`animalEggsPresumed`, `eggChartTitle` (Eier pro Monat),
`timelineAddEgg` (Ei-Ablage), plus fate labels (im Nest, Attrappe eingelegt,
entnommen, geschlüpft, zerbrochen, entsorgt, unbekannt) and fertility labels
(unbekannt, befruchtet, unbefruchtet). Reuse the existing `photoViewLabel`.

## Tests + gates

Reassign sheet writes `animal` + `attribution` for a whole clutch and reports
partial failure; candidate list resolves from `aviary_stays` at `laid_at`;
`_EggSection` empty / loaded / error states.

Final gates for the epic: `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed .`
clean from the repo root, `flutter analyze` clean, `flutter test` green, app
coverage still above 75% (`flutter test --coverage`), and `dart analyze` +
`dart test` for both touched packages.
acceptance_criteria: An egg or a whole derived clutch can be reassigned to a co-resident (from aviary_stays at laid_at) or any searched animal with one PATCH per row, reporting partial failure; the animal detail shows last laid, 12-month and total counts, unconfirmed count, recent clutches with thumbs and a 12-month bar chart; every string is in app_en.arb + app_de.arb; format/analyze/test green and app coverage above 75%.
close_reason: egg_reassign_sheet (scope: single vs derived clutch; candidates from aviary_stays at laid_at via new forAnimalAt/residentsAt, then reidSearch fallback; moves summary; sequential PATCH with partial-failure report), Bestaetigen wired, _EggSection with summary + capped clutch list + 12-month bar chart (fl_chart, presumed in a lighter shade), egg_records in liveRefresh + invalidation cascade, all l10n in en+de. 44 tests green (30 eggs + 11 animal detail + 3 stay queries); analyze/format clean, app suite 484 green, coverage 78.11% (gate 75), packages green. UI diverged from the spec after review with the user: (1) the card's clutch subheading only renders for clutches with >1 record - a one-record header repeated its own row verbatim; (2) the 'Last laid' line was dropped, the newest clutch header directly below carries that date; (3) rows are capped at 6 across 3 clutches because a clutch is DERIVED and one long laying streak is one unbounded clutch; (4) that cap needed an escape, so 'Show all (N)' opens the full ledger in a scrollable sheet - EggClutchList/EggRow/clutchHeader live in egg_clutch_list.dart and are shared by card and sheet.

title: eggs.3 — eggs feature folder, entry sheet with photos, case timeline event
description:
The eggs feature folder plus its case-timeline surface. Mirrors
`lib/features/cases/weights/` in structure and `journal_entry_sheet.dart` /
`journal_entry_tile.dart` for the photo handling.

## `lib/features/cases/eggs/eggs_providers.dart`

- `@riverpod Future<List<EggRecord>> eggsForAnimal(Ref ref, String animalId)` —
  straight off the repo (ascending).
- `@riverpod Future<List<EggRecord>> eggsForCase(Ref ref, String caseId)` — via
  `caseBundleList(ref, caseId, (b) => b.eggs, ...)`, then filtered to the case's
  own window: `admittedAt` -> latest disposition date, else now. Deliberate
  divergence from markings (which show the whole lifetime on every case
  timeline): a ring is a standing property, an egg is a dated event, and
  unfiltered lifetime events would swamp the chronology.
- `const int kClutchGapDays = 5;` + `groupIntoClutches(List<EggRecord>)` — single
  ascending pass, new clutch when the gap exceeds the const. A pigeon's two eggs
  come ~44 h apart, the next clutch weeks later.
- `EggLayingSummary`: `totalEggs` (SUM of `count`, not row count),
  `eggsLast12Months`, `lastLaidAt`, `presumedEggs` — confirmed and presumed kept
  separate so guesses never harden into facts.
- Label helpers `eggFateLabel` / `eggFertilityLabel` in
  `features/cases/cases_labels.dart`, resolving `l10n` like
  `admissionReasonLabel`.

## `egg_entry_sheet.dart`

`showEggEntrySheet(context, {required String animalId, EggRecord? egg})` — NO
`caseId` parameter anywhere in this feature.

Skeleton copied from `WeightEntrySheet`: `DiscardGuard` + `FormSheetState`,
`SheetScaffold`, `runSave`, `requireUserOrg`, `guardUnsavedChanges`. Fields:
`DateField` (`pickDate`, default now) / count stepper (min 1) / fertility
dropdown / fate dropdown / "Legerin unsicher" switch -> `attribution: presumed` /
photos / notes (`minLines: 2`).

Photos follow `journal_entry_sheet.dart` exactly:
- `ref.read(imagePickerProvider)` -> `pickMultiImage()` and
  `pickImage(source: ImageSource.camera)`, held in `_newPhotos`.
- `_multipartPhotos()` builds
  `http.MultipartFile.fromBytes('photos', bytes, filename: photo.name)`.
- Uses `createWithFiles` / `updateWithFiles`, NOT `create` / `update`.
- On edit the body sends `'photos': _existingPhotos` (the survivors) so removing
  a thumb actually deletes it, with new uploads appended on top.
- Edit never sends `animal` (that is reassignment) and never sends `org`.

## `egg_entry_tile.dart`

`TimelineItem` with `Icons.egg_outlined`,
`formatEventDate(materialL10n, e.laidAt ?? e.created)`, a title like
"1 Ei · unfruchtbar · Attrappe eingelegt", a "vermutlich" chip when
`attribution == presumed`, and a `TimelineEntryMenu` with Bearbeiten /
Bestätigen (only when presumed) / Umbuchen (wired in the next issue) / Löschen.

Delete is gated by a new `eggDeletableBy(egg, me)` in `core/auth/roles.dart`
mirroring `weightDeletableBy`, so the UI matches the server rule.

Photos render as the 96 px horizontal thumb strip from `journal_entry_tile.dart`:
`CachedFileImage(url: repo.fileUrl(egg.id, filename, thumb: '200x200'))` in a
`ClipRRect`, tapping into `showImageViewer` with the full-size URLs and the
existing `photoViewLabel` semantics. URLs stay token-free —
`ProtectedFileCacheManager` appends the file token at download time.

No "attributed to X" label is needed: an egg on a case timeline belongs to that
case's animal by construction.

## Case timeline + add menu

- `case_timeline.dart`: `_EggEvent extends _Event` sorted by
  `laidAt ?? created`, rendered as `EggEntryTile`, watched via
  `eggsForCaseProvider` and folded into the existing isLoading/error aggregation.
- `add_entry_sheet.dart`: `_AddKind.egg` in the clinical group ->
  `showEggEntrySheet(context, animalId: medicalCase.animal)`. Enabled regardless
  of recorded sex — pigeon sex is often unknown or wrong at intake, and a bird
  recorded as male that lays an egg is exactly the case you need to log.
- `case_realtime.dart`: `'egg_records'` in `_caseTimelineCollections` with
  `'egg_records' => true` in the `belongs` switch (NOT
  `data['animal'] == animalId`): a reassignment event carries the NEW animal id,
  so an animal-id filter would never fire for the case losing the egg. Same
  refetch-on-any escape `exam_findings` takes.

## Tests

`groupIntoClutches` around the 5-day boundary; `eggsForCase` window filtering;
sheet create + edit payloads (asserting `createWithFiles` gets one
`MultipartFile` per picked image on the `photos` field, and that editing with one
thumb removed sends the survivor list); tile menu gating by author/supervisor.

Mock `imagePickerProvider`; `registerFallbackValue(<http.MultipartFile>[])`
alongside `<String, dynamic>{}`. Gotchas: fake image bytes throw "Invalid image
data" so `Image.memory` needs an `errorBuilder`, and `XFile.name` can be empty in
tests.
acceptance_criteria: showEggEntrySheet(animalId:) creates/edits egg records via createWithFiles/updateWithFiles with up to 3 photos; EggEntryTile renders on the case timeline with the photo thumb strip, the vermutlich chip and author-or-supervisor delete; _AddKind.egg opens the sheet; eggsForCase filters to the case window; case_realtime refetches on any egg_records event; widget + unit tests green.
close_reason: eggs_providers (eggsForAnimal/eggsForCase/kClutchGapDays/groupIntoClutches/clutchContaining/EggLayingSummary), egg_entry_sheet with photos via createWithFiles/updateWithFiles, egg_entry_tile with thumb strip + presumed chip + author-or-supervisor delete, eggFateLabel/eggFertilityLabel, eggDeletableBy, _EggEvent, _AddKind.egg, egg_records in case_realtime with refetch-on-any. 23 tests green; analyze/format/full suite green. Two notes: (1) journal's private _PhotoStrip was extracted to a shared ui/widgets/EditablePhotoStrip instead of copied ~100 lines; journal_entry_sheet now uses it. (2) The clutch gap is compared as a Duration, not .inDays — inDays truncates so a 5.5-day gap would have merged two clutches. Menu items Bestätigen/Umbuchen deliberately deferred to 4agw.4 rather than shipping dead entries.

title: eggs.2 — EggRecord model, enums, repository, case-bundle expand
description:
Domain model, enums, repository and case-bundle wiring for `egg_records`.

## `packages/federfall_models`

`lib/src/enums.dart` — three enums in the established shape (`wire` value +
`static X? fromWire(Object? v) => pbEnum(values, (e) => e.wire, v);`):

- `EggFertility`: unknown / fertile / infertile
- `EggFate`: inNest('in_nest') / dummySwapped('dummy_swapped') / removed /
  hatched / broken / discarded / unknown
- `EggAttribution`: confirmed / presumed

`lib/src/models/egg_record.dart` (own file, like `marking.dart` — `clinical.dart`
is case-centric):

    @freezed
    abstract class EggRecord with _$EggRecord {
      const factory EggRecord({
        required String id,
        required String animal,
        @Default(1) int count,
        DateTime? laidAt,
        EggFertility? fertility,
        EggFate? fate,
        @Default(EggAttribution.confirmed) EggAttribution attribution,
        @Default(<String>[]) List<String> photos,
        String? notes,
        String? author,
        String? org,
        DateTime? created,
        DateTime? updated,
      }) = _EggRecord;
      factory EggRecord.fromRecord(RecordModel r) { ... }
    }

`fromRecord` uses `pbInt` / `pbDate` / `pbString` / `pbStringList`. NOTE: there
is no `case` field — by design (see the epic). Export from
`federfall_models.dart`.

`case_bundle.dart`:
- `caseBundleExpand` gains `animal.egg_records_via_animal`.
- `@Default(<EggRecord>[]) List<EggRecord> eggs`, mapped off `animalRec` with the

`PbEggRecordsRepository extends PbRepository<EggRecord>` in
`clinical_repositories.dart`, collection `egg_records`, with
`forAnimal(animalId)` sorted ASCENDING by `laid_at` (oldest first, like
`weights.forAnimal`) so it feeds both the chart and clutch grouping.

Provider in `apps/federfall/lib/data/repository_providers.dart`.

## Done when

`dart run build_runner build` in both packages, `dart test` + `dart analyze`
green, model tests cover: missing/garbage `count`, unknown enum wire -> null,

Model tests cover garbage count, unknown enum wire, laidAt fallback, absent photos; case_bundle_test asserts eggs come newest-first off the animal. Both packages + app analyze/test/format green. title: eggs.1 — egg_records collection, access rules + rule tests
description:
Create the `egg_records` collection with its access rules, and prove the rules
against a live stack.

## Migration `backend/pocketbase/pb_migrations/1700000056_egg_records.js`

Fields: `animal` (relation -> animals, required, cascadeDelete, maxSelect 1),
`laid_at` (date, not required), `count` (number, default 1, min 1), `fertility`
(select: unknown/fertile/infertile), `fate` (select: in_nest/dummy_swapped/
removed/hatched/broken/discarded/unknown), `attribution` (select:
confirmed/presumed), `photos` (file), `notes` (text), `author` (relation ->
users, optional, no cascade), `org` (relation -> organisations, required, no
cascade), `created`/`updated` autodate.

`photos` MUST be born correct — all four options inline, no retrofit:

    { name: "photos", type: "file", required: false, maxSelect: 3,
      maxSize: 10485760,
      mimeTypes: ["image/jpeg", "image/png", "image/webp", "image/gif"],
      thumbs: ["200x200"], protected: true }

1700000027 / 1700000048 / 1700000049 are repair passes over file fields that
shipped without `protected` / MIME allowlist / `thumbs`, and they carry hardcoded
target lists — a new field only gets that treatment if it is created with it.

## Rules (guest-safe form, per 1700000045)

    const AUTH = '@request.auth.id != "" && @request.auth.is_active = true'
               + ' && @request.auth.role != "guest"';
    list/view/create = `${AUTH} && org = @request.auth.org`
    update           = `${AUTH} && org = @request.auth.org`
                     + ' && @request.body.org:isset = false'
    delete           = `${AUTH} && org = @request.auth.org && `
                     + '(@request.auth.role = "supervisor" || author = @request.auth.id)'

Org-wide read/create/update mirrors the animal identity layer (5yg.4 for
weights); delete is author-or-supervisor per 1700000047.

The migration comment MUST record that `animal` is deliberately NOT guarded with
`@request.body.animal:isset = false`, citing 1700000043's exemption of org-wide
identity-layer collections — reassignment depends on it and a future audit will
otherwise "fix" it. Include a working `down` that deletes the collection.

## Rule tests (`backend/pocketbase/tests/test_rules.py`, run via run.sh)

Needs a live PB — cannot run in the Flutter suite.

- org scope on list/view/create/update; cross-org read and write rejected.
- delete: author yes, other carer no, supervisor yes.
- `animal` IS mutable: an active carer can PATCH `animal` to another animal in
  the same org (asserts the 1700000043 exemption is intentional).
- `org` is not mutable (isset guard rejects the PATCH).
- the existing guest sweep picks the collection up automatically.
acceptance_criteria: Migration 1700000056 creates egg_records with photos born protected + MIME-allowlisted + thumbs 200x200; rules are the guest-safe org-scoped set with author-or-supervisor delete; test_rules.py proves org scope, the delete guard, that animal IS mutable and that org is not; down migration drops the collection.
close_reason: Migration 1700000056 + pb_hooks/egg_records.pb.js + 22 rule assertions in test_rules.py, all 276 checks green against a live stack; down/up roundtrip verified. DEVIATION from the epic: a hook WAS needed. The rule tests caught that 'animal' being mutable (the reassignment exemption from 1700000043) also allows re-pointing a row at ANOTHER org's animal — a field ref in an UPDATE rule evaluates against the STORED record, so no rule can check the incoming animal's org. egg_records.pb.js enforces animal.org == record.org on create+update, like intake.pb.js/exam.pb.js do for their referenced records. Note: weights/markings likely have the same hole (filed separately).

title: Egg-laying records per animal (photos + reassignment)
description:
Track egg-laying as a longitudinal property of the ANIMAL, available with or
without an open case — the stance `weights` took in 1700000020. Attribution must
be correctable: in a pair you often don't know which hen laid a clutch until
later, so moving an egg record to another animal is a first-class one-tap
operation, not delete-and-retype. Optional photos document an abnormal egg
(e.g. a Windei).

Clinical value: chronic laying is the input to calcium-depletion / egg-binding
risk, and the laying history belongs to the bird when it moves between carers or
aviaries.

## Domain decisions

- **One row = one laying event**, with `count` (default 1). A clutch is ~2 eggs
  two days apart; per-event rows aggregate cleanly and `count` covers "found 2,
  exact dates unknown".
- **Clutch is derived, not stored**: gap > 5 days => new clutch
  (`kClutchGapDays = 5`; a pigeon's two eggs come ~44 h apart, the next clutch
  weeks later). Pure function of dates, no second collection, no hook.
- **No `case` field at all** — see "Why there is no case field" below. This is
  the decision everything else follows from.
- **Uncertain layer**: `attribution: confirmed | presumed`. Records the doubt
  instead of silently asserting a guess; reassignment flips it to `confirmed`.
- **No `aviary` field**: `aviary_stays` (1700000052) already answers "where was
  this bird on that date"; a copy would drift.
- **Egg binding / Legenot is NOT modelled here** — that is an acute finding and
  belongs in `case_conditions`. This ledger is the chronic-risk input.
- **No `shell` / abnormality select** (explicitly descoped by the user): a
  visibly abnormal egg is documented by the photo + notes. If "how many
  soft-shelled eggs has this hen laid" ever needs answering without opening
  photos, that is a follow-up field, not part of this epic.

## Why there is no case field

`markings` is the precedent: it has NO `case` relation. It owns `animal`, and
the case timeline shows markings by pulling `animal.markings_via_animal` through
the case bundle (`markingsForCase` -> `repo.forAnimal(bundle.medicalCase.animal)`).
Timeline membership is COMPUTED FROM THE ANIMAL, never stored.

Eggs go one step further and drop even markings' `applied_in_case` context
breadcrumb: a ring never changes owner, so a stale context id can't happen
there — whereas an egg's whole point is that attribution moves, and a stale case
pointer is worse than none.

Payoff: reassignment is a single meaningful field write, and the egg
automatically leaves the old bird's case timeline and appears on the new bird's,
with nothing derived, cleared or re-pointed.

Rejected alternatives:
- *Re-derive `case` on reassignment* — needs a transactional route + server-side
  case lookup to reconstruct information that isn't needed once membership is
  derived.
- *Keep `case` as recorded* — leaves an egg on a timeline belonging to a
  different animal.
- *Nullable `animal` + `aviary` so "unattributed" is a real state* —
  semantically clean, but costs the cascade-delete ownership story, an "orphan
  eggs" inbox nobody asked for, and a nullable relation in every aggregate.
  `attribution: presumed` buys the same honesty for one select field.

## Collection `egg_records` (migration 1700000056)

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `animal` | relation -> animals, required, cascadeDelete, maxSelect 1 | owning relation; MUTABLE (that is the reassignment) |
| `laid_at` | date, not required | UI always sets it; model falls back to `created`, like `weights.measured_at` |
| `count` | number, default 1, min 1 | eggs in this laying event |
| `fertility` | select maxSelect 1 | `unknown` (default) / `fertile` / `infertile` |
| `fate` | select maxSelect 1 | `in_nest` / `dummy_swapped` / `removed` / `hatched` / `broken` / `discarded` / `unknown` (default) |
| `attribution` | select maxSelect 1 | `confirmed` (default) / `presumed` |
| `photos` | file, maxSelect 3, maxSize 10485760, mimeTypes image/jpeg+png+webp+gif, thumbs ["200x200"], protected true | optional; all four options set INLINE (see below) |
| `notes` | text, optional | |
| `author` | relation -> users, optional, no cascade | drives the delete rule |
| `org` | relation -> organisations, required, no cascade | scope everything hangs on |
| `created` / `updated` | autodate | |

File-field options are set in the creating migration, not retrofitted:
1700000027 / 1700000048 / 1700000049 are each a repair pass over file fields
that shipped without `protected`, without a MIME allowlist (stored XSS via
`evil.svg` from the app's own origin) and without `thumbs` (every
`?thumb=200x200` silently served the full-size original). Those migrations carry
hardcoded target lists, so a new field only gets the treatment if it is born
with it.

`photos` is multi (maxSelect 3), not single: maxSelect 1 stores a string and
maxSelect 3 stores an array, so switching later changes `String? photo` ->
`List<String> photos` in the model and every call site. The multi path is free
because `journal_entries.attachments` already implements it.

## Access rules (animal identity layer, guest-safe)

    const AUTH = '@request.auth.id != "" && @request.auth.is_active = true'
               + ' && @request.auth.role != "guest"';
    listRule   = `${AUTH} && org = @request.auth.org`;
    viewRule   = `${AUTH} && org = @request.auth.org`;
    createRule = `${AUTH} && org = @request.auth.org`;
    updateRule = `${AUTH} && org = @request.auth.org`
               + ' && @request.body.org:isset = false';
    deleteRule = `${AUTH} && org = @request.auth.org && `
               + '(@request.auth.role = "supervisor" || author = @request.auth.id)';

Read/create/update org-wide because a laying date is low-sensitivity
animal-identity data that must stay visible across cases and aviary residency
(5yg.4's reasoning for weights). Delete is author-or-supervisor, copying
1700000047 — destruction is the part worth restricting, contribution isn't.

The migration comment MUST state that `animal` is deliberately absent from any
`@request.body.<field>:isset = false` guard, referencing 1700000043's exemption
of the org-wide identity-layer collections — otherwise a future security audit
will "fix" reassignment out of existence. `org` carries the guard because
re-scoping a row across orgs is never legitimate.

## No hooks, no view change

- No `pb_hooks/egg_records.pb.js`: with no `case` field there is no
  `case.animal == animal` invariant to enforce, and no side effect the way a
  disposition drives `lifetime_status`.
- No `case_activity` view migration: markings appear in that UNION only via
  `applied_in_case`; eggs have no case column. Accepted consequence — logging an
  egg does not bump a case's activity timestamp.
- No custom route: reassignment is a plain PATCH.

## Reassignment

    repo.update(egg.id, {'animal': target, 'attribution': 'confirmed'});

Sequentially over the selected rows (one egg, or a whole derived clutch). No
transaction and no custom route: nothing derived depends on it, so a partial
failure is harmless and retryable — the sheet reports "3 von 4 umgebucht" and you
re-run on the rest. If atomicity is ever wanted, a
`POST /api/federfall/eggs/reassign` can be added later without touching the
model. Photos are fields on the row, so they travel with it; a JSON PATCH that
omits a file field leaves it alone.

Known limitation: a row moves whole. If only 1 of a 2-egg row belongs to the
other hen, edit `count` down and add a row on the other animal — worth a
one-line hint in the sheet rather than a splitting UI.

## Client layers

- **models**: `EggFertility` / `EggFate` / `EggAttribution` in `enums.dart`
  (`wire` + `fromWire` shape); `EggRecord` in its own
  `lib/src/models/egg_record.dart` (clinical.dart is case-centric, marking.dart
  is the shape to copy); `caseBundleExpand` gains
  `animal.egg_records_via_animal` and `CaseBundle.eggs` maps off `animalRec`
  with the same `rel(...)` helper the `markings:` branch uses.
- **data**: `PbEggRecordsRepository extends PbRepository<EggRecord>` in
  `clinical_repositories.dart` with `forAnimal(id)` ascending by `laid_at`
  (oldest first, like `weights.forAnimal`).
- **app**: `lib/features/cases/eggs/` — `eggs_providers.dart` (eggsForAnimal,
  eggsForCase via `caseBundleList` filtered to the case window, clutch grouping,
  `EggLayingSummary`), `egg_entry_sheet.dart`, `egg_entry_tile.dart`,
  `egg_reassign_sheet.dart`; `_EggEvent` in `case_timeline.dart`;
  `_AddKind.egg` in `add_entry_sheet.dart`; `_EggSection` in
  `animal_detail_screen.dart`.

`eggsForCase` filters to the case's own window (`admittedAt` -> latest
disposition date, else now). Deliberate divergence from markings, which show the
whole lifetime on every case timeline: a ring is a standing property, an egg is a
dated event, and unfiltered lifetime events would swamp the chronology.

## Realtime

- `animal_detail_screen.dart`: `'egg_records'` in `ref.liveRefresh([...])` +
  `..invalidate(eggsForAnimalProvider(animalId))` in the cascade.
- `case_realtime.dart`: `'egg_records'` in `_caseTimelineCollections`, with
  `'egg_records' => true` in the `belongs` switch, NOT
  `data['animal'] == animalId`. A reassignment event carries the NEW animal id,
  so an animal-id filter would never fire for the case losing the egg and other
  viewers would keep showing it until a manual refresh. Refetch-on-any is the
  same escape `exam_findings` already takes.

## Decisions taken without asking (flag if unwanted)

- Clutch gap = 5 days, as a documented typed const (not org-configurable).
- Presumed eggs ARE counted in the 12-month chart, in a lighter shade, and
  surfaced as "K unbestätigt" in the section header — you see the real picture,
  flagged, rather than a chart that silently hides guesses.
- `_AddKind.egg` is enabled regardless of the animal's recorded sex: pigeon sex
  is often unknown or wrong at intake, and a bird recorded as male that lays an
  egg is exactly the case you need to log.

## Out of scope

Egg counts in `features/statistics`; breeding/pairing model (parentage, which
pair a clutch belongs to); incubation tracking / hatch-date projection;
automated Legenot risk alerting; joining `case_photo_gallery.dart` (no case
link, and there is no animal-level gallery today).
acceptance_criteria: A carer can log an egg-laying event on any animal with or without an open case, optionally with up to 3 photos; the egg appears on the animal's lifetime record and on the timeline of whichever case covers that date; a mis-attributed egg (or a whole clutch) can be moved to another animal in a few taps and then shows up under the new animal instead.
close_reason: All four children done. A carer can log an egg-laying event on any animal with or without an open case (with up to 3 photos, born protected + MIME-allowlisted + thumbed), the egg shows on the animal's lifetime card and on whichever case's timeline covers its date, and a record or a whole derived clutch can be re-attributed to a co-resident in a few taps. Gates: 276 backend rule assertions green against a live stack, 484 app tests, both packages green, analyze + format clean, coverage 78.11%. Two deviations from the epic, both recorded on the children: a hook WAS needed (egg_records.pb.js, cross-org animal re-point that no rule can catch — see federfall-ti77 for the same hole in weights/markings), and the animal card gained a 'Show all' history sheet because the clutch caps otherwise left older clutches unreachable.
