comments.author: Jan-Henrik Bruhn
comments.text:
Completed per the REVISED design (no format->geometry test needed — ReceiptPaperSize.widthPixels is a data-only enum; the 'repo URL building' unit tests already exist from Phase 2 in case_report_repository_test.dart's fetchReceiptPng tests).

Added widget/unit test coverage:
- test/features/printing/printer_settings_test.dart (7 tests): PrinterSettingsNotifier's shared_preferences persistence round-trip for all 4 device transports + paper size + clearDevice, verified via a FRESH ProviderContainer per assertion (a real cold-start reload, not just in-memory state).
- test/features/printing/printer_config_sheet_test.dart (5 tests) + fake_printer_service.dart: scan/select, empty-scan state, manual network entry (validation + success), paper-size persistence, all against a FakePrinterService (no real plugin/platform channel touched).
- test/features/profile/profile_screen_test.dart: 4 new tests for the Printer section (not-configured prompt, configured+test-print, failed-connect still disconnects, remove-with-confirmation).
- test/features/cases/case_detail_screen_test.dart: 3 new tests for the print action (no-printer-configured snackbar, fetch+print with the right widthDots, failed fetch still disconnects).

Found and fixed 3 real bugs via this test-writing pass (not just added coverage):
1. printer_config_sheet.dart had a genuine race: a manual .listen(null, onDone:...) on the scan's broadcast stream competed with the StreamBuilder's own subscription for the SAME single-emission stream — whichever won could starve the other, so a fast scan result could vanish before the UI ever rendered it. Fixed by removing the manual listener entirely and deriving scanning-vs-done state from the StreamBuilder's own snapshot.connectionState (mirrors the actual production symptom the user reported: 'shows discovered devices' only worked by luck before).
2. printer_config_sheet.dart's manual host/port entry had no MediaQuery.viewInsetsOf(context) bottom padding (unlike edit_profile_sheet.dart's established pattern), so the keyboard covered the fields on some devices — user-reported live.
3. case_detail_screen_test.dart's shared pump() helper had latent fragility: case_realtime.dart's live-refresh subscribes to collectionEventsProvider for 14 collections (chaining through a REAL pocketBaseProvider construction), never isolated in this test file. It silently worked by accident until introducing a real SharedPreferences.setMockInitialValues call (needed for the printer tests) perturbed that chain's timing enough to turn a latent retry loop into a hard 'Timer still pending' failure across EVERY test in the file, not just the new ones. Fixed properly by (a) isolating collectionEventsProvider to Stream.empty() (matching medication_reminders_test.dart's established pattern) and (b) overriding printerSettingsProvider directly with a fake read-only notifier (fake_printer_settings.dart) instead of touching real SharedPreferences at all, since the print button only reads settings.

Quality gate: dart format clean, flutter analyze clean (very_good_analysis strict), flutter test 444/444 passing, flutter test --coverage = 76.77% (was 74.42% before this session's additions; CI gate is >=75%), dart analyze + dart test 112/112 for federfall_data. flutter build apk (development debug) and flutter build web --wasm --release both succeed.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERION NOTE: 'manual test print verified on the network printer' — YES, confirmed live by the user this session against a real Epson TM-T88IV: test print, case receipt print (with the corrected margins/cut/all-black bold sans-mono font), AND a plain PDF share (the widthDots regression fix) were all explicitly tested and confirmed working end-to-end on real hardware, not just simulated.

title: Aviary detail: Pflege tab + flock timeline (journal + health rollup)
description: The UI surface for flock-care (parent federfall-d5co): restructure AviaryDetailScreen into Bestand/Pflege tabs and render a flock timeline combining aviary journal entries with a HISTORICAL rollup of health entries (conditions) from cases of animals that were resident during the entry's date — the use case the user explicitly wanted (accurate even after a bird moves to another aviary).
design: Restructure AviaryDetailScreen from single-scroll to Bestand/Pflege tabs, following the case-detail LayoutBuilder-on-pane-width pattern (see adaptive-two-pane-layout memory: >=720 side-by-side else tabs; automaticallyImplyLeading:!context.isExpanded). Mini case_timeline analog merging two _Event kinds into one date-sorted list: aviary journal events (editable) + rolled-up condition events (read-only, link to source case). HISTORICAL rollup query: aviaryStays.forAviary(X) -> resident animals + date windows -> their cases' case_conditions -> client-filter to conditions dated within each stay window (chunked '||' like animals_repository.byIds). Providers aviaryJournal(id) + aviaryHealthRollup(id); per-tab FAB (+Bewohner on Bestand, +Eintrag on Pflege). Depends on aviary_stays (d5co.1) for windows and extended journal_entries (d5co.2) for entries.

New l10n keys (aviaryTabBestand/Pflege, aviaryConditionOpenCase). Widget + provider tests green, analyze clean.

title: Extend journal_entries for aviary-scoped free-text logs
description: Allow free-text journal entries (cleaning, feed changes, group observations) written directly against an aviary, not a case (parent federfall-d5co). Decision made: EXTEND the existing journal_entries collection rather than a dedicated one — no field duplication; cost is a dual-parent access rule + XOR constraint + nullable caseId. Ripple is small: nothing dereferences entry.caseId (both sheet and tile take caseId as their own constructor param), so the nullable field only touches the model def, freezed regen, and clinical_mappers_test.dart.
design: Migration: journal_entries.case -> required:false; add optional aviary relation (cascadeDelete). XOR hook on journal_entries create+update: throw unless exactly one of case/aviary is set (PB can't enforce declaratively). Compound access rule: (case set -> existing childView/childEdit on case) OR (aviary set -> aviary-org rule like aviaries: any active member reads, coord/sup edits), guest-safe. Model: caseId -> String? caseId, add String? aviary; regen freezed; fix clinical_mappers_test.dart. Existing case path (journal_entry_sheet sets 'case') unchanged. Repo: add PbJournalRepository.forAviary(id). UI: aviary-variant journal sheet reusing SheetScaffold/FormSheetState; tile reusing TimelineItem/TimelineEntryMenu/confirmAndDelete. l10n de(primary)+en strings + label helpers.
acceptance_criteria: journal_entries accepts aviary-scoped entries; XOR enforced server-side; access rule covers both parents and is guest-safe; JournalEntry model caseId nullable + aviary field; forAviary repo method; aviary journal sheet+tile; existing case-journal flow unaffected; widget+mapper tests green; analyze clean; l10n regenerated.
close_reason: journal_entries extended to dual-parent (case OR aviary): migration 1700000053 preserves the 621 immutability guard + adds aviary, XOR hook, JournalEntry.caseId nullable + aviary field, forAviary repo method, JournalEntrySheet/Tile generalized for both parents, l10n already parent-agnostic. Python rule tests pass live (241/241).

title: Aviary residency ledger (aviary_stays) + centralized animals hook
description: Foundational residency history for flock-care (parent federfall-d5co). current_aviary is today a live pointer mutated in 5 places (disposition after-create/update/delete reconciles in pb_hooks/main.pb.js:160/222/275, merge_animals.pb.js:192, add_animal_sheet.dart:76) with NO history — so 'what happened in this enclosure over time' is unrecoverable once a bird moves on. Add an append-only aviary_stays ledger, maintained by ONE centralized hook on the animals collection so all 5 mutation sites are covered without patching each.
design: New collection aviary_stays: animal (rel, cascadeDelete), aviary (rel), started_at (date), ended_at (date, nullable = current), org. Append-only, mirrors Placement's shape; 'current residency' = latest row per animal (like active_carer derives from Placement). HOOKS on animals collection (NOT dispositions): onRecordAfterCreateSuccess opens a stay when current_aviary set; onRecordAfterUpdateSuccess diffs original().get('current_aviary') vs new — on change close the open stay (set ended_at) and open a new one. Centralizing on animals covers all 5 writers in one place; no recursion (writes only stay rows, never re-saves the animal). Backfill migration seeds one open stay per currently-housed animal (current_aviary != ''). Access rules: aviary-org read (like aviaries), server-side writes only, guest-safe (&& @request.auth.role != 'guest'). Package: AviaryStay freezed model + fromRecord, PbAviaryStaysRepository.forAviary(id). RISK: assumes every current_aviary change flows through a saved animals record (true for all 5 sites today); note in a code comment. Pre-ledger history unrecoverable (backfill = present only).
acceptance_criteria: aviary_stays collection + backfill migration committed; animals create/update hooks maintain stays across all 5 current_aviary writers; access rules guest-safe; AviaryStay model + repo with tests; python rule tests pass against live PB; flutter analyze clean.
close_reason: aviary_stays ledger + centralized animals hook shipped: migration 1700000052, pb_hooks/aviary_stays.pb.js, AviaryStay model+repo, backfill, guest-safe access rules, python rule tests pass live

Raise min_coverage in ci.yml back towards 80% incrementally as these land.

The only difference is that the conditions copy makes color/onColor nullable (defaulting to secondaryContainer/onSecondaryContainer) while the medication copy requires them.

No local _Tag copies remain.

title: Security: users.updateRule allows a supervisor to move users cross-org (plant supervisor in org B)
description: users.updateRule (1700000011) pins the TARGET's current org (org = @request.auth.org) but nothing constrains the NEW org value; the field guard in main.pb.js only blocks org/role changes by non-supervisors. So a supervisor of org A can create an account they control (create is org-bound), then update it to org=B, role=supervisor — planting a supervisor inside org B (OWASP A01). Moot on a single-org instance (org creation is superuser-only) but schema/hooks/tests all support multi-org. Fix: append a guard to users.updateRule — (@request.body.org:isset = false || @request.body.org = @request.auth.org) — via a new migration using the guest-safe predicate; add a test_rules.py case. Found in 2026-07-03 OWASP review.
acceptance_criteria: A supervisor's update setting org to a different org id is rejected; same-org updates unaffected; rule test covers it; guest sweep still passes.
close_reason: Added migration 1700000051 tightening users.updateRule to also constrain the request body's org field (equal to caller's org or unset), closing the cross-org escalation for both the self-update and supervisor-update branches. Added 3 assertions to test_rules.py (cross-org move of another user, cross-org self-move, same-org update still allowed) — full suite (214/214) passes.

title: Security: disable/scope Android Auto Backup (protected photo cache leaks to cloud backup)
description: apps/federfall/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml sets no android:allowBackup / android:dataExtractionRules, so Auto Backup defaults ON. Google cloud backup and device-to-device transfer copy app data in the clear — including the federfallProtectedFiles disk cache (downloaded clinical/intake/animal photos, i.e. the very files PocketBase marks Protected) and shared_preferences. The flutter_secure_storage token is Keystore-bound ciphertext and won't restore usable, but the image cache and prefs do (OWASP A05 / MASVS-STORAGE-2). Fix: android:allowBackup="false", or fullBackupContent + dataExtractionRules excluding the cache dir and prefs. Found in 2026-07-03 OWASP review.
acceptance_criteria: Merged release manifest has backup disabled or rules excluding the protected-file cache and prefs; verified via adb backup / bmgr on a debug build or manifest inspection.
close_reason: Set android:allowBackup="false" on the main AndroidManifest.xml <application> tag. App is online-only with the server as sole source of truth, so nothing is lost by disabling Auto Backup/device transfer; this removes the flutter_cache_manager SQLite catalog + shared_preferences from any backup path.

title: Security: verify PocketBase binary SHA256 in Dockerfile
description: Dockerfile:94 downloads the pinned PocketBase release zip over HTTPS with no checksum/signature verification, despite the stage comment claiming 'fetch + verify the pinned release'. A tampered GitHub release asset or CDN would ship a backdoored server binary into the production image undetected (OWASP A08). Fix: pin the release SHA256 per PB_VERSION/arch and run 'echo "<sha>  /tmp/pb.zip" | sha256sum -c' before unzip. Consider also pinning the Flutter SDK checkout and mock-oauth2-server (dev-only) by commit/digest. Found in 2026-07-03 OWASP review.
acceptance_criteria: Docker build fails if the downloaded pocketbase zip does not match a pinned SHA256; both amd64/arm64 covered.
close_reason: Pinned per-arch SHA256 checksums (from PocketBase v0.39.4's published checksums.txt) in the Dockerfile pbfetch stage and added a sha256sum -c verification step before unzip. Verified: build succeeds with the correct hash, and fails loudly with a corrupted/wrong hash (tested both). Comment instructs updating the checksums when PB_VERSION is bumped.

title: Photo thumbnails serve full-size originals, squished into square tiles
description: PocketBase only generates ?thumb=WxH when the size is whitelisted in the file field's thumbs option — none of the photo fields (cases.intake_photos, journal_entries.attachments, animals.photo) ever configured it, so every 200x200 thumb request returned the full-size original. The client's memCacheWidth+memCacheHeight decode (ResizeImage exact policy, commit 2019217) then stretched that non-square original into the square tile — visible as uncropped, ratio-distorted previews. Fix: migration 1700000049 whitelists 200x200 on all three fields (thumbs generate lazily, covers existing files); CachedFileImage decodes width-only so any non-thumbable source (gif) still keeps its aspect ratio.
close_reason: Fixed in f716ac3 (review bundle) and dba7ee3 (thumbs migration + decode fix); flutter analyze/test green, backend suite 196 passed

title: Location-search clear button doesn't track typing
description:
File: apps/federfall/lib/features/cases/location/location_picker_screen.dart:380 and :396-412

_SearchBar is a StatelessWidget reading controller.text.isNotEmpty without listening to the controller, and the TextField has no onChanged; nothing rebuilds while the user types. The clear (X) suffix only appears/disappears when some unrelated setState fires, so users can't clear a half-typed query.

Fix: wrap the suffix in ValueListenableBuilder(controller) or add an onChanged triggering a parent setState.

Source: flutter-reviewer codebase review 2026-07-02 (cases).
close_reason: Closed

title: Pull-to-refresh while offline raises an unhandled async error
description:
File: apps/federfall/lib/features/cases/case_realtime.dart:83-89 (used at case_detail_screen.dart:86-88, 208, 239)

CaseLive.refresh() awaits ref.read(caseByIdProvider(_caseId).future); when the server is unreachable that future rejects, and RefreshIndicator.onRefresh does not catch errors from the returned future. title: Add AsyncValue.widgetWhen extension for consistent loading/error UI
description:
Inspired by immich mobile (lib/extensions/asyncvalue_extensions.dart): an extension on AsyncValue<T> that wraps .when() with app-wide defaults:

- default loading widget (centered progress indicator) and default error body, overridable per call site
- skipLoadingOnRefresh: keeps showing stale data while a provider refreshes instead of flashing a spinner
- logs every error it renders (single choke point for surfacing async errors)

Especially valuable now that the app is online-only with no local cache: every screen hits the network, so loading/error states are the common case and should look + behave identically everywhere. Error default should include a retry affordance (ref.invalidate of the failing provider) and use l10n (app_en.arb + app_de.arb).

Sweep existing .when(...) call sites in apps/federfall/lib/features/ to adopt it where the custom handling is just boilerplate.

Error logging exists as a better choke point: LoggingProviderObserver.providerDidFail logs every provider failure app-wide (catches even unrendered failures), so the view stays render-only. This session moved the errorMessage(l10n, e) mapping INTO AsyncValueView as the default and removed the identical boilerplate from all 16 call sites (commit a5089e9). The one remaining raw .when() (new_case_screen re-id search) is genuinely custom (inline spinner, intentionally silent error) and was left as-is. Kept the widget form over an extension: const-able, testable, already established.

Once clients no longer write cases.finder directly, lock the field down entirely — extend the 1700000043 pattern with '@request.body.finder:isset = false' on cases CREATE and UPDATE rules (a new migration). That closes both the orphaned-PII-on-failure problem and the finder re-point/enumeration hole (9hy), including the update-side re-point that 1700000043 deliberately left open.

title: Logic: case-number generation permanently breaks at 1000 cases/year
description:
main.pb.js:27-43 picks the max case number by sorting -case_number lexicographically. Once '2026-1000' exists, '2026-999' still sorts first, so the hook computes seq 1000 again and every create that year fails on the unique index — no new cases can be opened without manual intervention.

Related in the same block:
- 'case_number ~ {:prefix}' is a CONTAINS match, so a manual number like 'ALT-2026-1' pollutes the lookup (should be startswith or numeric max).
- year comes from UTC admitted_at, so a case admitted just after midnight Jan 1 CET gets the previous year's number.
- concurrent creates race to the same seq; loser gets an unretried 400.

Fix: derive seq numerically (e.g. strip prefix, CAST max) and retry on unique conflict; consider org-local timezone for the year.
close_reason: Fixed in main.pb.js: seq derived numerically in SQL (COALESCE/MAX/CAST over substr), prefix match anchored with LIKE 'YYYY-%' so manual numbers like ALT-2026-1 can't pollute, and a no-op UPDATE on the org row grabs SQLite's write lock before the max is read so concurrent creates serialize instead of racing (unique index stays as final guard). Tests: crosses 1000, foreign-format pollution. UTC-year/multi-org follow-up: federfall-28m.

title: Security/Privacy: protected photo cache not purged on sign-out
description:
ProtectedFileCacheManager (apps/federfall/lib/data/protected_file_cache.dart) serves cache hits without any token check, and signOut (features/profile/profile_screen.dart:14) only clears the auth store — the image cache is never emptied. After logout (or when a different user signs into the same device/browser), previously viewed intake photos and journal attachments still render from disk, undoing the server-side protection from 1700000027_protect_file_fields.js.

Fix: call emptyCache() on sign-out and on account/server switch.

title: Security: guest wall missing on collections created after guest-role migration
description:
1700000033_guest_role.js appends 'role != "guest"' to every rule containing the shared AUTH predicate — but only for collections existing at that point. Migrations 36–42 (quarantine_records, case_quarantine view, admission_reasons, marking_types, medication_routes, animal_species view) copy the old predicate without the guest exclusion (e.g. 1700000036_quarantine_records.js:18, 1700000042_animal_species_view.js:19). Guests can read those code lists and views (species names, per-case quarantine dates), contradicting the 'walled off from all data' invariant. Pattern guarantees regression: every future migration copying the AUTH constant reopens the hole.

Fix: follow-up migration re-running the rewriteRules pass; use the guest-safe predicate in the migration template going forward. Add a guest-access test to test_rules.py.

CLAUDE.md + migration comment now mandate the guest-safe predicate.

title: Local medication-due reminder notifications
description: Schedule on-device (local) notifications reminding the active carer when a medication dose is due, built on the existing medication_due view. No server push — PB is push-less by design — so reminders are scheduled locally and reconciled when the app runs.
design:
Source of truth: the medication_due view (1700000024) already computes next_due per active prescription and is scoped to the signed-in carer's cases (MedicationDue.nextDue, active_carer). Only 'scheduled' (with interval) and 'once' produce a next_due; 'as_needed' none — mirror the view, do not invent scheduling here (MedicationFrequencyKind stays the source of timing).

Approach:
- Add flutter_local_notifications (+ timezone for zoned scheduling). OS-scheduled zoned notifications fire even when the app is closed / offline.
- A reconcile step: on app start, worklist refresh, after logging a dose, and after a prescription is created/edited/ended, fetch the carer's medication_due rows and (re)schedule. Use a STABLE notification id per prescription (derive from medication id) so rescheduling replaces the old one; cancel when next_due is null / prescription ended / a dose was just given (next recomputed).
- Notification content: drug + dose + case/animal; tap deep-links to the case (case_detail) or the log-dose action. Reuse worklist_labels formatting.
- Permissions: Android 13+ POST_NOTIFICATIONS + exact-alarm (SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM/USE_EXACT_ALARM) for precise timing; iOS request authorization. A per-user toggle to enable/disable reminders (persist locally; optional org default later).

KNOWN LIMITATION to document: without background fetch / push, prescriptions added or changed by OTHER users (or on other devices) won't schedule until this device's app next opens/refreshes. Optionally add workmanager/background-fetch reconcile later — out of scope for v1. Call this out in-app if needed.

Watch-outs: timezone init (local zone), DST, don't fire for past-due on every launch (fire-immediately vs skip — decide), dedupe across rapid reschedules, respect the app being logged out (cancel all on logout / clear on org switch).
acceptance_criteria: flutter_local_notifications integrated with a permission flow and a per-user enable toggle. A due 'scheduled'/'once' medication produces a local notification at next_due with drug + case; tapping opens the case. Reminders (re)schedule on app start / worklist refresh / dose logged / prescription changed, and cancel when the prescription ends, a dose is given, or the user logs out. Works with the app backgrounded/closed (OS-scheduled). flutter analyze clean + flutter test green. The 'changes by others lag until app open' limitation is documented.
close_reason: Implemented in de8c3a3. flutter_local_notifications 22 + timezone; keepAlive reconciler over the worklist source with realtime listeners; opt-in profile toggle with permission flow (notification + best-effort exact-alarm, inexact fallback); stable per-prescription notification ids; UTC-instant scheduling (no tz plugin needed); tap deep-links to the case incl. terminated-state launch; cancel-all on sign-out/toggle-off; web no-op. Decisions: past-due doses are skipped (worklist owns them, avoids re-firing on every launch); 'changes by others lag until next open' limitation documented in the toggle subtitle and provider docs. analyze clean, 335 tests green, dev APK builds.

title: Promote quarantine into the case timeline (default 14-day initial quarantine)
description:
Today quarantine is a single `quarantine_until` date field on the `cases` record
(migration `1700000004_cases.js:101`), defaulted to `admitted_at + 14 days` by the
create hook (`pb_hooks/main.pb.js:48-52`), shown as a static Overview detail row
(`case_detail_screen.dart:507`) and edited inline in the intake edit sheet
(`edit_case_intake_sheet.dart:280-298`).

Promote quarantine into the unified case chronology so it behaves like every other
clinical record (weight, condition, medication, journal, marking, placement,
disposition). Quarantine is expected to occur/change often (extensions, early lifts),
so a single mutable field loses that history — a timeline of quarantine events records
*when* and *to what date* quarantine was set or extended.

This mirrors the "initial weight record" pattern: at intake the entered weight becomes
a real `weights` record rather than a field on the case
(`new_case_screen.dart:274-287`). Quarantine should get the same treatment — a default
**initial 14-day quarantine** created as a timeline record at case creation.

## Goal

- New quarantine timeline kind following the established pattern (see CLAUDE.md "Case
  timeline pattern"): a collection + model + repo + `@riverpod` provider + `showXSheet()`
  bottom sheet (create/edit) + a `TimelineItem` tile + a sealed `_Event` subclass in
  `case_timeline.dart`.
- Each record carries the quarantine end date (`quarantine_until`) and an event timestamp
  (when it was set/extended); an optional reason/note. Multiple records = extensions /
  re-quarantine; the latest record's end date is the current quarantine status.
- Default initial quarantine of **14 days** from admission, created automatically — like
  the initial weight record.

## Open decision (resolve before implementing)

The worklist and dashboard currently sort/surface cases by `case.quarantine_until`
(`worklist.dart`, `dashboard_providers.dart`). Two options:

1. **Keep a denormalized `quarantine_until` mirror on the case**, maintained by a hook
   to always equal the latest quarantine record (parallels how case `status` /
   animal `lifetime_status` are hook-owned). Cheapest for worklist/dashboard; no extra
   joins. **(recommended)**
2. **Drop the field entirely** and have worklist/dashboard query the quarantine records.
   Cleaner data model but more query work and N+1 risk on list views.

Decide which before touching the backend; option 1 keeps worklist/dashboard untouched.

## Where the default is created

Match the initial-weight approach: prefer creating the default quarantine record in the
backend create hook (`main.pb.js`) so it exists regardless of client, OR in
`new_case_screen.dart` alongside the intake weight. Note `main.pb.js` already owns the
14-day quarantine default — repoint it to create a record instead of (or in addition to,
if option 1) setting the field.

## Likely touch points

Backend:
- New migration: `quarantine_records` collection (relation `case` cascade, `quarantine_until`
  date required, `reason` text optional, `set_by` user, `org`, timestamps) + access rules
  (`1700000010_access_rules.js`, org-scoped).
- `main.pb.js`: create the default 14-day quarantine record on case create; (option 1) keep
  `quarantine_until` mirror in sync.
- Rule/hook tests (`tests/test_rules.py`).

Models / data:
- `federfall_models`: add `Quarantine` model + `fromRecord` mapper (see `Disposition`).
- `federfall_data`: `QuarantineRecordsRepository` + provider wiring in
  `repository_providers.dart`.

App:
- `features/cases/quarantine/`: providers, `quarantine_sheet.dart`, `quarantine_tile.dart`.
- `case_timeline.dart`: `_QuarantineEvent` subclass + fetch in build.
- `add_entry_sheet.dart`: add quarantine to the "add" picker.
- `case_detail_screen.dart`: drop the static Overview quarantine row (now on History).
- `edit_case_intake_sheet.dart`: remove the inline quarantine field.
- l10n: `app_de.arb` + `app_en.arb` strings (German primary).

Don't forget codegen (`build_runner` for freezed/riverpod, `flutter gen-l10n`) and the
quality gates (`flutter analyze` + tests; package `dart analyze`/`dart test`).
design:
DECISION (resolved): use a PocketBase VIEW collection for the worklist/dashboard quarantine end date — NOT a denormalized mirror field and NOT a client-side join. This is the established pattern here (see medication_due_view 1700000024 — same shape: compute a derived date per record so the worklist gets it in one query). 'Current quarantine end per case' = MAX(quarantine_until) over the case's quarantine_records (or latest by event timestamp if early-lift records are allowed — decide alongside lift semantics).

Two shapes: (1) dedicated view 'quarantine_current' (id=case, quarantine_until=MAX(...)), org-scoped like medication_due; or (2) cheaper — add a computed quarantine_until column to the existing case_summaries view so current readers get it for free.

Realtime caveat is already solved: views emit no realtime, so add 'quarantine_records' to worklistLiveCollections (worklist_providers.dart) — the base-collection watch + 1-minute worklistTicker already handle the clock-driven 'quarantine ending' transition (the ticker comment literally names it). This means NO mirror field and NO sync hook: the only hook work is creating the default 14-day quarantine record at case create. Supersedes the option-1/option-2 'Open decision' in the description.
acceptance_criteria: Quarantine appears as a timeline kind in the case History (provider + showXSheet + TimelineItem tile + _Event subclass); a default 14-day quarantine record is created automatically at case creation (like the initial weight record); the static Overview quarantine row and the inline edit-sheet field are removed; worklist/dashboard quarantine sorting still works; flutter analyze clean + tests green; backend migration + hook + rule tests in place.

Gates green (analyze clean; 287 app + 47 models + 69 data tests). Migrations applied to dev stack. In-app behavioural spot-check left to the user.

title: Add background sync via WorkManager (iOS/Android) — push writes when app is backgrounded
description:
pocketbase_drift's sync retry only fires when the app is active and connectivity returns. For wildlife rehabilitators who log a medication and immediately put the phone in their pocket, the write queues locally but only syncs when they re-open the app.

- Evaluate adding workmanager (^3.0.0) to trigger sync on backgrounded iOS/Android
- On connectivity RESTORED event, schedule a WorkManager one-off task that calls _retrySyncForAllServices()
- On web: use ServiceWorker background sync API (navigator.serviceWorker.ready.then(...))
- Add retryLocal() progress reporting to the UI (sync indicator in app bar)
- Test: kill app immediately after creating a case offline → app restart should sync it

title: Handle logout — set clearOnLogout: false on $AuthStore; verify schema persistence
description:
pocketbase_drift's $AuthStore.clear() wipes the entire local Drift DB by default. For Federfall, the cache should be preserved on logout (carers may share a device), only cleared on explicit app reset.

- Set clearOnLogout: false on $AuthStore
- Verify schema (pb_schema.json) is NOT cleared on logout
- Verify case/case_condition/treatment data IS cleared on logout
- Test: log in → create a case offline → log out → log back in → case should be gone
- Remove SecureAuthTokenStorage / PrefsAuthTokenStorage once $AuthStore.prefs is wired

title: Adapt LiveRefresh / case_realtime.dart for pocketbase_drift's realtime bridge
description:
pocketbase_drift pipes PocketBase realtime events into the local Drift DB (onEvent() → $create / $update / $delete on local SQLite). Federfall's existing ServiceMixin, LiveRefresh and case_realtime.dart wiring should be checked for compatibility.

- Verify ServiceMixin's watchRecords() stream still fires and triggers UI rebuilds
- Verify onEvent() writes to Drift do not interfere with existing stream logic
- Adapt caseRealtime to use $PocketBase.realtime if needed
- Test: create/update/delete a case from Admin UI → verify Flutter app updates within 5s

Note: the realtime service is currently delegated to the base PocketBase SDK class (not overridden in $PocketBase).

title: Set up WASM SQLite for web (sqlite3.wasm + drift_worker.dart.js)
description:
pocketbase_drift uses Drift with SQLite. On web this requires WASM files served from the web/ directory.

- Download sqlite3.wasm from the sqlite3.dart releases
- Download drift_worker.dart.js from the drift package
- Place both in apps/federfall/web/
- Verify web build succeeds (flutter build web)
- Test offline reads/writes in browser (Chrome DevTools → Network → Offline)

Currently Federfall uses SharedPreferences (localStorage) for web cache — this replaces it with a proper SQLite store.

title: Migrate to pocketbase_drift — offline-first sync engine
description:
Replace the current read-through cache (PrefsRecordCache) with pocketbase_drift (^0.4.3), a proper offline-first SQLite-backed layer for PocketBase.

CURRENT BEHAVIOUR (broken):
- All writes (create/update/delete) throw RepositoryException.network immediately when offline
- Cache is bounded: 100 records / 20 lists per collection, no TTL, FIFO eviction
- offlineBanner shows "Offline – showing saved data" — misleading, because no writes are possible
- No background sync; writes never survive app restart

DESIRED BEHAVIOUR:
- Writes queue locally in SQLite when offline; sync automatically on reconnect
- Reads served from cache instantly; network updates in background
- Conflict resolution: 5 retries then silent discard (acceptable for wildlife rehab use case)
- Schema-bundled validation for local writes

See: https://pub.dev/packages/pocketbase_drift
See: internal code review — pocketbase_drift gap analysis

title: Sheets/dialogs lack PopScope for unsaved-changes / back-nav
description:
Sheets and dialogs don't use PopScope (or PopEntry) to control back navigation on Android. An accidental swipe or back gesture can dismiss a form with unsaved changes without confirmation.

Recommendation: wrap sheet/dialog content in PopScope to intercept dismissal when the form is dirty and prompt to confirm discarding unsaved changes.

Files: sheet/dialog widgets — add_entry_sheet.dart, edit_animal_sheet.dart, and the other showXSheet() bottom sheets.
Source: code review finding #2.

comments.author: Jan-Henrik Bruhn
comments.text:
Implemented a reusable DiscardGuard (lib/ui/discard_guard.dart, exported via ui.dart):

title: OAuth2 self-service provisioning: guest role + group gating + first-user supervisor
description: Make OAuth2 usable as a sign-in method that can also self-provision accounts, on top of federfall-uvf (which enabled OAuth2 + env provider config). Decided shape: HYBRID. (1) Add a 'guest' role; new self-registered OAuth2 users default to guest. (2) Guest-proof the access rules: a guest is is_active=true (can log in) but the access boundary excludes role='guest' everywhere, so they see/do nothing until promoted — show an 'awaiting access' state. (3) pb_hooks OAuth2 provisioning (onRecordAuthWithOAuth2Request, isNewRecord): read IdP groups from oAuth2User.rawUser; optional group->role mapping (env), optional allow-list gating (env); set role/org/is_active on the new record (also fixes the role-required 400 that blocks OAuth2 signup today). (4) Chicken-and-egg: the FIRST user (when no active supervisor exists) OR a configured supervisor group becomes supervisor. (5) Optional env toggle to disable password auth so OAuth2 can be the ONLY method (info endpoint already reports auth.password=false; login screen already hides the password form). title: Responsive/adaptive layouts for web & large screens (tablet)
description:
The app is built mobile-first and works well on phones, but on the web and larger screens (tablet, desktop browser) it just stretches the single-pane phone UI — navigating into a list item opens a whole new full-screen 'window' where a wide screen has room to show list AND detail together. Make the layout adaptive so large screens use their space.

Concrete opportunities:
- List-detail (two-pane): cases list, animals registry, aviaries — show the list on the left and the selected item's detail on the right on wide screens, instead of pushing a new route. Falls back to the current full-screen navigation on narrow screens.
- Case detail: on wide screens show Overview and History side-by-side simultaneously, rather than behind the Übersicht/Verlauf tabs. Keep the tabs on narrow screens.
- App chrome: NavigationRail (or extended rail) on wide screens vs the bottom NavigationBar on mobile (the nav shell).

Approach — derive proper UX concepts first, then implement the Flutter way, NO code duplication:
- Define breakpoints once (compact / medium / expanded, per Material 3 window-size classes) and a single place that maps them to layout decisions; don't sprinkle MediaQuery checks.
- Reuse the EXISTING composable widgets (CaseTimeline, the Overview sections, list tiles, DetailHeader, etc.) in both the single-pane and two-pane arrangements — the panes are just different containers around the same widgets, not reimplementations.
- Use Material 3 canonical layouts / adaptive scaffolding (LayoutBuilder + the official adaptive patterns, e.g. flutter_adaptive_scaffold or an equivalent in-house AdaptiveScaffold) and NavigationRail<->NavigationBar.
- Mind go_router: the selected list item / detail must stay URL-addressable (deep links, browser back) — likely a StatefulShellRoute or a selected-id query/path that drives the detail pane; the two-pane and pushed-route views should share one source of selection state.
- Keep it accessible and not regress the phone experience.

This is sizeable and design-led — start by producing the UX concept (breakpoints, which surfaces get two-pane, how selection/routing works, mockups), then split implementation per surface (it may warrant promotion to an epic with child issues once the concept is agreed).
acceptance_criteria: A documented adaptive-layout concept exists (breakpoints, per-surface behaviour, routing/selection model). On expanded widths: the cases/animals/aviaries lists show list+detail side-by-side and the case detail shows Overview+History together; on compact widths the current phone UX is unchanged. Layout decisions come from one shared breakpoint source; the same content widgets are reused across panes with no duplication; deep links and browser back still work; flutter analyze clean + tests green.

title: Gate all write-operation UI behind the user's permissions
description:
Across the app, hide (or disable) every write/mutating UI control when the current user is not allowed to perform it, so the UI matches the server access rules instead of offering actions that fail on save. The backend access rules in 1700000010_access_rules.js are the real boundary; this is about not surfacing dead-end controls (esp. to read-only shared viewers and lower-privileged roles).

Currently inconsistent: some surfaces gate (case Overview actions and the new add-entry FAB use 'active carer || supervisor'; team/admin screens use roles.dart helpers; aviary FAB uses canManage), while others don't (the per-tile edit/delete/overflow menus on every timeline tile — journal, weight, exam, condition, prescription, dose, marking, placement, follow-up, disposition — appear regardless of write permission).

Work:
- Establish ONE source of truth for 'can I write to this case' (e.g. a canEditCase(case, user) helper in core/auth/roles.dart, or a provider) and stop duplicating the inline 'activeCarer == me.id || supervisor' check (already copied in case_detail_screen _CaseActions and the add-entry FAB).
- Audit every write affordance and gate it: timeline tile edit/delete menus, the add-entry FAB (already done in xc8.1 — fold into the shared helper), case edit/status/share, sharing changes, aviary add/edit, animal edit, admin code-lists/team, profile, etc.
- Decide hide vs. disable per control (prefer hide for menus/FABs; disable+tooltip where the control must stay visible).
- Cover coordinator vs supervisor vs carer vs read-only-shared distinctions consistently (see existing roles.dart helpers).

Note: the org-scoped, private-by-default + opt-in sharing model means a user may have read-only access to a shared case — those viewers must see no write controls.
acceptance_criteria: A read-only viewer sees no write affordances (no add-entry FAB, no per-tile edit/delete menus, no edit/status/share) on cases shared read-only; permitted users see them as before; the case write check lives in one shared helper used everywhere; no UI offers an action the server will reject. Verified against the rule tests / a running stack where rules apply.
close_reason: Closed

title: Uploaded image doesn't appear until a manual refresh
description:
After adding/uploading a photo (e.g. a journal entry attachment), the image does not show immediately — it only appears after a pull-to-refresh, navigating away and back, or the next realtime tick. Looks like a race/refresh-ordering bug in the upload→display path.

Likely suspects to investigate:
- Provider refresh ordering: the create/update sheet invalidates the owning list provider (e.g. journalForCaseProvider) on save, but the new record's file field / the read-through cache may not yet reflect the just-uploaded file when the tile rebuilds.
- File token timing: protected file fields need a token from fileTokenProvider (FED-8.1); the attachment strip shows a spinner until repo+token resolve. If the token isn't ready, or the URL is built before it is, the first render can miss.
- Image cache: CachedFileImage keys by token-stripped URL (fileCacheKey, federfall-xu3). A freshly-created file id that was probed/cached as a 404/miss before the bytes existed could serve a stale negative result until evicted.
- Multipart create returns the record; confirm the attachments filename list on the returned RecordModel is used to build the URL immediately, rather than waiting for a re-fetch.

Repro: open a case → add a journal entry with a photo → save. Expected: the thumbnail appears in the new timeline tile right away. Actual: blank/absent until a manual refresh.

Touches: journal attachment strip (journal_entry_tile.dart _AttachmentStrip), the create/save + invalidate path (journal_entry_sheet.dart), fileTokenProvider, and CachedFileImage/fileCacheKey. Likely applies to other image fields too (exam/finder/clinical).
acceptance_criteria: A newly uploaded image renders in its tile immediately after save, without a manual refresh; no stale-cache miss; holds for journal attachments and any other image field that shares the path.
close_reason: Closed

title: Scope carer (Pflegestelle) visibility: only their own animals + aviaries
description:
Today the access rules (backend/pocketbase/pb_migrations/1700000010_access_rules.js) make animals, markings and aviaries org-wide readable by EVERY active member (list/view = 'org = @request.auth.org'). A 'carer' (role enum: carer|coordinator|supervisor — carer == Pflegestelle) should instead only see THEIR OWN data. Coordinators/supervisors keep the org-wide view.

REQUIREMENT
1. Aviaries: a carer sees only aviaries assigned to them. The 'aviaries' collection already has a 'keeper' relation -> users, so the carer branch is roughly: keeper = @request.auth.id (||
COORD_SUP for the wider roles). list+view rules.
2. Animals: a carer sees only 'their own' animals =
   (a) animals currently assigned to one of their aviaries — animals.current_aviary.keeper = @request.auth.id, AND
   (b) animals they have/had a case with — animals linked to a case where they are active_carer (cases_via_animal.active_carer ?= @request.auth.id). Confirm the exact back-relation name.

OPEN QUESTIONS (the '?' in the request)
- 'have (had?) a case with': active_carer is a single CURRENT field; past carers are not tracked except possibly via case_shares. Decide whether past involvement counts and, if so, how to express it (case_shares.shared_with? a carer-history?). 
- Re-identification tension: the rule comment + memory 'animals-created-via-intake-or-aviary-resident' treat animals/markings as an ORG-WIDE identity layer for re-identification/dedup. Scoping animal visibility per-carer may break carers re-identifying a returning bird. Decide: keep re-id server-side / coordinator-only, or leave markings org-wide while scoping animals?
- markings: scope alongside animals or keep org-wide for ring-number re-id?
- Does scoping animals break any current UI (animals registry, aviary detail resident list) for carers? Audit lib/features for queries that assume org-wide animals.

IMPLEMENTATION
- New migration that rewrites the animals + aviaries (and maybe markings) list/view rules with a role-gated branch: COORD_SUP -> org-wide; carer -> the scoped filter above. No schema change needed for aviaries (keeper exists) or animal-in-aviary (current_aviary exists); only a migration if 'had a case' needs new history.
- Rules are the real security boundary — add/extend cases in backend/pocketbase/tests/test_rules.py (run via tests/run.sh against a live PB) covering: carer sees own aviary + its residents + own-case animals; carer does NOT see another carer's aviary/animals; coordinator/supervisor still see all.

Relates to FED-1.11 (federfall-bhx, access rules) and Phase 8 hardening (federfall-49l).
close_reason: Decided the current org-wide animals/aviaries visibility model is fine as-is; carer-scoping not pursued.

title: Offline note shown spuriously after returning to the app
description:
After bringing the app back to the foreground, the offline note (core/connectivity/offline_banner.dart) sometimes appears even though the device is online — annoying false positive.

Likely cause in core/connectivity/connectivity.dart (onlineStatusProvider): on resume the server /health probe can transiently fail (network interface still waking up, or the probe times out) and latch OnlineStatus.offline, and re-evaluation only happens on a connectivity_plus interface change or the 30s heartbeat — so the stale 'offline' lingers. Returning from background may not emit an interface change, so nothing re-probes promptly.

Fix directions to evaluate:
- Re-probe on app lifecycle resume (AppLifecycleState.resumed), not just on interface change / heartbeat.
- Treat a single failed probe as tentative: require N consecutive failures (or a short retry) before showing offline, and re-check quickly after a failure rather than waiting for the next 30s tick.
- Avoid fl​ipping to offline during the brief resume window.

Acceptance: returning to the foreground while genuinely online does not flash the offline note; a real outage still surfaces it promptly. Touches connectivity.dart (onlineStatus) and possibly a lifecycle observer; offline_banner.dart unchanged.

title: Evaluate Protected file fields + tokens for case/animal photos
description:
PocketBase serves file fields PUBLICLY by full URL by default (the random
filename suffix is the only guard). Sensitive files can be marked **Protected**
in the field options, then fetched with a short-lived **file token**
(pb.files.getToken() → append ?token=... to the URL).

Today every image (intake_photos on cases, journal_entries.attachments,
animals.photo) uses an UNPROTECTED field — PbRepository.fileUrl() builds a
plain /api/files URL with no token (the doc-comment even notes "the file field
is unprotected, so the URL is usable without an auth token"). So anyone with
the URL can view a patient/finder photo, bypassing the org-scoped access rules
that protect the records themselves.

TASK:
1. Decide which file fields should be Protected. Clinical/finder-linked photos
   (case intake_photos, journal attachments, possibly animal photo) likely
   should be, to match the private-by-default record model. Pure-public assets
   (none currently) stay open.
2. Backend: migration to set `protected: true` on those file fields.
3. Client: fileUrl() must request and append a file token for protected fields
   (pb.files.getToken(), cache it ~the token TTL, append ?token=). Image.network
   needs the tokenised URL; the full-screen viewer + share path too. Handle
   token refresh/expiry and offline (cached images already fetched are fine;
   new fetches need a token → require connectivity).
4. Verify with backend rule tests: a protected file URL without a valid token
   is rejected; with a token from an authorized user it works; another org's
   user cannot get a usable token.

Touches: pb_migrations (protected flag), packages/federfall_data PbRepository
.fileUrl + a token helper, image_viewer + thumbnails + animal_avatar, tests.
Note: protected files are NOT thumbnail-cacheable by plain URL, and the token
is short-lived — factor that into the thumbnail/loading code.
close_reason: Protected the three clinical/finder-linked file fields (cases.intake_photos, journal_entries.attachments, animals.photo) via migration 1700000027; client appends a short-lived file token (fileTokenProvider -> pb.files.getToken(), ~90s cache) to file URLs via fileUrl(token:). Verified by backend rule tests (bare URL rejected, same-org token works, cross-org token rejected) + data-layer unit test. Thumbnail cache-churn deferred to federfall-xu3.

title: Exam: add weight + temperature; route intake weight to a Weight entry; drop dead case clinical fields
design:
GOAL
Reconcile the case's clinical fields with the relational exam/weights model.
Weight + temperature + mucous membranes become exam/weights data; the dead
exam_* columns and the case-only intake_weight_g are removed. Validated against
docs/REQUIREMENTS.md (lines 162, 168) — temperature/mm are spec'd; intake weight
is a spec headline fast-path field (lines 79, 281, 341), so it STAYS on the
intake form but writes a Weight entry instead of a case column.

PRINCIPLE: every exam datum is its own typed, optional field, persisted ONLY
when the user enters it (sparse). NOTHING is folded into free-text notes.

PART A — weight on the exam
- Optional weight field in the exam sheet vitals zone. On save, if entered,
  CREATE a Weight (animal, case, weight_g, measured_at = examined_at) via
  weightsRepository. Not stored on the exam record — `weights` stays the single
  source of truth + trend. Invalidate weightsForCaseProvider.
- Create-only on the exam-CREATE path (hide/disable on edit) to avoid dup; a
  weights.exam relation for true edit-sync is a later option.

PART B — temperature + mucous membranes (new clinical vitals, all spec-listed)
- Add to the exams collection + Exam model + sheet vitals zone, each optional
  and stored only when entered:
  - `temperature` (number, nullable; °C). Birds normal ~40-42 °C.
  - `mm_color` (select: pink/pale/cyanotic/icteric/injected) — new wire enum.
  - `mm_texture` (select: moist/tacky/dry) — new wire enum.
  (Free-text optional fields are the lighter alt to the selects, if preferred.)

PART C — intake weight: KEEP the field, change what it writes
- new_case_screen keeps ONE weight input (fast-path per spec). In _create,
  after the case is created, if a weight was entered, create a Weight
  (animal, case = created.id, weight_g, measured_at = admitted_at) instead of
  writing case.intake_weight_g.
- Note: if the optional entry exam (blp.4) is then opened, leave its weight
  field blank to avoid a duplicate at the same timestamp (or prefill from the
  just-created Weight). Minor; accept or refine.
- Remove the weight field from edit_case_intake_sheet (weights are edited on
  the timeline now).

PART D — remove dead case clinical columns
- The 14 cases.exam_* columns (exam_bcs, exam_dehydration, exam_attitude,
  exam_temperature, exam_mm_color, exam_mm_texture, exam_head, exam_cns,
  exam_cardiopulmonary, exam_gi, exam_musculoskeletal, exam_integument,
  exam_forelimb, exam_hindlimb) are mapped in the Case model but never read or
  written by any UI — pure vestige of the original flat-exam FED-4.8 plan, now
  superseded by exams/exam_findings. Drop them (migration) + remove the fields
  from medical_case.dart. They are empty (no writer) → NO backfill needed.
- intake_weight_g: keep the column for old rows; add a one-off migration
  backfilling existing intake_weight_g -> Weight (animal, case,
  measured_at = admitted_at) so historic intake weights reach the trend, then
  stop writing it (PART C). Drop the column + Case.intakeWeightG in a later
  migration once nothing reads it.
- case_detail_screen.dart:361 currently shows intake_weight_g — switch to read
  the earliest/latest Weight from the trend, or drop the standalone display.

TOUCHES: exams migration (temperature/mm_color/mm_texture), exam_sheet, exam

title: First-run: require a VERIFIED federfall server before login, and let it inform login options
description:
On mobile/native first start the user must configure the backend before the login screen appears (the gate already does native→/setup→/login). Two gaps remain:

1. GENUINE-FEDERFALL VERIFICATION. ServerProbe today only checks GET /api/health == 200, which ANY PocketBase (or anything returning a 200 health) passes — ProbeNotFederfall never fires for a generic PB. Add a federfall identity/capabilities endpoint (pb_hooks route, e.g. GET /api/federfall/info, unauthenticated) returning a federfall marker + schema/app version + min supported client + login options. Upgrade ServerProbe to require that marker before ProbeReachable; reject generic PB / random 200s with a clear 'not a Federfall server' message (server_probe.dart already has ProbeNotFederfall).

2. SERVER INFORMS LOGIN. The verified server's capabilities should drive the login screen: which auth methods are enabled (password, OAuth providers), self-signup vs invite-only, password-reset availability, org/branding name. Expose the fetched capabilities via a provider; the router gate must ensure they resolve before /login renders (login adapts its buttons/links accordingly). Optionally surface 'update required' when min-client > current build.

Touches: backend pb_hooks (new info route), core/server/server_probe.dart, server_config_controller.dart, features/server_setup/setup_screen.dart, features/auth/login_screen.dart, router gate. Acceptance: first start forces server entry; a non-federfall URL is rejected; once a verified server is set the login screen reflects that server's enabled options; config persists across restarts; rule/probe tests cover federfall-vs-generic-PB.
close_reason: Closed

title: Decide case status lifecycle — are in_treatment/rehab/ready_for_release needed?

The three middle stages are unreachable — no app UI and no hook transitions a case into them. The app only reads status (list, detail chip, dashboard). REQUIREMENTS.md:164 calls status 'derived/maintained'; the dashboard (REQUIREMENTS.md:289 / FED-7.1) breaks down 'cases by status', so today it would always show in_care=N and the other active stages 0.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Decide whether the intermediate stages (in_treatment/rehab/ready_for_release) are needed at all, or whether in_care + disposed suffices. 2) If KEPT: add a transition mechanism (manual status picker on case detail and/or derive from clinical state, e.g. ready_for_release when is_releasable, in_treatment when active meds). 3) If DROPPED: new migration removing them from the enum, plus remove labels (cases_labels.dart + l10n) and the dashboard breakdown rows. 4) Revisit the FED-7.1 dashboard breakdown either way (note: empty rows were hidden as an interim fix).
close_reason: Decided: 3-state lifecycle in_care -> ready_for_release -> disposed. Drop in_treatment/rehab (treatment detail lives in the timeline). ready_for_release is a manual flag; disposed set by disposition hook.

title: Audit the transfer of sponsor PII when a bird changes aviary
description:
Emit a no-PII audit event when a sponsored bird changes `current_aviary`, so who
gained access to sponsor PII and when is reconstructable.

## Why

Access to sponsorship data follows `animal.current_aviary.keeper` live, by
design — moving a bird moves its patronage. The move is therefore also a transfer
of personal data to a new reader, and nothing currently records it. The
disposition that caused it IS logged, but reading "who could see this sponsor's
address in March" out of the disposition history means replaying `lib_derive.js`'s
ordering by hand.

For a GDPR trail that is the wrong shape. One explicit event makes the question
answerable directly.

## Shape

- action `sponsorship.access_transferred`, added to `lib_audit.js`'s registry
  (additive — an older client renders an unknown action from the envelope alone,
  so this is `feat:`, not `feat!:`)
- payload: the animal's label, the from/to aviary as `from_label` / `to_label`,
  the new keeper's label, and a COUNT of affected patronages
- NO sponsor name, address or mobile — `audit_events` is supervisor-only and
  append-only with a tamper guard (1700000068), so anything in it outlives every
  scrub

## Where

Wherever `current_aviary` actually changes, which is `lib_derive.js`'s reconcile
path, not the disposition hook — `aviary_stays.pb.js` already reacts to that same
field change and is the model for hanging off it.

Emit only when the count is > 0, so unsponsored birds do not fill the log.

## Guards to respect

- `emit()` never throws by contract; a failed log must not turn a successful
  disposition into a 500.
- `test_rules.py`'s audit sweep fails on an action outside the registry and on an
  event too empty to be worth reading.
- `audit_labels_test.dart` parses `CONTENT_FIELDS` out of `lib_audit.js` and fails
  on any recorded field that renders as its raw column name in either language,
  so the new labels need `features/admin/audit/audit_labels.dart` entries in DE
  and EN.
close_reason: Closed

title: Decide: scrub sponsor contact data after a patronage ends (vs §147 AO)
description:
Decide whether a sponsorship whose patronage has ENDED (`ended_at` set) on a
still-living bird gets its contact fields scrubbed after a window — the
`finder_retention.pb.js` treatment, applied to sponsors.

Deliberately NOT built with federfall-5s5j.1, which only handles the orphan case
(the bird is gone). This one is a policy question, not a mechanism question.

## The conflict

Data minimisation says: once the patronage is over there is no reason to hold a
private person's address and mobile number.

German bookkeeping law says the opposite about part of the same row. A donation
that produced a Zuwendungsbestätigung falls under the retention duties in §147
AO / §257 HGB — on the order of 10 years — and the receipt is worthless without
the donor's name and address. Scrubbing them could put the org in breach.

So the scrub cannot be symmetrical with the finder scrub, which drops identity
and keeps location. Here the identity may be the part that must be kept.

## What to decide

1. Does this deployment issue Zuwendungsbestätigungen at all? If not, the
   conflict evaporates and the finder-style scrub applies unchanged.
2. If it does: is the retained copy of record inside federfall, or in the org's
   bookkeeping (where it would legally live anyway)? If bookkeeping holds it,
   federfall can scrub freely — which is the outcome to aim for.
3. Which fields fall on which side: `sponsor_name` + `address` are the receipt;
   `mobile`, `sponsor_pronouns` and `notes` are not, and can go regardless.

Ask the user before implementing anything here. A wrong guess in either
direction is a legal problem, not a bug.

## If it ships

Reuse `sponsorship_retention.pb.js` and `lib_org.js`'s `settingsOf`, and mark
scrubbed rows so the job never reprocesses them (`finder_retention.pb.js`'s
`pii_purged` flag). Keep `SENSITIVE.sponsorships` in `lib_audit.js` in step with
whatever field list this lands on — the finder equivalent of that pairing is
called out in CLAUDE.md precisely because a drift defeats the scrub with the
app's own audit trail.
close_reason:
DECIDED: keep the data. No scrub of an ended patronage.

A patronage that produced a Zuwendungsbestätigung falls under the retention
duties in §147 AO / §257 HGB, and the receipt is worthless without the donor's
name and address — so the identity is the part that must be KEPT here, which is
the opposite of the finder scrub's shape. Rather than split the row into "receipt
fields" and "the rest" and get the boundary wrong in a way that is a legal
problem instead of a bug, the whole row stays.

So `sponsorship_retention.pb.js` keeps exactly the one deletion path it shipped
with: an ORPHAN, i.e. a patronage whose bird no longer exists. An ended patronage
on a living bird is history, and history is kept.

Nothing to implement — this is the behaviour already in main as of e9424f0. The
decision is recorded in the cron's header and in CLAUDE.md so the absence of a
scrub reads as a decision rather than an omission.

title: Code-list ordering is label-matched, not explicit
description:

That leaves two gaps the ticket's preferred fix would not:
- an org whose catch-all is worded differently ('Keine Angabe', 'Rest') falls back to alphabetical and lands in the middle again;
- a supervisor renaming their catch-all silently moves it back.

The durable fix is an explicit sort_order number column on the five code-list collections (conditions, admission_reasons, marking_types, microscopy_finding_types, medication_routes) + medication_products, sorted '+sort_order,+label', backfilled from the current order (admission_reasons from 1700000039's SEED_REASONS, which already has 'other' last), with drag-to-reorder in CodelistAdminScreen.

Adding an optional column is wire-safe (not a breaking commit). When it lands, catchAllLast becomes the fallback for entries with no rank, or goes away entirely.

title: A disposition can place a bird into an enclosure whose keeper never agreed
description:
The asymmetry left standing after federfall-q7ks.2 / federfall-ftm2 and
federfall-mpm4: putting a bird into an enclosure requires KEEPING that
enclosure on one path and not on the other.

* `animals.create` (1700000077): `current_aviary = '' || COORD_SUP ||
  current_aviary.keeper = @request.auth.id`. The "add resident" sheet's own
  gate, made real — a carer cannot add a bird to someone else's aviary
  (`test_rules.py`, `[custody: animals]`).
* A `placed_in_aviary` disposition: no clause about the aviary at all. Since
  federfall-mpm4 the writer must hold the BIRD, which is the other half of the
  question; the enclosure is still whichever one they name.

So a carer finishing rehab can move the bird into any enclosure in the org,
including one whose keeper has no idea it is coming — and that write also makes
the bird theirs (`aviary_stays` opens a residency, and 1700000077's keeper
branch hands them custody of a bird they never accepted).

## Why it was not folded into mpm4

Because it is a product decision, not a hole in that fix. Gating the disposition
on `aviary.keeper` would mean a carer can only release a bird into an enclosure
they keep themselves — plausibly correct for a small rehab where the coordinator
places birds, and plausibly wrong for one where the carer walks the bird over.
mpm4's gate is about custody of the animal and answers regardless of which way
this goes.

## Shape a fix could take

* Mirror `animals.create` exactly: `aviary = '' || COORD_SUP ||
  aviary.keeper = @request.auth.id` on `dispositions` create/update. Cheap (a
  rule, not a hook, since `aviary` is a plain forward relation and CREATE
  resolves against the submitted record) but freezes the coordinator-places
  workflow.
* Or make it a placement REQUEST: the disposition names the enclosure, the
  keeper confirms. Right shape, needs a state machine and a notification
  channel neither of which exists yet.

Whichever way it goes, `aviaries.keeper` being required since 1700000076 means
there is always somebody to ask.
close_reason: By design (user's call, 2026-08-10): a placement may name any enclosure in the org, because the keeper is not stuck with it — they hold the bird the moment it lands (1700000077's keeper branch), 1700000078's create rule lets them open a case on their own resident (animal_detail_screen.dart's 'open case' action, gated on canOpenCaseOnAnimal), and from that open case they can place it elsewhere. Recourse after the fact rather than consent before it. federfall-ehzz stays readable as the record of why the asymmetry with animals.create is deliberate.

title: Mutable relations can name a row in another org
description:
Found by the `[relation guards]` sweep in test_rules.py (which now enumerates
every relation field on every client-writable collection). Filed rather than
fixed: it is the one caveat the `mutable` rows share, and it grants no access.

`pb_hooks/animal_org_scope.pb.js` checks that an incoming `animal` belongs to the
caller's org. Nothing does the equivalent for any OTHER relation. So every field
the sweep classifies `mutable` can be pointed at a row in a different
organisation:

  aviaries.keeper                       a user in another org
  cases.active_carer                    likewise
  placements.carer / from_user / to_user  likewise
  dispositions.aviary                   another org's enclosure
  case_conditions.condition             another org's code list entry
  cases.admission_reasons               likewise
  markings.type                         likewise
  medications.route / medication_administrations.route
    / medication_products.route         likewise
  microscopy_findings.finding_type      likewise
  users.invited_by                      a user in another org

## Why this is low

Naming a foreign row grants the named party nothing: every access rule also
compares `org = @request.auth.org`, so a foreign user set as `active_carer` or
`keeper` still cannot read the case or the animal. The realisable effect is a
foreign LABEL being displayed — expanding `case_conditions.condition` or
`markings.type` renders another org's code-list text inside this org's UI. That is
a small cross-tenant read of vocabulary, not of clinical data.

`dispositions.aviary` is the most interesting of them, because it feeds
`animals.current_aviary`, which is a custody pointer — but a foreign aviary's
keeper is a foreign user, who fails the org check on `animals` anyway. Tracked
separately as federfall-j163 for the ordering half of that field.

## Fix, if it is worth doing

One generic hook rather than eleven checks: extend the pattern
`animal_org_scope.pb.js` already establishes to every relation field whose target
collection carries an `org`, driven off the schema instead of a hand-kept list.
The sweep's own registry is the natural place to state which fields are in scope,
so the two stay in step.

Note the app cannot produce any of these: every picker is fed from an org-scoped
query. This is reachable only by a hand-crafted request from an authenticated
member of some org.
close_reason: Closed

title: Microscopy on the animal lifetime view
description:
Deferred from the Mikroskopie design (docs/MICROSCOPY_DESIGN.md section 2.2 + 7 +
10). A recurring worm burden across admissions is a real clinical signal, and it is
the only reason to denormalize `animal` onto a sample.

microscopy_samples deliberately has NO `animal` field today, which is what keeps it
out of merge_animals.pb.js's re-point list -- and a collection missing from that
list is not left behind, it is DESTROYED inside the merge transaction and answered
with a 200 (federfall-0ua6).

So if this is built, FIVE things move in ONE commit:
1. add the `animal` relation + backfill `sample.animal = case.animal`
2. merge_animals.pb.js collection list
3. test_rules.py [animal merge] block (the guard that would have caught it)
4. the moves summary on the merge screen
5. animal_org_scope.pb.js (re-pointing at a foreign org's bird is not expressible
   in an update rule -- 1700000043)
Plus the boundary-guard decision: guard `animal` (a sample belongs to its case),
unlike egg_records where reassignment IS the feature.

title: In-app video playback (video_player) for attachments

title: Profile: Sign out is the only filled button on the screen
description:
Sign out is rendered as a full-width filled button in the brand green, which makes leaving the app the most visually prominent action on the profile screen. Nothing else on that screen competes with it — and nothing on that screen deserves primary emphasis at all.

Found in a Dieter Rams design review (principle 2, useful — visual weight should follow importance).
design: lib/features/profile/profile_screen.dart — swap the FilledButton for a tonal or outlined button. Consider colorScheme.error for the label, which is the usual treatment for a destructive-ish exit, but do not give it a filled error background either: it is reversible, so it should not shout.
close_reason: Sign out is an outlined error-coloured button now, not a full-width filled primary.

title: Intake: reasons chip group shows the generic 'This field is required'
description:
Advancing past the intake step without picking a reason shows 'This field is required' under the chip group. That is a text-field string on a multi-select — it does not tell the carer that ONE chip is enough, and 'field' is not what they are looking at.

Found in a Dieter Rams design review (principle 4, understandable).
design:
lib/features/cases/new_case_screen.dart:825 uses l10n.fieldRequired for the _ReasonsField error slot.

Add a dedicated ARB string in app_en.arb + app_de.arb — 'Choose at least one reason' / 'Waehle mindestens einen Grund' — and run flutter gen-l10n. Note :795 uses fieldRequired for the species dropdown too; that one is a genuine single-value field and can stay.

title: Dashboard carer workload lists members with zero open cases
description:
The 'Carer workload' card is ordered busiest first and then keeps going: in the current data three carers appear with a count of 0. A row that says a carer is carrying nothing is not workload information, and it makes the card longer than the fact it reports.

Found in a Dieter Rams design review (principle 10, as little design as possible).
design:
lib/features/dashboard/dashboard_screen.dart:263 (_CarerWorkloadCard) renders every row from carerWorkloadProvider.

Drop rows with openCases == 0, or fold them into one trailing line ('3 others with no open cases'). Keep the deactivated-member note (_subtitle, :286) — a deactivated member WITH open cases is exactly the row that needs acting on, so filter on the count, not on activity.
close_reason: Members with no open cases fold into one footnote line instead of a row each; BreakdownCard grew an optional footnote slot for it.

title: Intakes chart: maxY adds an axis label off the tick interval (0,3,6,9,12,14)
description:
The y-axis of 'Intakes over time' reads 0, 3, 6, 9, 12, 14 — the top label breaks the interval and lands about 11px above the one below it, so the two nearly collide.

Cause: `maxY: (tallest + step)` with tallest=11 and step=3 gives 14, which is not a multiple of the tick interval, and fl_chart labels it anyway.

Found in a Dieter Rams design review (principle 8, thorough).
design:
lib/features/statistics/intake_series_chart.dart:90.

Round the ceiling up to the next multiple of step instead: `maxY = ((tallest ~/ step) + 1) * step`. For tallest=11, step=3 that gives 12 and the ticks land 0,3,6,9,12. Check the case where tallest is already an exact multiple (tallest=12 -> 15, one clear step of headroom, which is what the current +step was buying).

lib/features/cases/eggs/egg_month_chart.dart is a second BarChart — check whether it computes maxY the same way.
close_reason: Fixed in d514694: maxY is now (tallest ~/ step + 1) * step, so the top label always lands on the tick interval; 11 with step 3 gives 12 (0,3,6,9,12) instead of 14. A tallest already on a tick keeps a full step of headroom (12 -> 15). Checked EggMonthChart as the issue asked: it uses maxY = tallest + 1 with interval 1, so its ceiling is always a multiple of the interval — no equivalent bug. Two tests added in intake_series_chart_test.dart pinning both cases.

title: Statistics: 'Rates over N ended cases' caption sits under all five KPI tiles but qualifies only two
description:
The caption 'Rates over 6 ended cases' is rendered below the whole KPI block, so it reads as a qualifier on Intakes, In care and Avg. time in care as well. It only describes the denominator of Release rate and Mortality — the other three are not rates and are not over ended cases.

Found in a Dieter Rams design review (principle 4, understandable).
design:
lib/features/statistics/statistics_screen.dart — the caption follows the KpiGrid rather than belonging to the two rate tiles.

Move it into the two rate tiles as a subcaption (KpiCard would need an optional third line), or place it immediately after them. Disclosing the denominator at all is the right call and must be kept — this is only about what it appears to qualify.
close_reason: Fixed in HEAD: the denominator moved into the two rate tiles as KpiCard's new optional 'note' line ('of 8 ended cases' / 'von 8 abgeschlossenen Fällen'), and the caption under the grid is gone. Took the subcaption option rather than 'place it after the rate tiles' because KpiGrid wraps at 2-4 columns depending on window width — on a phone the two rate tiles are in different rows, so no fixed position stays adjacent to both. statsRatesBasis renamed to statsRateBasis and reworded for a tile; the =0 form ('No case has ended in this period yet') is unchanged and now explains the em dash on each tile. Tests: kpi_grid_test.dart pins the note inside its own tile and absent from a tile without one; statistics_screen_test asserts it appears twice, once per rate tile.

title: Timeline-adjacent tiles format server dates without .toLocal()
description:
Sibling of federfall-ao0k, found while fixing it. date_field.dart offers formatEventDate() precisely because PocketBase hands back UTC and MaterialLocalizations does not convert. Several tiles/screens call materialL10n.formatMediumDate() straight on a model value instead, so a date-only render is off by a day whenever the instant falls within the local UTC offset of midnight (CET/CEST = the 22:00-00:00 UTC band, i.e. late-evening entries show yesterday).

Candidates (all read pbDate-normalised UTC):
- features/cases/case_summary_tile.dart:32-35 (admittedAt / foundAt / endedAt)
- features/cases/conditions/condition_entry_tile.dart:105 (resolvedAt)
- features/cases/markings/marking_tile.dart:129 (removedAt)
- features/cases/quarantine/quarantine_tile.dart:117 (quarantine until)
- features/cases/medications/medication_tiles.dart:135 (plan endedAt)
- features/animals/animal_detail_screen.dart:253, 425, 551
- features/statistics/intake_map_screen.dart:279 (admittedAt)

Not affected (verified): new_case_screen.dart:1265 and edit_case_intake_sheet.dart:231/256 hold local state; the egg_* call sites already pass .toLocal(); case_intake_draft._date() converts on restore.

Fix is to route each through formatEventDate (or .toLocal()) and pin it with a widget test asserting isUtc is false on the value handed to the formatter, so the assertion survives a UTC-clocked CI.
close_reason: Fixed in 4bf3dc4. Closed the class rather than the 9 sites: formatEventDate + formatDateMaybeTime collapsed into formatLocalDate (always .toLocal()s, DateStyle.medium/short, nullable), now the only date formatter allowed under lib/. Two source sweeps in date_field_test.dart enforce it (Material formatters banned outside date_field.dart; DateFormat statements need toLocal() unless they build a DateTime inline) — both verified to fail on an injected violation. Documented in CLAUDE.md. Note animal_detail_screen:425 was already correct; the other 8 listed sites were real.

title: Prescription sheet shows the end date in UTC (missing .toLocal())
description: prescription_sheet.dart initState: _startedAt gets .toLocal() but _endedAt = p?.endedAt does not (line 86). Medication.endedAt comes back UTC (pbDate normalises .toUtc()), and DateField/formatDateMaybeTime documents 'value is expected to already be in local time'. Editing an existing plan therefore displays the end time 1-2h off for German users (wrong day near midnight), and pickDateTime seeded with the UTC value means re-confirming the shown time shifts the stored instant by the offset. Every sibling sheet (administration_sheet, edit_case_intake_sheet) converts; this one field misses it. One-line fix: _endedAt = p?.endedAt?.toLocal().
close_reason: Fixed in 3943115: _endedAt = p?.endedAt?.toLocal(). Pinned by 'editing seeds both dates in local time' in medications_test.dart (asserts isUtc on the DateField value, so it holds under a UTC CI clock). Same-family call sites elsewhere filed as federfall-yok0.

title: Outcome facet: a fully-refined-away page shows a false 'no matches' and pagination stalls
description: CaseBrowseFeed._load (cases_browser.dart) narrows the server page with _refineToTerminalOutcome while the outcome facet is set. If every row of a page refines away, the state is cases.isEmpty && hasMore=true — and cases_screen.dart's _results() shows the 'no matches' EmptyView (no ListView, no tail, not even pull-to-refresh), so the next page is never fetched even though matches may exist beyond the cursor. Partial refinement has a milder cousin: a page shrunk to a few rows shows the spinner tail but loadMore only fires from the scroll listener, so nothing advances until the user drags. Fix idea: after refinement, keep fetching pages until at least one visible row lands or hasMore is false (bounded), or trigger loadMore when the tail builds.
close_reason: Fixed in 0f4d6ce: _load consumes further server pages while the outcome facet refines them away (bounded at 10, cursor advances so the next loadMore resumes); the screen only shows 'no matches' when !hasMore; PagedListTail gained an onLoad fired post-frame, wired in cases/animals/audit, so a list too short to scroll still advances.

title: Animals registry sorts case-sensitively (SQLite BINARY collation)
description:
federfall-trep moved the registry to a server-side, name-keyset-paged list (PbAnimalsRepository.browse, sortKey +name,+id). The order is now SQLite's, i.e. BINARY collation, where the old client sort was (a.animal.name ?? '').toLowerCase().compareTo(...).

Effect: an all-lowercase name sorts after every capitalised one — 'Zora' before 'berta'. Names in this app are almost always capitalised, so it is cosmetic and rare, but it IS a regression from the previous ordering.

Not fixable with a sort parameter: PocketBase orders by a column, and there is no LOWER(name) to order by. The options are (a) live with it, (b) add a lowercase sort column — either a real 'name_key' field the app maintains, or a view over animals with COALESCE(LOWER(a.name),'') that the registry pages instead (the view is read-only, which is all the registry needs). Note the secondary sort by species is gone too: keyset paging needs one column plus id.

Also worth knowing before touching it: umlauts were ALREADY code-unit sorted on the device ('ähre' after 'zora'), so that half is unchanged — only case is.

title: Dashboard cards are ragged and the wide layout is keyed on the wrong width
description:
Two concrete problems, both visible on a desktop window.

1. KPI tiles in the same row have different heights. Measured at 400px wide with the dashboard's own labels: 'Active cases' renders 176px tall and 'Intakes this year' 196px, because the label wraps to a second line and KpiGrid's Wrap gives each child its intrinsic height. Every row is therefore ragged along the bottom. Affects the statistics screen too — KpiGrid is shared.

2.
