The dashboard's two-column split is keyed on context.isExpanded, i.e. the WINDOW width (>=840), but a NavigationRail sits beside the content on medium/expanded (nav_shell.dart:88), so the body gets 80-200px less than that. At the threshold each column is under 400px, and KpiGrid clamps to a minimum of two columns, so tiles render ~190px wide against a documented 240px minimum readable tile. The statistics screen already avoids this by keying on LayoutBuilder constraints (federfall e22cc71).

The dashboard also has no ContentBounds cap, so it stretches edge-to-edge on a 4K window while every other flat page is capped, and its card spacing is ad-hoc (a Card margin on Today, a Padding on the workload card, a SizedBox in the caseload) where the statistics screen spaces one way.

Adopt the statistics mechanism: LayoutBuilder on the width actually available, ContentBounds, one spacing rule.
close_reason: Closed

title: record .wait hides RepositoryException from the app's error mapping
description:
`(a, b, ...).wait` (the record extension) reports a failure as `ParallelWaitError<...>`, NOT as the underlying error — verified: a StateError thrown inside one future comes back as `ParallelWaitError<(int?, int?, int?), (AsyncError?, AsyncError?, AsyncError?)>`. `Future.wait` over a homogeneous List propagates the original error unchanged.

That matters because the app's error mapping tests the concrete type:
  - `isNetworkError(e)` => `e is RepositoryException && kind == network` (core/error/error_message.dart:48)
  - `loadErrorMessage` falls through to `errorGenericTitle` for anything else

So on a dropped connection any provider gathering with record `.wait` renders a GENERIC error instead of the offline copy, and — worse — misses `AsyncValueView`'s deliberate branch that keeps already-loaded data on screen through a network blip (async_value_view.dart:49). The user loses the content they were looking at, for a condition they can only wait out.

federfall-s0wk fixed BOTH providers in dashboard_providers.dart (homogeneous `Future.wait` for the counts; repo providers watched synchronously and awaited one at a time). The remaining sites:
  - features/worklist/worklist_providers.dart:122, :142
  - features/reminders/reminders.dart:67
  - features/cases/cases_browser.dart:230, :238
  - features/cases/case_facets.dart:115, :120

Fix per site: watch synchronously, then await the already-started futures one at a time. Note the trap carerWorkload hit — starting a second future early and awaiting it SECOND leaves a window where its failure has no handler, so if the first await throws you get an unhandled async error instead. Either await in the order the futures can fail, or accept one serial round trip.

A shared unwrap helper is not possible: ParallelWaitError's `errors` is a RECORD, not iterable.

Worth a widget test per fixed site: pump with a repo throwing RepositoryException(kind: network) and assert the offline copy renders, not errorGenericTitle. Such a test needs `ProviderContainer(retry: (_, _) => null)` — see the riverpod3-retry-hangs-error-tests memory.
close_reason: Closed

title: case_viewer_counts has no reader — drop it or make it the org-wide roll-up
description:
federfall-s0wk shipped the client half using server-side counts on `cases` (casesRepo.count() per status) rather than the `case_viewer_counts` view added in migration 1700000070, so that view is now dead weight: nothing reads it.

Why it was not used: the view is VIEWER-scoped (one row per active-carer/share recipient), but the dashboard is org-wide for coordinators and supervisors — `cases`.listRule grants them the whole org (1700000010_access_rules.js:93) and every KPI tile taps through to `CaseQuery(allScope: true)`, i.e. that same org-wide list. Filtering the view `viewer = @request.auth.id` would have shown a coordinator their personal load beside a list of the whole org's cases; summing all org rows instead double-counts a case shared with several people and drops cases with no active carer at all. The migration's comment claiming it 'reproduces exactly what the dashboard counts today' holds for a carer only.

Counting on `cases` avoids the problem entirely — the list rule scopes a count exactly as it scopes a list, so one code path is correct for every role.

Two ways to resolve:
  (a) drop the view in a new migration (keep `case_carer_load`, which IS read — it backs openByCarer), and trim its half of the '[dashboard count views]' block in tests/test_rules.py; or
  (b) keep it and add an org roll-up row (COUNT(DISTINCT case) per org+status, coordinator/supervisor-readable) so the dashboard can go back to one request per role instead of four counts.

(b) is only worth it if the four extra one-row requests per dashboard open turn out to matter; measure before doing it. Either way this is backend work needing a live PB for the rule tests.
close_reason: Option (a): 1700000071 drops the view; test_rules.py trimmed and pins that it is gone. 666/666 rule tests pass against a live PB.

title: Form sheets repeat the same scaffold: padding, busy, error text, unsaved guard
description:
A block of ~35-40 lines recurs across the entry sheets: guardUnsavedChanges + SafeArea + the same viewInsets padding, the same _busy/_error state, the same RepositoryException -> errorMessage / Object -> reportCaughtError + errorGenericTitle handler, and the same error Text styled with colorScheme.error.

Measured overlap (identical lines, blocks >= 6):
- add_animal_sheet.dart <-> edit_animal_sheet.dart: 106 of ~175 lines each (largest run 42) — these two are very nearly the same form twice
- egg_entry_sheet.dart <-> journal_entry_sheet.dart: 93
- codelist_admin / edit_profile_sheet / invite_member_sheet / edit_case_intake_sheet / org_settings_screen / confirm_reset_screen share the same save-and-catch block
- follow_up_sheet.dart <-> vet_appointment_sheet.dart: 45

Do NOT merge the sheets — one sheet per record kind is the deliberate timeline pattern (federfall-ui-prefers-unified-consistent-views). Extract the SCAFFOLD instead: a FormSheet widget owning padding + unsaved guard + busy + the error line, and a shared submit helper wrapping the two catch clauses. add_animal/edit_animal are the exception: they are close enough to be one sheet with a nullable animal, and should be looked at as such.

Value is consistency as much as size: the error handling is security-adjacent (reportCaughtError vs. showing a raw message) and it is currently re-typed each time.
close_reason: The scaffold already existed (ui/form_sheet.dart: FormSheetState + SheetScaffold, 17 adopters) — the fix was adoption, not extraction. Converted add_animal, edit_animal, edit_profile, invite_member, edit_case_intake, the codelist sheet, plus org_settings and confirm_reset (mixin only, they are screens). Added saveIcon and clearBusyOnSuccess to cover the two cases the mixin could not express. member_management (no Form, busy toggled around a dialog), login and new_case left hand-rolled deliberately. Net -370 lines.

comments.author: Jan-Henrik Bruhn
comments.text: Correction to this issue's own premise: the scaffold did NOT need extracting — it already existed as ui/form_sheet.dart (FormSheetState mixin + SheetScaffold), adopted by 17 sheets. The duplication was the sheets that never adopted it. So the fix is adoption, not extraction.

title: The animal re-ID search picker is copy-pasted between merge and egg-reassign
description:
merge_animal_screen.dart:251-341 and egg_reassign_sheet.dart:339-427 hold the same widget twice: the same constructor (controller/query/excludeAnimalId/enabled/onSearch/onPick), the same search field, the same reidSearchProvider(query).when(...) with the same loading/error/data handling and the same exclude filter. ~90 shared lines, the largest identical run 49.

Both are 'pick another animal of this org by re-ID search', so extract one widget (features/animals/animal_search_picker.dart) and let both call it. The two screens differ in what they do with the pick, which is the callback — nothing else has to move.

Worth doing because the behaviour is subtle: excluding the current animal, and how an empty/failed search renders. Two copies means the next fix to either lands in one of them.
close_reason: Extracted as features/animals/animal_search_picker.dart (AnimalSearchPicker); merge_animal_screen and egg_reassign_sheet both call it, with the field label as the only parameter.

title: Dashboard still aggregates client-side, and its year boundary disagrees with statistics
description:
federfall-nmwi moved the statistics screen's figures server-side (GET /api/federfall/stats, pb_hooks/lib_stats.js). The dashboard was left alone, and two things about it are now out of step.

**The year boundary disagrees.** buildDashboardSummary counts an intake with `admitted.year == now.year` (dashboard_providers.dart:81) where `admittedAt` is UTC — pbDate calls .toUtc() — and `now` is local. The statistics route resolves a year at the CALLER's midnight via ?tzOffsetMinutes=, which is what makes it agree with the annual report (test_rules.py asserts exactly this). So a bird admitted 1 Jan 00:30 in UTC+1 is a last-year intake on the dashboard and a this-year intake on statistics. Same figure, same org, two answers.

'Active' is likewise two definitions: the dashboard counts `status != disposed`, the statistics route counts cases with no terminal disposition. The disposition hooks keep those in step today; nothing enforces it.

**It still pulls two full collections to the device.** dashboardSummary reads casesRepo.list() + animalsRepo.list() unpaginated on every dashboard open — the load pattern federfall-80tc removed from the CSV export and federfall-nmwi removed from statistics.

Why it was not simply pointed at the new route: that route is org-wide by construction (case_report_rows is a coordinator/supervisor view) while the dashboard must work for a carer in their own scope (own + shared). Folding it in needs a caller-scoped mode server-side — a view or route that respects the access rules per caller — not just a new consumer. Scope this before implementing: the cheap half (fixing the year boundary to use local time, so the two screens stop disagreeing) is worth doing on its own even if the read stays client-side.
close_reason: Closed

title: case_report.pb.js still carries its own copy of the timezone helpers
description:
federfall-nmwi introduced pb_hooks/lib_stats.js, which owns the caller-local time helpers (lastSundayUTC / berlinOffsetMinutes / parseMs / partsOf / pbStamp) that annual_report.pb.js used to duplicate — a required module is the one thing isolated JSVM handlers can share.

case_report.pb.js is where that duplication originally came from and still has its own copy, so a fix to the DST rule or to the date parsing now has to be made twice. Point it at lib_stats.js's timeContext() as well.

Only the time helpers apply — the per-case report gathers its own rows (the whole case timeline, not case_report_rows), so there is nothing else to share.
close_reason: Extraction shipped in 58d943f (lib_time.js); this cleans up the comment that commit truncated.

title: Full-text search over journal entries and exam findings
description:
Case search matches structured identity only — case number, animal name, and since federfall-78b ring/chip codes (cases_screen.dart _SearchBar, cases_browser.dart filters). The clinical narrative is not searchable: journal_entries.text, exam findings and free-text condition notes hold the part of the record a carer actually writes, and there is no way to find it again. "Which bird had that wing droop we splinted", "what did we do last time we saw this" — the answer is in a journal entry nobody can retrieve without remembering the case.

Notes:
- Access rules must hold. A journal entry is readable only through its case, and cases are private-by-default with opt-in sharing (1700000010_access_rules.js). A search that returns a snippet from a case the user cannot open leaks the narrative — the very thing the rules protect. Filter server-side; do not filter results in the app.
- PocketBase filter ~ over a text field is a LIKE scan. Fine at one associations volume, but check it before assuming — journal_entries grows fastest of any collection here. If it does not hold, SQLite FTS5 via a view or a hook route is the escalation.
- Aviary-scoped journal entries (federfall-d5co.2, 1700000053) have no case, so they carry their own scope — cover them or exclude them deliberately, not by accident.
- Result shape: a matched entry is not a case row. Needs its own result tile (snippet + date + which case) rather than pretending it is a case hit, and the browser filters (cases_browser.dart) have to make room for a second result kind.

Wire contract: additive — feat:.
acceptance_criteria: Searching a phrase from a journal entry finds the entry and opens its case; an entry in a case the signed-in user cannot read never appears in results (rule test); aviary-scoped entries are handled deliberately.

title: Statistics: intakes over time, year-over-year and outcome rates
description:
REQUIREMENTS.md §10 asks for "intakes over time" and it never shipped. federfall-93o delivered totals (total/open/avg time in care), three breakdown cards (outcomes, species, conditions) and the intake map — every one of them a snapshot of now. Nothing in the app answers "is this year busier than last", which is the first question an annual report asks.

Missing:
- A time series of intakes (by month, and by week in season), with the previous year behind it for comparison.
- Outcome RATES, not just counts. federfall-93o counts dispositions; the number that matters to a rehab is the share released of cases that ended, and it cannot be read off a count breakdown when intake volume moves. Same for mortality.
- A period selector on the screen as a whole. The annual report already picks a year (annual_report_sheet.dart, ?year= on the hook, boundaries in the callers zone via ?tzOffsetMinutes=) — the statistics screen has no period concept at all, and the two should agree on what "2026" means.

Where it computes: statisticsProvider aggregates client-side over every readable case. A monthly series over all history is more than that should carry — see federfall-80tc, which hit exactly this loading three full collections on-device. The case_report_rows view (federfall-dk0c) already exists server-side and is the natural place, or a small aggregate route beside annual_report.pb.js.

Charting: egg_month_chart.dart already draws a per-month bar chart for egg records — look there first rather than adding a dependency.

Wire contract: a new route or new optional params, so additive — feat:.
acceptance_criteria: Statistics shows intakes per month with the prior year for comparison, a release/mortality rate over ended cases, and a period selector whose year boundaries match the annual report; the screen does not pull every case on-device to do it.
close_reason: Statistics now picks a period and reports intakes per month against the previous year, plus release/mortality rates over ended cases. Aggregation is server-side in GET /api/federfall/stats; period, rows and every figure come from pb_hooks/lib_stats.js, which annual_report.pb.js also requires — so the screen and the PDF resolve a year identically (asserted in test_rules.py). No client-side aggregation left. Follow-up filed for case_report.pb.js's duplicated tz helpers.

title: Nest-mates: admit siblings together and weigh them as a group
description:
A clutch of two or three squabs from one nest arrives as one find, and Federfall has no way to say so. new_case_screen.dart is a single-animal wizard, so the carer runs it three times and re-types the same finder, find location, admission reason and dates each time. The three cases then have no relationship: nothing on a case says "this bird has nest-mates", and the daily weigh-in of a brood is three separate navigations into three case timelines.

Note "clutch" is already taken in this codebase: federfall-4agw uses it for eggs LAID in care. This is about birds ADMITTED together — pick a distinct word (Geschwister / nest-mates).

Two halves, separable:

(a) Sibling intake. After a successful intake, offer "admit another from the same find" that carries the finder, find location, found_at/admitted_at and admission reasons over and starts at the animal step. Cheapest version needs no schema at all. Watch the intake idempotency key (1700000050) — a repeat submission must not be mistaken for a retry of the first.

(b) The link itself, and what it buys. Either a nullable sibling_group relation on cases, or derive it from finder + find location + admission date. Then: a nest-mates strip on case detail linking the siblings, and a group weigh-in that records one weight per bird in a single sheet. Weights are animal-scoped (federfall-5yg.4), so the batch write is n creates in one sheet, not a new record kind. A contagious diagnosis on one nest-mate is also exactly when you want to see the others — this is the same data federfall-8nm1s flag has no consumer for.

Decide (a) alone might be most of the value for a fraction of the work; do not build (b) speculatively.

Wire contract: additive if a new optional field, so feat:.
acceptance_criteria: Admitting a second bird from the same find does not re-type the finder or the location; siblings are reachable from each others case; a brood can be weighed in one pass.

title: Allow document attachments (PDF) on cases and journal entries
description:
Uploads are images only: 1700000048_upload_mime_allowlist.js:20 allowlists exactly image/jpeg,png,webp,gif on cases.intake_photos, journal_entries.attachments and animals.photo. So the one thing a clinical record most needs to carry — a vet report, a lab result, an X-ray, a euthanasia certificate, a transfer note — cannot be attached to a case at all. Today it gets photographed with a phone or lives outside Federfall entirely.

The allowlist is not an accident: federfall-8a5 closed a stored-XSS hole (a member uploads evil.svg/.html, any same-org member can mint a file token, the file is served from the SPA/Admin origin and executes there). Widening it must not reopen that.

Scope:
- New migration adding application/pdf to the two attachment fields (NOT animals.photo — an avatar is an image).
- Serve attachments with Content-Disposition: attachment so a PDF is never rendered inline in the app origin, and check the CSP in web_headers.pb.js covers object/embed. This is the part that keeps 8a5 fixed; the migration alone does not.
- Non-image tile: the journal/gallery paths assume Image.memory. A PDF needs a file-type tile (icon + filename + size) and must not reach the image viewer. case_photo_gallery.dart and journal_entry_tile.dart both branch on this.
- Case report PDF (case_report.pb.js) and the intake photo promotion (1700000065_animal_photo_from_intake.js) both assume image attachments — check neither picks up a PDF.

Wire contract: additive (a widened mimeTypes allowlist and a new optional file kind), so feat:, not feat!:.
acceptance_criteria: A PDF can be attached to a journal entry and downloads rather than rendering inline; a .svg/.html upload is still rejected; the non-image tile does not open the image viewer; animals.photo still accepts images only; rule tests cover the accept and the reject.

title: Wide admin: system/browser back still deselects before leaving
description:
On expanded widths the app-bar arrow beside 'Administration' now leaves the hub in one press (go(home), see management_screen.dart). The SYSTEM/browser back button still follows real history, so /admin/audit -> back -> /admin (hub with an empty right pane) -> back -> app.

Root cause is structural, measured 2026-08-04: in go_router a nested child route ALWAYS materialises its parent page (matches=2 for both go() and replace()), so the deselected /admin state is a genuine history entry and cannot be collapsed away by choosing a different navigation call.

Options if this is worth closing:
- put the section in a query param (/admin?section=audit) so there is one page and one history entry -- but then compact loses its section->hub back step, or the URL shape has to differ per width;
- intercept via PopScope on expanded to skip the intermediate (works for Android back, cannot override browser back on web).

Deliberately left as-is: the visible affordance is correct, and browser back following browser history is defensible.

title: Audit: a directly-edited exam finding lands on no case
description:
exam_findings has no `case` relation (1700000025: exam, system, status, note, org) — it reaches its case only through `exam`. emit() derives case_id from record.getString("case"), so an exam_finding.* event written through the collection API has an empty case_id and case_label: it cannot be found in the per-case activity section of the case it is actually about, and the audit screen's case correlation misses it.

Findings written by the exam ROUTE are fine — that path emits exam.saved against the exam, which does carry the case. This only affects a finding created/updated/deleted directly, which the access rules still allow (the reason EXAM_FINDING_* actions exist at all).

Fix: resolve the parent exam's case in emitRecordChange (one indexed read, same shape as the disposition refinement), or pass caseId explicitly. The uninformative-event sweep does not catch it because the row does carry `changes`.
close_reason: Closed

title: Audit feed: a failed page load throws into unawaited() and never reaches the user
description:
AuditFeed.loadMore() sets state back and then rethrows via Error.throwWithStackTrace. The only caller is the scroll listener in audit_screen.dart:68, which invokes it inside unawaited(), so the error becomes an unhandled zone error: the supervisor sees the spinner stop and nothing else. The doc comment claims 'the error surfaces once' — it surfaces in the log, not in the UI. Either surface it (a retry row at the end of the list, or a snackbar) or drop the rethrow and record the failure in AuditFeedState.

Also in the same file: AuditFeedState.copyWith cannot clear `cursor` (`cursor ?? this.cursor`). Harmless today because loadMore builds a fresh state, a trap later.
close_reason: Closed

title: emitLoginFailed's dedup query cannot use an index
description: lib_audit.js emitLoginFailed() filters audit_events on `action = ... && actor_id = ... && created >= ...` with no `org`. Every index on the collection leads with `org` (1700000068), so the dedup read cannot use one and degrades toward a scan of a table that only grows. It runs on EVERY failed attempt, not just the one that writes a row, so a login-failure storm scans repeatedly. record.getString("org") is already in hand one line below — adding it to the filter makes it an idx_audit_events_org_actor hit.
close_reason: Closed

title: Audit: the screen offers two filters while the query layer supports six
description:
AuditQuery already carries actorId, actions, subjectId and subjectCollection, and filterFor() builds bound filters for all of them (audit_events_repository.dart:10-100, 145-187). The screen exposes severity and period only (audit_screen.dart:88-94).

'What did this person do' and 'who deleted this' are the questions a supervisor arrives with, and the data layer can already answer them.

Fix: an actor chip (org members + the machine actors, matching on the snapshot id so a deleted member is still findable) and a domain chip that maps a domain to the AuditActions whose wire starts with it — 80-odd actions is too many to pick from, ~20 domains is not.
acceptance_criteria: actor and domain filters narrow the feed through the existing bound filter; combining them with severity and period composes; no filter string is built by hand.
close_reason: Person chip (org roster via orgMembersProvider, matched on the snapshot actor_id so a deleted member is still findable, plus the machine actors — which needed a new AuditQuery.actorKind, since a system row has no actor id at all) and Area chip (6 AuditTopics, each an explicit list of actions fed to the existing actions filter; a test asserts the partition is total and disjoint so a new action cannot be unreachable by filter). Caught in passing: 11 chips now overflow the row, which broke two existing filter tests tapping an off-screen chip — all chip taps go through a scroll-into-view helper.

title: Audit: decide whether a dashboard write to aviary_stays should be logged
description:
aviary_stays is exempt from auditing (federfall-qt96.3): its create/update/delete rules are null (1700000052) and every row is written by aviary_stays.pb.js from animals.current_aviary, so a request hook could only ever fire for one caller — a superuser typing into the admin dashboard. The human action, moving a bird, is audited as the animal.updated that caused it.

The residue: a superuser hand-writing an aviary_stays row IS unaudited. Narrow, but it is the one caller the tamper guard and the whole superuser-actor path exist for.

Decide: add it to COLLECTION_ACTIONS (costs three registry actions + ARB strings for a path that should never happen, and risks reading as a duplicate of the animal.updated beside it), or keep the exemption and say so explicitly in the NOT_AUDITED reason. Cheap either way; the point is that it be a decision on the record rather than a side effect of how the hooks work.
close_reason:
DECIDED (by the user, 2026-08-04): keep the exemption. aviary_stays has null write rules and is written only by aviary_stays.pb.js from animals.current_aviary, so the only caller a request hook could ever see there is a superuser in the PocketBase admin UI — and that event would sit beside the animal.updated that caused the same move, reading as a duplicate.

The reasoning is now written where it is enforced: the NOT_AUDITED entry in test_rules.py and the COLLECTION_ACTIONS comment in lib_audit.js both say it is a decision, not an artefact of how hooks fire.

title: Audit: retention cron + Datenauskunft inclusion + operator docs
description:
cronAdd("auditRetention", "30 3 * * *") honouring org.settings.audit_retention_days (default 730, 0 = keep forever), deleting only rows past the floor the tamper guard allows. Emits audit.purged with a count.
Audit rows are personal data about STAFF, so they must appear in the GDPR data-subject export (federfall-qocb) — coordinate the shape there.
Cron jobs are invisible to test_rules.py: verify the documented way (copy pb_hooks to a tempdir, rewrite the schedule to * * * * *, run a throwaway container).
Document the collection, the settings key and the ip/user_agent opt-in in the self-host docs.
acceptance_criteria: A row older than the window is deleted, a newer one is not, and the tamper guard still refuses a manual delete of a recent row; verified against a live container.
close_reason:
auditRetention cron in pb_hooks/audit.pb.js + a DEPLOYMENT.md section for operators (who can read the log, the append-only guarantee, what it never contains, retention, and the IP opt-in).

Verified live the documented way (pb_hooks copied to a tempdir, schedule rewritten to every minute): an org with a tiny window had all 4 rows purged and kept a single audit.purged row with count=4; an org with audit_retention_days=0 kept all 3. The tamper guard refusing manual deletes of recent rows is already pinned by test_rules.py.

DEFERRED, not done: Datenauskunft inclusion. federfall-qocb does not exist yet — a note is on that issue saying it must include audit_events rows (personal data about staff) and emit gdpr.export.

title: German Excel opens the report CSV as one column (comma delimiter)
description: The annual-report CSV (federfall-dk0c, pb_hooks/annual_report.pb.js) is comma-delimited with a UTF-8 BOM and CRLF — RFC 4180, and what the superseded Dart encoder emitted. German-locale Excel/LibreOffice expect ';' and will show a comma-delimited file as a single column unless the user goes through the import assistant. Options: a leading 'sep=;' line (Excel-specific, not RFC), a ';' delimiter for lang=de, or a ?delimiter= param. Deliberately NOT changed in dk0c: it would silently alter the bytes of an existing export people may already parse.

title: Annual report: let the user pick an arbitrary year
description: federfall-dk0c's export sheet offers this year / last year / all time (SegmentedButton, mirroring intake_map_screen's _Period). The route itself already takes any ?year=, so re-filing an older year (2023) needs only a picker — e.g. a dropdown seeded from the years that actually have intakes, which would need a distinct-year query or a small view. Left out of dk0c deliberately: the filing case is 'the year just ended', which the default covers.
close_reason: Closed

title: Calendar export (.ics) for vet appointments
description:
Follow-up to federfall-fnpo (vet appointments). On-device reminders cover the
"don't forget" case, but a carer who plans their day in a real calendar
(Nextcloud, Google, whatever the phone is synced to) still has to retype the
appointment. Add an export action so it lands in the system calendar.

## Shape

An overflow-menu action on the vet-appointment tile (and/or its sheet) that
builds a minimal **iCalendar (`.ics`) VEVENT** and hands it to the OS:

- `UID` = the PocketBase record id + a stable domain suffix, so re-exporting the
  same appointment **updates** the calendar entry instead of duplicating it
  (paired with `SEQUENCE`, bumped from the record's `updated`).
- `DTSTART`/`DTEND` in UTC (`…Z`) from `starts_at`; there is no duration field,
  so pick a sane default (30 min) — do not invent a new backend field for this.
- `SUMMARY` = vet + case number/animal name; `DESCRIPTION` = the reason;
  `LOCATION` = the vet field if it looks like an address (or just leave it in
  SUMMARY and skip LOCATION — simpler and never wrong).
- `VALARM` mirroring the user's configured reminder lead time, so the calendar
  reminds them the same way the app does.
- CRLF line endings and 75-octet line folding — some calendar apps are strict.

Delivery: write the `.ics` to a temp file and share it via `share_plus` (already
a dependency) rather than adding a calendar-plugin dependency. On Android/iOS the
share sheet offers the calendar app; on web it becomes a download. That keeps
this a pure client feature — no backend, no new permissions, no plugin.

Worth deciding while implementing: whether a whole-case export (all appointments
+ open follow-ups as one `VCALENDAR`) is the more useful action. It is barely
more code and probably what a carer with several birds actually wants.

## Not in scope

Two-way calendar sync, CalDAV, or subscribing to a live feed — that needs a
server-side authenticated ICS endpoint and a whole token story. File separately
if it ever comes up.

## Acceptance

- Exporting an appointment produces an `.ics` that imports cleanly into at least
  one real calendar app (Nextcloud/Thunderbird or the Android calendar).
- Re-exporting after editing the appointment updates the existing event rather
  than creating a second one.
- Strings in `app_en.arb` + `app_de.arb`; `dart format`/`flutter analyze` clean,
  `flutter test` green.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Jan-Henrik Bruhn
comments.text:
Implemented with `add_2_calendar` (per the user's call), NOT the `.ics` +
`share_plus` shape this issue was written around. The trade-offs differ, so
recording what actually shipped:

**What the plugin does:** hands an `ACTION_INSERT` intent (Android) /
`EKEventEditViewController` (iOS) to the OS with the fields prefilled — the
user confirms and saves in their own calendar app. Nothing is written behind
their back, and no `WRITE_CALENDAR` permission is requested.

**Consequently NOT met — the UID/SEQUENCE acceptance criterion:** there is no
event identity to address, so re-exporting after an edit creates a SECOND
entry rather than updating the first. The plugin's API has no hook for this
(an `.ics` with a stable `UID` was the only way to get it). Mitigations: the
action is explicit rather than automatic on save, the user sees the editor
before anything is stored, and the doc comment on `_addToCalendar` says so
plainly. If duplicate entries turn out to bite in practice, the fix is the
original `.ics`/`share_plus` shape — file it fresh.

**Also platform-asymmetric:** the reminder lead is carried as an iOS `EKAlarm`
only. Android's insert intent has no alarm extra, so there the calendar
applies its own default notice. The lead itself resolves exactly like the app
reminder (record override → device default, nothing when muted) and is
deliberately NOT gated on the device-wide reminder switch — someone who turned
notifications off in favour of their calendar is who exports this.

**Dropped from scope:** whole-case export (one `VCALENDAR` with every
appointment). The plugin adds one event per call, so that would be N modal
hand-offs — not the "barely more code" it would have been with an `.ics`.

Other notes: LOCATION is omitted as the issue suggested (the `vet` field is a
practice NAME, not an address). The `<queries>`/`ACTION_INSERT` manifest block
is load-bearing, not boilerplate — the plugin calls `resolveActivity()`, which
returns null for undeclared intents under API 30+ package visibility, so
without it the action reports "nothing was added" on every modern device. The
action lives in the tile's edit menu, so it needs `canEdit`; a read-only viewer
of a shared case can't export (TimelineEntryMenu requires an edit action, so a
calendar-only menu would mean restructuring it — not worth it here).

title: Vector map path: fix the 256/512 tileOffset mismatch, and spike flutter_map_maplibre
description:
Raster is the default as of the map-mode flip (vector rendering was judged ugly and slow). Vector stays supported — a self-hosted OpenFreeMap/OpenMapTiles stack is much cheaper to serve than raster — so it is worth making it not-bad. Two separate items:

1. CHEAP, one line. MapTileLayer passes no tileOffset, so VectorTileLayer sits at TileOffset.DEFAULT (256px tiles, zoomOffset 0). OpenFreeMap's liberty style is OpenMapTiles-schema, authored for 512px tiles the way MapLibre GL renders them — that is TileOffset.mapbox (zoomOffset -1). Mismatched reference scale makes label sizes and line widths render wrong, a known cause of coarse-looking OpenMapTiles output in vector_map_tiles. Needs a human to eyeball the before/after; not verifiable from tests.

   Note while measuring: VectorTileLayer's 'concurrency' has NO EFFECT in debug mode (vector_tile_layer.dart:92), so debug-build impressions of vector performance are misleading. Judge in --profile.

   Also note layerMode already defaults to VectorTileLayerMode.raster, the package's best-frame-rate path — there is no free perf left there. The ceiling is inherent: Dart canvas rasterization, no GPU.

2. BIGGER. flutter_map_maplibre (real MapLibre GL, GPU) is the only path to genuinely good vector rendering. Previously deferred over CSP — see the federfall-map-provider-openfreemap memory — but that reads worse than it is: worker-src 'self' blob: is already in the policy (web_headers.pb.js:113), which is what maplibre-gl-js needs beyond script-src 'self', and vendoring maplibre-gl.js/.css same-origin is the pattern already used for Roboto. The real risk is platform-view interop: an HtmlElementView under a skwasm-rendered flutter_map, with app markers composited on top. Spike that before committing to it.

Do (1) first — if it makes vector acceptable, (2) may not be worth it.

comments.author: Jan-Henrik Bruhn
comments.text: Dependency-side note from the 2026-08-07 dep sweep: nothing moved upstream, so this is unaffected. vector_map_tiles 9.0.0-beta.11 (2026-07-23) is still the newest 9.x, and the 10.x line has had no release since 10.0.0-beta.2 on 2025-10-19 — i.e. no new 10.x to retry the web build against. The 9.x pin stands for the reason recorded in the federfall-map-provider-openfreemap memory. Also still pinned by it: vector_tile 2.0.1 (4.0.0 available).

title: Proxy map tiles through PocketBase so the provider key can stay secret
description:
Follow-up to federfall-el1f, which made the tile source runtime-configurable via /api/federfall/info including an optional FEDERFALL_MAP_API_KEY.

That endpoint is unauthenticated, so the key is public by construction. Acceptable (a web bundle exposes its key to devtools anyway, and the release APK is a public download) but it reduces extraction to a single GET.

A tile proxy in pb_hooks — same shape as geocode.pb.js — would fix that properly and pick up two more wins:
  * the key never leaves the server
  * tiles become same-origin, which retires the CSP origin derivation in web_headers.pb.js entirely
  * server-side caching/rate-limiting, like the geocode proxy already does

Costs to weigh before starting: all tile bandwidth flows through PocketBase, cache storage/eviction has to be designed (tiles are far higher volume than geocode results), and both client paths need a base-URL switch (flutter_map TileLayer template + vector_map_tiles StyleReader, whose style JSON references absolute source URLs that would need rewriting server-side).

Probably only worth it for operators on a keyed commercial provider — keep the direct path as the default.

title: Detect app/server version skew mid-session, not just at login
description:
federfall-1wm added the major-version compatibility gate but only enforces it on
the login screen (`lib/features/auth/login_screen.dart`, via
`serverCompatibilityProvider`). A signed-in session never re-checks.

That leaves the realistic window open: the operator runs `docker compose pull`
while carers are signed in and working. Their app keeps issuing calls against a
backend that no longer speaks their wire contract, and they see whatever
incidental error that produces (a 404 on a hook route, a missing field) rather
than "update required".

`serverInfoProvider` is `keepAlive` and fetched once per app launch, so it is
also the thing holding the stale answer.

Approach (not settled — decide when picking this up):
- Invalidate `serverInfoProvider` on `AppLifecycleState.resumed` and re-evaluate
  `serverCompatibilityProvider`. Cheap, and resume is when a container upgrade
  has most likely happened since the app was last foregrounded.
- Optionally also re-probe when a repository call fails in a way that smells
  like skew (404 on a `/api/federfall/*` route the app knows should exist).
- Surface it above the shell rather than per-screen — a blocking overlay or a
  non-dismissible dialog on `NavShell`, since no screen is usable once the
  contract is broken. Note the login screen's notice is a `_UpdateRequiredNotice`
  widget in `login_screen.dart`; extract it if both paths should share the copy.

Keep the fail-open bias from `checkServerCompatibility`: a failed re-probe must
never eject a working session.

title: flutter_web_auth_2 applies Kotlin Gradle Plugin — future Flutter will fail the build
description:
Every Android build now warns:

  WARNING: Your app uses the following plugins that apply Kotlin Gradle Plugin (KGP): flutter_web_auth_2
  Future versions of Flutter will fail to build if your app uses plugins that apply KGP.

flutter_web_auth_2 5.0.3 is the newest stable release, so there is no fix to upgrade into yet. The 6.0.0 line exists only as prereleases (6.0.0-alpha.1 … alpha.5) — check whether one of those has migrated to Built-in Kotlin, and whether it is stable enough to adopt (it is on the OIDC login path).

Migration guide: https://docs.flutter.dev/release/breaking-changes/migrate-to-built-in-kotlin/for-app-developers

Deadline is whenever Flutter turns the warning into a hard error, so this should be resolved before a Flutter major bump, not after.

comments.author: Jan-Henrik Bruhn
comments.text:
Rechecked 2026-08-07. The fix EXISTS but is still prerelease-only, so not adopted.

flutter_web_auth_2 6.0.0-alpha.0's changelog says "Regenerate entire project skeleton (also migrates to built-in Kotlin)" — that is precisely the KGP migration this ticket needs. Latest stable is still 5.0.3; the 6.0.0 line is now at alpha.6 (published today, 2026-08-07 — it is actively worked on, not abandoned).

6.0.0-alpha.6 requires sdk ^3.12.0 / flutter >=3.44.0, both of which we already satisfy, so it would resolve today. Not taking it: this sits on the OIDC login path and an alpha there risks locking users out, while the warning is still only a warning.

One breaking API change to handle when adopting: `cleanUpDanglingCalls` was renamed to `clearAllDanglingCalls` in alpha.0. We do not call either today (grep clean), so the migration is currently a version bump only.

Recheck when 6.0.0 goes stable, or sooner if a Flutter beta turns the KGP warning into an error.

title: Dependency ceiling: riverpod 3.4.x / freezed 4 / analyzer 13+ cohort is blocked upstream
description:
Two independent ceilings keep a cohort of deps pinned (verified 2026-07-26, Flutter 3.44.3 / Dart 3.12.2). The riverpod one is BINDING; the Flutter one only matters afterwards.

== Ceiling 1 (binding): riverpod's analyzer ^12 cap ==
riverpod_generator 4.0.4 and riverpod_lint 3.1.4 both require analyzer ^12.0.0, holding analyzer at 12.1.0. They also pin riverpod to exactly 3.3.2, which pins flutter_riverpod 3.3.2 and riverpod_annotation 4.0.3.

The newer versions cannot be adopted because upstream published a contradictory set: riverpod_generator 4.0.6 and riverpod_lint 3.1.6 require analyzer ^13.0.0 AND riverpod_analyzer_utils 1.0.0-dev.10, but dev.10 (still the newest) requires analyzer ^12.0.0. Unresolvable for anyone, not just us. Nothing to do until riverpod publishes a riverpod_analyzer_utils that accepts analyzer 13.

Fixing this alone (no Flutter change needed) unblocks: flutter_riverpod/riverpod 3.4.1, riverpod_annotation 4.0.5, riverpod_generator 4.0.6, riverpod_lint 3.1.6, analyzer 13.0.0 (13.0.0 still accepts meta ^1.18.0, so it fits current Flutter), freezed 4.0.0-dev.3, dart_style 3.1.9.

== Ceiling 2: Flutter SDK exact pins ==
Flutter 3.44.x pins meta: 1.18.0, test_api: 0.7.11, matcher: 0.12.19, vector_math: 2.2.0 and flutter_localizations pins intl: 0.20.2 — all EXACT, so those move only with Flutter. analyzer 13.1.0+ needs meta ^1.18.3, capping analyzer at 13.0.0 here.

Upgrading within stable does NOT help: 3.44.8 (newest stable, 2026-07-23) has byte-identical pins to 3.44.3 — same Dart 3.12.2. The pins become carets only in beta 3.47.0-0.1.pre (Dart 3.13.0): meta ^1.18.3, vector_math ^2.4.0, matcher 0.12.20, test_api 0.7.12, intl ^0.20.3. Not worth moving to beta.

Fixing this (a Dart-3.13 Flutter reaching stable) unblocks: build_runner 2.15.2 (needs analyzer >=13.3.0 -> meta ^1.18.3), test 1.31.2 (test_api 0.7.13), meta 1.19.0, vector_math 2.4.1, matcher 0.12.20, intl 0.20.3, package_config 3.0.0.

== Unrelated to both ==
flutter_secure_storage_darwin 0.4.0 is capped by flutter_secure_storage 10.3.1 requiring ^0.3.2 — waiting on that package.

== Action ==
Recheck riverpod_analyzer_utils first; that is the gate. Do the riverpod+freezed+analyzer bump as one pass when it lands, then a second pass after the next Flutter stable.

comments.author: Jan-Henrik Bruhn
comments.text:
Rechecked 2026-07-26 evening. The riverpod side is a SAME-DAY publishing slip, not a long stall — recheck in days, not months.

riverpod 3.4.0 (17:28 UTC), 3.4.1 (17:31), riverpod_generator 4.0.6 (17:32) and riverpod_lint 3.1.6 (17:32) all went out today. riverpod_analyzer_utils was NOT part of that release: newest is still 1.0.0-dev.10 from 2026-04-23 with analyzer ^12.0.0. They shipped the analyzer-13 migration without the helper package it pins.

Confirmed with pub's solver on a throwaway package rather than by reading constraints:

  Because riverpod_analyzer_utils >=1.0.0-dev.10 depends on analyzer ^12.0.0 and
  riverpod_generator >=4.0.6 depends on analyzer ^13.0.0, riverpod_analyzer_utils
  >=1.0.0-dev.10 is incompatible with riverpod_generator >=4.0.6.

Runtime-only bump is also impossible (tested): riverpod_annotation 4.0.3 pins riverpod to exactly 3.3.2, and we need it for @riverpod. So the 3.4.0 fixes are out of reach until codegen moves — notably invalidate/refresh not finding providers when called from a scoped ProviderScope with overrides, a markNeedsBuild exception when flushing a provider inside the widget lifecycle, and a listener leak when ConsumerState.dispose throws.

Watch for riverpod_analyzer_utils 1.0.0-dev.11 (or any release accepting analyzer 13). That single publish unblocks riverpod 3.4.1 + generator 4.0.6 + lint 3.1.6 + analyzer 13.0.0 + freezed 4.0.0-dev.3 + dart_style 3.1.9 on the CURRENT Flutter — no SDK upgrade needed.

comments.author: Jan-Henrik Bruhn
comments.text:
CORRECTION to the earlier comment: a riverpod fix ALONE is not enough. Both ceilings must lift, and the Flutter one binds through test_api, not meta.

Tried the obvious workaround for real — riverpod_analyzer_utils overridden to git (master already has analyzer ^13.0.0 and sdk ^3.12.0 under the SAME version number 1.0.0-dev.10; they bumped the constraint without bumping the version, which is why the published tarball still says analyzer ^12.0.0 and why their own CI missed it: the monorepo uses resolution: workspace, so they never resolve the published artifact).

The override resolves fine in a throwaway pure-Dart package (analyzer 13.3.0, riverpod 3.4.1, meta 1.19.0). It does NOT resolve in this workspace:

  because federfall depends on flutter_test from sdk which depends on test_api 0.7.11,
  test >=1.24.3 ... requires analyzer >=8.0.0 <11.0.0
  ... test 1.31.0 depends on analyzer >=8.0.0 <13.0.0 and every version of
  riverpod_analyzer_utils from git depends on analyzer ^13.0.0

Chain: flutter_test pins test_api: 0.7.11 EXACTLY -> the only  matching that is 1.31.0 (1.31.1 wants test_api 0.7.12) -> test 1.31.0 requires analyzer >=8.0.0 <13.0.0. federfall_models and federfall_data depend on test ^1.25.0, and a pub workspace is ONE resolution shared with the Flutter app, so analyzer is capped below 13 for the whole repo. The meta: 1.18.0 pin I flagged first would only have capped analyzer at 13.0.0; test_api caps it at 12.x, so test_api is the tighter Flutter-side constraint.

Consequence: analyzer 13 (hence freezed 4, riverpod 3.4.x, generator 4.0.6, lint 3.1.6, dart_style 3.1.9+) needs BOTH (a) riverpod to publish a fixed riverpod_analyzer_utils and (b) a Flutter stable on Dart 3.13, whose flutter_test pins test_api 0.7.12 (verified in beta 3.47.0-0.1.pre) allowing test 1.31.1+ which permits analyzer <14.

Also note for whoever does the bump: riverpod_lint's version is declared TWICE — apps/federfall/pubspec.yaml dev_dependencies AND the workspace-root analysis_options.yaml 'plugins:' key (^3.1.4). Both need editing.

comments.author: Jan-Henrik Bruhn
comments.text:
Rechecked 2026-08-07 (Flutter 3.44.3 / Dart 3.12.2 locally; newest stable 3.44.9). CEILING 1 IS GONE. CEILING 2 IS NOW THE SOLE BLOCKER, and it is unchanged.

Ceiling 1 (riverpod) — resolved upstream, exactly as predicted:
riverpod_analyzer_utils 1.0.0-dev.11 was published 2026-07-27, the day after this ticket, with analyzer ^13.0.0. riverpod_generator 4.0.7/4.0.8 and riverpod_lint 3.1.7/3.1.8 (2026-07-27/28) pin dev.11, so the set is self-consistent again. Nothing left to wait for on the riverpod side.

Ceiling 2 (Flutter SDK) — still binding, and no stable moved.
Stable is 3.44.9 (2026-08-06), still Dart 3.12.2, and its flutter_test still pins `test_api: 0.7.11` + `matcher: 0.12.19` EXACTLY (read out of the installed SDK, not inferred). Dart 3.13 remains beta-only: 3.47.0-0.4.pre (2026-08-05). So the whole 3.44.x line is byte-identical on the pins that matter, as the earlier comment found for 3.44.8.

Verified by resolution, not by reading constraints — temporarily bumped riverpod_generator ^4.0.8, riverpod_lint ^3.1.8, freezed ^4.0.0-dev.3 (app + federfall_models, which declares freezed too) and ran pub get:

  And because federfall depends on flutter_test from sdk which depends on test_api 0.7.11,
  test >=1.24.3 <1.31.0-∞ or >1.31.0 requires analyzer >=8.0.0 <11.0.0.
  And because test 1.31.0 depends on analyzer >=8.0.0 <13.0.0 and federfall_models depends
  on test ^1.25.0, analyzer >=8.0.0 <13.0.0 is required.
  So, because federfall depends on riverpod_generator ^4.0.8 which depends on analyzer ^13.0.0,
  version solving failed.

Reverted; the repo is back on the pinned cohort.

The exact version wanted is `test`, which has three rungs and only one fits: 1.31.0 -> test_api 0.7.11 + analyzer <13 (what we get), 1.31.1 -> test_api 0.7.12 + analyzer <14, 1.31.2 -> test_api 0.7.13 + analyzer >=13 <15. So the single upstream event to watch is now a Flutter STABLE whose flutter_test pins test_api 0.7.12 or newer. Watch flutter stable release notes, not pub.

Still pinned behind it: riverpod/flutter_riverpod 3.4.2, riverpod_annotation 4.0.6, riverpod_generator 4.0.8, riverpod_lint 3.1.8, analyzer 13/14, freezed 4.0.0-dev.3, build_runner 2.16.0, test 1.31.2, mockito 5.8.1, meta 1.19.0, dart_style 3.1.12, intl 0.20.3.

Done separately today: flutter_secure_storage 11.0.0 shipped 2026-08-06 and IS adopted (commit 9b6857c), which closes the "unrelated to both ceilings" item — flutter_secure_storage_darwin is on 0.4.0 now. Also picked up go_router 17.4.0 and json_serializable 6.14.1 within existing constraints.

Reminder for the eventual bump, still true: riverpod_lint's version is declared TWICE — apps/federfall/pubspec.yaml dev_dependencies AND the workspace-root analysis_options.yaml 'plugins:' key.

title: Drop the quarantine-days field from the intake wizard
description:
Step 1 of the intake wizard asks for quarantine duration
(`features/cases/new_case_screen.dart:629`), prefilled from
`orgQuarantineDefaultDaysProvider`.

It fails the subtraction test:

- The backend hook applies the org default anyway. The submit path only sends the
  value when it differs from the default it prefilled
  (`new_case_screen.dart:320-323`), and the code says so: "The org-default
  duration is applied by the backend hook anyway, so only an explicit per-case
  override travels with the intake."
- Quarantine is no longer a static case field — it is its own timeline record
  kind with its own sheet (`quarantine_sheet.dart`, federfall-uvm), editable on
  the case at any point.

So the field surfaces a decision to every single intake in order to let a carer
override a value they can equally override afterwards, on a screen better suited
to it. It costs a field, an `initState` async prefill, a controller, and a branch
in the submit payload.

Fix: remove it from the wizard and let the hook's default stand. The per-case
override stays available through the quarantine timeline record. If a
frequently-overridden default is a real workflow, the better answer is fixing the
org default in admin, not asking at every intake.

Source: general design review (cognitive load — unnecessary decisions).

comments.author: Jan-Henrik Bruhn
comments.text:
Checked whether the hook overrides the wizard value (it does not — no hook bug here).

Two hooks interlock correctly:
- `intake.pb.js` creates the `quarantine_records` row inside the intake transaction when `quarantine_days` is present.
- `main.pb.js`'s after-create default hook queries for an existing quarantine row first and skips if it finds one ("a case that somehow already has a quarantine row gets no second default").

So an explicit per-case duration WINS, and atomically. The issue's line "the backend hook applies the org default anyway" describes the *unchanged* case only: the wizard omits `quarantine_days` from the payload when it still equals the prefilled org default (new_case_screen.dart:320-323), so the hook's default row stands. Nothing is clobbered.

That leaves this as purely the product question it was filed as — does the field earn a slot in every intake when the same value is editable afterwards on the quarantine timeline record — not a backend fix. No hook change needed either way.

title: Accessibility pass: no text-scale handling, almost no Semantics
description:
No accessibility pass appears to have been done on the app. Findings from a
sweep of `apps/federfall/lib`:

- **Text scale is never considered.** Zero references to `textScaler`,
  `TextScaler` or `textScaleFactor` anywhere. The one place this is already known
  to bite is the statistics KPI's `SizedBox(width: 160)` around wrapping text
  (tracked separately in the KPI-unification issue).
- **`Semantics` appears in 4 files only** — `animal_avatar.dart`,
  `egg_entry_tile.dart`, `journal_entry_tile.dart`, `case_detail_screen.dart`.
  Material widgets carry their own semantics so this is not automatically a
  defect, but it means nothing has been checked deliberately.
- **No a11y test coverage.** No golden or semantics assertions; `federfall-aws`
  (golden tests) is the nearest open issue.

Things that already look right and should not be "fixed": 44 `tooltip:`
arguments cover the icon-only controls, and overdue worklist rows carry the
overdue state in *words* (`worklistOverdueHours`/`worklistOverdueDays` in
`worklist_labels.dart:65`), so the error colour is redundant rather than the sole
signal — colour-only meaning is not a problem here.

Scope for this issue: run the app at 200% text scale and with TalkBack over the
core paths (intake wizard, case detail, add-entry sheet, dose calculator), fix
what breaks, and file specifics as children.

Source: Dieter Rams design review (principle 8, thorough).

comments.author: Jan-Henrik Bruhn
comments.text:
Adjacent finding from the iOS plist fix (federfall-clu1): `apps/federfall/web/index.html` opens with a bare `<html>` — no `lang` attribute — so on web a screen reader has no language hint for the document and guesses pronunciation.

Note it is NOT a matter of just hardcoding `lang="de"`: as of federfall-qdsa the app follows the device language, and Flutter does not update `<html lang>` when it resolves a locale. So the fix is either a small bootstrap script that stamps the resolved locale onto `document.documentElement.lang`, or accepting the fallback language as the document default. Worth folding into this pass rather than filing separately.

title: caseReadOnlyTooltip is the only German string using formal address
description:
`app_de.arb` addresses the user informally everywhere — 21 strings use du/dein
(`errorOffline`, `errorUnauthorized`, `errorUnknownOutcome`, `serverUnreachable`,
`authResetDescription`, `discardChangesMessage`, `printerRemoveConfirmMessage`,
and others).

Exactly one uses "Sie":

    caseReadOnlyTooltip: "Sie haben nur Lesezugriff auf diesen Fall"

Fix: "Du hast nur Lesezugriff auf diesen Fall." (en side needs no change.)

Verified by sweeping every non-metadata string in `app_de.arb` for
Sie/Ihr/Ihnen vs du/dein — this is the only hit on the formal side.

Source: Dieter Rams design review (principle 8, thorough down to the last
detail).
close_reason: Fixed: app_de.arb's caseReadOnlyTooltip now uses du ('Du hast nur Lesezugriff auf diesen Fall'), matching the other 21 informal strings.

title: Statistics breakdown rows are dead ends
description:
Every KPI on the dashboard taps through to the cases it counts — `_KpiCard`
seeds a `CaseQuery` and switches to the Cases tab
(`features/dashboard/dashboard_screen.dart:276`). That is the pattern the app
establishes: a number is a way in.

The statistics screen breaks it. `_Breakdown`
(`features/statistics/statistics_screen.dart:230`) renders outcome, species and
condition counts as plain non-interactive rows. A supervisor who sees "Euthanized
· 14" has no way to ask which fourteen; the only route out is the CSV export.

Fix: make each breakdown row tap through to the Cases tab with the matching
filter, reusing `pendingCaseQueryProvider` exactly as the dashboard KPIs do.
`CaseQuery` already supports species; outcome and condition would need facets
adding (check `filterCases` in `cases_browser.dart` first — this may be the bulk
of the work, and it is worth confirming the query model can express these before
committing).

Source: Dieter Rams design review (principle 2 useful / 4 understandable —
inconsistent with a pattern the app already sets).
close_reason: Outcome + condition are real CaseQuery facets, resolved via a new lazily-loaded CaseFacets projection (features/cases/case_facets.dart) so the plain Cases tab keeps its existing fetches. Condition matches on label, not code-list id, because a case_conditions row is either a reference or free text. computeStatistics counts conditions through the same projection, so count and tap-through list agree (and the count is now distinct-per-case). Dashboard's _showCases extracted to showCasesFiltered. Filter sheet shows the two facets as removable chips, not pickers.

title: Dose calculator: drop the duplicated unit field, read the Dose field for per-Tier
description:
Review finding on federfall-6d3a.1 (user's own observation): the calculator panel asks for things the sheet already knows.

1. The panel's Unit field duplicates the administration sheet's Unit field -- two inputs labelled 'Einheit' in one form. Drop the panel's; read the sheet's unit (it is already passed in as initialUnit) and use it for the mg/kg and mg/ml suffixes. Saves half a row.
2. For basis = per Tier the rate IS the dose, so the panel's rate input duplicates the Dose field too. There, hide the rate input and read the Dose field above: the panel then only asks for the concentration and answers 'that is X ml to draw'.

NOT applicable to per kg: there the rate is the input and the mg is derived, so the rate field and the explicit 'Uebernehmen' step both stay (decided against live-writing the Dose field while typing -- a clinical field that rewrites itself as you type is unpleasant, and the button is the one deliberate 'yes, this number' moment).
close_reason: Panel now reads the administration sheet's dose + unit controllers live (ListenableBuilder over Listenable.merge) instead of holding copies. Unit field removed. Per-kg unchanged (rate input + explicit Uebernehmen); per-Tier hides both the rate input and the button, converting the sheet's dose to ml and cross-checking it via the new DoseCalculation.ratePerKg. Blank record unit falls back to mg for display and is written back on apply. 508 app tests + 83 model tests green, analyze/format clean, coverage 78.68%.

title: Fluid-therapy & crop-feed volume calculators (reuse dose calc plumbing)
description:
Subcutaneous fluid volume (% of body weight per day) and crop-feed volume (~10% BW per feed) are the two weight-based calculations pigeon rehab performs most often, and they reuse the same latest-weight plumbing and pure calculation function as the dose calculator (federfall-6d3a).

They are NOT drug doses and must not be modelled on `medications` — needs its own thinking about where the result is recorded (journal entry? own record kind on the case timeline?). Revisit once federfall-6d3a.1 has shipped and we know whether the calculator panel gets used.

title: Phase 3 — Org-managed drug catalogue (rates, ranges, concentrations)
description:
Give the org a supervisor-managed drug catalogue so rate, route, concentration and
frequency prefill themselves and the clinical truth has an owner. docs/REQUIREMENTS.md:185
already anticipates this ("`drug` -> medications code list or free text").

Backend:
- New org-scoped collection (`medication_products` or `drugs`) following the code-list
  pattern of 1700000041_medication_routes_codelist.js: supervisor-only write, org-scoped
  read, `active` flag. Fields: label, default route (relation -> medication_routes),
  default rate + rate unit, rate min/max (the range check), concentration value + unit,
  default frequency preset, note.
- `medications.drug` stays free text; the catalogue is a prefill source, not a
  constraint — ad-hoc drugs must remain possible. Consider an optional `product`
  relation alongside it for reporting.

App:
- Repository + riverpod providers (mirror medication_routes_providers.dart).
- Admin screen: `CodelistSpec` (features/admin/codelist_specs.dart) is generic over
  {label, active} plus a couple of bolt-ons — a drug entry has ~6 more typed fields, so
  this needs its own screen wired into ManagementScreen, NOT another spec literal.
  Decide whether to generalise CodelistSpec or write a bespoke screen; bespoke is
  probably cheaper and honest.
- prescription_sheet.dart: pick a product -> prefill drug, route, rate, concentration,
  frequency preset; everything stays editable.
- Range check from min/max wired into the calculator warnings from Phase 1 (warn above
  max, block >10x max).
- Seeding: ship NO clinical values in the migration. An empty catalogue that the org's
  vet fills is the whole point — see the epic's rejection of a bundled formulary.
acceptance_criteria: A supervisor can maintain an org-scoped drug catalogue; picking a product in the prescription sheet prefills drug, route, rate, concentration and frequency, all still editable; the catalogue's min/max drives the calculator's range warnings; the migration seeds no clinical values.
close_reason: Migration 1700000060: medication_products collection, org-scoped read + supervisor-only write, seeded with 3 PLACEHOLDER rows (Medikament 1..3, no dosing numbers) at the user's request instead of an empty list — no clinical values ship. Fields mirror the prescription (dose_unit, dose_rate, concentration_per_ml, route, frequency_kind+interval_hours) so an entry pours in with no unit conversion, plus rate_min/rate_max as an ADVISORY range (warns, still saves). DEVIATIONS from the plan: (1) no product relation stored on medications — the entry supplies defaults and the range in-memory only, the plan stands on its own numbers (revisit if reporting needs it); (2) the range check lives in the prescription form at entry time, not in calculateDose, since by administration time the rate came from an already-checked plan. Own admin screen (medication_products_screen.dart) wired into ManagementScreen + a /admin/medications route — CodelistSpec is {label,active}+ and could not stretch to six typed fields. LESSON: the guest-wall sweep in test_rules.py caught the new collection's read rule missing role != guest before it shipped. 323 backend rule tests, 516 app + 80 model tests, analyze/format clean, coverage 78.68%.

title: Phase 2 — Persist the rate: weight-adaptive prescriptions + auditable doses
description:
Make the prescription weight-adaptive and the administered dose auditable. This is the
actual payoff of the epic — a plan that stays correct as the bird gains weight.

Schema (new numbered migration, never hand-edit):
- medications: `dose_rate` (number), `dose_rate_unit` (select: mg/kg | ml/kg | IU/kg |
  per_bird), and structured concentration — `concentration_value` (number) +
  `concentration_unit` (text) — migrating the dormant free-text `concentration`
  (1700000007_clinical_logs.js:70), which no UI currently writes. Decide in the migration
  whether to parse existing text (it is almost certainly empty in practice) or leave it
  as a legacy note field.
- medication_administrations: `weight_g_used` (number), `volume_ml` (number) — the
  derivation inputs, denormalized like drug/dose/route already are so the dose stays
  self-explaining if the plan is deleted.
- Access rules: children follow the parent case, unchanged; no new rule shape. Check
  whether `medication_due` needs the new columns (it selects dose/dose_unit today) —
  if so the view must be dropped and recreated in the same migration, see
  1700000041 for the pattern.

App:
- Model fields on Medication / MedicationAdministration (+ fromRecord), build_runner.
- prescription_sheet.dart: rate + rate unit + concentration inputs, live preview of what
  the rate means at the current weight.
- administration_sheet.dart: prefill the dose from plan.rate x current weight instead of
  the plan's fixed amount; persist weight_g_used + volume_ml with the dose.
- Fall back to the plan's fixed `dose` when no rate is set (every existing plan).
- Tile/timeline display of a rate-based plan (medication_tiles.dart).
- Rule/hook verification needs a live PB stack (backend/pocketbase/tests/test_rules.py
  via run.sh) — cannot run in the Flutter suite.
acceptance_criteria: A prescription can carry a mg/kg-style rate and a structured concentration; the administration sheet derives the dose from that rate times the current weight and stores weight_g_used + volume_ml; plans without a rate still behave exactly as today; migration is numbered and committed, and rules/hooks verified against a live PB stack.
notes: Scope change from 6d3a.4 review: the per-bird dose basis was REMOVED (DoseBasis enum + DoseCalculation.ratePerKg deleted in f5c9e62). The calculator is one workflow only — rate per kg + concentration per ml -> amount + volume. So the migration's dose_rate_unit does NOT need a per_bird value unless a real need shows up; design it as mg/kg | ml/kg | IU/kg and add per-bird later with tests if asked.
close_reason: Migration 1700000058: medications.dose_rate + concentration_per_ml (both in the plan's existing dose_unit — DEVIATION from the original plan: no separate dose_rate_unit/concentration_unit, one unit per prescription makes mg/kg vs mg/ml mismatch impossible and dose_unit 'ml'/'IU' already covers fluids and biologicals), legacy free-text concentration migrated then dropped, medication_administrations.weight_g_used + volume_ml, medication_due dropped/recreated over the new columns (worklist rebuilds a Medication from it). App: prescription sheet takes rate+strength with a live 'what it means for this bird' preview; calculator seeds from the plan and stores the derivation; typing over the amount drops it; rateless plans unchanged; tile shows the rate. Verified on a live stack: 315 rule tests pass (incl. new assertions for the view columns and derivation round-trip). 510 app + 78 model tests green, analyze/format clean, coverage 78.68%.

title: Phase 1 — Pure dose calculation + calculator panel in the administration sheet
description:
Ship the arithmetic with zero schema change, so we learn whether it gets used before
paying for a migration and an admin screen.

Scope:
- Pure `DoseCalculation` in packages/federfall_models (new dosing.dart): takes rate +
  rate unit + body weight in grams + optional concentration (value + unit), returns the
  amount, the volume (when a concentration is given), and the warnings (stale/missing
  weight, sub-syringe volume, out-of-range once ranges exist). No Flutter import.
- g -> kg conversion lives ONLY inside that function.
- An expandable "Dosisrechner" panel in
  apps/federfall/lib/features/cases/medications/administration_sheet.dart: reads the
  case's latest weight via weightsForCaseProvider (show value + measurement date), takes
  a manually entered rate and concentration, shows the derivation, and writes the result
  into the existing dose field on tap. Never auto-fills silently.
- Comma decimal separator accepted (the sheets already do `.replaceAll(',', '.')`).
- l10n in app_de.arb + app_en.arb, `flutter gen-l10n`.

Nothing is persisted beyond the existing `dose` / `dose_unit` in this phase.
acceptance_criteria: DoseCalculation is a pure, Flutter-free function in federfall_models with unit tests covering g/kg conversion, missing/stale weight, sub-syringe volume and comma decimals; the administration sheet has a Dosisrechner panel that shows the latest weight with its date and writes the computed dose into the field only on an explicit tap; dart format + flutter analyze clean, flutter test green, coverage above 75%.
close_reason: Shipped: pure calculateDose in federfall_models (g->kg in one tested place, missing/stale-weight + unmeasurable-volume warnings with a dilution suggestion, 4-significant-digit rounding) plus the inline DoseCalculatorPanel in the administration sheet. 19 model tests + 13 widget tests; analyze/format clean, 506 app tests green, coverage 78.6%. Learned the hard way in review: the app theme's filledButtonTheme sets an INFINITE minimum width (Size.fromHeight), so a filled button as a non-flex Row child fails layout and the Card's antiAlias clip silently swallows the whole panel -- widget tests must pump AppTheme.light to catch that class of bug (none of the repo's other tests do). Expansion uses AnimationStyle.noAnimation so the post-frame Scrollable.ensureVisible has a settled height. Follow-up filed for the duplicated unit field.

title: Dose calculator (weight-based medication dosing)
description:
Dose calculation for medications: rate (mg/kg) x body weight -> amount, / product
concentration (mg/ml) -> volume to draw. The arithmetic is trivial; the design work is
where the three inputs come from and what gets persisted.

## State of play (what exists)

- weight: `weights` collection, `Weight.weightG`, `weightsForCaseProvider` /
  `weightsForAnimalProvider` (apps/federfall/lib/features/cases/weights/weights_providers.dart).
- concentration: `medications.concentration` exists as free text
  (1700000007_clinical_logs.js:70, mapped in clinical.dart:48) but NO UI writes it —
  a dormant field.
- rate: does not exist anywhere. This is the gap.

## Core design decision — store the RATE, not just the resulting amount

`medications.dose` today is an absolute amount ("0.5 mg"). For a bird in rehab that goes
wrong within a week: a thin pigeon admitted at 240 g is 330 g by day ten and the plan
silently under-doses. Adding `dose_rate` + `dose_rate_unit` (mg/kg | ml/kg | IU/kg |
per-bird) makes the plan weight-adaptive — every dose re-derives from the current weight,
exactly the way `medication_due` already re-derives *when* the next dose falls.

On `medication_administrations` we keep storing the amount ACTUALLY given (that
collection is deliberately denormalized so a dose survives its plan) plus the derivation
inputs (`weight_g_used`, computed `volume_ml`). Without those, "why was 0.35 ml given on
the 3rd?" is unanswerable — which for a controlled substance (`is_controlled`) is the
whole point of the record.

## Where the rates come from — org catalogue, NOT a shipped formulary

Rejected: shipping a built-in formulary (Carpenter et al.). Licensing, staleness, and it
would make us the source of a number that killed a bird.
Chosen: a supervisor-owned, org-scoped drug catalogue (label, default route, default rate
+ min/max range, stock concentration, default frequency preset, note). The org's vet owns
the clinical truth, the app owns the arithmetic. docs/REQUIREMENTS.md:185 already
anticipates this ("`drug` -> medications code list or free text").
Cost to be honest about: `CodelistSpec` (features/admin/codelist_specs.dart) is generic
over {label, active} plus a couple of bolt-ons; a drug entry has ~6 more typed fields, so
this needs its OWN admin screen, not another spec literal.

## UI placement — no standalone calculator screen

A separate "Dosisrechner" tab is a thing people forget exists and then do on paper. The
calculator lives where the dose is already being typed, in the two sheets that already
have the case id and can watch the latest weight:
- prescription_sheet.dart — vet enters rate + concentration when writing the plan; sheet
  shows what that means today ("20 mg/kg x 262 g = 5,2 mg = 0,35 ml").
- administration_sheet.dart — carer's path; prefills from plan.rate x current weight with
  the derivation visible under the field and editable. Never silently. This also covers
  the worklist "Dosis eintragen" quick action, which opens the same sheet.

## Safety rails (in priority order)

1. g<->kg conversion in EXACTLY one place, a pure tested function — weights are stored in
   grams, rates are per kg; that decimal shift is the classic kill.
2. Weight staleness: no weight, or older than ~3-7 days -> do not prefill, say "Vogel
   wiegen". A stale weight silently used is worse than no calculator.
3. Range check against the catalogue min/max — warn above, block absurd (>10x max).
4. Syringe reality: below ~0.05 ml a number is fiction. Show volume at 0.01 ml resolution
   and surface a dilution hint (1:10 -> 0.3 ml). For a 250 g pigeon on concentrated stock
   this is the common case, not an edge case.
5. Always show the formula so a carer can check it against the paper protocol.

The calculation itself is a pure function in packages/federfall_models (not a widget
method) — it is the one piece here that deserves exhaustive unit tests, and it tests
without Flutter.

## Out of scope (noted for later)

Fluid therapy (% body weight/day, subcutaneous) and crop-feed volume (~10% BW per feed)
are the two calculations pigeon rehab actually does most, and they reuse the same weight
plumbing. They are NOT drug doses and must not ride on `medications`. If Phase 1 lands
well, they are the obvious second consumer of the pure function.
acceptance_criteria: A carer logging a dose sees the amount derived from the bird's current weight and the prescribed rate, with the formula visible and editable; the derivation is persisted with the administration; the org's supervisor owns the drug rates. No clinical values ship with the app.
close_reason: All 4 phases delivered. Dose calculation now runs end to end: a supervisor maintains the org's drug catalogue (placeholder-seeded, no clinical values), a prescription carries the mg/kg rate and mg/ml strength (both in one dose_unit so they cannot disagree), and logging a planned dose needs no taps — the calculator opens pre-filled from the plan and the bird's newest weight, stores what it derived from (weight_g_used, volume_ml), and refuses to pre-fill off a stale weight. Pure calculateDose in federfall_models is the single place grams become kilograms. Three lessons worth keeping: widget tests must pump AppTheme.light (see flutter-tests-need-app-theme memory), PocketBase numbers have no null (pocketbase-numbers-have-no-null memory), and the guest-wall sweep in test_rules.py catches new collections that copy the auth predicate. Follow-up federfall-qzi8 (fluid therapy / crop-feed volumes) reuses the same weight plumbing.

title: App locale is hardcoded to German (English l10n exists but is unreachable)
description:
Discovered while building federfall-gdp8's PDF report and confirming it's OK
to hardcode German output there: apps/federfall/lib/app/view/app.dart:29 pins
`locale: const Locale('de')` unconditionally - it does not follow the device/
system locale, and there is no in-app language switch anywhere. The same
hardcoding is repeated in features/reminders/medication_reminders.dart:74 for
notification text, with an explicit comment explaining why ("the app's UI
language is fixed... so the notification copy follows it").

app_en.arb is fully maintained alongside app_de.arb (CLAUDE.md's l10n
convention) and AppLocalizations.supportedLocales includes both, but English
is currently unreachable at runtime - dead translation work if this is
permanent, or a gap if a language switch was always intended.

Not urgent (no user complaint driving it, and German-only matches the current
target audience), but worth a decision: either (a) commit to German-only and
consider dropping/not-maintaining app_en.arb to stop the double-translation
tax, or (b) add a real locale switch (system locale by default, or a settings
toggle) and update app.dart + medication_reminders.dart accordingly.

If (b) is ever chosen: the case-report PDF hook (pb_hooks/case_report.pb.js,
federfall-gdp8) hardcodes German label maps for its enums and would need to
pick between a German/English table too, e.g. via Accept-Language or an
explicit query param - contained change, the label maps are already isolated
in one place.
close_reason: Resolved with option (b): the app follows the device language. app.dart uses localeListResolutionCallback -> resolveAppLocale (new, in l10n/l10n.dart), which matches on language code and falls back to kFallbackLocale = de rather than leaning on gen-l10n's alphabetically-sorted supportedLocales.first. medication_reminders.dart resolves the same way via WidgetsBinding's platformDispatcher.locales instead of pinning Locale('de'). app_en.arb is now reachable. Server-side report localization filed separately.

title: Per-case timeline CSV export
description:
Export one case's chronology (weights, medications, journal, etc. - the same
records federfall-gdp8's PDF report covers) as a CSV, one row per timeline
entry. Deliberately deferred out of the federfall-gdp8 PDF-report work
(2026-07-05 session) - user asked to defer CSV and file a separate issue.

Independent of:
- the existing org-wide case-list CSV export in
  apps/federfall/lib/features/statistics/case_report.dart (that's one row per
  CASE across the org, not one case's internal timeline)
- federfall-dk0c (annual-report PDF)

Low priority / backlog - no concrete use case driving it yet.

title: Show entry source info as subtext in the fullscreen image viewer
description: ImageViewerScreen (lib/ui/widgets/image_viewer.dart) currently has no per-image caption/subtitle mechanism -- the app bar only shows an 'i/total' index counter. Requested: show some subtext about the photo's source (e.g. which record it came from -- intake vs. a specific journal entry, its date) when viewing full-screen. Needs new infra: a per-image label/caption passed through showImageViewer's imageUrls (currently just List<String>, would need to become a richer type or a parallel List<String?> of captions) and rendered in the ImageViewerScreen app bar/body. Affects all three callers: case_photo_gallery.dart's caseGalleryProvider (already carries enough info per CasePhoto to build a caption -- e.g. intake vs. journal entry + date), journal_entry_tile.dart's _AttachmentStrip, and animal_avatar.dart. Deferred from federfall-6rdd because the viewer had no such feature to hook into yet.

title: Photo tap targets use deferToChild GestureDetector, untappable while loading
description: journal_entry_tile.dart's _AttachmentStrip wraps each photo thumbnail in a plain GestureDetector (default HitTestBehavior.deferToChild). Since the thumbnail is a CachedFileImage, taps only register once the image has actually decoded a frame -- while loading (or on any load failure) the tile is silently untappable, because nothing in the placeholder's render chain (Container/LimitedBox/ConstrainedBox) reports hitTestSelf=true. Found and fixed for the new case photo gallery (federfall-6rdd) by adding behavior: HitTestBehavior.opaque to its GestureDetector; the journal attachment strip has the same bug and should get the same one-line fix. See bd memory gesturedetector-defertochild-image-tap for the full writeup.
close_reason: Fixed: journal_entry_tile.dart's _AttachmentStrip GestureDetector now sets behavior: HitTestBehavior.opaque, same one-line fix the case photo gallery got in federfall-6rdd.

title: Case photo gallery on the Overview tab
description: Photos are currently scattered across timeline tiles (intake, journal, exam). Add a consolidated photo grid on the case-detail Overview tab showing all images for the case — intake photo first, then journal/exam photos — each tappable to a full-screen viewer. Aligns with federfall-ui-prefers-unified-consistent-views (one consistent view over fragmented sections). Consider extending to an animal-lifetime gallery across re-admission episodes as a follow-up. Reuse fileUrl(id, name, {thumb}) for thumbnails.
close_reason: Implemented: caseGalleryProvider + _CasePhotoGallery card on Overview, replaced inline intake-photo strip, added l10n key, widget tests (ordering, empty state, tap-to-viewer).
